about: A subject matter relation between an entity (e.g., a creative work, event, or communication) and the topic it concerns. Also called concerning, regarding, on the topic of, related to. Examples: "A book about quantum physics.", "A lecture about climate change.", "A certification about data privacy."
abridged: An abridgment status indicating whether a book is a shortened version. Also called shortened, condensed, edited for length. Examples: "An abridged edition of 'Les Misérables' is true.", "An abridged version of 'Moby Dick' is false."
abstract: An abstract relation between a creative work and a short text summarizing its content. Also called summary, synopsis, précis, overview. Examples: "A research paper's abstract describes its findings.", "A movie's abstract outlines its plot."
accelerationTime: An acceleration time relation between a vehicle and the quantitative value representing the time it takes to accelerate between specified velocities. Also called 0-60 mph time, speed-up duration, sprint time. Examples: "A sports car's acceleration time is 3.5 seconds (0-60 mph).", "An electric vehicle's acceleration time is 2.8 seconds (0-100 km/h)."
acceptedAnswer: An accepted answer relation between a question and the answer(s) deemed best or most appropriate. Also called best answer, chosen solution, preferred response. Examples: "A forum question's accepted answer is 'Use a screwdriver'.", "A quiz question's accepted answer is 'Option B'."
acceptedOffer: An accepted offer relation between an order and the specific offer(s) that were agreed upon and included in it. Also called purchased offer, confirmed offer, included offer. Examples: "A customer's order accepted an offer for a laptop.", "The order accepted an offer for two books."
acceptedPaymentMethod: An accepted payment method relation between an organization, demand, or offer and the payment methods it allows. Also called payment options, payment types, accepted forms of payment. Examples: "A store accepts credit card payments.", "An online offer accepts PayPal.", "The organization accepts bank transfers."
acceptsReservations: A reservation acceptance status indicating whether a food establishment allows bookings. Also called takes reservations, booking available, reservation policy. Examples: "A restaurant accepts reservations is true.", "The cafe accepts reservations via its website URL.", "This diner accepts reservations is 'No'."
accessCode: An access code relation between a delivery event and the text string required to access the delivered item. Also called delivery PIN, locker code, entry code. Examples: "The package delivery event has an access code '12345'.", "The locker delivery access code is 'PIN6789'."
accessMode: An access mode relation between a creative work and the human sensory or cognitive system through which its content can be perceived. Also called perceptual mode, sensory access, content modality. Examples: "A video's access mode is 'visual'.", "An audiobook's access mode is 'auditory'.", "A text document's access mode is 'textual'."
accessModeSufficient: A sufficient access mode relation between a creative work and a list of access modes that are adequate for understanding its full intellectual content. Also called sufficient perceptual modes, adequate access methods. Examples: "A captioned video's sufficient access modes are 'visual' and 'textual'.", "A podcast with a transcript's sufficient access modes are 'auditory' and 'textual'."
accessibilityAPI: An accessibility API compatibility relation between a creative work and the accessibility API it supports. Also called API support, accessibility interface. Examples: "A software application's accessibility API is 'AT-SPI'.", "A web page's accessibility API is 'ARIA'."
accessibilityControl: An accessibility control relation between a creative work and the input methods sufficient for its full control. Also called control methods, input compatibility, interaction modes. Examples: "A video game's accessibility control is 'keyboard'.", "A web application's accessibility control is 'mouse'."
accessibilityFeature: An accessibility feature relation between a creative work and its specific features designed to enhance accessibility. Also called accessible features, accessibility enhancements, content adaptations. Examples: "A movie's accessibility feature is 'captions'.", "An image's accessibility feature is 'altText'.", "A document's accessibility feature is 'highContrast'."
accessibilityHazard: An accessibility hazard relation between a creative work and a characteristic that poses a physiological danger to some users. Also called accessibility risk, dangerous feature, user hazard. Examples: "A video's accessibility hazard is 'flashingLights'.", "A game's accessibility hazard is 'motionSimulation'."
accessibilitySummary: An accessibility summary relation between a creative work and a human-readable text describing its accessibility features and deficiencies. Also called accessibility overview, access statement, accessibility report. Examples: "A website's accessibility summary states 'Short descriptions are present but long descriptions will be needed for non-visual users'.", "A document's accessibility summary notes 'Fully navigable by keyboard'."
accommodationCategory: An accommodation category relation between an accommodation and its classification type, often following real estate conventions. Also called property type, lodging category, dwelling classification. Examples: "A hotel room's accommodation category is 'Suite'.", "An apartment's accommodation category is 'Condo'.", "A house's accommodation category is 'SingleFamilyResidence'."
accommodationFloorPlan: An accommodation floor plan relation between an accommodation or residence and its architectural layout. Also called layout diagram, property blueprint, room arrangement. Examples: "A hotel suite's accommodation floor plan shows two bedrooms.", "The residence's accommodation floor plan includes a garage."
accountId: An account identifier relation between an invoice and the text string identifying the account to which its payment will be applied. Also called billing account ID, customer account number, payment account reference. Examples: "An invoice's account ID is 'CUST12345'.", "The utility bill's account ID is '987654321'."
accountMinimumInflow: An account minimum inflow relation between a bank account and the monetary amount that must be deposited monthly. Also called minimum monthly deposit, required inflow, minimum payment. Examples: "A savings account's minimum inflow is $50.", "The checking account's minimum inflow is €100."
accountOverdraftLimit: An account overdraft limit relation between a bank account and the monetary amount representing the maximum credit extension allowed when funds are depleted. Also called overdraft maximum, credit limit, borrowing allowance. Examples: "A checking account's overdraft limit is $500.", "The business account's overdraft limit is £1000."
accountablePerson: An accountable person relation between a creative work and the individual legally responsible for it. Also called legally responsible person, liable party, responsible individual. Examples: "A news article's accountable person is its editor-in-chief.", "A company report's accountable person is the CEO."
acquireLicensePage: An acquire license page relation between a creative work and the web page or resource detailing how its licenses can be obtained. Also called licensing information page, purchase license URL, rights acquisition page. Examples: "A stock photo's acquire license page is its licensing terms URL.", "A software's acquire license page describes its purchase options."
acquiredFrom: An acquired from relation between ownership information and the organization or person from whom a product was obtained. Also called purchased from, obtained from, source of acquisition. Examples: "The car's ownership info indicates it was acquired from 'Dealership X'.", "The book's ownership info shows it was acquired from 'John Doe'."
acrissCode: An ACRISS code relation between a bus, coach, or car and its standardized classification code used by car rental companies. Also called car classification code, vehicle rental code. Examples: "A rental car's ACRISS code is 'ECAR'.", "A luxury sedan's ACRISS code is 'LDAR'."
actionAccessibilityRequirement: An action accessibility requirement relation between a consume action and the specifications that must be met to perform it. Also called action prerequisites, access conditions, fulfillment requirements. Examples: "A 'watch movie' action's accessibility requirement is 'subscription'.", "A 'download software' action's accessibility requirement is 'login'."
actionApplication: An action application relation between an entry point and the software application capable of fulfilling the associated request. Also called handling application, processing app, execution software. Examples: "A 'send email' entry point's action application is 'Gmail'.", "A 'edit document' entry point's action application is 'Microsoft Word'." Distinct from application, which is a more general property for an application that can complete the request.
actionOption: An action option relation between a choose action and the available choices or alternatives. Also called choice alternatives, selection options, available choices. Examples: "A 'choose color' action's action option is 'red'.", "A 'select size' action's action option is 'large'."
actionPlatform: An action platform relation between an entry point and the high-level digital platform(s) where the associated action can be performed. Also called execution platform, supported environment, operating system. Examples: "A web application's action platform is 'WebPlatform'.", "A mobile app's action platform is 'iOS'."
actionProcess: An action process relation between an action and the step-by-step instructions or method by which it was carried out. Also called execution method, procedure, how-to guide. Examples: "A 'bake cake' action's action process is a recipe.", "A 'repair car' action's action process is a repair manual."
actionStatus: An action status relation between an action and its current disposition or state. Also called action state, status of action, disposition. Examples: "A 'purchase' action's action status is 'CompletedActionStatus'.", "A 'shipment' action's action status is 'PotentialActionStatus'."
actionableFeedbackPolicy: An actionable feedback policy relation between a news media organization or organization and a creative work or URL detailing its public engagement and feedback mechanisms. Also called public engagement policy, feedback guidelines, reader interaction policy. Examples: "A news organization's actionable feedback policy is its 'Corrections and Feedback' page.", "The company's actionable feedback policy outlines how customers can submit suggestions."
activeIngredient: An active ingredient relation between a dietary supplement, drug, drug strength, or substance and its primary chemical or biologic component. Also called main component, primary substance, key compound. Examples: "A pain reliever's active ingredient is 'ibuprofen'.", "A vitamin supplement's active ingredient is 'Vitamin C'."
activityDuration: An activity duration relation between an exercise plan and the length of time recommended for engaging in the activity. Also called exercise length, workout time, session duration. Examples: "An exercise plan's activity duration is '30 minutes'.", "The yoga routine's activity duration is '1 hour'."
activityFrequency: An activity frequency relation between an exercise plan and how often the activity should be performed. Also called exercise frequency, workout schedule, repetition rate. Examples: "An exercise plan's activity frequency is '3 times per week'.", "The meditation guide's activity frequency is 'daily'."
actor: An actor relation between a creative work (e.g., movie, episode, video game) or event and a person or performing group who performs in it. Also called performer, cast member, player. Examples: "A movie's actor is 'Tom Hanks'.", "A play's actor is 'The Ensemble Theatre'.", "An episode's actor is 'Jane Doe'." Distinct from actors, which is a deprecated property for the same concept.
actors: An actor relation between a creative work (e.g., movie, episode, video game) and a person who performs in it. Also called performer, cast member, player. Examples: "A movie's actors include 'Brad Pitt'.", "An episode's actors include 'Jennifer Aniston'." Distinct from actor, which is the preferred and more general property that also allows PerformingGroup.
addOn: An add-on relation between a base offer and an additional offer that can only be acquired in conjunction with it. Also called supplementary offer, bundled offer, extra option. Examples: "A car purchase offer has an add-on for extended warranty.", "A software license offer has an add-on for premium support."
additionalName: An additional name relation between a person and a supplementary name, such as a middle name. Also called middle name, secondary name, other name. Examples: "A person's additional name is 'Marie'.", "John's additional name is 'Fitzgerald'."
additionalNumberOfGuests: An additional number of guests relation between an RSVP action and the count of extra attendees beyond the invitee. Also called plus-one count, extra guests, total additional attendees. Examples: "An RSVP action's additional number of guests is '2'.", "The wedding RSVP indicates an additional number of guests of '1'."
additionalProperty: An additional property relation between an entity (e.g., product, offer, place) and a property-value pair describing a characteristic not covered by specific schema.org properties. Also called extra characteristic, custom attribute, supplementary detail. Examples: "A product's additional property is 'waterResistance: IP68'.", "A place's additional property is 'historicalSignificance: high'."
additionalType: An additional type relation between a thing and a more specific type from an external vocabulary or a descriptive text. Also called supplementary type, extended type, semantic type. Examples: "A person's additional type is 'foaf:Agent'.", "A document's additional type is 'schema:Report'."
additionalVariable: An additional variable relation between an exercise plan and any extra components of the exercise prescription, such as exercise order or progression details. Also called exercise detail, workout parameter, prescription addendum. Examples: "An exercise plan's additional variable is 'Perform exercises in circuit order'.", "The rehabilitation plan's additional variable is 'Increase repetitions by 2 each week'."
address: An address relation between an entity (e.g., organization, person, place) and its physical postal address. Also called physical location, mailing address, street address. Examples: "A company's address is '123 Main St, Anytown'.", "A person's address is 'PO Box 123'.", "The restaurant's address is '456 Oak Ave'."
addressCountry: An address country relation between a defined region, geo-coordinates, geo-shape, or postal address and the country it is located within. Also called nation, country code, geographic country. Examples: "A postal address's address country is 'US'.", "The coordinates' address country is 'France'."
addressLocality: An address locality relation between a postal address and the city or town where it is situated. Also called city, town, municipality. Examples: "A postal address's address locality is 'Mountain View'.", "The address locality is 'London'."
addressRegion: An address region relation between a defined region or postal address and the administrative division (e.g., state, province) it belongs to. Also called state, province, administrative area. Examples: "A postal address's address region is 'CA'.", "The address region is 'Bavaria'."
administrationRoute: An administration route relation between a drug and the method by which it is intended to be given. Also called dosage route, delivery method, intake method. Examples: "A medication's administration route is 'oral'.", "An injection's administration route is 'intravenous'."
advanceBookingRequirement: An advance booking requirement relation between a demand or offer and the minimum time needed between acceptance and actual usage. Also called lead time, booking lead time, reservation notice. Examples: "A flight offer's advance booking requirement is '24 hours'.", "The concert ticket demand has an advance booking requirement of '7 days'."
adverseOutcome: An adverse outcome relation between a medical device or therapeutic procedure and a possible complication or side effect. Also called side effect, complication, negative reaction. Examples: "A surgery's adverse outcome is 'infection'.", "A medical device's adverse outcome is 'skin irritation'." Distinct from seriousAdverseOutcome, which is specifically for life-threatening or severe complications.
affectedBy: An affected by relation between a medical test and the drugs that can influence its results. Also called influenced by, impacted by, drug interaction. Examples: "A blood test's results are affected by 'anticoagulants'.", "The diagnostic test is affected by 'caffeine'."
affiliation: An affiliation relation between a person and an organization they are associated with. Also called associated with, member of, works for, belongs to. Examples: "A professor's affiliation is 'Harvard University'.", "A player's affiliation is 'Local Soccer Club'." Distinct from alumniOf, which specifies a past association with an educational organization.
afterMedia: An after media relation between a how-to direction and a media object or URL depicting the state or circumstances after completing that step. Also called post-step media, result image, outcome visual. Examples: "A recipe direction's after media is an image of the mixed ingredients.", "The assembly instruction's after media is a video of the connected parts."
agent: An agent relation between an action and the organization or person who directly performs or drives it. Also called performer, doer, initiator, actor. Examples: "A 'write book' action's agent is 'John Doe'.", "A 'deliver package' action's agent is 'Delivery Service Inc'."
agentInteractionStatistic: An agent interaction statistic relation between an organization or person and a counter representing their completed interactions in a specific agent role and context. Also called interaction count, activity metric, engagement statistic. Examples: "A customer service agent's interaction statistic shows '150 calls handled'.", "A company's agent interaction statistic indicates '1000 sales completed'."
aggregateElement: An aggregate element relation between an item list and a prototype element used to store collective information about the list's contents. Also called list prototype, aggregate item, representative element. Examples: "A list of products' aggregate element holds the average rating.", "An item list's aggregate element contains the total price of all items."
aggregateRating: An aggregate rating relation between an item (e.g., product, service, creative work) and its overall rating derived from multiple reviews. Also called overall score, collective rating, average review. Examples: "A product's aggregate rating is '4.5 stars'.", "A movie's aggregate rating is '8.2/10'."
aircraft: An aircraft relation between a flight and the specific type of vehicle used for air travel. Also called airplane type, plane model, flight vehicle. Examples: "A flight's aircraft is 'Boeing 747'.", "The flight uses an 'Airbus A320'."
album: An album relation between a music group and a music album they have released. Also called record, studio album, LP. Examples: "A band's album is 'The Dark Side of the Moon'.", "The artist's album is '21'." Distinct from albums, which is a deprecated property for the same concept.
albumProductionType: An album production type relation between a music album and its classification based on content type (e.g., studio, live, soundtrack). Also called album category, production style, content type. Examples: "A music album's production type is 'StudioAlbum'.", "The album's production type is 'LiveAlbum'."
albumRelease: An album release relation between a music album and a specific release instance of that album. Also called album edition, release version, publication. Examples: "A music album's album release is its 'Deluxe Edition'.", "The album's album release is its 'Vinyl Remaster'."
albumReleaseType: An album release type relation between a music album and its classification as a single, EP, or full album. Also called release format, publication type, record type. Examples: "A music album's release type is 'AlbumRelease'.", "The music album's release type is 'EPRelease'."
albums: An album relation between a music group and a collection of music albums they have released. Also called records, discography, LPs. Examples: "A band's albums include 'Abbey Road'.", "The artist's albums include 'Thriller'." Distinct from album, which is the preferred property for a single album.
alcoholWarning: An alcohol warning relation between a drug and any precautions or contraindications regarding alcohol consumption while using it. Also called alcohol interaction, drinking advisory, alcohol caution. Examples: "A medication's alcohol warning states 'Do not consume alcohol'.", "The drug's alcohol warning advises 'Limit alcohol intake'."
algorithm: An algorithm relation between a medical risk score and the set of rules or computational method used to calculate it. Also called calculation method, scoring rules, computation logic. Examples: "A medical risk score's algorithm is 'Framingham Risk Score formula'.", "The diagnostic score's algorithm is 'CHA2DS2-VASc'."
alignmentType: An alignment type relation between an alignment object and the category describing the connection between a learning resource and a framework node. Also called alignment category, mapping type, relation type. Examples: "A learning resource's alignment type is 'requires'.", "The educational content's alignment type is 'readingLevel'."
alternateName: An alternate name relation between a thing and an alias or alternative designation for it. Also called alias, alternative designation, other name. Examples: "A city's alternate name is 'The Big Apple'.", "A person's alternate name is 'Liz'."
alternativeHeadline: An alternative headline relation between a creative work and its secondary title. Also called subtitle, secondary title, sub-headline. Examples: "A news article's alternative headline is 'Local Hero Saves Cat'.", "A book's alternative headline is 'A Novel of Intrigue'."
alternativeOf: An alternative of relation between a gene and another gene that represents a variation of it. Also called gene variant, genetic alternative, allele. Examples: "A gene's alternative of is 'Gene B (variant)'.", "Gene A's alternative of is 'Gene A-prime'."
alumni: An alumni relation between an educational organization or organization and a person who is a former student or member. Also called former student, graduate, past member. Examples: "A university's alumni include 'Jane Doe'.", "The club's alumni include 'John Smith'." Distinct from alumniOf, which describes the inverse relationship (person to organization).
alumniOf: An alumni of relation between a person and an educational organization or organization they are a former student or member of. Also called graduated from, formerly attended, past affiliation. Examples: "A person is alumni of 'MIT'.", "John Doe is alumni of 'Boy Scouts of America'." Distinct from alumni, which describes the inverse relationship (organization to person).
amenityFeature: An amenity feature relation between an accommodation, floor plan, lodging business, or place and a characteristic or service it offers. Also called facility, service, characteristic, convenience. Examples: "A hotel room's amenity feature is 'free Wi-Fi'.", "The apartment's amenity feature is 'gym access'.", "A park's amenity feature is 'playground'."
amount: An amount relation between a financial entity (e.g., loan, grant, money transfer) and the monetary value or number associated with it. Also called value, sum, quantity of money. Examples: "A loan's amount is '$10,000'.", "The grant's amount is '€5,000'.", "A money transfer's amount is '250'."
amountOfThisGood: An amount of this good relation between a type and quantity node and the numerical quantity of a specific good included in an offer. Also called quantity, number of items, item count. Examples: "A shopping cart item's amount of this good is '2'.", "The offer specifies an amount of this good as '5'."
announcementLocation: An announcement location relation between a special announcement and the specific civic structure or local business it pertains to. Also called relevant location, associated place, specific venue. Examples: "A special announcement's announcement location is 'City Hall'.", "The emergency announcement's announcement location is 'Local Grocery Store'." Distinct from spatialCoverage, which is used for larger geographic regions.
annualPercentageRate: An annual percentage rate relation between a financial product and the yearly cost of funds, expressed as a percentage, including all fees. Also called APR, yearly interest rate, effective annual rate. Examples: "A loan's annual percentage rate is '5.99%'.", "The credit card's annual percentage rate is '18.5%'."
answerCount: An answer count relation between a question and the total number of answers it has received. Also called number of responses, reply count, solution count. Examples: "A forum question's answer count is '5'.", "The quiz question's answer count is '10'."
answerExplanation: An answer explanation relation between an answer and a comment or web content providing a detailed clarification or step-by-step reasoning. Also called solution explanation, answer justification, detailed response. Examples: "An answer's answer explanation details the calculation steps.", "The correct answer's explanation clarifies the underlying principle."
antagonist: An antagonist relation between a muscle and another muscle whose action opposes it. Also called opposing muscle, counteracting muscle. Examples: "The biceps' antagonist is the 'triceps'.", "The quadriceps' antagonist is the 'hamstrings'."
appearance: An appearance relation between a claim and a creative work where that claim is found or occurs. Also called occurrence in, mentioned in, found in. Examples: "A claim's appearance is in 'News Article X'.", "The factual claim's appearance is in 'Research Paper Y'."
applicableCountry: An applicable country relation between a merchant return policy and the country where it is valid. Also called valid in country, country of application, policy region. Examples: "A return policy's applicable country is 'US'.", "The merchant return policy applies to 'Germany'."
applicableLocation: An applicable location relation between a drug cost or drug legal status and the administrative area where it is valid. Also called valid location, jurisdiction, region of applicability. Examples: "A drug's legal status's applicable location is 'California'.", "The drug cost's applicable location is 'Europe'."
applicantLocationRequirements: An applicant location requirements relation between a job posting and the administrative area(s) from which candidates can apply, especially for remote positions. Also called remote work location, eligible application region, telecommuting area. Examples: "A job posting's applicant location requirements include 'Anywhere in the US'.", "The remote job's applicant location requirements are 'Europe'."
application: An application relation between an entry point and the software application capable of fulfilling the associated request. Also called handling application, processing app, execution software. Examples: "A 'view document' entry point's application is 'Adobe Reader'.", "A 'play music' entry point's application is 'Spotify'." Distinct from actionApplication, which is a more specific property for an application that can complete the request.
applicationCategory: An application category relation between a software application and its general classification type. Also called software type, app category, program classification. Examples: "A software application's application category is 'Game'.", "The program's application category is 'Productivity'."
applicationContact: An application contact relation between a job posting and the contact point for additional information. Also called job contact, hiring contact, recruitment contact. Examples: "A job posting's application contact is the 'HR Department email'.", "The job's application contact is a 'recruiter's phone number'."
applicationDeadline: An application deadline relation between an educational or occupational program and the date or text indicating when applications close for an enrollment cycle. Also called submission deadline, application closing date, enrollment cutoff. Examples: "A university program's application deadline is '2023-03-15'.", "The training program's application deadline is 'Rolling admissions'."
applicationStartDate: An application start date relation between an educational or occupational program and the date when it begins accepting applications for an enrollment cycle. Also called application opening date, submission start date. Examples: "A university program's application start date is '2022-09-01'.", "The scholarship program's application start date is 'January 1st'."
applicationSubCategory: An application sub-category relation between a software application and its more specific classification type. Also called software sub-type, app sub-category, program sub-classification. Examples: "A game's application sub-category is 'Arcade Game'.", "A productivity app's application sub-category is 'Word Processor'."
applicationSuite: An application suite relation between a software application and the name of the larger software suite it is part of. Also called software bundle, program collection, suite membership. Examples: "Microsoft Excel's application suite is 'Microsoft Office'.", "Adobe Photoshop's application suite is 'Adobe Creative Cloud'."
appliesToDeliveryMethod: An applies to delivery method relation between a charge specification and the delivery method(s) to which it is relevant. Also called delivery method scope, applicable shipping method. Examples: "A delivery charge specification applies to 'ShippingMethod.Express'.", "The payment charge specification applies to 'DeliveryMethod.Pickup'."
appliesToPaymentMethod: An applies to payment method relation between a payment charge specification and the payment method(s) to which it is relevant. Also called payment method scope, applicable payment type. Examples: "A payment charge specification applies to 'PaymentMethod.CreditCard'.", "The charge applies to 'PaymentMethod.PayPal'."
archiveHeld: An archive held relation between an archive organization and a collection, fonds, or item maintained by it. Also called archival holding, collection maintained, item preserved. Examples: "The National Archives' archive held is 'Presidential Papers'.", "The historical society's archive held is 'Local Family Records'."
archivedAt: An archived at relation between a creative work and the URL or web page where an archived version of it can be found. Also called archival location, preserved at, stored at. Examples: "A news article's archived at is 'archive.org/news-article-url'.", "The web page's archived at is 'web.archive.org/page-snapshot'."
area: An area relation between a broadcast service and the geographic place where its users can access it. Also called service region, coverage area, broadcast zone. Examples: "A radio station's area is 'Greater London'.", "The TV service's area is 'North America'."
areaServed: An area served relation between a contact point, offer, organization, or service and the geographic region where it is available. Also called service area, coverage region, delivery zone. Examples: "A restaurant's area served is 'Downtown'.", "The delivery service's area served is 'California'.", "An organization's area served is 'Worldwide'."
arrivalAirport: An arrival airport relation between a flight and the airport where it concludes. Also called destination airport, landing airport, final airport. Examples: "A flight's arrival airport is 'LAX'.", "The flight's arrival airport is 'Heathrow Airport'."
arrivalBoatTerminal: An arrival boat terminal relation between a boat trip and the terminal or port where it concludes. Also called destination boat terminal, disembarkation port. Examples: "A boat trip's arrival boat terminal is 'Port of Miami'.", "The ferry trip's arrival boat terminal is 'Dover Terminal'."
arrivalBusStop: An arrival bus stop relation between a bus trip and the station or stop where it concludes. Also called destination bus stop, final bus station. Examples: "A bus trip's arrival bus stop is 'Grand Central Station'.", "The bus trip's arrival bus stop is 'Main Street Stop'."
arrivalGate: An arrival gate relation between a flight and the identifier for its arrival gate. Also called gate number, landing gate. Examples: "A flight's arrival gate is 'Gate B23'.", "The flight's arrival gate is 'Terminal 1, Gate 15'."
arrivalPlatform: A platform identification for a train trip's arrival location. Also called: train arrival platform, destination platform. Examples: "TrainTrip 123 arrivalPlatform 'Platform 7'", "TrainTrip to London arrivalPlatform 'Track 1'", "TrainTrip from Paris arrivalPlatform 'Gate C'."
arrivalStation: A station where a train trip concludes. Also called: train destination, end station, terminal station. Examples: "TrainTrip 456 arrivalStation 'Grand Central Station'", "TrainTrip from Rome arrivalStation 'Termini Station'", "TrainTrip to Berlin arrivalStation 'Hauptbahnhof'". Distinct from arrivalPlatform, which specifies the specific platform within a station.
arrivalTerminal: A terminal identifier for a flight's arrival location. Also called: flight destination terminal, terminal of arrival. Examples: "Flight BA286 arrivalTerminal 'Terminal 5'", "Flight from Tokyo arrivalTerminal 'North Terminal'", "Flight to JFK arrivalTerminal 'Terminal 4'". Distinct from arrivalStation, which is for train trips.
arrivalTime: An expected time of arrival for a trip. Also called: estimated arrival, scheduled arrival, landing time. Examples: "Trip to NYC arrivalTime '2023-10-27T14:30:00'", "Flight 789 arrivalTime '18:00'", "Bus Trip arrivalTime 'tomorrow 09:15'."
artEdition: A numerical or textual description of the total number of copies produced for a piece of visual artwork. Also called: edition size, print run, limited edition count. Examples: "VisualArtwork 'Sunset' artEdition '20'", "VisualArtwork 'Lithograph' artEdition '1/50'", "VisualArtwork 'Sculpture' artEdition 'Unique'."
artMedium: A material or technique used in the creation of a visual artwork. Also called: artistic medium, material used, technique. Examples: "VisualArtwork 'Portrait' artMedium 'Oil on canvas'", "VisualArtwork 'Sketch' artMedium 'Pencil'", "VisualArtwork 'Digital Art' artMedium 'Digital'". Distinct from artform, which describes the general category of art.
arterialBranch: A relation between an artery and the anatomical structures that comprise its branches. Also called: artery branches, vascular branches. Examples: "Artery 'Aorta' arterialBranch 'Femoral Artery'", "Artery 'Coronary Artery' arterialBranch 'Left Anterior Descending Artery'."
artform: A category or style of visual artwork. Also called: art type, artistic style, genre of art. Examples: "VisualArtwork 'Mona Lisa' artform 'Painting'", "VisualArtwork 'David' artform 'Sculpture'", "VisualArtwork 'Ansel Adams Photo' artform 'Photograph'". Distinct from artMedium, which describes the specific materials or techniques used.
articleBody: The main textual content of an article. Also called: article content, body text, main text. Examples: "Article 'News Report' articleBody 'The city council voted...'", "Article 'Research Paper' articleBody 'Our findings indicate...'", "Article 'Blog Post' articleBody 'Today I learned...'."
articleSection: A categorization of an article within a larger publication, such as a magazine or newspaper. Also called: article category, section heading, publication section. Examples: "Article 'Sports News' articleSection 'Sports'", "Article 'Lifestyle Piece' articleSection 'Lifestyle'", "Article 'Editorial' articleSection 'Opinion'."
artist: A person who is the primary creator of a comic issue, comic story, or visual artwork, especially in non-line art mediums. Also called: creator, illustrator, visual creator. Examples: "VisualArtwork 'Starry Night' artist 'Vincent van Gogh'", "ComicIssue 'Issue #1' artist 'Frank Miller'", "ComicStory 'Origin Story' artist 'Alex Ross'". Distinct from author, which is a more general term for the creator of content, often textual.
artworkSurface: A supporting material or substrate for a visual artwork. Also called: art substrate, painting surface, canvas type. Examples: "VisualArtwork 'Landscape' artworkSurface 'Canvas'", "VisualArtwork 'Sketch' artworkSurface 'Paper'", "VisualArtwork 'Mural' artworkSurface 'Wall'."
asin: An Amazon Standard Identification Number (ASIN) associated with a demand, offer, or product. Also called: Amazon product ID, ASIN identifier. Examples: "Product 'Book' asin 'B00005N53N'", "Offer 'Laptop' asin 'B07XXXXXXX'", "Demand 'Toy' asin 'B08YYYYYYY'."
aspect: A specific area or topic of medical practice considered on a medical webpage. Also called: medical topic, health aspect, clinical focus. Examples: "MedicalWebPage 'Diabetes' aspect 'diagnosis'", "MedicalWebPage 'Flu' aspect 'treatment'", "MedicalWebPage 'Cancer' aspect 'prognosis'."
assembly: A library file name associated with an API reference. Also called: library name, API library, component file. Examples: "APIReference 'System.Web' assembly 'System.Web.dll'", "APIReference 'mscorlib' assembly 'mscorlib.dll'."
assemblyVersion: A product or technology version associated with an API reference. Also called: API version, product version, technology version. Examples: "APIReference 'ASP.NET' assemblyVersion '.NET Framework 4.5'", "APIReference 'Java API' assemblyVersion 'Java SE 11'."
assesses: A relation between a creative work, education event, or learning resource and the competency or learning outcome it is intended to evaluate. Also called: evaluates, measures, tests, gauges. Examples: "LearningResource 'Quiz' assesses 'Understanding of Algebra'", "EducationEvent 'Exam' assesses 'Problem-solving skills'", "CreativeWork 'Rubric' assesses 'Writing proficiency'."
associatedAnatomy: An anatomical structure, system, or superficial anatomy related to a medical condition or physical activity. Also called: related anatomy, anatomical connection, affected anatomy. Examples: "MedicalCondition 'Arthritis' associatedAnatomy 'Knee Joint'", "PhysicalActivity 'Running' associatedAnatomy 'Leg Muscles'", "MedicalCondition 'Migraine' associatedAnatomy 'Brain'."
associatedArticle: A news article linked to a media object. Also called: related article, accompanying article, news story link. Examples: "MediaObject 'Video of Protest' associatedArticle 'NewsArticle on Protest'", "MediaObject 'Photo of Event' associatedArticle 'Article about Event'."
associatedClaimReview: A claim review related to another review by common content, topic, or claim. Also called: related claim review, linked claim assessment. Examples: "Review 'MediaReview of Article' associatedClaimReview 'ClaimReview of Statement'", "Review 'FactCheck' associatedClaimReview 'Another FactCheck'". Distinct from associatedMediaReview, which links to a media review.
associatedDisease: A medical condition or URL representing a disease linked to a biochemical entity. Also called: related disease, disease connection, disease association. Examples: "BioChemEntity 'Insulin' associatedDisease 'Diabetes'", "BioChemEntity 'Gene X' associatedDisease 'Cancer'", "BioChemEntity 'Drug Y' associatedDisease 'Hypertension'."
associatedMedia: A media object that encodes a creative work. Also called: media encoding, embedded media, content media. Examples: "CreativeWork 'Song' associatedMedia 'AudioObject of Song'", "CreativeWork 'Movie' associatedMedia 'VideoObject of Movie'", "CreativeWork 'Book' associatedMedia 'eBook File'."
associatedMediaReview: A media review related to another review by common content, topic, or claim. Also called: related media review, linked media assessment. Examples: "Review 'ClaimReview of Statement' associatedMediaReview 'MediaReview of Article'", "Review 'ProductReview' associatedMediaReview 'VideoReview'". Distinct from associatedClaimReview, which links to a claim review.
associatedPathophysiology: A description of the pathophysiology, including abnormal changes, linked to an anatomical structure, system, or superficial anatomy. Also called: related pathophysiology, disease mechanism, functional changes. Examples: "AnatomicalSystem 'Cardiovascular System' associatedPathophysiology 'Hypertension leads to...'", "AnatomicalStructure 'Lung' associatedPathophysiology 'Asthma causes inflammation...'", "SuperficialAnatomy 'Skin' associatedPathophysiology 'Eczema involves barrier dysfunction...'."
associatedReview: A review related to another review. Also called: linked review, related assessment. Examples: "Review 'Product Review A' associatedReview 'Product Review B'", "Review 'Movie Review' associatedReview 'Critic Review'."
athlete: A person who is a performing member of a sports team. Also called: player, team member, sportsman/sportswoman. Examples: "SportsTeam 'Lakers' athlete 'LeBron James'", "SportsTeam 'Red Sox' athlete 'Mookie Betts'", "SportsTeam 'National Team' athlete 'Megan Rapinoe'". Distinct from coach, which is a non-playing role.
attendee: A person or organization present at an event. Also called: participant, guest, visitor. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendee 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendee 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendee 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendees, which is the plural form.
attendees: A person present at an event. Also called: participants, guests, visitors. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendees 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendees 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendees 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendee, which is the singular form.
audience: An intended group for whom a creative work, event, lodging business, play action, product, or service was created. Also called: target group, demographic, intended recipient. Examples: "CreativeWork 'Children's Book' audience 'Children'", "Event 'Tech Conference' audience 'Developers'", "Product 'Luxury Car' audience 'High-net-worth individuals'."
audienceType: A textual description of the target group associated with a given audience. Also called: target demographic, audience category, group type. Examples: "Audience 'Veterans' audienceType 'veterans'", "Audience 'Car Owners' audienceType 'car owners'", "Audience 'Musicians' audienceType 'musicians'."
audio: An embedded audio object associated with a creative work. Also called: audio file, sound recording, soundtrack. Examples: "CreativeWork 'Podcast Episode' audio 'AudioObject of Episode'", "CreativeWork 'Movie' audio 'Soundtrack Clip'", "CreativeWork 'Webpage' audio 'Background Music'."
auditDate: A date when a certification was last audited. Also called: last audit, certification audit date. Examples: "Certification 'ISO 9001' auditDate '2023-01-15'", "Certification 'Organic' auditDate '2022-07-01'."
authenticator: An organization responsible for authenticating a user's subscription to a media subscription. Also called: subscription authenticator, access provider, verification organization. Examples: "MediaSubscription 'Streaming Service' authenticator 'Cable Provider'", "MediaSubscription 'News App' authenticator 'Satellite Company'."
author: An organization or person who created content or a rating. Also called: creator, writer, originator, composer. Examples: "CreativeWork 'Novel' author 'Jane Austen'", "Rating 'Product Review' author 'Consumer Reports'", "CreativeWork 'Article' author 'New York Times'". Distinct from artist, which is typically for visual or comic art.
availability: The current status of an item's availability for demand or offer. Also called: stock status, item status, product availability. Examples: "Offer 'Product X' availability 'InStock'", "Demand 'Service Y' availability 'OutOfStock'", "Offer 'Limited Edition' availability 'PreOrder'."
availabilityEnds: A date or time marking the end of availability for a product or service in an offer or access specification. Also called: availability end date, offer expiration, access end time. Examples: "Offer 'Sale Item' availabilityEnds '2023-12-31'", "ActionAccessSpecification 'Early Bird' availabilityEnds '2023-10-30T23:59:59'". Distinct from availabilityStarts, which marks the beginning.
availabilityStarts: A date or time marking the beginning of availability for a product or service in an offer or access specification. Also called: availability start date, offer start, access start time. Examples: "Offer 'New Product' availabilityStarts '2023-11-01'", "ActionAccessSpecification 'Pre-sale' availabilityStarts '2023-10-20T09:00:00'". Distinct from availabilityEnds, which marks the end.
availableAtOrFrom: A place from which an offer can be obtained. Also called: pickup location, sales point, distribution point. Examples: "Offer 'Groceries' availableAtOrFrom 'Supermarket A'", "Offer 'Concert Tickets' availableAtOrFrom 'Venue Box Office'."
availableChannel: A means of accessing a service. Also called: service access, contact channel, delivery method. Examples: "Service 'Customer Support' availableChannel 'Phone Line'", "Service 'Online Banking' availableChannel 'Website'", "Service 'Consultation' availableChannel 'Physical Location'."
availableDeliveryMethod: A delivery method available for an offer. Also called: shipping option, delivery option, fulfillment method. Examples: "Offer 'Product Z' availableDeliveryMethod 'DeliveryMode.Shipping'", "Offer 'Food' availableDeliveryMethod 'DeliveryMode.Pickup'."
availableFrom: A date and time when an item is available for pickup from a store or locker. Also called: pickup start time, ready for collection. Examples: "DeliveryEvent 'Package' availableFrom '2023-10-27T10:00:00'", "DeliveryEvent 'Order' availableFrom '2023-10-28'". Distinct from availableThrough, which specifies the end of pickup availability.
availableIn: An administrative area where a drug strength is available. Also called: market availability, regional availability. Examples: "DrugStrength '500mg' availableIn 'US'", "DrugStrength '10mg' availableIn 'EU'."
availableLanguage: A language that can be used with or at an item, service, or place. Also called: supported language, language option, communication language. Examples: "ContactPoint 'Support' availableLanguage 'en'", "Course 'Programming' availableLanguage 'es'", "LodgingBusiness 'Hotel' availableLanguage 'fr'". Distinct from inLanguage, which specifies the language of the content itself.
availableOnDevice: A device required to run a software application. Also called: compatible device, supported device, device requirement. Examples: "SoftwareApplication 'Game' availableOnDevice 'iPhone 15'", "SoftwareApplication 'Editor' availableOnDevice 'Windows 11'."
availableService: A medical procedure, test, or therapy offered by a hospital, medical clinic, or physician. Also called: medical offering, service provided, treatment option. Examples: "Hospital 'City Hospital' availableService 'Emergency Care'", "MedicalClinic 'Dental Clinic' availableService 'Dental Checkup'", "Physician 'Dr. Smith' availableService 'Consultation'."
availableStrength: An available dosage strength for a drug. Also called: drug dosage, dosage option, strength variant. Examples: "Drug 'Pain Reliever' availableStrength 'DrugStrength 200mg'", "Drug 'Antibiotic' availableStrength 'DrugStrength 500mg'."
availableTest: A diagnostic test or procedure offered by a diagnostic lab. Also called: lab test, diagnostic offering, test procedure. Examples: "DiagnosticLab 'LabCorp' availableTest 'Blood Test'", "DiagnosticLab 'Imaging Center' availableTest 'MRI Scan'."
availableThrough: A date and time after which an item will no longer be available for pickup. Also called: pickup end time, collection deadline. Examples: "DeliveryEvent 'Package' availableThrough '2023-10-30T17:00:00'", "DeliveryEvent 'Order' availableThrough '2023-11-01'". Distinct from availableFrom, which specifies the start of pickup availability.
award: An award won by or for a creative work, organization, person, product, or service. Also called: honor, prize, recognition. Examples: "CreativeWork 'Movie' award 'Oscar'", "Organization 'Company X' award 'Best Employer'", "Person 'Scientist' award 'Nobel Prize'". Distinct from awards, which is the plural form.
awards: Awards won by or for a creative work, organization, person, or product. Also called: honors, prizes, recognitions. Examples: "CreativeWork 'Movie' awards 'Oscar'", "Organization 'Company X' awards 'Best Employer'", "Person 'Scientist' awards 'Nobel Prize'". Distinct from award, which is the singular form.
awayTeam: A person or sports team designated as the away team in a sports event. Also called: visiting team, opponent. Examples: "SportsEvent 'Football Match' awayTeam 'Team B'", "SportsEvent 'Basketball Game' awayTeam 'Lakers'". Distinct from homeTeam, which is the team playing at their home venue.
backstory: A textual summary providing context and explanation for how and why an article was created. Also called: background story, context, origin story. Examples: "Article 'Investigative Report' backstory 'The journalist spent months...'", "NewsArticle 'Exposed Scandal' backstory 'This article originated from a tip-off...'."
bankAccountType: A textual or URL description of the type of a bank account. Also called: account type, banking account category. Examples: "BankAccount 'Checking' bankAccountType 'Checking Account'", "BankAccount 'Savings' bankAccountType 'Savings Account'."
baseSalary: A monetary amount, number, or price specification representing the base salary of a job or an employee role. Also called: starting salary, basic pay, compensation. Examples: "JobPosting 'Software Engineer' baseSalary '$120,000'", "EmployeeRole 'Manager' baseSalary 'MonetaryAmount 80000 USD'."
bccRecipient: A contact point, organization, or person who is a blind carbon copy recipient of a message. Also called: blind copy recipient, hidden recipient. Examples: "Message 'Email' bccRecipient 'Compliance Department'", "Message 'Newsletter' bccRecipient 'Marketing Team'". Distinct from recipient and ccRecipient, which are visible to other recipients.
bed: A description of the type and quantity of beds included in an accommodation or hotel room. Also called: bed type, sleeping arrangement, bedding. Examples: "Accommodation 'Room 101' bed 'King size bed'", "HotelRoom 'Suite' bed 'BedDetails: 2 Queen beds'."
beforeMedia: A media object representing the circumstances prior to performing a how-to direction. Also called: pre-action media, initial state media. Examples: "HowToDirection 'Install Shelf' beforeMedia 'Image of empty wall'", "HowToDirection 'Bake Cake' beforeMedia 'Video of ingredients on counter'."
beneficiaryBank: A bank, branch, or financial institution operating the beneficiary's bank account or releasing funds for a money transfer. Also called: recipient bank, receiving bank, destination bank. Examples: "MoneyTransfer 'Wire Transfer' beneficiaryBank 'Bank of America'", "MoneyTransfer 'International Transfer' beneficiaryBank 'HSBC'."
benefits: A description of benefits associated with a job posting. Also called: job perks, employee benefits, compensation package details. Examples: "JobPosting 'Marketing Manager' benefits 'Health insurance, 401k, paid time off'", "JobPosting 'Developer' benefits 'Flexible hours, remote work option'."
benefitsSummaryUrl: A URL that links directly to the summary of benefits and coverage for a health insurance plan. Also called: summary of benefits link, plan benefits URL. Examples: "HealthInsurancePlan 'Standard Plan A' benefitsSummaryUrl 'http://example.com/planA-benefits.pdf'."
bestRating: A number or text representing the highest value allowed in a rating system. Also called: maximum rating, top score, highest possible rating. Examples: "Rating 'Product Review' bestRating '5'", "Rating 'Movie Score' bestRating '10'". Distinct from worstRating, which is the lowest value.
billingAddress: A postal address used for billing an order. Also called: invoice address, payment address. Examples: "Order 'Online Purchase' billingAddress '123 Main St, Anytown, USA'", "Order 'Subscription' billingAddress 'PO Box 456'". Distinct from shippingAddress, which is where the item is sent.
billingDuration: A duration, number, or quantitative value specifying how long a price or price component will be billed. Also called: billing period length, contractual duration, payment plan length. Examples: "UnitPriceSpecification 'Subscription' billingDuration 'P1Y' (1 year)", "UnitPriceSpecification 'Service Plan' billingDuration '12' (months)."
billingIncrement: A number specifying the minimal quantity and rounding increment for billing. Also called: billing unit, minimum billing quantity. Examples: "UnitPriceSpecification 'Data Usage' billingIncrement '1' (GB)", "UnitPriceSpecification 'Consulting' billingIncrement '0.25' (hours)."
billingPeriod: A duration representing the time interval used to compute an invoice. Also called: invoice period, billing cycle. Examples: "Invoice 'Monthly Bill' billingPeriod 'P1M'", "Invoice 'Quarterly Statement' billingPeriod 'P3M'."
billingStart: A number specifying after how much time a price or price component becomes valid and billing starts. Also called: billing commencement, price validity start. Examples: "UnitPriceSpecification 'Subscription' billingStart '1' (month, for a price increase after the first month)", "UnitPriceSpecification 'Service' billingStart '0'."
bioChemInteraction: A biochemical entity known to interact with another biochemical entity. Also called: biochemical interaction, molecular interaction, binding partner. Examples: "BioChemEntity 'Enzyme A' bioChemInteraction 'Substrate B'", "BioChemEntity 'Drug X' bioChemInteraction 'Protein Y'."
bioChemSimilarity: A biochemical entity that is similar to another biochemical entity, often based on fingerprint similarity algorithms. Also called: biochemical analog, similar compound, structural analog. Examples: "BioChemEntity 'Compound A' bioChemSimilarity 'Compound B'", "BioChemEntity 'Molecule X' bioChemSimilarity 'Molecule Y'."
biologicalRole: A defined term describing the role played by a biochemical entity within a biological context. Also called: biological function, physiological role, molecular role. Examples: "BioChemEntity 'Enzyme' biologicalRole 'Catalyst'", "BioChemEntity 'Hormone' biologicalRole 'Signaling Molecule'."
biomechnicalClass: A textual description of the biomechanical properties of a bone within a joint. Also called: bone mechanics, joint biomechanics. Examples: "Joint 'Knee Joint' biomechnicalClass 'Hinge Joint'", "Joint 'Shoulder Joint' biomechnicalClass 'Ball-and-socket Joint'."
birthDate: A date representing a person's birth. Also called: date of birth, birthday. Examples: "Person 'John Doe' birthDate '1980-05-15'", "Person 'Jane Smith' birthDate '1992-11-22'."
birthPlace: A place where a person was born. Also called: place of birth, birthplace. Examples: "Person 'Albert Einstein' birthPlace 'Ulm, Germany'", "Person 'Marie Curie' birthPlace 'Warsaw, Poland'."
bitrate: A textual description of the bitrate of a media object. Also called: data rate, transfer rate, bandwidth. Examples: "MediaObject 'Video File' bitrate '10 Mbps'", "MediaObject 'Audio Stream' bitrate '320 kbps'."
blogPost: A blog posting that is part of a blog. Also called: blog entry, post, article. Examples: "Blog 'My Travel Blog' blogPost 'BlogPosting about Paris'", "Blog 'Tech News' blogPost 'BlogPosting on AI trends'". Distinct from blogPosts, which is the plural form.
blogPosts: A blog posting that is part of a blog. Also called: blog entries, posts, articles. Examples: "Blog 'My Travel Blog' blogPosts 'BlogPosting about Paris'", "Blog 'Tech News' blogPosts 'BlogPosting on AI trends'". Distinct from blogPost, which is the singular form.
bloodSupply: A blood vessel that carries blood from the heart to a muscle. Also called: muscle blood flow, arterial supply. Examples: "Muscle 'Bicep' bloodSupply 'Brachial Artery'", "Muscle 'Heart' bloodSupply 'Coronary Arteries'."
boardingGroup: An airline-specific indicator of boarding order or preference for a flight reservation. Also called: boarding zone, priority boarding. Examples: "FlightReservation 'Flight 123' boardingGroup 'Group A'", "FlightReservation 'Flight 456' boardingGroup 'Zone 3'."
boardingPolicy: A type of boarding policy used by an airline or for a flight. Also called: boarding procedure, airline boarding rules. Examples: "Airline 'United' boardingPolicy 'BoardingPolicyType.ZoneBoarding'", "Flight 'Flight 789' boardingPolicy 'Group-based boarding'."
bodyLocation: A textual description of the location in the body of an anatomical structure or for a medical procedure. Also called: anatomical site, body region, procedure location. Examples: "AnatomicalStructure 'Heart' bodyLocation 'Chest'", "MedicalProcedure 'Appendectomy' bodyLocation 'Abdomen'."
bodyType: A qualitative value, text, or URL indicating the design and body style of a vehicle. Also called: vehicle style, car type, chassis type. Examples: "Vehicle 'Ford Focus' bodyType 'Hatchback'", "Vehicle 'Mercedes C-Class' bodyType 'Sedan'."
bookEdition: A textual description of the edition of a book. Also called: edition number, publication edition. Examples: "Book 'The Lord of the Rings' bookEdition 'First Edition'", "Book 'Textbook' bookEdition '2nd Edition'."
bookFormat: A type of book format for a book. Also called: publication format, book binding. Examples: "Book 'Novel' bookFormat 'BookFormatType.Hardcover'", "Book 'Ebook' bookFormat 'BookFormatType.EBook'."
bookingAgent: An organization or person acting as a broker or booking agent for a reservation. Also called: reservation agent, travel agent, broker. Examples: "Reservation 'Hotel Stay' bookingAgent 'Booking.com'", "Reservation 'Flight' bookingAgent 'Travel Agency X'."
bookingTime: A date and time when a reservation was booked. Also called: reservation time, booking date. Examples: "Reservation 'Restaurant' bookingTime '2023-10-26T19:00:00'", "Reservation 'Car Rental' bookingTime '2023-10-25'."
borrower: A person who borrows the object being lent in a lend action. Also called: recipient of loan, loan taker. Examples: "LendAction 'Book Loan' borrower 'Jane Doe'", "LendAction 'Tool Rental' borrower 'John Smith'". Distinct from lender, which is the person providing the object.
box: A textual representation of a rectangular area defined by two points (lower and upper corners) for a geo shape. Also called: bounding box, geographic box, spatial extent. Examples: "GeoShape 'Region A' box '34 -118 36 -116'", "GeoShape 'Area B' box '40.71 -74.01 40.78 -73.95'."
branch: An anatomical structure that delineates from a nerve bundle. Also called: nerve branch, neural branch. Examples: "Nerve 'Sciatic Nerve' branch 'Tibial Nerve'", "Nerve 'Trigeminal Nerve' branch 'Ophthalmic Nerve'". Distinct from branchOf, which describes an organizational hierarchy.
branchCode: A short textual code that uniquely identifies a place of business, typically assigned by the parent organization. Also called: store code, location ID, business code. Examples: "Place 'Starbucks' branchCode '3047'", "Place 'Bank Branch' branchCode 'NY001'."
branchOf: An organization that a local business is a branch of. Also called: parent organization, corporate parent, subsidiary of. Examples: "LocalBusiness 'Local Cafe' branchOf 'Coffee Chain Inc.'", "LocalBusiness 'Branch Bank' branchOf 'National Bank'". Distinct from branch, which refers to anatomical nerve branches.
brand: A brand or organization associated with a product, service, or maintained by an organization or person. Also called: product brand, service brand, corporate brand. Examples: "Product 'Smartphone' brand 'Apple'", "Service 'Cloud Storage' brand 'Google'", "Organization 'Company X' brand 'Brand Y'."
breadcrumb: A set of links that helps a user understand and navigate a website hierarchy on a webpage. Also called: breadcrumb trail, navigation path, site path. Examples: "WebPage 'Product Page' breadcrumb 'Home > Category > Product'", "WebPage 'Article' breadcrumb 'Blog > Year > Month > Article Title'."
breastfeedingWarning: Any precaution, guidance, or contraindication related to a drug's use by breastfeeding mothers. Also called: lactation warning, nursing caution, breastfeeding safety. Examples: "Drug 'Medication X' breastfeedingWarning 'Consult doctor before use'", "Drug 'Drug Y' breastfeedingWarning 'Not recommended for breastfeeding mothers'."
broadcastAffiliateOf: An organization representing the media network(s) whose content is broadcast on a broadcast service. Also called: network affiliation, broadcast network. Examples: "BroadcastService 'Local TV Station' broadcastAffiliateOf 'NBC'", "BroadcastService 'Radio Station' broadcastAffiliateOf 'NPR'."
broadcastChannelId: A unique address by which a broadcast service can be identified in a provider lineup. Also called: channel number, broadcast ID, station ID. Examples: "BroadcastChannel 'Channel 7' broadcastChannelId '7'", "BroadcastChannel 'ESPN' broadcastChannelId '206'."
broadcastDisplayName: A name displayed in the channel guide for a broadcast service. Also called: channel name, station display name. Examples: "BroadcastService 'Local News' broadcastDisplayName 'WXYZ-TV'", "BroadcastService 'Music Radio' broadcastDisplayName 'KEXP 90.3 FM'."
broadcastFrequency: A frequency used for over-the-air broadcasts for a broadcast channel or service. Also called: broadcast frequency, radio frequency, channel frequency. Examples: "BroadcastChannel 'FM Station' broadcastFrequency '87.9 FM'", "BroadcastService 'TV Channel' broadcastFrequency 'BroadcastFrequencySpecification 500 MHz'."
broadcastFrequencyValue: A number or quantitative value representing the frequency in MHz for a particular broadcast. Also called: frequency in MHz, broadcast megahertz. Examples: "BroadcastFrequencySpecification 'FM 98.1' broadcastFrequencyValue '98.1'", "BroadcastFrequencySpecification 'TV Channel 25' broadcastFrequencyValue '539'."
broadcastOfEvent: An event that is being broadcast by a broadcast event. Also called: televised event, event broadcast. Examples: "BroadcastEvent 'Super Bowl Live' broadcastOfEvent 'Super Bowl LVIII'", "BroadcastEvent 'Concert Stream' broadcastOfEvent 'Live Music Concert'."
broadcastServiceTier: A textual description of the type of service required to access a broadcast channel. Also called: channel tier, service level, subscription tier. Examples: "BroadcastChannel 'Premium Movies' broadcastServiceTier 'Premium'", "BroadcastChannel 'Basic News' broadcastServiceTier 'Standard'."
broadcastSignalModulation: A qualitative value or text describing the modulation (e.g., FM, AM) used by a particular broadcast service. Also called: signal modulation, broadcast modulation type. Examples: "BroadcastFrequencySpecification 'Radio Station' broadcastSignalModulation 'FM'", "BroadcastFrequencySpecification 'AM Station' broadcastSignalModulation 'AM'."
broadcastSubChannel: A subchannel identification for a broadcast frequency specification. Also called "subchannel of broadcast", "broadcast channel identifier". Examples: "FM 98.1 specification broadcastSubChannel 'HD2'", "Digital TV channel 5 specification broadcastSubChannel '5.3'".
broadcastTimezone: A timezone specification for a broadcast service. Also called "timezone of broadcast", "service timezone". Examples: "BBC One broadcastTimezone 'Europe/London'", "NBC broadcast service broadcastTimezone 'America/New_York'".
broadcaster: An ownership or operational relation between a broadcast service and the organization responsible for it. Also called "service provider", "operated by", "owned by", "broadcast by". Examples: "BBC Radio 4 broadcaster BBC", "CNN broadcast service broadcaster Warner Bros. Discovery".
broker: An intermediary relation between an invoice, order, reservation, or service and the organization or person who arranges the exchange. Also called "arranged by", "intermediary", "agent". Examples: "Flight reservation broker Expedia", "Real estate service broker John Doe", "Stock order broker Fidelity". Distinct from seller or buyer, which indicate direct parties in an exchange, whereas broker facilitates it without taking ownership.
browserRequirements: A description of browser requirements for a web application. Also called "browser compatibility", "required browser features". Examples: "Online banking app browserRequirements 'Requires Chrome 80+ or Firefox 75+'", "Video streaming service browserRequirements 'Supports HTML5 video and DRM'".
busName: A naming relation between a bus trip and the specific name of the bus. Also called "name of bus", "bus line name". Examples: "Bus trip from NYC to Boston busName 'Bolt Express'", "Local route 10 bus trip busName 'CityLink'".
busNumber: An identification relation between a bus trip and its unique identifier. Also called "bus ID", "bus route number", "bus identifier". Examples: "Bus trip from NYC to Boston busNumber 'B101'", "Local route 10 bus trip busNumber '4567'". Distinct from busName, which is a human-readable name, whereas busNumber is a unique identifier.
businessDays: A specification of the days of the week when a service period or shipping delivery time typically operates. Also called "operating days", "days of operation", "working days". Examples: "Customer service businessDays Monday to Friday", "Standard shipping businessDays Weekday".
businessFunction: A characterization of the business function associated with a demand, offer, or component of a bundle. Also called "purpose of offer", "transaction type", "commercial role". Examples: "Product offer businessFunction Sell", "Car lease offer businessFunction Lease", "Repair service offer businessFunction Repair".
buyer: A participation relation in a sell action, indicating the organization or person who purchased the object. Also called "purchaser", "customer", "acquired by". Examples: "Online purchase sell action buyer Jane Doe", "Company acquisition sell action buyer Acme Corp". Distinct from seller, which is the party offering the object for sale.
byArtist: A performance relation between a music album or recording and the music group or person who performed it. Also called "performed by", "artist of", "featuring artist". Examples: "Album 'Thriller' byArtist Michael Jackson", "Recording 'Bohemian Rhapsody' byArtist Queen". Distinct from composer, which is the person who wrote the music, whereas byArtist is the performer.
byDay: A temporal specification for a schedule, indicating the day(s) of the week on which a recurring event occurs. Also called "days of week", "weekly recurrence", "on day". Examples: "Weekly meeting schedule byDay Monday", "Class schedule byDay 'MO,WE,FR'".
byMonth: A temporal specification for a schedule, indicating the month(s) of the year on which a recurring event occurs. Also called "months of year", "monthly recurrence", "in month". Examples: "Annual conference schedule byMonth 10", "Quarterly report schedule byMonth 3,6,9,12".
byMonthDay: A temporal specification for a schedule, indicating the day(s) of the month on which a recurring event occurs. Also called "day of month", "monthly day recurrence", "on day of month". Examples: "Rent payment schedule byMonthDay 1", "Board meeting schedule byMonthDay 15".
byMonthWeek: A temporal specification for a schedule, indicating the week(s) of the month on which a recurring event occurs. Also called "week of month", "monthly week recurrence", "on week of month". Examples: "Book club schedule byMonthWeek 2", "Team sync schedule byMonthWeek 1,3".
callSign: An identification relation between a broadcast service, person, or vehicle and its unique callsign. Also called "radio identifier", "station ID", "vehicle identifier". Examples: "Radio station broadcast service callSign 'KEXP'", "Amateur radio operator person callSign 'W1AW'", "Aircraft vehicle callSign 'N123AB'".
calories: A quantitative measurement of energy content in nutrition information. Also called "energy content", "caloric value", "kcal". Examples: "Nutrition information calories 250 kcal", "Meal nutrition calories 600 Energy".
candidate: A participation relation in a vote action, indicating the person who is being voted for. Also called "voted for", "nominee", "electoral candidate". Examples: "Election vote action candidate Jane Smith", "Award vote action candidate John Doe".
caption: A descriptive text or media object providing a caption for an audio, image, or video object. Also called "description", "subtitle", "alt text". Examples: "Image object caption 'Sunset over the mountains'", "Video object caption 'English subtitles'", "Audio object caption 'Transcript of speech'".
carbohydrateContent: A quantitative measurement of carbohydrate mass in nutrition information. Also called "carbs", "total carbohydrates", "carbohydrate amount". Examples: "Nutrition information carbohydrateContent 30 grams", "Food item nutrition carbohydrateContent 50 Mass".
cargoVolume: A quantitative measurement of the available volume for cargo or luggage in a vehicle. Also called "trunk volume", "luggage capacity", "storage volume". Examples: "Car vehicle cargoVolume 400 LTR", "Truck vehicle cargoVolume 100 FTQ".
carrier: A provider relation between a flight or parcel delivery and the organization that provides the service. Also called "provider", "airline", "delivery service". Examples: "Flight from London to NYC carrier British Airways", "Parcel delivery carrier FedEx".
carrierRequirements: A description of specific carrier requirements for a mobile application. Also called "network compatibility", "mobile operator requirements", "carrier restrictions". Examples: "Mobile app carrierRequirements 'Requires AT&T network'", "Messaging app carrierRequirements 'Works on all major carriers'".
cashBack: A benefit offered by a payment card, indicating whether cashback is available and its percentage or value. Also called "cash rebate", "cash rewards", "cash return". Examples: "Credit card cashBack 2%", "Debit card cashBack true", "Payment card cashBack 0.01".
catalog: A containment relation between a dataset and the data catalog that holds it. Also called "contained in catalog", "part of catalog", "dataset catalog". Examples: "Census data dataset catalog National Data Archive", "Research dataset catalog University Data Repository".
catalogNumber: An identification relation between a music release and its unique catalog number. Also called "release ID", "record label number", "product number". Examples: "Album release catalogNumber 'ABC-123'", "Single release catalogNumber 'XYZ-456'".
category: A classification relation assigning a category to an item such as an offer, product, service, or announcement. Also called "type", "classification", "genre", "tag". Examples: "Product category 'Electronics'", "Service category 'Home Repair'", "Offer category 'Seasonal Sale'".
cause: A causal relation between a medical condition and its medical cause. Also called "etiology", "origin", "caused by". Examples: "Flu medical condition cause Influenza virus", "Heart attack medical condition cause Coronary artery disease". Distinct from causeOf, which describes what a medical cause leads to, whereas cause describes what leads to a condition.
causeOf: A causal relation between a medical cause and the medical entity (condition, complication, symptom) it produces. Also called "results in", "leads to", "produces". Examples: "Influenza virus medical causeOf Flu", "Smoking medical causeOf Lung cancer". Distinct from cause, which describes what leads to a condition, whereas causeOf describes what a medical cause leads to.
ccRecipient: A recipient relation for a message, indicating a contact point, organization, or person who is copied on it. Also called "carbon copy recipient", "copied to", "CC'd party". Examples: "Email message ccRecipient John Doe", "Internal memo message ccRecipient HR Department".
certificationIdentification: An identification relation for a certification instance, providing its unique identifier. Also called "certification ID", "certificate number", "registration ID". Examples: "ISO 9001 certification certificationIdentification 'CERT-12345'", "Organic certification certificationIdentification 'BIO-XYZ'".
certificationRating: A rating relation for a certification instance, indicating the level to which its requirements are fulfilled. Also called "certification level", "certificate rating", "compliance rating". Examples: "Energy efficiency certification certificationRating 'A+'", "Food safety certification certificationRating 'Excellent'".
certificationStatus: A status relation for a certification, indicating whether it is active or inactive. Also called "certificate status", "certification validity", "status of certification". Examples: "Product certification certificationStatus Active", "Company certification certificationStatus Inactive".
character: A fictional role relation between a creative work and a person who is a character within it. Also called "fictional person", "role played by", "depicted character". Examples: "Novel 'Pride and Prejudice' character Elizabeth Bennet", "Movie 'Star Wars' character Luke Skywalker".
characterAttribute: An attribute relation describing a particular aspect of a fictional character within a game or video game series. Also called "character trait", "character property", "game attribute". Examples: "Video game character attribute 'Strength'", "RPG game character attribute 'Magic Resistance'".
characterName: A naming relation for a performance role, indicating the name of the character being played. Also called "role name", "played character", "fictional name". Examples: "Actor's performance role characterName 'Hamlet'", "Actress's performance role characterName 'Juliet'". Distinct from character, which refers to the fictional person itself, whereas characterName is the name of the character in a specific performance.
cheatCode: A utility relation between a video game or series and a creative work containing cheat codes for it. Also called "game cheats", "unlock codes", "game secrets". Examples: "Video game 'Grand Theft Auto V' cheatCode 'Invincibility code'", "Game series 'The Sims' cheatCode 'Money cheat'".
checkinTime: A temporal specification for a lodging business or reservation, indicating the earliest time for check-in. Also called "arrival time", "earliest check-in", "check-in starts". Examples: "Hotel lodging business checkinTime '15:00'", "Flight reservation checkinTime '2023-10-26T14:00:00'". Distinct from checkoutTime, which specifies the latest time for departure.
checkoutPageURLTemplate: A URL template for an offer, providing the structure for its checkout page. Also called "checkout URL", "purchase link template", "order page URL". Examples: "Product offer checkoutPageURLTemplate 'https://example.com/checkout{?productId,quantity}'", "Service offer checkoutPageURLTemplate 'https://shop.example.org/buy/{id}'".
checkoutTime: A temporal specification for a lodging business or reservation, indicating the latest time for check-out. Also called "departure time", "latest check-out", "check-out ends". Examples: "Hotel lodging business checkoutTime '11:00'", "Flight reservation checkoutTime '2023-10-27T10:00:00'". Distinct from checkinTime, which specifies the earliest time for arrival.
chemicalComposition: A descriptive relation for a chemical substance, detailing its identity and relative ratio of chemical elements. Also called "molecular formula", "chemical makeup", "compositional analysis". Examples: "Water chemical substance chemicalComposition 'H2O'", "Salt chemical substance chemicalComposition 'NaCl'".
chemicalRole: A functional relation describing the role played by a chemical substance or molecular entity within a chemical context. Also called "chemical function", "biochemical role", "molecular role". Examples: "Enzyme chemical role 'Catalyst'", "Drug chemical role 'Agonist'".
childMaxAge: A demographic specification for a parent audience, indicating the maximal age of a child. Also called "maximum child age", "upper age limit for child", "child age cap". Examples: "Parent audience for toddlers childMaxAge 3", "Parent audience for teens childMaxAge 17". Distinct from childMinAge, which specifies the minimal age.
childMinAge: A demographic specification for a parent audience, indicating the minimal age of a child. Also called "minimum child age", "lower age limit for child", "child age floor". Examples: "Parent audience for infants childMinAge 0", "Parent audience for school-age children childMinAge 5". Distinct from childMaxAge, which specifies the maximal age.
childTaxon: A hierarchical relation between a taxon and its closest child taxa. Also called "subtaxon", "descendant taxon", "lower taxon". Examples: "Genus 'Homo' childTaxon 'Homo sapiens'", "Family 'Felidae' childTaxon 'Genus Felis'".
children: A familial relation between a person and their child. Also called "offspring", "son", "daughter". Examples: "John children Jane", "Mary children Peter". Distinct from parent, which indicates the inverse relationship.
cholesterolContent: A quantitative measurement of cholesterol mass in nutrition information. Also called "cholesterol amount", "cholesterol level", "mg cholesterol". Examples: "Nutrition information cholesterolContent 50 milligrams", "Food item nutrition cholesterolContent 100 Mass".
circle: A geometric definition for a geo shape, describing a circular region by its center coordinates and radius. Also called "circular region", "geographic circle", "radius definition". Examples: "Geo shape circle '34.0522,-118.2437 1000'", "Search area geo shape circle '40.7128,-74.0060 5000'".
citation: A reference relation between a creative work and another creative work or text that it cites. Also called "reference", "cited work", "source". Examples: "Research paper citation 'Smith, J. (2020). Article Title.'", "Blog post citation 'https://example.com/article'".
claimInterpreter: An interpretation relation between a claim and the organization or person who interpreted it from media content. Also called "interpreted by", "claim analyst", "fact-checker". Examples: "News claim claimInterpreter FactCheck.org", "Social media claim claimInterpreter Jane Doe".
claimReviewed: A summary relation for a claim review, providing a short text of the specific claims being reviewed. Also called "reviewed claim", "claim summary", "subject of review". Examples: "Fact-check review claimReviewed 'Eating apples cures cancer'", "Product claim review claimReviewed 'This product doubles battery life'".
clincalPharmacology: A descriptive relation for a drug, detailing its absorption, elimination, concentration (pharmacokinetics), and biological effects (pharmacodynamics). Also called "drug pharmacology", "pharmacokinetics", "pharmacodynamics".
