Examples: "Drug 'Aspirin' clincalPharmacology 'Rapidly absorbed, metabolized in liver.'", "Medication 'Insulin' clincalPharmacology 'Regulates blood glucose levels.'".
clinicalPharmacology: A descriptive relation for a drug, detailing its absorption, elimination, concentration (pharmacokinetics), and biological effects (pharmacodynamics). Also called "drug pharmacology", "pharmacokinetics", "pharmacodynamics". Examples: "Drug 'Aspirin' clinicalPharmacology 'Rapidly absorbed, metabolized in liver.'", "Medication 'Insulin' clinicalPharmacology 'Regulates blood glucose levels.'".
clipNumber: A positional relation for a clip, indicating its order within a group of clips. Also called "clip index", "clip position", "sequence number". Examples: "Video clip clipNumber 3", "Audio clip clipNumber 'Part 1'".
closes: A temporal specification for opening hours, indicating the closing time for a place or service on a given day. Also called "closing time", "end of hours", "closes at". Examples: "Store opening hours closes '18:00'", "Service opening hours closes '22:30'". Distinct from opens, which specifies the opening time.
coach: A leadership relation between a sports team and the person who acts as its coach. Also called "team coach", "trainer", "manager". Examples: "Basketball team coach John Smith", "Soccer team coach Jane Doe".
code: An identification relation for a medical entity, providing its medical code from a controlled vocabulary. Also called "medical identifier", "diagnosis code", "procedure code". Examples: "Medical condition 'Flu' code 'J10.0'", "Drug 'Paracetamol' code 'RxNorm:161'".
codeRepository: A location relation for software source code, providing a URL to its repository. Also called "source code URL", "repository link", "code host". Examples: "Software project codeRepository 'https://github.com/example/project'", "Library source code codeRepository 'https://svn.example.org/repo'".
codeSampleType: A classification relation for software source code, indicating the type of code sample. Also called "code type", "sample format", "code snippet type". Examples: "Example code codeSampleType 'code snippet'", "Project template codeSampleType 'full solution'".
codeValue: An identification relation for a category code or medical code, providing a short textual value that uniquely identifies it. Also called "code identifier", "unique code", "value code". Examples: "Medical code codeValue 'ICD-10-CM:J10.0'", "Category code codeValue 'ELECTRONICS'". Distinct from codingSystem, which specifies the system the code belongs to, whereas codeValue is the specific code itself.
codingSystem: A classification relation for a medical code, indicating the coding system it belongs to. Also called "code scheme", "vocabulary system", "ontology". Examples: "Medical code 'J10.0' codingSystem 'ICD-10'", "Medical code '161' codingSystem 'RxNorm'". Distinct from codeValue, which is the specific code, whereas codingSystem is the system it belongs to.
colleague: A professional relation between a person and another person who is their colleague. Also called "co-worker", "associate", "professional peer". Examples: "John colleague Jane", "Professor Smith colleague 'https://example.com/prof-jones'". Distinct from colleagues, which is a plural form, though semantically similar.
colleagues: A professional relation between a person and other persons who are their colleagues. Also called "co-workers", "associates", "professional peers". Examples: "John colleagues [Jane, Peter]", "Mary colleagues [Sarah, Tom]". Distinct from colleague, which is a singular form, though semantically similar.
collection: A target relation for an update action, indicating the collection that is being updated. Also called "target collection", "updated collection", "collection object". Examples: "Add item update action collection 'Shopping Cart'", "Remove item update action collection 'Wishlist'".
collectionSize: A quantitative measurement for a collection, indicating the total number of items it contains. Also called "number of items", "collection count", "size of collection". Examples: "Art collection collectionSize 500", "Dataset collection collectionSize 10000".
color: A descriptive relation for a product, indicating its color. Also called "product color", "hue", "shade". Examples: "Car product color 'Red'", "Shirt product color 'Blue'". Distinct from colorSwatch, which provides an image of the color.
colorSwatch: A visual representation for a product, providing an image object or URL of its color swatch. Also called "color image", "color sample", "swatch URL". Examples: "Product 'T-shirt' colorSwatch 'https://example.com/red-swatch.jpg'", "Product 'Paint' colorSwatch ImageObject". Distinct from color, which is the textual description of the color.
colorist: A creative role relation between a comic issue, comic story, or visual artwork and the person who adds color to it. Also called "color artist", "inker", "colorer". Examples: "Comic book colorist John Smith", "Graphic novel colorist Jane Doe".
comment: A feedback relation between a creative work or RSVP action and a user-generated comment. Also called "user comment", "feedback", "review". Examples: "Article comment 'Great read!'", "Event RSVP comment 'Looking forward to it!'". Distinct from commentText, which is the text content of the comment itself.
commentCount: A quantitative measurement for a creative work, indicating the total number of comments it has received. Also called "number of comments", "comment total", "feedback count". Examples: "Blog post commentCount 15", "Article commentCount 200".
commentText: A textual content relation for user comments, providing the actual text of the comment. Also called "comment content", "message text", "user feedback text". Examples: "User comment commentText 'This is a very insightful article.'", "Review commentText 'Product arrived quickly and works great.'". Distinct from comment, which refers to the comment object itself, whereas commentText is its textual content.
commentTime: A temporal specification for user comments, indicating the date or date and time when the comment was made. Also called "comment date", "posted time", "submission time". Examples: "User comment commentTime '2023-10-26T10:30:00'", "Review commentTime '2023-09-15'".
companyRegistration: An official registration relation for an organization, providing its business registration information as a certification. Also called "business registration", "corporate certification", "legal registration". Examples: "Company organization companyRegistration 'Company House Certificate'", "Non-profit organization companyRegistration 'Charity Commission Registration'".
competencyRequired: A requirement relation for an educational credential or learning resource, specifying the knowledge, skill, or ability needed. Also called "required skill", "prerequisite competency", "learning outcome". Examples: "Certification competencyRequired 'Problem-solving skills'", "Course learning resource competencyRequired 'Basic algebra'".
competitor: A participation relation in a sports event, indicating a person or sports team that is competing. Also called "participant", "opponent", "rival". Examples: "Olympic race sports event competitor Usain Bolt", "Football match sports event competitor Manchester United".
composer: A creative role relation between an event or music composition and the organization or person who wrote it. Also called "writer", "creator", "author of music". Examples: "Symphony music composition composer Ludwig van Beethoven", "Concert event composer Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart". Distinct from byArtist, which is the performer of a musical work.
comprisedOf: A compositional relation between an anatomical system and the anatomical structures or other systems that physically comprise it. Also called "composed of", "consists of", "includes". Examples: "Circulatory system comprisedOf Heart", "Digestive system comprisedOf Stomach".
conditionsOfAccess: A descriptive relation for a creative work, detailing the natural language conditions affecting its availability or access methods. Also called "access restrictions", "availability terms", "usage conditions". Examples: "Archival document conditionsOfAccess 'Available by appointment only'", "Digital artwork conditionsOfAccess 'Requires institutional login'".
confirmationNumber: An identification relation for an invoice or order, providing a number that confirms its receipt. Also called "order confirmation", "booking reference", "receipt number". Examples: "Online order confirmationNumber 'ABC-12345'", "Flight invoice confirmationNumber 'XYZ-67890'".
connectedTo: A connection relation between an anatomical structure and other anatomical structures it is connected to. Also called "linked to", "adjoins", "connects with". Examples: "Femur anatomical structure connectedTo Tibia", "Brain anatomical structure connectedTo Spinal cord".
constraintProperty: A definitional relation for a constraint node, indicating a property used as a constraint. Also called "constraining property", "restricted by property", "property constraint". Examples: "Statistical variable constraint node constraintProperty 'schema:age'", "Data filter constraintProperty 'dc:gender'".
contactOption: A feature relation for a contact point, indicating an available option such as a toll-free number or accessibility support. Also called "contact feature", "available option", "support option". Examples: "Customer service contact point contactOption 'TollFree'", "Accessibility contact point contactOption 'HearingImpairedSupported'".
contactPoint: A communication relation between a health insurance plan, organization, or person and one of their contact points. Also called "contact info", "point of contact", "reach at". Examples: "Company organization contactPoint 'Customer Service'", "Person contactPoint 'Email Address'". Distinct from contactPoints, which is the plural form, though semantically similar.
contactPoints: A communication relation between an organization or person and their various contact points. Also called "contact information", "points of contact", "ways to reach". Examples: "Company organization contactPoints [Customer Service, Press Office]", "Person contactPoints [Email, Phone]". Distinct from contactPoint, which is the singular form, though semantically similar.
contactType: A classification relation for a contact point, specifying its purpose or kind. Also called "type of contact", "contact purpose", "department". Examples: "Phone number contact point contactType 'Sales'", "Email address contact point contactType 'Support'".
contactlessPayment: A feature relation for a payment card, indicating whether it supports contactless payment technology. Also called "NFC payment", "tap to pay", "RFID payment". Examples: "Credit card contactlessPayment true", "Debit card contactlessPayment false".
containedIn: A spatial containment relation between a place and the larger place that contains it. Also called "located in", "part of", "within". Examples: "City 'Paris' containedIn 'France'", "Building 'Eiffel Tower' containedIn 'Paris'". Distinct from containedInPlace, which is a synonym, and containsPlace, which is the inverse.
containedInPlace: A spatial containment relation between a place and the larger place that contains it. Also called "located in", "part of", "within". Examples: "City 'Paris' containedInPlace 'France'", "Building 'Eiffel Tower' containedInPlace 'Paris'". Distinct from containedIn, which is a synonym, and containsPlace, which is the inverse.
containsPlace: A spatial containment relation between a place and another smaller place that it contains. Also called "includes place", "encompasses", "holds". Examples: "Country 'France' containsPlace 'Paris'", "City 'Paris' containsPlace 'Eiffel Tower'". Distinct from containedIn or containedInPlace, which are the inverse relations.
containsSeason: A compositional relation between a radio, TV, or video game series and a creative work season that is part of it. Also called "includes season", "has season", "season of series". Examples: "TV series 'Friends' containsSeason 'Season 1'", "Video game series 'Halo' containsSeason 'Halo: Combat Evolved'".
contentLocation: A descriptive relation for a creative work, indicating the place depicted or described within its content. Also called "depicted location", "setting", "place of content". Examples: "Photograph contentLocation 'Eiffel Tower'", "Novel contentLocation 'London'".
contentRating: An official classification relation for a creative work, indicating its content rating. Also called "age rating", "maturity rating", "content advisory". Examples: "Movie contentRating 'PG-13'", "Video game contentRating 'ESRB Teen'".
contentReferenceTime: A temporal reference relation for a creative work, indicating the specific date and time described or emphasized within its content. Also called "event time", "depicted time", "time of content". Examples: "News article contentReferenceTime '2023-10-26T14:00:00Z'", "Historical documentary contentReferenceTime '1945-09-02'".
contentSize: A quantitative measurement for a media object, indicating its file size. Also called "file size", "media size", "data size". Examples: "Image file contentSize '2.5MB'", "Video file contentSize '500MB'".
contentType: A specification relation for an entry point, indicating the supported content type(s) for its response. Also called "response type", "media type", "MIME type". Examples: "API endpoint contentType 'application/json'", "Web page entry point contentType 'text/html'".
contentUrl: A location relation for a media object, providing the URL to its actual bytes or file. Also called "media URL", "file URL", "download link". Examples: "Image object contentUrl 'https://example.com/image.jpg'", "Video object contentUrl 'https://example.com/video.mp4'".
contraindication: A medical restriction relation for a medical device or therapy, indicating a contraindication. Also called "medical warning", "precaution", "not recommended for". Examples: "Drug therapy contraindication 'Pregnancy'", "Medical device contraindication 'Pacemaker users'".
contributor: A secondary participation relation for a creative work or event, indicating an organization or person who contributed to it. Also called "additional contributor", "supporting role", "collaborator". Examples: "Book creative work contributor 'Editor Jane Doe'", "Conference event contributor 'Sponsor Acme Corp'". Distinct from author or creator, which typically denote primary responsibility.
cookTime: A temporal measurement for a recipe, indicating the duration required to cook the dish. Also called "cooking duration", "preparation time", "time to cook". Examples: "Recipe 'Chicken Curry' cookTime 'PT30M'", "Recipe 'Cake' cookTime 'PT45M'". Distinct from prepTime, which is the time for preparation before cooking, and totalTime, which is the sum of all time.
cookingMethod: A descriptive relation for a recipe, indicating the method of cooking used. Also called "cooking technique", "preparation method", "culinary method". Examples: "Recipe 'Fried Chicken' cookingMethod 'Frying'", "Recipe 'Steamed Vegetables' cookingMethod 'Steaming'".
copyrightHolder: A legal ownership relation between a creative work and the person or organization holding its copyright. Also called: copyright owner, rights holder, legally owned by. Examples: "The Mona Lisa" copyright holder "The Louvre Museum", "Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone" copyright holder "J.K. Rowling", "Microsoft Windows" copyright holder "Microsoft Corporation".
copyrightNotice: A textual declaration relation between a creative work and the statement describing its copyright aspects. Also called: copyright statement, copyright declaration, copyright text. Examples: "My Novel" copyright notice "© 2023 John Doe", "Company Website" copyright notice "Copyright 2023 Example Corp. All Rights Reserved.", "Academic Paper" copyright notice "Published under CC BY 4.0 license". Distinct from copyrightHolder, which identifies the entity owning the copyright.
copyrightYear: A temporal relation between a creative work and the year its copyright was first asserted. Also called: year of copyright, copyright date, first copyright year. Examples: "Classic Album" copyright year "1970", "Software Version 1.0" copyright year "2005", "Research Paper" copyright year "2022". Distinct from datePublished, which is the date of first publication or broadcast.
correction: A modification relation between a creative work and the comment, text, or document detailing a correction to it. Also called: erratum, amendment, revision, fix. Examples: "News Article" correction "Editor's Note: A previous version of this article misstated...", "Software Manual" correction "See errata sheet for updates.", "Research Paper" correction "Correction published in Vol. 15, Issue 3.".
correctionsPolicy: A policy relation between an organization and the statement describing its disclosure and correction policy for errors. Also called: error policy, editorial policy, disclosure policy. Examples: "The New York Times" corrections policy "Our commitment to accuracy and transparency...", "Example Corp." corrections policy "Policy on correcting factual errors.", "Academic Journal" corrections policy "Guidelines for authors on submitting corrections.".
costCategory: A classification relation between a drug cost and its specific category. Also called: cost type, price category, expense classification. Examples: "Drug X price" cost category "wholesale", "Medication Y cost" cost category "reimbursement cap", "Prescription Z cost" cost category "retail".
costCurrency: A monetary unit relation between a drug cost and the currency in which it is expressed. Also called: currency of cost, price currency, cost unit. Examples: "Drug A cost" cost currency "USD", "Medication B price" cost currency "EUR", "Prescription C expense" cost currency "JPY". Distinct from currency, which is a more general property for monetary amounts.
costOrigin: A source relation between a drug cost and additional details about where the cost data originated. Also called: cost data source, price origin, expense source. Examples: "Drug X cost" cost origin "Medicare Part B", "Medication Y price" cost origin "Private Insurance", "Prescription Z expense" cost origin "Manufacturer's List Price".
costPerUnit: A pricing relation between a drug cost and the cost associated with a single unit of the drug. Also called: unit price, price per unit, cost rate. Examples: "Insulin" cost per unit "10 USD per vial", "Antibiotic" cost per unit "5 EUR per pill", "Vaccine" cost per unit "50 GBP per dose".
countriesNotSupported: A geographical restriction relation between a software application and the countries where it is not supported. Also called: unsupported regions, restricted countries, unavailable in. Examples: "App X" countries not supported "Cuba", "Software Y" countries not supported "Iran, North Korea", "Game Z" countries not supported "Syria". Distinct from countriesSupported, which lists where the application is supported.
countriesSupported: A geographical availability relation between a software application and the countries where it is supported. Also called: supported regions, available in, operational in. Examples: "App X" countries supported "USA, Canada", "Software Y" countries supported "Germany, France, UK", "Game Z" countries supported "Japan, South Korea". Distinct from countriesNotSupported, which lists where the application is not supported.
countryOfAssembly: A manufacturing location relation between a product and the country where it was assembled. Also called: assembled in, manufacturing country, assembly location. Examples: "Smartphone" country of assembly "China", "Car" country of assembly "Mexico", "Laptop" country of assembly "Vietnam". Distinct from countryOfOrigin, which refers to the country of the principal offices or where the product originates.
countryOfLastProcessing: A final processing location relation between a product and the country where it underwent its last processing and testing before importation. Also called: last processed in, final testing country, pre-importation processing location. Examples: "Electronic Component" country of last processing "Malaysia", "Textile Product" country of last processing "Bangladesh", "Automotive Part" country of last processing "Thailand". Distinct from countryOfOrigin, which is about the origin of the product itself.
countryOfOrigin: A provenance relation between a creative work or product and its country of origin. Also called: origin country, produced in, made in. Examples: "French Wine" country of origin "France", "Japanese Anime" country of origin "Japan", "German Car" country of origin "Germany", "Hollywood Movie" country of origin "United States". Distinct from countryOfAssembly, which specifies where the product was put together.
course: A location relation between an exercise action and the course where it was performed. Also called: exercise location, training course, activity venue. Examples: "Morning Run" course "Central Park Loop", "Golf Game" course "Augusta National", "Cycling Race" course "Tour de France Route".
courseCode: An identifier relation between a course and the code used by its provider. Also called: course ID, course number, catalog number. Examples: "Introduction to Programming" course code "CS101", "Calculus I" course code "MATH101", "Art History Survey" course code "AH205".
courseMode: A delivery method relation between a course instance and its mode of study or delivery. Also called: study mode, delivery mode, course format. Examples: "Online Course" course mode "online", "Evening Class" course mode "onsite", "Blended Learning Program" course mode "blended", "Self-paced Module" course mode "asynchronous".
coursePrerequisites: A requirement relation between a course and the conditions or prior knowledge needed to take it. Also called: prerequisites, required courses, entry requirements. Examples: "Advanced Algorithms" course prerequisites "Data Structures", "Calculus II" course prerequisites "Calculus I", "Graduate Seminar" course prerequisites "permission of instructor".
courseSchedule: A temporal structure relation between a course instance and its length and pace. Also called: course timetable, class schedule, academic calendar. Examples: "Fall Semester Course" course schedule "Mondays and Wednesdays, 10:00-11:30 AM", "Intensive Workshop" course schedule "Full-day, 5 days", "Online Module" course schedule "Self-paced, complete within 8 weeks".
courseWorkload: An effort expectation relation between a course instance and the amount of work expected from students. Also called: student workload, expected effort, study hours. Examples: "Introductory Physics" course workload "3 hours lecture, 2 hours lab, 4 hours independent study per week", "Literature Seminar" course workload "10-15 pages reading per week, one essay per month", "Programming Project" course workload "20 hours total".
coverageEndTime: A temporal boundary relation between a live blog posting and the time when its event coverage concludes. Also called: coverage end, reporting end time, live blog conclusion. Examples: "Election Night Live Blog" coverage end time "2024-11-06T04:00:00Z", "Sports Event Live Update" coverage end time "2023-07-15T19:30:00Z", "Conference Live Blog" coverage end time "2023-10-27T17:00:00Z". Distinct from coverageStartTime, which indicates when coverage begins.
coverageStartTime: A temporal boundary relation between a live blog posting and the time when its event coverage begins. Also called: coverage start, reporting start time, live blog commencement. Examples: "Election Night Live Blog" coverage start time "2024-11-05T18:00:00Z", "Sports Event Live Update" coverage start time "2023-07-15T14:00:00Z", "Conference Live Blog" coverage start time "2023-10-27T09:00:00Z". Distinct from coverageEndTime, which indicates when coverage concludes.
creativeWorkStatus: A lifecycle stage relation between a creative work and its current status. Also called: work status, publication status, development stage. Examples: "Draft Novel" creative work status "Draft", "Published Article" creative work status "Published", "Archived Website" creative work status "Obsolete", "In-progress Film" creative work status "Incomplete".
creator: An authorship relation between a creative work or user comment and the person or organization responsible for its creation. Also called: author, originator, producer, made by. Examples: "Novel" creator "Jane Doe", "Software" creator "Acme Corp.", "Blog Post" creator "John Smith", "User Review" creator "Anonymous User". Distinct from copyrightHolder, which is about legal ownership.
credentialCategory: A classification relation between a credential and its type or category. Also called: credential type, certification category, award type. Examples: "PhD" credential category "degree", "PMP" credential category "certificate", "Scout Badge" credential category "badge", "Driver's License" credential category "license".
creditText: An attribution relation between a creative work and the text used to credit associated persons or organizations. Also called: attribution text, credit line, acknowledgment. Examples: "Movie" credit text "Directed by...", "Photograph" credit text "Photo by John Doe", "Research Paper" credit text "Funding provided by...". Distinct from creator, which identifies the primary author/creator.
creditedTo: An attribution relation between a music release and the group or artist it is credited to, if different from the primary artist. Also called: attributed to, release credit, presented by. Examples: "Album 'Red and Blue'" credited to "Stefani Germanotta Band", "Single 'X'" credited to "The Session Musicians", "Soundtrack" credited to "Various Artists".
cssSelector: An identification relation between a speakable specification or web page element and its CSS selector. Also called: CSS path, element selector, style selector. Examples: "Page Title" CSS selector "h1.main-title", "Article Body" CSS selector "div#article-content", "Navigation Menu" CSS selector "nav ul li a".
currenciesAccepted: A payment method relation between a local business and the currencies it accepts. Also called: accepted currency, payment currency, currency options. Examples: "Coffee Shop" currencies accepted "USD, EUR", "Online Store" currencies accepted "USD, BTC", "Local Market" currencies accepted "Ithaca HOUR". Distinct from currency, which specifies the currency of a monetary amount.
currency: A monetary unit relation between a monetary amount or specification and the currency in which it is expressed. Also called: monetary currency, unit of money, payment unit. Examples: "Product Price" currency "USD", "Loan Amount" currency "EUR", "Exchange Rate" currency "JPY", "Salary" currency "GBP". Distinct from costCurrency, which is specific to drug costs.
currentExchangeRate: A value relation between an exchange rate specification and the current price of a currency. Also called: exchange value, currency rate, conversion rate. Examples: "USD to EUR" current exchange rate "0.92 EUR per USD", "GBP to JPY" current exchange rate "180 JPY per GBP".
customer: A transactional role relation between an invoice or order and the person or organization placing the order or paying the invoice. Also called: buyer, client, purchaser, payer. Examples: "Online Order" customer "Jane Doe", "Service Invoice" customer "Acme Corp.", "Product Purchase" customer "John Smith".
customerRemorseReturnFees: A return policy relation between a merchant return policy and the type of fees applied when a product is returned due to customer remorse. Also called: remorse return fees, change-of-mind return fees, customer-initiated return charges. Examples: "Electronics Store" customer remorse return fees "ReturnShippingFees", "Clothing Retailer" customer remorse return fees "RestockingFee", "Bookstore" customer remorse return fees "NoFees".
customerRemorseReturnLabelSource: A return policy relation between a merchant return policy and the method by which a customer obtains a return shipping label for a remorse return. Also called: remorse return label method, return label provision, customer-initiated return label source. Examples: "Online Retailer" customer remorse return label source "DownloadAndPrint", "Apparel Store" customer remorse return label source "InStore", "Electronics Vendor" customer remorse return label source "ShippedWithProduct".
customerRemorseReturnShippingFeesAmount: A return policy relation between a merchant return policy and the amount of shipping costs for a product returned due to customer remorse. Also called: remorse return shipping cost, customer-initiated return shipping fee, shipping fee for remorse return. Examples: "Online Purchase" customer remorse return shipping fees amount "10 USD", "Clothing Order" customer remorse return shipping fees amount "5 EUR", "Electronics Return" customer remorse return shipping fees amount "15 GBP". Distinct from customerRemorseReturnFees, which specifies the type of fees.
cutoffTime: A temporal boundary relation between a service period or shipping delivery time and the time after which orders are no longer processed on that day. Also called: order cutoff, daily processing limit, last order time. Examples: "Same-day Delivery" cutoff time "14:00:00-05:00", "Next-day Shipping" cutoff time "17:00:00Z", "Warehouse Processing" cutoff time "23:30:00-05:00".
cvdCollectionDate: A temporal reference relation between a CDCPMD record and the date for which patient counts are reported. Also called: data collection date, reporting date, patient count date. Examples: "Hospital Data Record" cvd collection date "2023-01-15", "Facility Report" cvd collection date "2023-02-01T12:00:00Z".
cvdFacilityCounty: A geographical identification relation between a CDCPMD record and the county of the NHSN facility it applies to. Also called: facility county, hospital county, reporting county. Examples: "COVID-19 Data" cvd facility county "Los Angeles County", "NHSN Record" cvd facility county "Cook County", "Hospital Report" cvd facility county "King County". Distinct from cvdFacilityId, which is the identifier of the facility.
cvdFacilityId: An identification relation between a CDCPMD record and the identifier of the NHSN facility it applies to. Also called: facility ID, hospital ID, reporting facility identifier. Examples: "COVID-19 Data" cvd facility ID "NHSN12345", "Hospital Record" cvd facility ID "FACILITY-ABC", "Medical Report" cvd facility ID "HOSPITAL-XYZ". Distinct from cvdFacilityCounty, which is the county of the facility.
cvdNumBeds: A capacity relation between a CDCPMD record and the total number of inpatient beds in the hospital. Also called: total inpatient beds, hospital bed count, staffed beds. Examples: "Hospital A Data" cvd num beds "500", "Facility B Report" cvd num beds "250", "Medical Center C" cvd num beds "1000". Distinct from cvdNumBedsOcc, which is the number of occupied beds.
cvdNumBedsOcc: An occupancy relation between a CDCPMD record and the total number of staffed inpatient beds that are occupied. Also called: occupied inpatient beds, bed occupancy count, current bed usage. Examples: "Hospital A Data" cvd num beds occ "450", "Facility B Report" cvd num beds occ "200", "Medical Center C" cvd num beds occ "800". Distinct from cvdNumBeds, which is the total number of beds.
cvdNumC19Died: A mortality count relation between a CDCPMD record and the number of patients with suspected or confirmed COVID-19 who died in the hospital, ED, or overflow location. Also called: COVID-19 deaths, C19 fatalities, pandemic deaths. Examples: "Hospital A Data" cvd num c19 died "10", "Facility B Report" cvd num c19 died "3", "Medical Center C" cvd num c19 died "25".
cvdNumC19HOPats: A patient count relation between a CDCPMD record and the number of patients hospitalized with hospital-onset suspected or confirmed COVID-19. Also called: hospital-onset COVID patients, nosocomial COVID cases, C19 HO patients. Examples: "Hospital A Data" cvd num c19 hopats "5", "Facility B Report" cvd num c19 hopats "1", "Medical Center C" cvd num c19 hopats "12". Distinct from cvdNumC19HospPats, which is all hospitalized COVID patients.
cvdNumC19HospPats: A patient count relation between a CDCPMD record and the number of patients currently hospitalized with suspected or confirmed COVID-19. Also called: hospitalized COVID patients, current C19 inpatients, COVID-19 hospitalizations. Examples: "Hospital A Data" cvd num c19 hosppats "50", "Facility B Report" cvd num c19 hosppats "20", "Medical Center C" cvd num c19 hosppats "100". Distinct from cvdNumC19HOPats, which is specific to hospital-onset cases.
cvdNumC19MechVentPats: A patient count relation between a CDCPMD record and the number of hospitalized patients with suspected or confirmed COVID-19 who are on a mechanical ventilator. Also called: ventilated COVID patients, C19 mechanical ventilation, COVID patients on vents. Examples: "Hospital A Data" cvd num c19 mech vent pats "15", "Facility B Report" cvd num c19 mech vent pats "5", "Medical Center C" cvd num c19 mech vent pats "30". Distinct from cvdNumC19OFMechVentPats, which is for ED/overflow locations.
cvdNumC19OFMechVentPats: A patient count relation between a CDCPMD record and the number of patients with suspected or confirmed COVID-19 in the ED or overflow locations awaiting an inpatient bed and on a mechanical ventilator. Also called: ED/overflow ventilated COVID patients, C19 overflow mechanical ventilation, emergency ventilated COVID patients. Examples: "Hospital A Data" cvd num c19 of mech vent pats "3", "Facility B Report" cvd num c19 of mech vent pats "1", "Medical Center C" cvd num c19 of mech vent pats "7". Distinct from cvdNumC19MechVentPats, which is for inpatient care locations.
cvdNumC19OverflowPats: A patient count relation between a CDCPMD record and the number of patients with suspected or confirmed COVID-19 in the ED or any overflow location awaiting an inpatient bed. Also called: ED/overflow COVID patients, C19 overflow patients, emergency COVID patients. Examples: "Hospital A Data" cvd num c19 overflow pats "10", "Facility B Report" cvd num c19 overflow pats "4", "Medical Center C" cvd num c19 overflow pats "20". Distinct from cvdNumC19HospPats, which is for hospitalized patients.
cvdNumICUBeds: A capacity relation between a CDCPMD record and the total number of staffed inpatient intensive care unit (ICU) beds. Also called: total ICU beds, ICU bed count, intensive care capacity. Examples: "Hospital A Data" cvd num icu beds "50", "Facility B Report" cvd num icu beds "20", "Medical Center C" cvd num icu beds "100". Distinct from cvdNumICUBedsOcc, which is the number of occupied ICU beds.
cvdNumICUBedsOcc: An occupancy relation between a CDCPMD record and the total number of staffed inpatient ICU beds that are occupied. Also called: occupied ICU beds, ICU bed occupancy, current ICU usage. Examples: "Hospital A Data" cvd num icu beds occ "45", "Facility B Report" cvd num icu beds occ "18", "Medical Center C" cvd num icu beds occ "90". Distinct from cvdNumICUBeds, which is the total number of ICU beds.
cvdNumTotBeds: A capacity relation between a CDCPMD record and the total number of all inpatient and outpatient hospital beds. Also called: total hospital beds, all beds count, overall bed capacity. Examples: "Hospital A Data" cvd num tot beds "1200", "Facility B Report" cvd num tot beds "600", "Medical Center C" cvd num tot beds "2500". Distinct from cvdNumBeds, which is only inpatient beds.
cvdNumVent: A capacity relation between a CDCPMD record and the total number of mechanical ventilators available. Also called: total ventilators, available ventilators, ventilator count. Examples: "Hospital A Data" cvd num vent "100", "Facility B Report" cvd num vent "40", "Medical Center C" cvd num vent "200". Distinct from cvdNumVentUse, which is the number of ventilators in use.
cvdNumVentUse: An occupancy relation between a CDCPMD record and the total number of mechanical ventilators currently in use. Also called: ventilators in use, occupied ventilators, ventilator usage. Examples: "Hospital A Data" cvd num vent use "70", "Facility B Report" cvd num vent use "30", "Medical Center C" cvd num vent use "150". Distinct from cvdNumVent, which is the total number of ventilators available.
data: An association relation between an instantaneous event and the data linked to it. Also called: event data, associated data, event information. Examples: "Sensor Reading Event" data "temperature: 25C, humidity: 60%", "Log Entry Event" data "User 'admin' logged in from IP 192.168.1.1", "System Alert Event" data "Error code 500: Database connection failed".
dataFeedElement: A containment relation between a data feed and an item within it. Also called: feed item, data element, feed entry. Examples: "News Feed" data feed element "Latest Article", "Product Catalog Feed" data feed element "Product ID 123", "Event Listing Feed" data feed element "Concert on Friday".
dataset: A containment relation between a data catalog and a dataset included within it. Also called: cataloged dataset, included dataset, data collection. Examples: "Government Data Catalog" dataset "Population Census 2020", "Research Data Repository" dataset "Climate Change Projections", "Open Data Portal" dataset "Public Transport Schedules".
datasetTimeInterval: A temporal applicability relation between a dataset and its relevant time range. Also called: dataset time range, temporal coverage, data period. Examples: "Census Data" dataset time interval "2011", "Historical Weather Data" dataset time interval "1950-2000", "Economic Survey" dataset time interval "2022-01-01/2022-12-31".
dateCreated: A temporal origin relation between a creative work or data feed item and the date it was created or added. Also called: creation date, date of origin, initial date. Examples: "Painting" date created "1889-05-01", "Blog Post" date created "2023-03-15T10:00:00Z", "Data Feed Entry" date created "2023-01-01". Distinct from datePublished, which is the date of first public release.
dateDeleted: A temporal removal relation between a data feed item and the datetime it was removed from the feed. Also called: deletion date, removal date, date of removal. Examples: "Expired Job Posting" date deleted "2023-06-30", "Outdated Product Listing" date deleted "2023-01-01T00:00:00Z".
dateIssued: A temporal issuance relation between a ticket and the date it was issued. Also called: issuance date, date of issue, ticket date. Examples: "Concert Ticket" date issued "2023-04-01", "Flight Ticket" date issued "2023-01-10T14:30:00Z", "Parking Permit" date issued "2023-07-01".
dateModified: A temporal revision relation between a creative work or data feed item and the date it was most recently modified. Also called: last modified date, revision date, update date. Examples: "Wikipedia Article" date modified "2023-10-26T11:45:00Z", "Software Documentation" date modified "2023-09-01", "Data Feed Entry" date modified "2023-01-05". Distinct from dateCreated, which is the initial creation date.
datePosted: A temporal publication relation between a CDCPMD record, job posting, real estate listing, or special announcement and its online publication date. Also called: posting date, publication date, listing date. Examples: "Job Opening" date posted "2023-10-25", "Apartment for Rent" date posted "2023-10-20", "Public Health Alert" date posted "2023-03-01T09:00:00Z". Distinct from datePublished, which is a more general property for first publication.
datePublished: A temporal release relation between a certification or creative work and its date of first publication or broadcast. Also called: publication date, broadcast date, release date. Examples: "Book" date published "1984-06-08", "TV Show Episode" date published "2023-01-01", "Certification" date published "2022-12-01". Distinct from dateCreated, which is the date of creation, and datePosted, which is for online listings.
dateRead: A temporal interaction relation between a message and the date/time it was read by the recipient. Also called: read date, message read time, recipient read time. Examples: "Email" date read "2023-10-26T10:30:00Z", "Chat Message" date read "2023-10-26T10:35:00Z". Distinct from dateReceived, which is when the message arrived.
dateReceived: A temporal arrival relation between a message and the date/time it was received by the recipient. Also called: reception date, message arrival time, delivery time. Examples: "Email" date received "2023-10-26T10:25:00Z", "Package Notification" date received "2023-10-26T11:00:00Z". Distinct from dateSent, which is when the message was dispatched.
dateSent: A temporal dispatch relation between a message and the date/time it was sent. Also called: sending date, message dispatch time, transmission time. Examples: "Email" date sent "2023-10-26T10:20:00Z", "SMS Message" date sent "2023-10-26T10:30:00Z". Distinct from dateReceived, which is when the message arrived.
dateVehicleFirstRegistered: A temporal registration relation between a vehicle and the date of its first registration with public authorities. Also called: first registration date, initial registration, vehicle registration date. Examples: "Car" date vehicle first registered "2018-03-15", "Motorcycle" date vehicle first registered "2020-07-01", "Truck" date vehicle first registered "2015-11-20".
dateline: A textual origin relation between a news article and the brief text describing where and when the story was written or filed. Also called: news origin, article origin, reporting location. Examples: "News Report" dateline "BEIRUT, Lebanon, June 2.", "Article" dateline "Paris, France", "Dispatch" dateline "December 19, 2017 11:43AM Reporting from Washington". Distinct from locationCreated, which is a structured representation of the creation location.
dayOfWeek: A temporal specification relation between an educational or occupational program or opening hours specification and the day of the week it is valid for. Also called: valid day, operating day, schedule day. Examples: "Store Hours" day of week "Monday", "Class Schedule" day of week "Tuesday", "Program Availability" day of week "Saturday".
deathDate: A temporal event relation between a person and their date of death. Also called: date of demise, passing date, decease date. Examples: "Historical Figure" death date "1963-11-22", "Family Member" death date "2020-05-10". Distinct from birthDate, which is the date of birth.
deathPlace: A geographical event relation between a person and the place where they died. Also called: place of demise, passing location, decease location. Examples: "Historical Figure" death place "Dallas, Texas", "Family Member" death place "London, UK". Distinct from birthPlace, which is the place of birth.
defaultValue: A value assignment relation between a property value specification and its default value. Also called: default setting, initial value, preset value. Examples: "Text Input Field" default value "Enter text here", "Number Selector" default value "0", "Color Picker" default value "#FFFFFF".
deliveryAddress: A destination relation between a parcel delivery and its destination postal address. Also called: shipping address, recipient address, delivery location. Examples: "Package" delivery address "123 Main St, Anytown, USA", "Food Order" delivery address "Apt 4B, 567 Oak Ave", "Mail" delivery address "P.O. Box 100".
deliveryLeadTime: A temporal delay relation between a demand or offer and the typical time between order receipt and goods leaving the warehouse or being ready for pickup. Also called: lead time, dispatch time, preparation time. Examples: "Product Offer" delivery lead time "2-3 business days", "Custom Order" delivery lead time "1 week", "In-store Pickup" delivery lead time "2 hours". Distinct from deliveryTime, which is the total time until the goods reach the customer.
deliveryMethod: A logistical approach relation between an order, receive, send, or track action and the method used for delivery. Also called: shipping method, delivery mode, transport method. Examples: "Online Purchase" delivery method "Standard Shipping", "Document Send" delivery method "Email", "Package Tracking" delivery method "Courier Service".
deliveryStatus: A logistical progress relation between a parcel delivery and the events marking its journey from shipment to final delivery. Also called: shipment status, package status, tracking updates. Examples: "Package" delivery status "In Transit", "Order" delivery status "Out for Delivery", "Shipment" delivery status "Delivered".
deliveryTime: A temporal duration relation between delivery time settings or offer shipping details and the total delay from order receipt to goods reaching the final customer. Also called: total delivery time, shipping duration, estimated delivery. Examples: "Standard Shipping" delivery time "5-7 business days", "Express Delivery" delivery time "1-2 days", "International Shipment" delivery time "2-3 weeks". Distinct from deliveryLeadTime, which is the time until dispatch or pickup readiness.
department: An organizational structure relation between an organization and one of its departments. Also called: organizational unit, division, branch. Examples: "University" department "Computer Science Department", "Hospital" department "Emergency Room", "Retail Store" department "Pharmacy".
departureAirport: A geographical origin relation between a flight and the airport from which it originates. Also called: origin airport, departure airfield, flight departure point. Examples: "Flight BA249" departure airport "London Heathrow Airport", "Flight UA123" departure airport "San Francisco International Airport". Distinct from arrivalAirport, which is the destination airport.
departureBoatTerminal: A geographical origin relation between a boat trip and the terminal or port from which it departs. Also called: origin boat terminal, departure port, ferry terminal. Examples: "Ferry Trip" departure boat terminal "Dover Ferry Terminal", "Cruise" departure boat terminal "PortMiami". Distinct from arrivalBoatTerminal, which is the destination terminal.
departureBusStop: A geographical origin relation between a bus trip and the stop or station from which it departs. Also called: origin bus stop, departure bus station, bus departure point. Examples: "Bus Route 101" departure bus stop "Central Bus Station", "Intercity Bus" departure bus stop "Port Authority Bus Terminal". Distinct from arrivalBusStop, which is the destination stop.
departureGate: An identification relation between a flight and its departure gate identifier. Also called: gate number, boarding gate, flight gate. Examples: "Flight BA249" departure gate "Gate A12", "Flight UA123" departure gate "Gate 34B". Distinct from arrivalGate, which is the arrival gate.
departurePlatform: An identification relation between a train trip and the platform from which it departs. Also called: platform number, train platform, departure track. Examples: "Train to Paris" departure platform "Platform 5", "Commuter Train" departure platform "Track 3". Distinct from arrivalPlatform, which is the arrival platform.
departureStation: A geographical origin relation between a train trip and the station from which it departs. Also called: origin train station, departure rail station, train departure point. Examples: "Train to Paris" departure station "London St Pancras International", "Commuter Train" departure station "Grand Central Terminal". Distinct from arrivalStation, which is the destination station.
departureTerminal: An identification relation between a flight and its departure terminal identifier. Also called: terminal number, flight terminal, departure building. Examples: "Flight BA249" departure terminal "Terminal 5", "Flight UA123" departure terminal "Terminal 3". Distinct from arrivalTerminal, which is the arrival terminal.
departureTime: A temporal event relation between a trip and its expected departure time. Also called: scheduled departure, leaving time, takeoff time. Examples: "Flight" departure time "2023-11-01T08:00:00Z", "Bus Trip" departure time "14:30:00", "Train Journey" departure time "2023-12-25T10:00:00". Distinct from arrivalTime, which is the expected arrival time.
dependencies: A prerequisite relation between a tech article and the requirements needed to fulfill its steps. Also called: technical requirements, prerequisites, required components. Examples: "Software Installation Guide" dependencies "Python 3.8, pip", "Hardware Setup Article" dependencies "Screwdriver, Internet connection", "Programming Tutorial" dependencies "Basic understanding of algorithms".
depth: A dimension relation between an offer shipping details, product, shipping conditions, or visual artwork and its depth measurement. Also called: dimension depth, product depth, artwork depth. Examples: "Book" depth "2.5 cm", "Painting" depth "5 inches", "Shipping Box" depth "30 cm". Distinct from width and height, which are other dimensions.
description: A descriptive relation between a thing and its textual description. Also called: item description, details, explanation. Examples: "Product" description "A versatile smartphone with advanced camera features.", "Event" description "An annual conference for tech enthusiasts.", "Person" description "A renowned scientist and author.". Distinct from disambiguatingDescription, which is specifically for disambiguation.
device: A compatibility relation between a software application and the specific device required to run it. Also called: required device, compatible device, hardware requirement. Examples: "Mobile Game" device "iPhone 15", "VR Application" device "Oculus Quest 2", "Desktop Software" device "Windows PC".
diagnosis: A diagnostic outcome relation between a DDx element or patient and one or more alternative medical conditions considered in the differential diagnosis process. Also called: medical diagnosis, differential diagnosis, identified condition. Examples: "Patient X" diagnosis "Common Cold", "DDx Element" diagnosis "Influenza", "Medical Case" diagnosis "Allergic Reaction". Distinct from differentialDiagnosis, which is the set of competing diagnoses.
diagram: An illustrative relation between an anatomical structure and an image containing a diagram of it. Also called: anatomical illustration, structural diagram, visual representation. Examples: "Human Heart" diagram "Image of heart chambers and vessels", "Brain Anatomy" diagram "Diagram showing lobes and functions", "Skeletal System" diagram "Illustration of bone structure".
diet: A nutritional input relation between an exercise action and the diet used in conjunction with it. Also called: exercise diet, nutritional plan, dietary regimen. Examples: "Weight Loss Program" diet "Low-carb diet", "Marathon Training" diet "High-protein diet", "Bodybuilding Routine" diet "Calorie-controlled diet". Distinct from dietFeatures, which describes the specific nutritional information of a diet.
dietFeatures: A nutritional characteristic relation between a diet and its specific nutritional information or recommendations. Also called: diet specifics, nutritional guidelines, dietary recommendations. Examples: "Keto Diet" diet features "Avoid carbohydrates, high fat intake", "Vegan Diet" diet features "No animal products, focus on plant-based proteins", "Mediterranean Diet" diet features "Emphasis on whole grains, fruits, vegetables, olive oil". Distinct from diet, which is the diet itself.
differentialDiagnosis: A diagnostic comparison relation between a medical condition and one of a set of closely-related or competing diagnoses. Also called: competing diagnosis, alternative diagnosis, diagnostic possibilities. Examples: "Headache" differential diagnosis "Migraine", "Chest Pain" differential diagnosis "Heartburn", "Fever" differential diagnosis "Influenza". Distinct from diagnosis, which is the final identified condition.
digitalSourceType: A source classification relation between a creative work and an IPTCDigitalSourceEnumeration code indicating the nature of its digital source(s). Also called: digital origin type, source media type, digital asset source. Examples: "News Photo" digital source type "OriginalDigital", "Archival Document" digital source type "DigitizedAnalog", "Scanned Artwork" digital source type "ScannedPrint".
directApply: An application method relation between a job posting and whether direct online application is enabled via its associated URL. Also called: direct application, online application enabled, apply directly. Examples: "Job Posting A" direct apply "True", "Job Posting B" direct apply "False", "Career Opportunity" direct apply "True".
director: A creative leadership relation between a clip, creative work season, episode, event, movie, or video game and a person who directed it. Also called: directed by, filmmaker, showrunner. Examples: "Movie" director "Steven Spielberg", "TV Episode" director "Ava DuVernay", "Video Game" director "Hideo Kojima". Distinct from directors, which is a plural property for multiple directors.
directors: A creative leadership relation between a clip, episode, movie, or video game and the persons who directed it. Also called: directed by, filmmakers, showrunners. Examples: "Movie" directors "Joel Coen, Ethan Coen", "TV Episode" directors "Various Directors", "Video Game" directors "Hideo Kojima, Yoji Shinkawa". Distinct from director, which is a singular property for a single director.
disambiguatingDescription: A clarifying description relation between a thing and a short text used to distinguish it from similar items. Also called: clarifying description, distinguishing text, unique description. Examples: "Apple" disambiguating description "The fruit, not the company.", "Mercury" disambiguating description "The planet, not the element.", "Jaguar" disambiguating description "The animal, not the car brand.". Distinct from description, which is a general description.
discount: A price reduction relation between an order and any discount applied to it. Also called: price reduction, markdown, rebate. Examples: "Online Order" discount "10%", "Bulk Purchase" discount "25 USD", "Promotional Order" discount "Free Shipping".
discountCode: A discount code relation between an order and the text string representing a code used to redeem a discount. Also called "coupon code", "promo code", "voucher code". Examples: "Order #123 discountCode 'SAVE20'", "Online purchase discountCode 'FREESHIP'", "Grocery order discountCode 'SUMMERDEAL'".
discountCurrency: A discount currency relation between an order and the text string indicating the currency in which a discount is expressed. Also called "currency of discount", "discount denomination". Examples: "Order #456 discountCurrency 'USD'", "Sale order discountCurrency 'EUR'", "Crypto purchase discountCurrency 'BTC'".
discusses: A discussion relation between a user comment and the creative work it is associated with. Also called "comments on", "pertains to", "about". Examples: "User comment 'Great movie!' discusses 'The Matrix'", "Blog post comment discusses 'Article on AI'", "Review discusses 'New Album by Artist X'". Distinct from discussionUrl, which is a link to the page containing comments about a creative work.
discussionUrl: A discussion URL relation between a creative work and the URL of the page where its comments are located. Also called "comments page link", "forum link", "feedback URL". Examples: "Movie 'Inception' discussionUrl 'example.com/inception/comments'", "Article 'Quantum Physics' discussionUrl 'forum.example.org/quantum'", "Book '1984' discussionUrl 'goodreads.com/1984/discussion'". Distinct from discusses, which is the creative work that a user comment is about.
diseasePreventionInfo: A disease prevention information relation between a special announcement and a URL or web content providing details about disease prevention. Also called "prevention guidelines", "health advice". Examples: "Special announcement diseasePreventionInfo 'cdc.gov/prevention'", "Public health alert diseasePreventionInfo 'WebContent on handwashing'", "COVID-19 update diseasePreventionInfo 'who.int/prevention'".
diseaseSpreadStatistics: A disease spread statistics relation between a special announcement and a dataset, observation, URL, or web content containing statistical information about the spread of a disease. Also called "epidemic data", "infection rates", "case statistics". Examples: "Special announcement diseaseSpreadStatistics 'Dataset of daily cases'", "Public health update diseaseSpreadStatistics 'WebContent on regional spread'", "COVID-19 alert diseaseSpreadStatistics 'URL to dashboard'".
displayLocation: A display location relation between a creative work or product and the place where it can be viewed or experienced in-person. Also called "viewing location", "exhibition place", "experience venue". Examples: "Painting 'Mona Lisa' displayLocation 'Louvre Museum'", "Product 'New Car Model' displayLocation 'Dealership Showroom'", "Sculpture displayLocation 'Art Gallery'".
dissolutionDate: A dissolution date relation between an organization and the date when it was dissolved. Also called "closure date", "ceased operations date", "disbandment date". Examples: "Company 'Acme Corp' dissolutionDate '2023-01-15'", "Non-profit organization dissolutionDate '2022-07-01'", "Partnership dissolutionDate '2024-03-10'".
distance: A distance relation between an exercise action or travel action and the length travelled. Also called "travelled distance", "route length", "journey distance". Examples: "Exercise action 'Running' distance '10 km'", "Travel action 'Road Trip' distance '500 miles'", "Cycling activity distance '25 mi'".
distinguishingSign: A distinguishing sign relation between a differential diagnosis element and a medical sign or symptom that helps differentiate it from other diagnoses.
