Examples: "Job posting 'Software Engineer' estimatedSalary '$120,000'", "Occupation 'Teacher' estimatedSalary 'MonetaryAmountDistribution for $50k-$70k'", "Job 'Data Scientist' estimatedSalary '150000'".
estimatesRiskOf: A risk estimation relation between a medical risk estimator and the medical entity whose risk is being assessed. Also called "predicts risk for", "assesses likelihood of", "calculates risk of". Examples: "Medical risk estimator 'Framingham Score' estimatesRiskOf 'Cardiovascular Disease'", "Genetic test estimatesRiskOf 'Type 2 Diabetes'", "Screening tool estimatesRiskOf 'Breast Cancer'".
ethicsPolicy: An ethics policy relation between an organization (e.g., news media) and the creative work or URL describing its ethical standards and practices. Also called "code of ethics", "conduct policy", "ethical guidelines". Examples: "News media organization ethicsPolicy 'example.com/ethics'", "Restaurant ethicsPolicy 'Statement on sustainable sourcing'", "Company ethicsPolicy 'CreativeWork detailing corporate values'". Distinct from diversityPolicy, which specifically addresses diversity and inclusion.
event: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.
eventAttendanceMode: An event attendance mode relation between an event and the enumeration indicating whether it occurs online, offline, or a mix. Also called "attendance format", "event delivery mode", "participation mode". Examples: "Event 'Conference' eventAttendanceMode 'OnlineEventAttendanceMode'", "Event 'Workshop' eventAttendanceMode 'OfflineEventAttendanceMode'", "Event 'Hybrid Meeting' eventAttendanceMode 'MixedEventAttendanceMode'".
eventSchedule: An event schedule relation between an event and a schedule that defines a series of repeating occurrences for it. Also called "recurring schedule", "event timetable", "series schedule". Examples: "Gym class eventSchedule 'Weekly schedule for Yoga'", "Concert series eventSchedule 'Schedule for monthly performances'", "Webinar series eventSchedule 'Schedule for bi-weekly sessions'". Distinct from schedule, which is a more general property for any schedule.
eventStatus: An event status relation between an event and its current status type. Also called "event condition", "status of event", "event state". Examples: "Event 'Concert' eventStatus 'EventCancelled'", "Event 'Meeting' eventStatus 'EventScheduled'", "Event 'Festival' eventStatus 'EventRescheduled'".
events: An events association relation between an organization or place and the events connected to it. Also called "associated events", "related events", "features events". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' events 'Art Exhibition, Lecture Series'", "Place 'Park' events 'Summer Festival, Winter Fair'", "Company 'Tech Solutions' events 'Annual Conference, Product Launch'". Distinct from event, which is the singular form.
evidenceLevel: An evidence level relation between a medical guideline and the strength of evidence used to formulate it. Also called: evidence strength, data strength, guideline evidence. Examples: "AHA Guideline for Hypertension" evidence level "Strong", "NICE Guideline for Diabetes" evidence level "Moderate", "WHO Guideline for COVID-19" evidence level "Weak". Distinct from evidenceOrigin, which is the source of the data.
evidenceOrigin: An evidence origin relation between a medical guideline and the source of data used to formulate it. Also called: data source, guideline source, origin of evidence. Examples: "AHA Guideline for Hypertension" evidence origin "RCT", "NICE Guideline for Diabetes" evidence origin "Consensus Opinion", "WHO Guideline for COVID-19" evidence origin "Observational Studies". Distinct from evidenceLevel, which is the strength of the evidence.
exampleOfWork: An example relation between a creative work and another creative work that it is an instance, realization, or derivation of. Also called: instance of, realization of, derivation of, based on. Examples: "Mona Lisa (print)" example of work "Mona Lisa (original painting)", "Hamlet (film)" example of work "Hamlet (play)", "Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)" example of work "Star Wars: A New Hope (film)".
exceptDate: An exception date relation between a schedule and a specific date or datetime when a scheduled event will not take place. Also called: exclusion date, cancelled date, unavailable date. Examples: "Weekly Yoga Class Schedule" except date "2023-12-25", "Daily Bus Route Schedule" except date "2024-01-01T08:00:00", "Monthly Book Club Schedule" except date "2023-11-11".
exchangeRateSpread: An exchange rate spread relation between an exchange rate specification and the difference between the buy and sell prices of foreign currency. Also called: currency spread, bid-ask spread, broker margin. Examples: "USD/EUR Exchange Rate" exchange rate spread "0.005", "GBP/JPY Exchange Rate" exchange rate spread "0.01", "Currency Exchange Service" exchange rate spread "0.008".
executableLibraryName: An executable library name relation between an API reference and the file name of the library. Also called: library filename, DLL name, assembly name. Examples: "System.Net API" executable library name "System.dll", "OpenGL API" executable library name "opengl32.dll", "Python Requests Library" executable library name "requests.py".
exerciseCourse: An exercise course relation between an exercise action and the specific place or course where the action was performed. Also called: workout location, training venue, activity course. Examples: "Morning Run" exercise course "Central Park Loop", "Swimming Practice" exercise course "Olympic Pool Lane 3", "Cycling Race" exercise course "Mountain Bike Trail". Distinct from fromLocation, which is the original location before the action.
exercisePlan: An exercise plan relation between an exercise action and the specific plan or routine followed during the action. Also called: workout routine, training regimen, fitness program. Examples: "Morning Run" exercise plan "Couch to 5K Plan", "Weightlifting Session" exercise plan "StrongLifts 5x5", "Yoga Practice" exercise plan "Beginner Vinyasa Flow".
exerciseRelatedDiet: An exercise-related diet relation between an exercise action and the diet followed in conjunction with that action. Also called: workout diet, fitness diet, training nutrition. Examples: "Marathon Training" exercise related diet "High-Carb Diet", "Bodybuilding Workout" exercise related diet "High-Protein Diet", "Weight Loss Program" exercise related diet "Calorie-Restricted Diet".
exerciseType: An exercise type relation between an exercise action or plan and the specific category or kind of physical activity. Also called: activity type, workout category, training style. Examples: "Morning Run" exercise type "Aerobics", "Weightlifting Session" exercise type "Strength Training", "Yoga Practice" exercise type "Flexibility Training".
exifData: An EXIF data relation between an image object and its embedded exchangeable image file format metadata. Also called: image metadata, photo data, camera info. Examples: "Sunset Photo.jpg" exif data "ISO: 100, Aperture: f/8", "Portrait.png" exif data "Camera Model: Canon EOS 5D Mark IV", "Landscape.tiff" exif data "GPS Latitude: 34.0522".
expectedArrivalFrom: An expected arrival from relation between a parcel delivery and the earliest date or datetime the package is anticipated to arrive. Also called: earliest arrival, minimum delivery date, estimated start arrival. Examples: "Amazon Order #123" expected arrival from "2023-10-26", "UPS Package #456" expected arrival from "2023-10-27T09:00:00", "International Shipment" expected arrival from "2023-11-01". Distinct from expectedArrivalUntil, which is the latest arrival date.
expectedArrivalUntil: An expected arrival until relation between a parcel delivery and the latest date or datetime the package is anticipated to arrive. Also called: latest arrival, maximum delivery date, estimated end arrival. Examples: "Amazon Order #123" expected arrival until "2023-10-28", "UPS Package #456" expected arrival until "2023-10-27T17:00:00", "International Shipment" expected arrival until "2023-11-05". Distinct from expectedArrivalFrom, which is the earliest arrival date.
expectedPrognosis: An expected prognosis relation between a medical condition and its likely short-term or long-term outcome. Also called: anticipated outcome, predicted course, outlook. Examples: "Common Cold" expected prognosis "Full recovery within a week", "Type 2 Diabetes" expected prognosis "Manageable with lifestyle changes and medication", "Stage 4 Cancer" expected prognosis "Poor, with limited treatment options".
expectsAcceptanceOf: An expects acceptance of relation between an action access specification, consume action, or media subscription and an offer that must be accepted before the action can be performed. Also called: requires offer, prerequisite offer, conditional offer. Examples: "Watch Movie Action" expects acceptance of "Movie Purchase Offer", "Download Software Action" expects acceptance of "Software License Offer", "Access Premium Content" expects acceptance of "Subscription Offer".
experienceInPlaceOfEducation: An experience in place of education relation indicating whether a job posting accepts relevant experience as an alternative to formal educational qualifications. Also called: experience substitutes education, education equivalency, alternative qualification. Examples: "Senior Developer Job" experience in place of education "true", "Entry-Level Marketing Position" experience in place of education "false", "Project Manager Role" experience in place of education "true".
experienceRequirements: An experience requirements relation between a job posting or occupation and the necessary skills and experience for the role. Also called: required experience, skill requirements, professional background. Examples: "Software Engineer Job" experience requirements "5+ years in Java development", "Marketing Manager Occupation" experience requirements "Proven track record in digital marketing campaigns", "Chef Position" experience requirements "Culinary school degree and 3 years restaurant experience".
expertConsiderations: An expert considerations relation between a diet and the medical expert advice pertinent to that dietary plan. Also called: medical advice, professional guidance, health warnings. Examples: "Keto Diet" expert considerations "Consult a doctor if you have kidney issues", "Vegan Diet" expert considerations "Ensure adequate B12 supplementation", "Low-Sodium Diet" expert considerations "Monitor blood pressure regularly".
expires: An expiration relation between a certification or creative work and the date or datetime when its validity, usefulness, or availability ends. Also called: valid until, end date, availability end. Examples: "Software License" expires "2024-12-31", "News Article" expires "2023-10-30T23:59:59", "Professional Certification" expires "2025-06-01".
expressedIn: An expressed in relation between a gene and the anatomical structure, system, or biological entity where its activity has been experimentally observed. Also called: gene activity location, observed in, found in. Examples: "Gene A" expressed in "Brain", "Gene B" expressed in "Liver", "Gene C" expressed in "Digestive System".
extendedAddress: An extended address relation between a postal address and additional details like an apartment number, care of information, or alternative name. Also called: address line 2, apartment number, suite number. Examples: "123 Main St" extended address "Apt 4B", "PO Box 123" extended address "C/O John Doe", "456 Oak Ave" extended address "Suite 100".
familyName: A family name relation between a person and their last name. Also called: last name, surname. Examples: "John Doe" family name "Doe", "Jane Smith" family name "Smith", "Alice Wonderland" family name "Wonderland". Distinct from givenName, which is the first name.
fatContent: A fat content relation between nutrition information and the total mass of fat present. Also called: total fat, fat grams. Examples: "Nutrition Label for Cereal" fat content "5g", "Nutrition Label for Milk" fat content "8g", "Nutrition Label for Yogurt" fat content "2g".
faxNumber: A fax number relation between a contact point, organization, person, or place and its associated fax telephone number. Also called: facsimile number, fax line. Examples: "Acme Corp" fax number "+1-555-123-4567", "Dr. Smith's Office" fax number "555-987-6543", "Public Library" fax number "555-111-2222".
featureList: A feature list relation between a software application and the functionalities or modules it provides. Also called: application features, software capabilities, module list. Examples: "Word Processor" feature list "Spell Check, Grammar Check, Document Templates", "Photo Editor" feature list "Layers, Filters, Cropping", "Operating System" feature list "Multitasking, File Management, User Accounts".
feesAndCommissionsSpecification: A fees and commissions specification relation between a financial product or service and a description of its associated charges, commissions, and terms. Also called: fee structure, pricing terms, cost breakdown. Examples: "Checking Account" fees and commissions specification "Monthly maintenance fee: $5, ATM withdrawal fee: $2.50", "Investment Fund" fees and commissions specification "Management fee: 1.5%, Sales load: 0.5%", "Credit Card" fees and commissions specification "Annual fee: $95, Late payment fee: $39".
fiberContent: A fiber content relation between nutrition information and the total mass of dietary fiber present. Also called: dietary fiber, fiber grams. Examples: "Nutrition Label for Oatmeal" fiber content "4g", "Nutrition Label for Apple" fiber content "3g", "Nutrition Label for Lentils" fiber content "15g".
fileFormat: A file format relation between a creative work and its media type, typically expressed as a MIME format. Also called: media type, content type, file extension. Examples: "Document.pdf" file format "application/pdf", "Image.jpg" file format "image/jpeg", "Video.mp4" file format "video/mp4".
fileSize: A file size relation between a software application and the size of its executable or package. Also called: application size, package size, download size. Examples: "Text Editor App" file size "25MB", "Mobile Game" file size "150MB", "Operating System Update" file size "2.5GB".
financialAidEligible: A financial aid eligibility relation between a course or educational program and the types of financial aid students can use to cover its costs. Also called: aid programs, funding options, scholarship eligibility. Examples: "Computer Science Course" financial aid eligible "Federal Pell Grant", "MBA Program" financial aid eligible "Student Loans", "Vocational Training" financial aid eligible "GI Bill".
firstAppearance: A first appearance relation between a claim and the creative work where it was initially known to occur. Also called: initial publication, original mention, debut in. Examples: "Claim: Earth is flat" first appearance "Ancient Greek Texts", "Claim: COVID-19 is a hoax" first appearance "Social Media Post", "Claim: New drug cures cancer" first appearance "Unverified Online Article".
firstPerformance: A first performance relation between a music composition and the event where it was initially performed. Also called: premiere, debut performance, initial staging. Examples: "Beethoven's 5th Symphony" first performance "Vienna, 1808 Concert", "Hamilton Musical" first performance "Public Theater, NYC 2015", "New Opera 'The Siren'" first performance "Royal Opera House Gala".
flightDistance: A flight distance relation between a flight and the total distance covered during its journey. Also called: journey distance, air travel distance, flight length. Examples: "Flight UA123" flight distance "1500 miles", "Flight BA456" flight distance "2400 km", "Flight LH789" flight distance "Long-haul".
flightNumber: A flight number relation between a flight and its unique identifier, typically including the airline IATA code. Also called: flight ID, airline code, flight identifier. Examples: "Flight from London to New York" flight number "BA177", "Flight from Tokyo to San Francisco" flight number "UA838", "Flight from Sydney to Dubai" flight number "EK413".
floorLevel: A floor level relation between an accommodation, local business, or residence and its specific floor within a multi-storey building. Also called: storey number, level, floor number. Examples: "Hotel Room 501" floor level "5", "Office Suite 10A" floor level "10", "Apartment 3B" floor level "3".
floorLimit: A floor limit relation between a payment card and the monetary amount above which credit card transactions require authorization. Also called: authorization threshold, transaction limit, credit card limit. Examples: "Visa Credit Card" floor limit "$500", "Mastercard Debit Card" floor limit "$200", "Corporate Payment Card" floor limit "$1000".
floorSize: A floor size relation between an accommodation or floor plan and its total area, typically measured in square meters or square feet. Also called: area, square footage, room size. Examples: "Hotel Suite" floor size "50 square meters", "Apartment Floor Plan" floor size "800 sq ft", "Conference Room" floor size "120 sq yd".
followee: A followee relation between a follow action and the person or organization that is being followed. Also called: followed entity, subject of follow, target of follow. Examples: "User A follows User B" followee "User B", "Fan follows Band X" followee "Band X", "Journalist follows News Organization Y" followee "News Organization Y". Distinct from follows, which is the general social relation.
follows: A follows relation representing a generic uni-directional social connection between two people. Also called: is following, subscribes to, tracks. Examples: "Alice follows Bob", "Charlie follows David", "Eve follows Frank". Distinct from followee, which is the object of a follow action.
followup: A followup relation between a medical procedure and the typical or recommended post-procedure care. Also called: aftercare, post-procedure care, follow-up instructions. Examples: "Surgery" followup "Rest for 2 weeks, avoid heavy lifting", "Dental Cleaning" followup "Brush twice daily, floss regularly", "Vaccination" followup "Monitor for side effects, schedule booster shot".
foodEstablishment: A food establishment relation between a cook action and the specific place or food establishment where the cooking occurred. Also called: cooking location, restaurant, kitchen. Examples: "Chef prepares meal" food establishment "Gourmet Restaurant", "Home Cook makes dinner" food establishment "My Kitchen", "Baker bakes bread" food establishment "Local Bakery". Distinct from foodEvent, which is a specific event.
foodEvent: A food event relation between a cook action and the specific food-related event where the cooking took place. Also called: culinary event, cooking event, gastronomic occasion. Examples: "Chef prepares meal" food event "Annual Food Festival", "Home Cook makes dinner" food event "Family Dinner Party", "Baker bakes bread" food event "Charity Bake Sale". Distinct from foodEstablishment, which is a specific place.
foodWarning: A food warning relation between a drug and any precautions, guidance, or contraindications regarding food consumption while taking it. Also called: dietary restrictions, food interactions, consumption advice. Examples: "Warfarin" food warning "Avoid grapefruit, limit Vitamin K rich foods", "Antibiotics" food warning "Do not take with dairy products", "MAOIs" food warning "Avoid aged cheeses and cured meats".
founder: A founder relation between an organization and the person or organization that established it. Also called: established by, created by, initiated by. Examples: "Microsoft" founder "Bill Gates", "Apple Inc." founder "Steve Jobs", "Google" founder "Larry Page". Distinct from founders, which is specifically for multiple people.
founders: A founders relation between an organization and the people who established it. Also called: co-founders, creators, originators. Examples: "Google" founders "Larry Page, Sergey Brin", "Apple Inc." founders "Steve Jobs, Steve Wozniak, Ronald Wayne", "Microsoft" founders "Bill Gates, Paul Allen". Distinct from founder, which can be a single person or organization.
foundingDate: A founding date relation between an organization and the specific date it was established. Also called: establishment date, creation date, inception date. Examples: "Microsoft" founding date "1975-04-04", "Apple Inc." founding date "1976-04-01", "Google" founding date "1998-09-04".
foundingLocation: A founding location relation between an organization and the place where it was established. Also called: place of origin, establishment location, birthplace. Examples: "Microsoft" founding location "Albuquerque, New Mexico", "Apple Inc." founding location "Los Altos, California", "Google" founding location "Menlo Park, California".
free: A free relation indicating whether a publication event, item, or place is accessible without cost. Also called: no charge, complimentary, gratis. Examples: "Online Article Publication" free "true", "Concert Event" free "false", "Public Park Access" free "true".
freeShippingThreshold: A free shipping threshold relation between shipping rate settings and the monetary value at or above which shipping becomes free. Also called: free delivery minimum, shipping waiver amount, no-cost shipping limit. Examples: "Standard Shipping" free shipping threshold "$50", "Express Shipping" free shipping threshold "$100", "International Shipping" free shipping threshold "$200".
frequency: A frequency relation between a dose schedule and how often the dose is administered. Also called: dosage frequency, administration rate, regularity. Examples: "Medication Schedule" frequency "Twice daily", "Vaccine Schedule" frequency "Annually", "Treatment Plan" frequency "Every 8 hours".
fromLocation: A from location relation between an exercise, move, or transfer action and the original place of the object or agent before the action occurred. Also called: origin location, starting point, departure place. Examples: "Package Delivery" from location "Warehouse A", "Person Moving" from location "Old Apartment", "Data Transfer" from location "Server Room 1". Distinct from toLocation, which is the destination after the action.
fuelCapacity: A fuel capacity relation between a vehicle and the total storage capacity of its fuel tank or battery. Also called: tank capacity, battery capacity, fuel volume. Examples: "Sedan Car" fuel capacity "60 liters", "Electric Vehicle" fuel capacity "75 kWh", "Motorcycle" fuel capacity "15 gallons".
fuelConsumption: A fuel consumption relation between a vehicle and the amount of fuel it uses to travel a specific distance or duration. Also called: fuel usage, gas mileage (inverse), liters per 100km. Examples: "Compact Car" fuel consumption "7 L/100 km", "SUV" fuel consumption "12 L/100 km", "Electric Car" fuel consumption "15 kWh/100 km". Distinct from fuelEfficiency, which is a reciprocal measure (distance per unit fuel).
fuelEfficiency: A fuel efficiency relation between a vehicle and the distance it travels per unit of fuel consumed. Also called: miles per gallon, kilometers per liter, fuel economy. Examples: "Compact Car" fuel efficiency "40 mpg", "Hybrid Vehicle" fuel efficiency "55 mpg", "Motorcycle" fuel efficiency "60 km/L". Distinct from fuelConsumption, which is a reciprocal measure (fuel per unit distance).
fuelType: A fuel type relation between an engine specification or vehicle and the kind of fuel it is designed to use. Also called: energy source, power type, fuel kind. Examples: "Gasoline Engine" fuel type "Unleaded Gasoline", "Diesel Truck" fuel type "Diesel", "Electric Car" fuel type "Electricity".
fulfillmentType: A fulfillment type relation between a shipping service and the method by which orders are fulfilled. Also called: delivery method, order processing type, shipping mode. Examples: "Standard Shipping" fulfillment type "Delivery", "Click & Collect" fulfillment type "Pickup", "Digital Download" fulfillment type "Download".
functionalClass: A functional class relation between a joint and the degree of mobility it permits. Also called: joint mobility, range of motion, movement classification. Examples: "Knee Joint" functional class "Diarthrosis (freely movable)", "Skull Sutures" functional class "Synarthrosis (immovable)", "Vertebral Joints" functional class "Amphiarthrosis (slightly movable)".
fundedItem: A funded item relation between a grant and the biochemical entity, creative work, event, medical entity, organization, person, or product that receives direct or indirect funding or sponsorship. Also called: grant recipient, sponsored item, supported entity. Examples: "Research Grant" funded item "Cancer Research Project", "Arts Grant" funded item "Local Theater Production", "Educational Grant" funded item "Student Scholarship Program". Distinct from funding, which is the grant itself.
funder: A funder relation between a creative work, event, grant, organization, or person and the organization or person providing financial support or sponsorship. Also called: sponsor, benefactor, financial supporter. Examples: "Art Exhibition" funder "National Endowment for the Arts", "Research Project" funder "NIH", "Charity Event" funder "Local Bank". Distinct from fundedItem, which is the item receiving funding.
funding: A funding relation between a biochemical entity, creative work, event, medical entity, organization, person, or product and the grant that provides its direct or indirect financial support. Also called: grant received, sponsorship, financial support. Examples: "Cancer Research Project" funding "NIH Grant R01", "Local Theater Production" funding "Arts Council Grant", "Student Scholarship Program" funding "University Endowment Grant". Distinct from funder, which is the entity providing the funding.
game: A game relation between a game server and the video game that is hosted and played on it. Also called: hosted game, server game, game played. Examples: "Minecraft Server" game "Minecraft", "World of Warcraft Realm" game "World of Warcraft", "CS:GO Server" game "Counter-Strike: Global Offensive".
gameAvailabilityType: A game availability type relation between a play game action and the specific version or availability status of the game content. Also called: game version, content type, access type. Examples: "Play 'New Game'" game availability type "Full Version", "Play 'Game Demo'" game availability type "Demo", "Play 'Early Access'" game availability type "Early Access".
gameEdition: A game edition relation between a video game and its specific version or release edition. Also called: game version, release edition, special edition. Examples: "Cyberpunk 2077" game edition "Ultimate Edition", "The Witcher 3" game edition "Game of the Year Edition", "Minecraft" game edition "Java Edition".
gameItem: A game item relation between a game or video game series and an object within its virtual world that can be collected. Also called: in-game item, collectible, virtual object. Examples: "RPG Game" game item "Health Potion", "Adventure Game" game item "Golden Key", "Strategy Game" game item "Resource Pack".
gameLocation: A game location relation between a game or video game series and a real or fictional place where the game or part of it is set. Also called: game setting, virtual world, game environment. Examples: "Grand Theft Auto V" game location "Los Santos", "The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild" game location "Hyrule", "Assassin's Creed Valhalla" game location "England".
gamePlatform: A game platform relation between a video game or series and the electronic systems on which it can be played. Also called: gaming console, supported platform, system compatibility. Examples: "The Last of Us Part II" game platform "PlayStation 4", "Halo Infinite" game platform "Xbox Series X", "Cyberpunk 2077" game platform "PC".
gameServer: A game server relation between a video game and the server where it can be played. Also called: hosted on, playable server, game host. Examples: "Minecraft" game server "Hypixel Network", "World of Warcraft" game server "Frostmourne Realm", "Call of Duty" game server "Dedicated Server". Distinct from game, which is the game itself.
gameTip: A game tip relation between a video game and a creative work providing tips, tactics, or strategies for playing it. Also called: game guide, strategy guide, walkthrough. Examples: "Elden Ring" game tip "Fextralife Wiki", "Chess" game tip "Opening Strategy Guide", "Fortnite" game tip "Building Tactics Video".
gender: A gender relation between a person or sports team and their gender identity or classification. Also called: sex, gender identity, team gender. Examples: "John Doe" gender "Male", "Jane Smith" gender "Female", "Mixed Doubles Team" gender "Mixed".
genre: A genre relation between a broadcast channel, creative work, or music group and its category or style. Also called: category, style, type. Examples: "Novel '1984'" genre "Dystopian Fiction", "BBC News" genre "News", "Rock Band 'Queen'" genre "Rock".
geo: A geo relation between a place and its geographical coordinates or shape. Also called: geographic location, coordinates, spatial data. Examples: "Eiffel Tower" geo "Latitude: 48.8584, Longitude: 2.2945", "Central Park" geo "Polygon GeoShape", "Mount Everest" geo "Point GeoCoordinates".
geoContains: A geo contains relation representing a spatial relationship where one geometry or place fully encloses another, with at least one interior point in common. Also called: encloses, encompasses, includes. Examples: "Country 'France'" geo contains "City 'Paris'", "Continent 'Europe'" geo contains "Country 'Germany'", "Building 'Empire State'" geo contains "Office 'Suite 100'". Distinct from geoWithin, which is the inverse relation.
geoCoveredBy: A geo covered by relation representing a spatial relationship where a geometry or place is entirely covered by another geometry or place. Also called: is covered by, lies within, is contained by. Examples: "City 'Paris'" geo covered by "Country 'France'", "Lake 'Superior'" geo covered by "North America", "House '123 Main St'" geo covered by "City 'Springfield'". Distinct from geoCovers, which is the inverse relation.
geoCovers: A geo covers relation representing a spatial relationship where one geometry or place completely covers another, meaning every point of the covered entity is within the covering entity. Also called: covers, encompasses, overlies. Examples: "Country 'France'" geo covers "City 'Paris'", "North America" geo covers "Lake 'Superior'", "City 'Springfield'" geo covers "House '123 Main St'". Distinct from geoCoveredBy, which is the inverse relation.
geoCrosses: A geo crosses relation representing a spatial relationship where two geometries or places intersect, sharing some but not all interior points, and their intersection has a lower dimension than at least one of them. Also called: intersects, traverses, cuts across. Examples: "River 'Mississippi'" geo crosses "State 'Missouri'", "Road 'Route 66'" geo crosses "City 'Chicago'", "Flight Path" geo crosses "Mountain Range".
geoDisjoint: A geo disjoint relation representing a symmetric spatial relationship where two geometries or places have no points in common and are entirely disconnected. Also called: separate from, not overlapping, unconnected. Examples: "Country 'USA'" geo disjoint "Country 'China'", "Island 'Hawaii'" geo disjoint "Continent 'Europe'", "Building 'A'" geo disjoint "Building 'B'". Distinct from geoIntersects, which has at least one point in common.
geoEquals: A geo equals relation representing a symmetric spatial relationship where two geometries or places are topologically identical, sharing the same interior and boundary without intersecting each other's exterior. Also called: identical to, same location as, equivalent geometry. Examples: "City Boundary A" geo equals "City Boundary B (updated)", "Park Outline (old)" geo equals "Park Outline (new)", "Country Shape (vector)" geo equals "Country Shape (raster)".
geoIntersects: A geo intersects relation representing a spatial relationship where two geometries or places share at least one common point. Also called: overlaps with, touches, crosses. Examples: "River 'Thames'" geo intersects "City 'London'", "Road 'Main Street'" geo intersects "Park 'Central Park'", "Country 'USA'" geo intersects "Country 'Canada'". Distinct from geoDisjoint, which has no points in common.
geoMidpoint: A geo midpoint relation between a geo circle and the geographical coordinates representing its center. Also called: center coordinates, geographic center, central point. Examples: "Circular Search Area" geo midpoint "Latitude: 34.0, Longitude: -118.0", "GeoCircle around City" geo midpoint "City Center Coordinates", "Radar Range" geo midpoint "Radar Station Location".
geoOverlaps: A geo overlaps relation representing a spatial relationship where two geometries or places share some, but not all, common points. Also called: partially overlaps, shares area with, intersects partially. Examples: "City Park" geo overlaps "Residential Area", "Forest Reserve" geo overlaps "Hiking Trail Network", "Economic Zone A" geo overlaps "Economic Zone B". Distinct from geoContains (one fully encloses the other) and geoDisjoint (no common points).
geoRadius: A geo radius relation between a geo circle and its approximate radial distance from the center. Also called: circle radius, geographic radius, extent. Examples: "Search Area GeoCircle" geo radius "5000 meters", "Weather Alert Zone" geo radius "10 miles", "GPS Accuracy Circle" geo radius "10 feet".
geoTouches: A geo touches relation representing a symmetric spatial relationship where two geometries or places share at least one boundary point but no interior points. Also called: borders, adjoins, meets at boundary. Examples: "Country A" geo touches "Country B", "Property Line 1" geo touches "Property Line 2", "Lake Shore" geo touches "Land Mass". Distinct from geoIntersects, which can share interior points.
geoWithin: A geo within relation representing a spatial relationship where a geometry or place is located entirely inside the interior of another containing geometry or place. Also called: is inside, contained in, located within. Examples: "City 'Paris'" geo within "Country 'France'", "Office 'Suite 100'" geo within "Building 'Empire State'", "State 'California'" geo within "Country 'USA'". Distinct from geoContains, which is the inverse relation.
geographicArea: A geographic area relation between an audience and the administrative area it is associated with. Also called: target region, audience location, demographic area. Examples: "Local News Audience" geographic area "Springfield County", "National Election Voters" geographic area "United States", "European Market Audience" geographic area "European Union".
gettingTestedInfo: A getting tested info relation between a special announcement and information regarding testing for a medical condition. Also called: testing information, diagnostic details, screening guidance. Examples: "COVID-19 Announcement" getting tested info "CDC Testing Guidelines", "Flu Season Alert" getting tested info "Local Clinic Testing Sites", "Public Health Notice" getting tested info "Symptoms and Testing Advice".
givenName: A given name relation between a person and their first name. Also called: first name, personal name. Examples: "John Doe" given name "John", "Jane Smith" given name "Jane", "Alice Wonderland" given name "Alice". Distinct from familyName, which is the last name.
globalLocationNumber: A global location number relation between an organization, person, or place and its unique 13-digit GLN identifier. Also called: GLN, International Location Number, ILN. Examples: "Acme Corp Warehouse" global location number "1234567890123", "Hospital Main Campus" global location number "9876543210987", "Distribution Center X" global location number "1122334455667".
governmentBenefitsInfo: A government benefits info relation between a special announcement and information about associated government services or benefits. Examples: "Pandemic Relief Announcement" government benefits info "Unemployment Benefits Program", "Housing Crisis Alert" government benefits info "Rental Assistance Program", "Disaster Recovery Notice" government benefits info "FEMA Aid Services".
gracePeriod: A grace period relation between a loan or credit and the duration after a due date before a default is declared. Also called: payment grace period, default deferral, late payment window. Examples: "Mortgage Loan" grace period "15 days", "Credit Card" grace period "21 days", "Student Loan" grace period "6 months".
grantee: A grantee relation between a digital document permission and the audience, contact point, organization, or person to whom the permission is granted. Examples: "Document Access Permission" grantee "Team Members", "File Sharing Permission" grantee "John Doe", "API Access Permission" grantee "Developer Organization".
greater: A greater relation indicating that one qualitative value is superior or larger than another. Also called: is greater than, exceeds, is more than. Examples: "High" greater "Medium", "Excellent" greater "Good", "Large" greater "Small". Distinct from greaterOrEqual, which includes equality.
greaterOrEqual: A greater or equal relation indicating that one qualitative value is superior to or the same as another. Also called: is greater than or equal to, at least, no less than. Examples: "High" greater or equal "Medium", "Good" greater or equal "Good", "Large" greater or equal "Medium". Distinct from greater, which does not include equality.
gtin: A Global Trade Item Number (GTIN) relation identifying a demand, offer, or product with its unique numeric identification code. Also called: product identifier, trade item number, barcode number. Examples: "Product X" gtin "01234567890128", "Offer for Item Y" gtin "9876543210987", "Demand for Service Z" gtin "https://id.gs1.org/01/12345678901231". Distinct from gtin8, gtin12, gtin13, gtin14, which are more specific GTIN types.
gtin12: A GTIN-12 relation identifying a demand, offer, or product with its 12-digit Global Trade Item Number. Also called: UPC code, GTIN-12 identifier, 12-digit barcode. Examples: "Grocery Item" gtin12 "012345678901", "Consumer Product" gtin12 "789012345678", "Retail Offer" gtin12 "000001111111". Distinct from gtin, which is the general GTIN.
gtin13: A GTIN-13 relation identifying a demand, offer, or product with its 13-digit Global Trade Item Number, equivalent to EAN-13 or ISBN. Also called: EAN-13, ISBN-13, GTIN-13 identifier. Examples: "Book Product" gtin13 "9781234567890", "European Retail Item" gtin13 "5012345678901", "Offer for Book" gtin13 "9780123456789". Distinct from gtin, which is the general GTIN.
gtin14: A GTIN-14 relation identifying a demand, offer, or product with its 14-digit Global Trade Item Number, often used for trade items at different packaging levels. Also called: ITF-14, GTIN-14 identifier, shipping container code. Examples: "Case of Cans" gtin14 "10012345678905", "Pallet of Goods" gtin14 "00000012345678", "Wholesale Product" gtin14 "40123456789012". Distinct from gtin, which is the general GTIN.
gtin8: A GTIN-8 relation identifying a demand, offer, or product with its 8-digit Global Trade Item Number, also known as EAN-8. Also called: EAN-8, GTIN-8 identifier, 8-digit barcode. Examples: "Small Retail Item" gtin8 "12345670", "Confectionery Product" gtin8 "98765432", "Offer for Small Product" gtin8 "00000001". Distinct from gtin, which is the general GTIN.
guideline: A guideline relation between a medical entity and a related medical guideline. Also called: related guideline, medical recommendation, clinical protocol. guidelineSubject: A guideline subject relation between a medical guideline and the medical conditions, treatments, or other entities it addresses. Also called: guideline topic, subject matter, focus. handlingTime: A processing time relation between a shipping service or delivery time and the duration required for order fulfillment. hasAdultConsideration: An adult suitability relation between an offer or product and its intended audience or content rating. hasBioChemEntityPart: A part-whole relation between a biochemical entity and one of its constituent biochemical entities. Also called composed of, contains, includes part, made of. hasBroadcastChannel: A channel association relation between a broadcast service and one of its broadcast channels. Also called includes channel, offers channel, channel of. hasCategoryCode: A code inclusion relation between a category code set and one of its contained category codes. Also called contains code, includes code, code within. hasCertification: A certification relation between an entity (organization, person, place, product, or service) and its associated certification. hasCourse: A course inclusion relation between an educational or occupational program and one of its constituent courses. Also called includes course, program course, course part of. hasCourseInstance: A course offering relation between a course and a specific instance of that course. Also called course offering, instance of course, course session. hasCredential: A credential relation between an organization or person and an awarded credential. Also called holds credential, awarded credential, possesses credential. hasDefinedTerm: A term inclusion relation between a defined term set or taxon and one of its contained defined terms. Also called contains term, includes term, term within. hasDeliveryMethod: A delivery method relation between a delivery event or parcel delivery and the method used for its delivery. Also called delivery via, shipping method, method of delivery. hasDigitalDocumentPermission: A document permission relation between a digital document and an associated access permission. Also called document access, permission for document, document rights. hasDriveThroughService: A drive-through service availability relation for a place, indicating whether it offers services accessible by driving through. hasEnergyConsumptionDetails: An energy consumption detail relation between a product and its energy efficiency information. hasMerchantReturnPolicy: A merchant return policy relation between an offer, organization, or product and its applicable return policy. Also called return policy, refund policy, returns information. hasOfferCatalog: An offer catalog relation between an organization, person, or service and an associated offer catalog. Also called offers catalog, catalog of offers, product catalog. hasShippingService: A shipping service relation between offer shipping details or an organization and a shipping service it provides. Also called offers shipping, shipping option, delivery service. Distinct from hasDefinedTerm, which describes the inverse (set has term).
inLanguage: A language relation between a broadcast service, communicate action, creative work, event, link role, pronounceable text, or write action and the language used. Also called language of, written in, spoken in. Examples: "A creative work is in language 'en-US'.", "The broadcast service is in language 'es'.", "This text is in language 'fr'."
inPlaylist: A playlist inclusion relation between a music recording and the music playlist it belongs to. Also called part of playlist, on playlist, playlist track. Examples: "A music recording is in a playlist titled 'Workout Mix'.", "The song is in a playlist.", "This recording belongs to a specific playlist.". Distinct from inAlbum, which refers to a music album.
inProductGroupWithID: A product group ID relation between a product and the identifier of the product group it is a variant of. Also called product group ID, variant group ID, group identifier. Examples: "A product is in a product group with ID 'PG123'.", "The variant belongs to a product group with ID.", "This product's group ID is specified."
inStoreReturnsOffered: An in-store returns offering relation for a merchant return policy, indicating whether returns can be made in a physical store. Also called in-store returns available, physical store returns, returns accepted in store. Examples: "A merchant return policy has in-store returns offered.", "The policy indicates if in-store returns are offered.", "This return policy allows in-store returns."
inSupportOf: A support relation between a thesis and the qualification, candidature, degree, or application it supports. Also called supports for, for the purpose of, in aid of. Examples: "A thesis is in support of a PhD degree.", "The research is in support of a qualification.", "This thesis is written in support of an application."
incentiveAmount: An incentive amount relation between a financial incentive and the value that can be redeemed. Also called incentive value, redeemable amount, benefit amount. Examples: "A financial incentive has an incentive amount of $500.", "The incentive offers an incentive amount as a percentage.", "This incentive provides an incentive amount as a loan."
incentiveCompensation: An incentive compensation relation between a job posting and a description of its bonus and commission aspects. Also called bonus structure, commission details, performance pay. Examples: "A job posting has incentive compensation details.", "The job offers incentive compensation based on sales.", "This role includes incentive compensation.". Distinct from incentives, which is a more general description of incentives.
incentiveStatus: An incentive status relation between a financial incentive and its current operational status. Also called status of incentive, incentive condition, program status. Examples: "A financial incentive has an incentive status 'active'.", "The program's incentive status is 'on hold'.", "This incentive has a retired incentive status."
incentiveType: An incentive type relation between a financial incentive and the specific type of incentive offered. Also called type of benefit, incentive category, subsidy type. Examples: "A financial incentive has an incentive type 'tax credit'.", "The program offers an incentive type 'rebate'.", "This incentive is a 'subsidy' incentive type."
incentives: An incentives relation between a job posting and a description of its bonus and commission compensation. Also called job bonuses, compensation package, additional pay. Examples: "A job posting includes incentives for performance.", "The role offers various incentives.", "This job has incentives described in the posting.". Distinct from incentiveCompensation, which is a more specific property for bonus and commission.
incentivizedItem: An incentivized item relation between a financial incentive and the product or service it encourages. Also called target item, promoted product, incentivized service. Examples: "A financial incentive applies to an incentivized item 'solar panels'.", "The rebate is for an incentivized item category.", "This incentive targets a specific incentivized item."
includedComposition: A composition inclusion relation between a music composition and a smaller music composition that is part of it. Also called part of composition, contains composition, movement of. Examples: "A symphony has an included composition as a movement.", "A musical work includes a composition.", "This composition contains several included compositions.". Distinct from hasPart, which is a general part-whole relation for creative works.
includedDataCatalog: A data catalog inclusion relation between a dataset and the data catalog that contains it. Also called part of catalog, contained in catalog, catalog member. Examples: "A dataset is included in a data catalog.", "The data is part of an included data catalog.", "This dataset belongs to a specific included data catalog."
includedInDataCatalog: A data catalog inclusion relation between a dataset and the data catalog that contains it. Also called part of catalog, contained in catalog, catalog member. Examples: "A dataset is included in a data catalog.", "The data is part of an included in data catalog.", "This dataset belongs to a specific included in data catalog."
includedInHealthInsurancePlan: A health insurance plan inclusion relation between a drug and a health insurance plan that covers it. Also called covered by plan, plan coverage, drug coverage. Examples: "A drug is included in a health insurance plan.", "The medication is covered by an included in health insurance plan.", "This drug is part of a specific health insurance plan."
includedRiskFactor: A risk factor inclusion relation between a medical risk estimator and a risk factor used in its calculation. Also called risk factor in calculation, factor considered, included element. Examples: "A medical risk estimator includes a risk factor of age.", "The estimator considers an included risk factor of smoking.", "This tool uses an included risk factor for calculation."
includesAttraction: An attraction inclusion relation between a tourist destination and a tourist attraction located within it. Also called contains attraction, destination attraction, features attraction. Examples: "A tourist destination includes an attraction like a museum.", "The city includes an attraction for historical sites.", "This destination features a famous includes attraction."
includesHealthPlanFormulary: A health plan formulary inclusion relation between a health insurance plan and a formulary it covers. Also called plan formulary, covered formulary, formulary of plan. Examples: "A health insurance plan includes a health plan formulary.", "The plan covers an includes health plan formulary.", "This insurance plan features a specific formulary."
includesHealthPlanNetwork: A health plan network inclusion relation between a health insurance plan and a network it covers. Also called plan network, covered network, network of plan. Examples: "A health insurance plan includes a health plan network.", "The plan covers an includes health plan network.", "This insurance plan features a specific network."
includesObject: A composition relation between an offer or product collection and the specific products and their quantities it contains. Also called composed of, contains, comprises, consists of, has as object. Examples: An offer includesObject a TypeAndQuantityNode for 2 apples. A product collection includesObject a TypeAndQuantityNode for 5 books. A demand includesObject a TypeAndQuantityNode for 1 car.
incomeLimit: A financial constraint relation indicating the maximum income for which a financial incentive is applicable. Also called income cap, income threshold, maximum income, income eligibility. Examples: A tax credit has an incomeLimit of $100,000. A scholarship has an incomeLimit of '150% of poverty line'. A housing subsidy has an incomeLimit of $75,000.
increasesRiskOf: A risk amplification relation between a medical risk factor and the medical entity (condition, complication) whose likelihood it increases. Also called heightens risk of, raises risk of, predisposes to, contributes to risk of. Examples: Smoking increasesRiskOf lung cancer. High blood pressure increasesRiskOf heart attack. Obesity increasesRiskOf type 2 diabetes.
industry: An industry classification relation between a job posting and the sector of economic activity it belongs to. Also called sector, business area, field, domain. Examples: A software engineer job posting has an industry of 'Technology'. A nurse job posting has an industry of 'Healthcare'. A marketing manager job posting has an industry of 'Advertising'.
ineligibleRegion: A geographical exclusion relation between an action access specification, delivery charge specification, demand, media object, or offer, and the region where it is not valid or available. Also called restricted region, excluded region, unavailable in, not valid in. Examples: An offer has an ineligibleRegion of 'Alaska'. A delivery charge specification has an ineligibleRegion of 'Hawaii'. A media object has an ineligibleRegion of 'EU'. Distinct from eligibleRegion, which specifies where something *is* valid or available.
infectiousAgent: A causative agent relation between an infectious disease and the specific microorganism or pathogen that causes it. Also called causative organism, pathogen, disease agent, etiological agent. Examples: Influenza has an infectiousAgent of 'Influenza virus'. Tuberculosis has an infectiousAgent of 'Mycobacterium tuberculosis'. Malaria has an infectiousAgent of 'Plasmodium falciparum'. Distinct from infectiousAgentClass, which specifies the *type* of agent (e.g., bacteria, virus).
infectiousAgentClass: A causative agent classification relation between an infectious disease and the general category of infectious agent responsible for it. Also called agent type, pathogen class, type of infectious agent. Examples: Influenza has an infectiousAgentClass of 'Virus'. Tuberculosis has an infectiousAgentClass of 'Bacteria'. Mad Cow Disease has an infectiousAgentClass of 'Prion'. Distinct from infectiousAgent, which specifies the *specific* agent (e.g., Influenza virus, Mycobacterium tuberculosis).
ingredients: A component relation between a recipe and the individual food items or substances required for its preparation. Also called components, recipe items, constituents, elements. Examples: A cake recipe lists 'flour' as an ingredient. A soup recipe lists 'carrots' as an ingredient. A cocktail recipe lists 'gin' as an ingredient.
inker: A creative role relation between a comic issue, comic story, or visual artwork and the person responsible for inking the pencil drawings. Also called ink artist, inking artist, ink illustrator. Examples: A comic issue has an inker named 'Joe Smith'. A visual artwork lists 'Jane Doe' as its inker. A comic story credits 'Bob Johnson' as the inker.
insertion: An anatomical attachment relation between a muscle and the anatomical structure where it inserts, or the structure it moves. Also called attachment point, insertion point, moves, connects to. Examples: The biceps muscle has an insertion on the 'radius bone'. The deltoid muscle has an insertion on the 'humerus'. The gastrocnemius muscle has an insertion on the 'calcaneus'. Distinct from origin, which is the fixed attachment point of a muscle.
installUrl: A download location relation between a software application and the URL from which it can be installed. Also called download URL, installation link, app download link. Examples: A software application has an installUrl of 'https://example.com/app/download'. A mobile game has an installUrl of 'https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.game'. A desktop utility has an installUrl of 'https://software.org/installer.exe'. Distinct from url, which is the general URL for the item, not specifically for installation.
instructor: An instructional role relation between a course instance and the person who teaches or assists in teaching it. Also called teacher, lecturer, tutor, educator, faculty. Examples: A calculus course instance has 'Dr. Smith' as its instructor. A yoga class has 'Jane Doe' as its instructor. A coding bootcamp lists 'John Johnson' as an instructor.
instrument: A tool or means relation between an action and the object used by an agent to perform that action. Also called tool, means, device, implement, apparatus. Examples: A writing action uses a 'pen' as its instrument. A cooking action uses a 'knife' as its instrument. A painting action uses a 'brush' as its instrument. Distinct from object, which is the primary entity acted upon, not the tool used.
intensity: A physical exertion measure relation between an exercise plan and the degree of force or effort involved in the exercise. Also called exertion level, effort level, vigor, strenuousness. Examples: An exercise plan has an intensity of 'moderate'. A running plan specifies an intensity of '150 bpm'. A weightlifting plan has an intensity of 'high'.
interactingDrug: A drug interaction relation between two drugs, where one affects the action or safety of the other. Also called drug-drug interaction, co-administered drug, reactive drug. Examples: Warfarin has an interactingDrug of 'Aspirin'. Antibiotics have an interactingDrug of 'Oral contraceptives'. Statins have an interactingDrug of 'Grapefruit juice'. Distinct from contraindication, which typically refers to a disease or condition that makes a drug unsuitable.
interactionCount: A deprecated property indicating the number of user interactions with an item. Also called user interactions, engagement count, activity count. Examples: (No active examples for deprecated properties).
interactionService: A platform relation between an interaction counter and the software application or website where the user interactions were recorded. Also called interaction platform, service provider, host application, interaction source. Examples: An interaction counter has an interactionService of 'Facebook'. An interaction counter has an interactionService of 'YouTube'. An interaction counter has an interactionService of 'Twitter'.
interactionStatistic: An interaction metric relation between a creative work, organization, or person, and a counter that quantifies user interactions with it. Also called engagement metrics, user activity, interaction data, usage statistics. Examples: A blog post has an interactionStatistic of a 'LikeAction' counter. An organization has an interactionStatistic of a 'CommentAction' counter. A person has an interactionStatistic of a 'ShareAction' counter.
interactionType: A classification relation between an interaction counter and the specific type of action it represents. Also called type of engagement, action category, interaction kind. Examples: An interaction counter has an interactionType of 'LikeAction'. An interaction counter has an interactionType of 'CommentAction'. An interaction counter has an interactionType of 'ShareAction'.
interactivityType: A learning mode relation between a creative work and the predominant way it supports learning. Also called learning style, engagement mode, pedagogical approach. Examples: A textbook has an interactivityType of 'expositive'. An online quiz has an interactivityType of 'active'. A workshop has an interactivityType of 'mixed'.
interestRate: A financial cost/gain relation between a financial product and the percentage rate of interest charged or paid on it. Also called rate of interest, yield, return rate. Examples: A savings account has an interestRate of '0.5%'. A loan has an interestRate of '4.99%'. A bond has an interestRate of '3.2% fixed'. Distinct from annualPercentageRate, which is the total cost of borrowing over a year, including fees.
interpretedAsClaim: A claim extraction relation between a creative work or media object and a specific assertion or statement derived from its content. Also called contains claim, implies claim, claim extracted from, claim derived from. Examples: A news article is interpretedAsClaim 'The sky is blue'. A scientific paper is interpretedAsClaim 'Drug X cures Y'. A video is interpretedAsClaim 'Candidate Z made promise A'.
inventoryLevel: A stock quantity relation between a demand, offer, or product and its current approximate availability in inventory. Also called stock level, quantity in stock, available quantity, current stock. Examples: An offer has an inventoryLevel of '100 units'. A product has an inventoryLevel of 'low stock'. A demand has an inventoryLevel of '50 units available'.
inverseOf: A property relationship indicating that two properties describe the same association between entities but in opposite directions. Also called reciprocal property, opposite property, reverse property. Examples: The 'alumni' property is an inverseOf 'alumniOf'. The 'parent' property is an inverseOf 'child'. The 'employee' property is an inverseOf 'worksFor'.
isAcceptingNewPatients: A patient status relation indicating whether a medical organization is currently accepting new patients. Also called accepting new patients, open to new patients, taking new patients. Examples: A clinic has isAcceptingNewPatients set to 'true'. A hospital has isAcceptingNewPatients set to 'false'. A doctor's office has isAcceptingNewPatients set to 'true'.
isAccessibleForFree: An access cost relation indicating whether a creative work, event, or place can be accessed without charge. Also called free access, no charge, complimentary access, free of cost. Examples: A public park has isAccessibleForFree set to 'true'. An online article has isAccessibleForFree set to 'true'. A concert has isAccessibleForFree set to 'false'.
isAccessoryOrSparePartFor: A product compatibility relation between a product and the other products for which it serves as an accessory or spare part. Also called accessory for, spare part for, compatible with, used with. Examples: A phone case isAccessoryOrSparePartFor 'iPhone 15'. A replacement battery isAccessoryOrSparePartFor 'Laptop Model X'. A camera lens isAccessoryOrSparePartFor 'DSLR Camera Y'. Distinct from isConsumableFor, which refers to items that are used up.
isAvailableGenerically: A drug availability relation indicating whether a drug is available in a generic formulation. Also called generic form available, generic equivalent, generic option. Examples: A drug has isAvailableGenerically set to 'true'. A brand-name medication has isAvailableGenerically set to 'false'. A common painkiller has isAvailableGenerically set to 'true'. Distinct from isProprietary, which indicates if the *name* is proprietary.
isBasedOn: A derivation relation between a creative work and the resource (another work, product, or URL) from which it is adapted or modified. Also called derived from, adapted from, based on, inspired by, modification of. Examples: A movie isBasedOn 'a novel'. A software update isBasedOn 'previous version'. A remix isBasedOn 'original song'. Distinct from isBasedOnUrl, which specifically points to a URL as the source.
isBasedOnUrl: A source URL relation between a creative work and a specific URL that served as a resource for its creation. Also called source URL, derived from URL, based on URL, reference URL. Examples: A research paper has an isBasedOnUrl of 'https://arxiv.org/abs/1234.5678'. A blog post has an isBasedOnUrl of 'https://example.com/original-article'. A web page has an isBasedOnUrl of 'https://old-version.com/page'. Distinct from isBasedOn, which can refer to any CreativeWork or Product, not just a URL.
isConsumableFor: A product dependency relation between a product and the other products that consume it or require it for operation. Also called consumable for, used by, required by, compatible consumable. Examples: An ink cartridge isConsumableFor 'Printer Model X'. Coffee pods areConsumableFor 'Coffee Machine Y'. Batteries areConsumableFor 'Remote Control Z'. Distinct from isAccessoryOrSparePartFor, which refers to items that are not used up.
isEncodedByBioChemEntity: A genetic encoding relation between a biochemical entity and the gene that encodes it. Also called encoded by, gene source, genetic origin. Examples: A protein isEncodedByBioChemEntity 'Gene A'. An RNA molecule isEncodedByBioChemEntity 'Gene B'. A specific enzyme isEncodedByBioChemEntity 'Gene C'.
isFamilyFriendly: A content suitability relation indicating whether a creative work, offer, or product is appropriate for families. Also called family-safe, suitable for all ages, kid-friendly, appropriate for families. Examples: A movie has isFamilyFriendly set to 'true'. A video game has isFamilyFriendly set to 'false'. A restaurant offer has isFamilyFriendly set to 'true'.
isGift: A transaction intent relation indicating whether an order was placed as a gift for a recipient other than the buyer. Also called gift purchase, purchased as gift, gift order. Examples: An order has isGift set to 'true'. A purchase has isGift set to 'false'. A book order has isGift set to 'true' with gift wrapping.
isInvolvedInBiologicalProcess: A biological function relation between a biochemical entity and the biological process it participates in. Also called participates in process, role in biological process, contributes to process. Examples: A protein is isInvolvedInBiologicalProcess 'cell division'. An enzyme is isInvolvedInBiologicalProcess 'metabolism'. A hormone is isInvolvedInBiologicalProcess 'growth regulation'.
isLiveBroadcast: A broadcast status relation indicating whether a broadcast event is being transmitted in real-time. Also called live stream, real-time broadcast, live transmission. Examples: A sports game broadcast has isLiveBroadcast set to 'true'. A news report broadcast has isLiveBroadcast set to 'true'. A recorded TV show broadcast has isLiveBroadcast set to 'false'.
isLocatedInSubcellularLocation: A subcellular localization relation between a biochemical entity and its specific location within a cell. Also called found in subcellular location, localized to, present in subcellular compartment. Examples: A protein is isLocatedInSubcellularLocation 'cytoplasm'. DNA is isLocatedInSubcellularLocation 'nucleus'. Mitochondrial enzymes are isLocatedInSubcellularLocation 'mitochondrion'.
isPartOf: A part-whole relation indicating that an item or creative work is a component of a larger creative work or resource. Also called component of, member of, contained in, element of. Examples: A chapter isPartOf 'a book'. An episode isPartOf 'a TV series'. A web page isPartOf 'a website'. Distinct from hasPart, which expresses the inverse relationship (the whole *has* a part).
isPartOfBioChemEntity: A biochemical part-whole relation indicating that one biochemical entity is a component of another larger biochemical entity. Also called component of biochem entity, contained within biochem entity, element of biochem entity. Examples: A protein domain isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a larger protein'. A subunit isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a protein complex'. A specific gene sequence isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a chromosome'.
isPlanForApartment: A descriptive relation between a floor plan and the accommodation unit it illustrates. Also called plan for, describes accommodation, layout for. Examples: A floor plan isPlanForApartment 'Apartment 3B'. A floor plan isPlanForApartment 'a studio apartment'. A floor plan isPlanForApartment 'Unit 101'.
isProprietary: A naming status relation indicating whether a dietary supplement or drug is identified by a proprietary or brand name. Also called brand name, proprietary name, trademarked name. Examples: A drug has isProprietary set to 'true' (e.g., Tylenol). A dietary supplement has isProprietary set to 'false' (e.g., Acetaminophen). A medication has isProprietary set to 'true'. Distinct from isAvailableGenerically, which indicates if a generic *form* exists, not if the *name* itself is proprietary.
isRelatedTo: A general association relation between two products or services that have some unspecified connection. Also called associated with, connected to, linked to, relevant to. Examples: A smartphone isRelatedTo 'a smart watch'. A car service isRelatedTo 'car insurance'. A book isRelatedTo 'a movie adaptation'. Distinct from isSimilarTo, which implies functional similarity, and isAccessoryOrSparePartFor or isConsumableFor, which imply specific functional dependencies. This is a very general relation.
isResizable: A model property relation indicating whether a 3D model can be scaled or resized. Also called resizable, scalable, adjustable size. Examples: A 3D model of a chair has isResizable set to 'true'. A 3D model of a building has isResizable set to 'false'. A 3D model of a character has isResizable set to 'true'.
isSimilarTo: A functional resemblance relation between two products or services that share similar characteristics or purposes. Also called similar to, comparable to, analogous to, like. Examples: Product A isSimilarTo 'Product B' (a competitor's product). Service X isSimilarTo 'Service Y' (an alternative service). A specific brand of coffee isSimilarTo 'another brand of coffee'. Distinct from isRelatedTo, which is a more general association without implying functional similarity.
isStoreOn: A platform hosting relation between an online store and the e-commerce marketplace where it operates. Also called hosted on, operates on, platform for, marketplace for. Examples: An online store isStoreOn 'Amazon'. A small business's online store isStoreOn 'Etsy'. A vendor's shop isStoreOn 'eBay'.
isTierOf: A membership hierarchy relation between a member program tier and the larger member program it belongs to. Also called tier within, part of program, level of program. Examples: A 'Gold' tier isTierOf 'Loyalty Program X'. A 'Premium' tier isTierOf 'Subscription Service Y'. A 'Bronze' tier isTierOf 'Rewards Program Z'.
isUnlabelledFallback: A default setting relation indicating whether delivery time or shipping rate settings serve as a general fallback for unlabelled shipping details. Also called default settings, fallback rule, general application, unlabelled default. Examples: DeliveryTimeSettings has isUnlabelledFallback set to 'true'. ShippingRateSettings has isUnlabelledFallback set to 'true'. These settings are isUnlabelledFallback for all products.
isVariantOf: A product variation relation between a product or product model and the base product or product group from which it is a specific variant. Also called variant of, version of, derived from product, specific model of. Examples: A 'red iPhone 15' isVariantOf 'iPhone 15 Pro'. A 'size L t-shirt' isVariantOf 'Basic T-Shirt ProductGroup'. A 'diesel car model' isVariantOf 'Car Model X'. Distinct from isRelatedTo or isSimilarTo, as it implies a direct hierarchical relationship of variation from a base product or group.
isbn: A book identification relation between a book and its International Standard Book Number. Also called book identifier, ISBN number, publication code. Examples: A book has an isbn of '978-0321765723'. A novel has an isbn of '978-1234567890'. A textbook has an isbn of '0-13-110362-8'.
isicV4: An industry classification relation between an organization, person, or place and its International Standard Industrial Classification of All Economic Activities (ISIC) Revision 4 code. Also called ISIC code, industry classification code, economic activity code. Examples: An organization has an isicV4 of '6201' (Computer programming activities). A person has an isicV4 of '8620' (Medical and dental practice activities). A place has an isicV4 of '5510' (Hotels and similar accommodation).
iso6523Code: An organization identification relation between an organization and its globally standardized ISO 6523 code. Also called ISO 6523 identifier, organization code, international organization ID. Examples: An organization has an iso6523Code of '0060:802000000'. A company has an iso6523Code of '0199:LEI1234567890'. A business has an iso6523Code of '0088:1234567890123'. Distinct from leiCode, duns, globalLocationNumber, vatID, or taxID, as this is a more general, structured international identifier that can encompass those.
isrcCode: A music recording identification relation between a music recording and its International Standard Recording Code. Also called ISRC identifier, recording code, music track ID. Examples: A music recording has an isrcCode of 'US-S1Z-99-00001'. A song has an isrcCode of 'GB-LFB-04-00001'. An album track has an isrcCode of 'QZ-F89-12-00001'. Distinct from iswcCode, which is for musical compositions, not recordings.
issn: A serial publication identification relation between a blog, creative work series, dataset, or website and its International Standard Serial Number. Also called serial identifier, ISSN number, publication code. Examples: A journal has an issn of '1234-5678'. A magazine series has an issn of '9876-5432'. An online blog has an issn of '2345-6789'. Distinct from isbn, which is for books.
issueNumber: A publication identifier relation between a publication issue and its specific identifying number or designation within a series. Also called issue ID, volume number, edition number, publication identifier. Examples: A journal issue has an issueNumber of '5'. A comic book has an issueNumber of 'Vol. 2, Issue #3'. A magazine has an issueNumber of 'Summer 2023'. Distinct from volumeNumber, which is for the larger volume a publication issue belongs to.
issuedBy: An issuing authority relation between a certification, permit, or ticket and the organization that granted or provided it. Also called granted by, provided by, authorized by, issuer. Examples: A driver's license is issuedBy 'Department of Motor Vehicles'. A concert ticket is issuedBy 'Ticketmaster'. A professional certification is issuedBy 'Certification Body X'.
issuedThrough: A service channel relation between a permit and the specific service used to obtain it. Also called obtained via, granted through, service channel. Examples: A building permit was issuedThrough 'Online Permit Application System'. A fishing license was issuedThrough 'State Wildlife Service'. A visa was issuedThrough 'Consular Services Department'. Distinct from issuedBy, which is the organization, not the service.
iswcCode: A music composition identification relation between a music composition and its International Standard Musical Work Code. Also called ISWC identifier, composition code, musical work ID. Examples: A music composition has an iswcCode of 'T-034.045.001-6'. A song has an iswcCode of 'T-901.234.567-8'. A classical piece has an iswcCode of 'T-123.456.789-0'. Distinct from isrcCode, which is for music recordings, not compositions.
item: A list element relation between a data feed item or list item and the entity it represents within a collection. Also called represents, refers to, entry, element. Examples: A list item has an item of 'John Doe'. A data feed item has an item of 'Product X'. A list entry has an item of 'Event Y'.
itemCondition: A product state relation indicating the physical condition of a product or service, or the condition required for returns. Also called product state, condition of item, quality status, return condition. Examples: An offer has an itemCondition of 'NewCondition'. A product has an itemCondition of 'UsedCondition'. A return policy specifies itemCondition 'SellerRefurbished'.
itemDefectReturnFees: A return cost relation between a merchant return policy and the type of fees associated with returning defective products. Also called defect return fees, faulty item return cost, return fees for defects. Examples: A return policy has itemDefectReturnFees of 'FreeReturn'. A return policy has itemDefectReturnFees of 'RestockingFee'. A return policy has itemDefectReturnFees of 'ReturnShippingFees'. Distinct from itemDefectReturnShippingFeesAmount, which specifies the *amount* of shipping fees, not the *type* of fees.
itemDefectReturnLabelSource: A return label provision relation between a merchant return policy and the method by which a customer obtains a shipping label for defective product returns. Also called defect return label method, faulty item return label source, return label for defects. Examples: A return policy has itemDefectReturnLabelSource of 'InStore'. A return policy has itemDefectReturnLabelSource of 'PrintAtHome'. A return policy has itemDefectReturnLabelSource of 'DownloadAndPrint'.
itemDefectReturnShippingFeesAmount: A return shipping cost relation between a merchant return policy and the monetary amount of shipping fees for defective product returns. Also called defect return shipping cost, faulty item return shipping fees, shipping cost for defects. Examples: A return policy has itemDefectReturnShippingFeesAmount of '$5.00'. A return policy has itemDefectReturnShippingFeesAmount of '$0.00'. A return policy has itemDefectReturnShippingFeesAmount of '$10.50'. Distinct from itemDefectReturnFees, which specifies the *type* of fees, not the specific monetary amount of shipping fees.
itemListElement: A list composition relation between an item list and its individual elements, which can be simple text, existing entities, or list items with additional context. Also called list components, list entries, elements of list, items in list. Examples: An item list has itemListElement 'First Item'. An item list has itemListElement 'Product A'. An item list has itemListElement a ListItem for 'Task 1'. Distinct from item, which refers to the entity *within* a ListItem, not the ListItem itself or a direct string/entity in the list.
itemListOrder: A list arrangement relation between an item list and the specified order of its elements. Also called list sorting, order of items, list sequence, arrangement type. Examples: An item list has itemListOrder 'Ascending'. An item list has itemListOrder 'Descending'. An item list has itemListOrder 'Unordered'.
itemLocation: A physical location relation between an archive component and its current place, postal address, or textual description of location. Also called current location, item whereabouts, storage location, physical location. Examples: An archive component has an itemLocation of 'Shelf 3, Box 12'. An archive component has an itemLocation of 'Library Basement'. An archive component has an itemLocation of '123 Main St, Anytown'.
itemOffered: A transaction subject relation between a demand or offer and the specific item, product, service, or event being requested or provided. Also called offered item, demanded item, subject of offer, product/service offered. Examples: An offer has an itemOffered of 'a new car'. A demand has an itemOffered of 'web design service'. An offer has an itemOffered of 'a concert ticket'. Distinct from itemReviewed, which is the subject of a review, not an offer/demand.
itemReviewed: A review subject relation between an aggregate rating or review and the entity that is being evaluated or rated. Also called reviewed item, rated item, subject of review, evaluated entity. Examples: A review has an itemReviewed of 'Restaurant X'. An aggregate rating has an itemReviewed of 'Movie Y'. A product review has an itemReviewed of 'Smartphone Z'. Distinct from itemOffered, which is the subject of an offer or demand.
itemShipped: A shipment content relation between a parcel delivery and the product(s) being transported. Also called shipped product, contents of shipment, parcel contents, delivered item. Examples: A parcel delivery has an itemShipped of 'a book'. A parcel delivery has an itemShipped of 'clothing items'. A parcel delivery has an itemShipped of 'electronic device'.
itinerary: A travel plan relation between a trip and the sequence of places or an item list detailing the destinations. Also called travel route, trip plan, destinations, journey path. Examples: A trip has an itinerary of 'Paris, Rome, London'. A trip has an itinerary of an ItemList detailing stops. A vacation package has an itinerary of 'Hawaii'.
iupacName: A chemical nomenclature relation between a molecular entity and its systematic name according to IUPAC recommendations. Also called IUPAC name, systematic chemical name, chemical nomenclature. Examples: A molecular entity has an iupacName of 'sulfuric acid'. A compound has an iupacName of 'ethanol'. A chemical has an iupacName of 'sodium chloride'. Distinct from name, which is a common or trivial name.
jobBenefits: An employment perk relation between a job posting and the description of advantages or entitlements offered with the position.
