Also called employee benefits, job perks, compensation package, employment advantages. Examples: A job posting lists jobBenefits as 'Health insurance, 401k, paid time off'. A job posting includes jobBenefits like 'flexible hours and remote work option'. A job posting details jobBenefits such as 'gym membership and free meals'. Distinct from salaryCurrency or baseSalary, which are about monetary compensation.
jobDuration: An employment term relation between a job posting and the expected length of the employment period. Also called employment length, contract duration, job term, period of employment. Examples: A job posting has a jobDuration of '6 months'. A job posting has a jobDuration of '1 year contract'. A job posting has a jobDuration of 'seasonal'.
jobImmediateStart: An employment timing relation indicating whether a job position is available for an immediate start. Also called immediate start, urgent hire, start now, ready to begin. Examples: A job posting has jobImmediateStart set to 'true'. A job posting has jobImmediateStart set to 'false'. This position has jobImmediateStart as 'true' for qualified candidates. Distinct from jobStartDate, which specifies a particular date.
jobLocation: An employment location relation between a job posting and the primary geographic place where the work is performed. Also called work location, employment site, job site, place of work. Examples: A job posting has a jobLocation of 'New York City'. A job posting has a jobLocation of 'San Francisco Bay Area'. A job posting has a jobLocation of 'Remote'. Distinct from jobLocationType, which describes the *type* of location (e.g., 'TELECOMMUTE').
jobLocationType: An employment location type relation between a job posting and a textual description of its work arrangement, such as telecommuting. Also called work arrangement, location type, remote work status. Examples: A job posting has a jobLocationType of 'TELECOMMUTE'. A job posting has a jobLocationType of 'Hybrid'. A job posting has a jobLocationType of 'On-site'. Distinct from jobLocation, which specifies the actual geographic place.
jobStartDate: An employment start date relation between a job posting and the anticipated date for a successful applicant to begin work. Also called start date, commencement date, employment beginning. Examples: A job posting has a jobStartDate of '2024-09-01'. A job posting has a jobStartDate of 'Fall 2024'. A job posting has a jobStartDate of 'as soon as possible'. Distinct from jobImmediateStart, which is a boolean flag for immediate availability.
jobTitle: An occupational role relation between a person and their formal designation within an organization. Also called position, role, occupation, professional title. Examples: A person has a jobTitle of 'Software Engineer'. A person has a jobTitle of 'Chief Executive Officer'. A person has a jobTitle of 'Marketing Manager'.
jurisdiction: A legal scope relation between a government service or legislation and the administrative area or territory where it applies. Also called legal authority, governing area, applicable region, domain of law. Examples: A government service has a jurisdiction of 'California'. Legislation has a jurisdiction of 'United States federal law'. A permit applies to the jurisdiction of 'City of London'. Distinct from eligibleRegion or ineligibleRegion, which are about availability, not legal authority.
keywords: A descriptive tagging relation between an item (creative work, event, organization, place, product) and the terms or phrases used to categorize or describe it. Also called tags, descriptors, categories, labels, search terms. Examples: A blog post has keywords 'AI, machine learning, future tech'. An event has keywords 'music festival, summer, outdoor'. A product has keywords 'eco-friendly, sustainable, organic'. Distinct from about, which describes the primary topic, not just descriptive tags.
knownVehicleDamages: A vehicle condition relation between a vehicle and a textual description of its known damages, whether repaired or not. Also called vehicle damage report, damage history, known defects, condition notes. Examples: A used car has knownVehicleDamages 'minor dent on rear bumper'. A vehicle has knownVehicleDamages 'repaired fender bender'. A truck has knownVehicleDamages 'scratches on passenger side door'. Distinct from vehicleCondition, which is a general assessment, not specific damages.
knows: A general acquaintance relation between two people who are known to each other socially or professionally. Also called acquainted with, familiar with, knows personally, has met. Examples: John knows 'Jane'. Sarah knows 'her colleague Tom'. The CEO knows 'the board members'. Distinct from follows, friend, or memberOf, which imply more specific types of relationships.
knowsAbout: A knowledge domain relation between an organization or person and a topic or entity they possess knowledge about. Also called knowledgeable about, familiar with topic, understands, has expertise in (without implying skill level). Examples: A person knowsAbout 'artificial intelligence'. An organization knowsAbout 'renewable energy policy'. A researcher knowsAbout 'quantum physics'. Distinct from hasOccupation or alumniOf, which are about formal roles or education, not general knowledge.
knowsLanguage: A language proficiency relation between an organization or person and a language they are able to communicate in. Also called speaks language, fluent in, understands language, conversant in. Examples: A person knowsLanguage 'English'. An organization knowsLanguage 'Spanish'. A diplomat knowsLanguage 'French' (fr).
labelDetails: A drug information relation between a drug and the URL providing access to its detailed label information. Also called drug label link, prescribing information, medication details URL. Examples: A drug has labelDetails 'https://www.fda.gov/drug/label/drugX'. A medication has labelDetails 'https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=12345'. A pharmaceutical product has labelDetails 'https://example.com/drug-info/label.pdf'. Distinct from url, which is a general URL for the drug, not specifically its label details.
landlord: A property ownership relation between a rent action and the person or organization that owns and leases the real estate. Also called property owner, lessor, rental owner, proprietor. Examples: A rent action has a landlord of 'John Doe'. A rent action has a landlord of 'Property Management Inc.'. A lease agreement lists 'Sarah Smith' as the landlord. Distinct from agent, which is the general actor of an action.
language: A communication medium relation between a communicate action or write action and the language employed in that action. Also called language used, medium of communication, spoken in, written in. Examples: A communicate action uses the language 'English'. A write action uses the language 'French'. A conversation has the language 'Spanish'. Distinct from inLanguage, which is for the language of a creative work itself, not the action of communicating/writing.
lastReviewed: A content review relation between a web page and the date its content was last checked for accuracy or completeness. Also called last updated, review date, content last checked, revision date. Examples: A web page has a lastReviewed date of '2023-10-26'. An article has a lastReviewed date of '2024-01-15'. A product page has a lastReviewed date of 'yesterday'. Distinct from dateModified or datePublished, which refer to content modification or initial publication, not specifically a review.
latitude: A geographical coordinate relation between geo-coordinates or a place and its north-south position on the Earth's surface. Also called lat, north-south coordinate, parallel. Examples: GeoCoordinates have a latitude of '34.0522'. A place has a latitude of '-33.8688'. The city's latitude is '40.7128'. Distinct from longitude, which is the east-west position.
layoutImage: A visual representation relation between a floor plan and an image depicting its layout. Also called floorplan image, layout diagram, schematic image, visual layout. Examples: A floor plan has a layoutImage of 'floorplan.jpg'. A floor plan has a layoutImage of 'https://example.com/layout.png'. The apartment's floor plan includes a layoutImage. Distinct from image, which is a general image of the item, not specifically the layout.
learningResourceType: A learning resource classification relation between a creative work or learning resource and its predominant type or format. Also called resource format, learning material type, educational resource kind. Examples: A learning resource has a learningResourceType of 'presentation'. A creative work has a learningResourceType of 'handout'. An online course module has a learningResourceType of 'interactive simulation'. Distinct from resourceType, which is a more general property for any resource.
leaseLength: A rental term relation between an accommodation, offer, or real estate listing and the duration of its lease agreement. Also called lease duration, rental period, term of lease, tenancy length. Examples: An accommodation has a leaseLength of '12 months'. An offer specifies a leaseLength of '2 years'. A real estate listing has a leaseLength of '6-month minimum'. Distinct from duration, which is a general duration for any event or item.
legalAddress: An official location relation between an organization and its legally registered postal address for administrative and tax purposes. Also called registered address, official address, corporate address, statutory address. Examples: An organization has a legalAddress of '100 Main St, Anytown, USA'. A company's legalAddress is 'Suite 200, Business Park, City'. The corporation's legalAddress is its registered office. Distinct from address, which is a general contact address, and branchOf, which is about organizational hierarchy.
legalName: An official identification relation between an organization and its formally registered name. Also called registered name, official company name, corporate name, full legal name. Examples: An organization has a legalName of 'Acme Corporation Inc.'. A company's legalName is 'Global Solutions LLC'. The charity's legalName is 'Helping Hands Foundation'. Distinct from name, which is the common or display name.
legalRepresentative: A legal representation relation between an organization and the person(s) authorized to act on its behalf in legal matters. Also called authorized representative, legal agent, official representative, corporate officer. Examples: An organization has a legalRepresentative of 'its CEO'. A company's legalRepresentative is 'its sole administrator'. The board appointed 'Jane Doe' as legalRepresentative. Distinct from employee, which is a general employment relation, not specifically legal representation.
legalStatus: A regulatory status relation between a dietary supplement, drug, or medical entity and its legal classification, including controlled substance schedules. Also called regulatory status, legal classification, controlled substance status, drug schedule. Examples: A drug has a legalStatus of 'PrescriptionOnly'. A dietary supplement has a legalStatus of 'OverTheCounter'. A medication has a legalStatus of 'Schedule II controlled substance'. Distinct from drugClass, which is a medical classification, not a legal one.
legislationAmends: A legislative modification relation between a piece of legislation and another legislation that it alters or revises. Also called amends law, modifies legislation, revises act, changes statute. Examples: Legislation A legislationAmends 'Legislation B'. The new act legislationAmends 'the previous statute'. This bill legislationAmends 'the tax code'. Distinct from legislationChanges, which is a broader term for any change, whereas legislationAmends specifically introduces legal changes.
legislationApplies: An informative legislative transfer relation indicating that a piece of legislation incorporates or references another legislation within a different legal context, without legal binding. Also called incorporates legislation, references law, applies provisions of, draws from legislation. Examples: A national law legislationApplies 'a European Directive'. A local ordinance legislationApplies 'state regulations'. This consolidated law legislationApplies 'the original act'. Distinct from legislationTransposes, which implies a legally binding transposition.
legislationChanges: A legislative alteration relation between a piece of legislation and another legislation that it modifies, replaces, corrects, or repeals. Also called alters law, modifies statute, replaces act, repeals legislation. Examples: Legislation X legislationChanges 'Legislation Y'. The new regulation legislationChanges 'several existing laws'. This amendment legislationChanges 'the previous version of the act'. Distinct from legislationAmends, which is a specific type of change (introducing legal changes), and legislationConsolidates, which is about creating a consolidated version.
legislationCommences: A legislative activation relation between a piece of legislation and another legislation that it brings into legal effect. Also called brings into force, enacts, activates law, sets into effect. Examples: Legislation A legislationCommences 'Legislation B'. The enabling act legislationCommences 'the new regulations'. This decree legislationCommences 'the policy changes'.
legislationConsolidates: A legislative consolidation relation between a consolidated legislation and the original or amending legislations that were integrated into it. Also called integrates legislation, combines laws, incorporates acts, merges statutes. Examples: Consolidated Law X legislationConsolidates 'Original Act Y'. The revised statute legislationConsolidates 'Amendment Z'. This consolidated version legislationConsolidates 'several previous laws'. Distinct from legislationChanges, which describes the act of changing, not the resulting consolidated text.
legislationCorrects: A textual correction relation between two pieces of legislation, where one introduces non-legal changes to the other. Also called: corrects text, amends textually, revises without legal impact. Examples: "Act A legislationCorrects Act B", "Regulation X legislationCorrects Directive Y", "Law 123 legislationCorrects Statute 456". Distinct from legislationAmends, which introduces modifications with legal impact.
legislationCountersignedBy: A countersignature relation between a piece of legislation and the person or organization that countersigned it. Also called: countersigned by, officially endorsed by, co-signed by. Examples: "The Bill of Rights legislationCountersignedBy President Washington", "EU Directive 2023/45 legislationCountersignedBy European Commission", "Local Ordinance legislationCountersignedBy City Clerk".
legislationDate: A date relation between a piece of legislation and its official adoption or signature date. Also called: date of adoption, signature date, enactment date. Examples: "The Civil Rights Act legislationDate 1964-07-02", "GDPR legislationDate 2016-04-27", "Local Bylaw legislationDate 2023-01-15".
legislationDateOfApplicability: An applicability date relation between a piece of legislation and the date it becomes applicable. Also called: date of application, effective date, date becomes active. Examples: "New Tax Law legislationDateOfApplicability 2024-01-01", "Environmental Regulation legislationDateOfApplicability 2023-07-01", "Consumer Protection Act legislationDateOfApplicability 2025-03-10". Distinct from legislationDate, which is the date of adoption or signature.
legislationDateVersion: A version date relation between a piece of legislation and the point-in-time at which its description is valid. Also called: version date, snapshot date, as-of date. Examples: "National Insurance Contributions Act 2015 legislationDateVersion 2016-04-07", "Consolidated Statute legislationDateVersion 2023-01-01", "EU Treaty legislationDateVersion 2022-11-15".
legislationEnsuresImplementationOf: An implementation assurance relation between two pieces of legislation, where one ensures the implementation of the other by modifying national laws. Also called: implements, ensures compliance with, enforces. Examples: "National Law A legislationEnsuresImplementationOf EU Regulation B", "State Statute legislationEnsuresImplementationOf Federal Act", "Local Ordinance legislationEnsuresImplementationOf Regional Directive". Distinct from legislationTransposes, which specifically refers to fulfilling objectives by passing implementation measures.
legislationIdentifier: An identifier relation between a piece of legislation and its unique string or URL-based identifier. Also called: legal identifier, official ID, legislative code. Examples: "EU Regulation 2016/679 legislationIdentifier CELEX:32016R0679", "French Law legislationIdentifier NOR:XXXXXX", "UK Act legislationIdentifier URN-Lex:XXXX".
legislationJurisdiction: A jurisdiction relation between a piece of legislation and the administrative area from which it originates. Also called: originating jurisdiction, legal territory, governing region. Examples: "Federal Law legislationJurisdiction United States", "State Statute legislationJurisdiction California", "EU Directive legislationJurisdiction European Union".
legislationLegalForce: A legal force status relation between a piece of legislation and its current state of being in force. Also called: force status, legal validity, in effect status. Examples: "New Act legislationLegalForce InForce", "Old Regulation legislationLegalForce NotInForce", "Partial Amendment legislationLegalForce PartiallyInForce".
legislationLegalValue: A legal value relation between a legislation file and its level of legal authority. Also called: legal authority, official value, legal weight. Examples: "Digitally Signed PDF legislationLegalValue StrongerLegalValue", "HTML Version legislationLegalValue WeakerLegalValue", "Certified Copy legislationLegalValue HighLegalValue".
legislationPassedBy: A passing authority relation between a piece of legislation and the organization or person that originally enacted it. Also called: enacted by, made by, legislated by. Examples: "Primary Legislation legislationPassedBy Parliament", "Secondary Legislation legislationPassedBy Government", "Local Bylaw legislationPassedBy City Council". Distinct from legislationResponsible, which refers to the ministry or individual in charge of elaborating or addressing questions about the legislation.
legislationRepeals: A repeal relation between two pieces of legislation, where one cancels or abrogates the other. Also called: cancels, abrogates, revokes. Examples: "New Act legislationRepeals Old Act", "Regulation X legislationRepeals Directive Y", "Law 123 legislationRepeals Statute 456".
legislationResponsible: A responsibility relation between a piece of legislation and the individual or organization accountable for its elaboration or inquiries. Also called: responsible for, overseen by, managed by. Examples: "Health Act legislationResponsible Ministry of Health", "Environmental Law legislationResponsible EPA", "Tax Reform legislationResponsible Treasury Department". Distinct from legislationPassedBy, which refers to the original enacting authority.
legislationTransposes: A transposition relation between two pieces of legislation, where one fulfills the objectives of the other through implementation measures. Also called: transposes, implements directive, fulfills objectives of. Examples: "Member State Law legislationTransposes EU Directive", "Regional Act legislationTransposes National Regulation", "Local Ordinance legislationTransposes State Mandate". Distinct from legislationEnsuresImplementationOf, which implies modifying national legislations to avoid contradiction, rather than fulfilling objectives.
legislationType: A type relation between a piece of legislation and its classification (e.g., law, act, directive). Also called: legislative type, legal category, form of law. Examples: "GDPR legislationType regulation", "Civil Rights Act legislationType law", "EU Directive legislationType directive".
leiCode: A Legal Entity Identifier (LEI) code relation between an organization and its unique identifier as defined in ISO 17442. Also called: LEI, legal entity ID, ISO 17442 identifier. Examples: "Acme Corp leiCode 549300XXXXXX", "Global Bank leiCode 213800XXXXXX", "Tech Solutions Inc leiCode 894500XXXXXX".
lender: A lending participant relation between a borrow action and the person or organization providing the object being borrowed. Also called: loan provider, creditor, financing entity. Examples: "BorrowAction lender Bank of America", "BorrowAction lender John Doe", "BorrowAction lender Library".
lesser: A lesser ordering relation between two qualitative values, indicating that the subject value is smaller than the object value. Also called: is less than, is smaller than, falls below. Examples: "Low lesser Medium", "Small lesser Large", "Cold lesser Warm". Distinct from lesserOrEqual, which includes equality.
lesserOrEqual: A lesser or equal ordering relation between two qualitative values, indicating that the subject value is smaller than or equal to the object value. Also called: is less than or equal to, is at most, does not exceed. Examples: "Low lesserOrEqual Medium", "Small lesserOrEqual Small", "Cold lesserOrEqual Cold". Distinct from lesser, which strictly indicates a smaller value.
letterer: A lettering contribution relation between a comic issue, comic story, or visual artwork and the person who adds lettering. Also called: provides lettering, adds text, responsible for speech balloons. Examples: "Comic Issue #1 letterer John Workman", "Graphic Novel letterer Todd Klein", "Manga Chapter letterer Studio Art".
license: A licensing relation between a creative work and the license document that applies to its content. Also called: governed by license, licensed under, copyright license. Examples: "Software Project license MIT License", "Image license Creative Commons Attribution 4.0", "Music Track license Public Domain".
lifeEvent: A life event relation between a person and a significant event in their life. Also called: significant event, personal milestone, biographical event. Examples: "John Doe lifeEvent Baptism", "Jane Smith lifeEvent Graduation Ceremony", "Family lifeEvent Wedding".
line: A line representation relation between a geographic shape and its textual description as a series of points. Also called: path coordinates, point series, geographic line. Examples: "Road Segment line '34.05,-118.25 34.06,-118.26'", "River Path line '40.71,-74.00 40.72,-74.01'", "Borderline line '50.00,0.00 51.00,1.00'".
linkRelationship: A link relationship type relation between a link role and its descriptive text. Also called: hyperlink relation, link type, relationship attribute. Examples: "LinkRole linkRelationship 'nofollow'", "LinkRole linkRelationship 'alternate'", "LinkRole linkRelationship 'canonical'".
liveBlogUpdate: An update relation between a live blog posting and a specific blog posting that serves as an update. Also called: blog update, live update, news update. Examples: "Election Live Blog liveBlogUpdate 'Candidate X wins state Y'", "Sports Match Live Blog liveBlogUpdate 'Goal scored by Team A'", "Breaking News Live Blog liveBlogUpdate 'Emergency services on scene'".
loanMortgageMandateAmount: A mortgage mandate amount relation between a mortgage loan and the monetary amount that can be converted into a mortgage. Also called: mortgage potential, convertible mortgage amount, mandate value. Examples: "Home Loan loanMortgageMandateAmount $200,000", "Property Mortgage loanMortgageMandateAmount €150,000", "Commercial Loan loanMortgageMandateAmount £500,000".
loanPaymentAmount: A payment amount relation between a repayment specification and the monetary amount of a single payment. Also called: single payment amount, installment amount, payment value. Examples: "Monthly Repayment loanPaymentAmount $1,500", "Quarterly Installment loanPaymentAmount €750", "Final Payment loanPaymentAmount £10,000".
loanPaymentFrequency: A payment frequency relation between a repayment specification and the number of months between payments. Also called: payment interval, repayment frequency, billing cycle. Examples: "Monthly Repayment loanPaymentFrequency 1", "Quarterly Installment loanPaymentFrequency 3", "Annual Payment loanPaymentFrequency 12".
loanRepaymentForm: A repayment form relation between a loan or credit and its specification for paying back borrowed money. Also called: repayment method, loan repayment structure, payment plan. Examples: "Student Loan loanRepaymentForm Income-Driven Repayment", "Mortgage loanRepaymentForm Amortized Payments", "Credit Card loanRepaymentForm Minimum Payment".
loanTerm: A loan duration relation between a loan or credit and the quantitative value representing its agreement term. Also called: loan duration, credit term, repayment period. Examples: "Car Loan loanTerm '60 months'", "Mortgage loanTerm '30 years'", "Personal Loan loanTerm '5 years'".
loanType: A loan type relation between a loan or credit and its specific category. Also called: credit type, loan category, financing type. Examples: "Home Loan loanType 'Mortgage'", "Student Loan loanType 'Federal Student Loan'", "Business Loan loanType 'SBA Loan'".
location: A location relation between an action, event, interaction counter, or organization and its physical or virtual place. Also called: situated at, takes place at, found at. Examples: "Conference Event location New York Hilton", "Company Organization location 123 Main St", "Online Meeting location Virtual Conference Room".
locationCreated: A creation location relation between a creative work and the place where it was created. Also called: place of creation, origin location, created in. Examples: "Painting locationCreated Paris", "Novel locationCreated London", "Film locationCreated Hollywood". Distinct from location, which refers to the current or general location of an entity.
lodgingUnitDescription: A unit description relation between a lodging reservation and a full textual description of the lodging unit. Also called: room description, accommodation details, unit features. Examples: "Hotel Reservation lodgingUnitDescription 'King-size bed, ocean view, balcony'", "Apartment Rental lodgingUnitDescription 'Two bedrooms, fully equipped kitchen, city view'", "Cabin Booking lodgingUnitDescription 'Rustic cabin, fireplace, lake access'".
lodgingUnitType: A unit type relation between a lodging reservation and the textual or qualitative description of the unit. Also called: room type, accommodation category, unit classification. Examples: "Hotel Reservation lodgingUnitType 'Suite'", "Motel Booking lodgingUnitType 'Double Room'", "Resort Reservation lodgingUnitType 'Villa'".
logo: A logo relation between a brand, certification, organization, place, product, or service and its associated image or URL. Also called: brand logo, official emblem, corporate identity. Examples: "Apple Inc. logo Apple Logo Image", "Nike Product logo Nike Swoosh", "Olympic Games logo Olympic Rings".
longitude: A longitude relation between geographic coordinates or a place and its longitudinal value. Also called: geographic longitude, east-west coordinate, meridian position. Examples: "Eiffel Tower longitude 2.2945", "Statue of Liberty longitude -74.0445", "Mount Everest longitude 86.9250".
loser: A losing participant relation between a win action and the person who lost. Also called: defeated participant, vanquished, runner-up. Examples: "Chess Match WinAction loser Opponent B", "Race WinAction loser Second Place Runner", "Debate WinAction loser Team B".
lowPrice: A lowest price relation between an aggregate offer and the lowest price among all available offers. Also called: minimum price, cheapest price, starting price. Examples: "Product Bundle lowPrice 9.99", "Flight Deals lowPrice 150.00", "Software License lowPrice 49.99". Distinct from minPrice, which is the lowest price in a range for a single price specification.
lyricist: A lyricist relation between a music composition and the person who wrote its words. Also called: songwriter, words by, author of lyrics. Examples: "Bohemian Rhapsody lyricist Freddie Mercury", "Yesterday lyricist Paul McCartney", "Hallelujah lyricist Leonard Cohen".
lyrics: A lyrics relation between a music composition and the creative work containing its words. Also called: song words, text of song, musical text. Examples: "Bohemian Rhapsody lyrics 'Is this the real life? Is this just fantasy?'", "Yesterday lyrics 'Yesterday, all my troubles seemed so far away'", "Hallelujah lyrics 'I've heard there was a secret chord'".
mainContentOfPage: A main content relation between a web page and the web page element that constitutes its primary subject. Also called: primary content, central element, core content. Examples: "Article Page mainContentOfPage ArticleBody", "Product Page mainContentOfPage ProductDescription", "Blog Post mainContentOfPage PostContent".
mainEntity: A main entity relation between a creative work and the primary entity it describes. Also called: primary subject, about entity, central topic. Examples: "Wikipedia Article mainEntity Albert Einstein", "News Report mainEntity The Election", "Research Paper mainEntity Quantum Physics". Distinct from mainEntityOfPage, which indicates the page for which this thing is the main entity.
mainEntityOfPage: A main entity of page relation between a thing and the creative work or URL for which it is the primary described entity. Also called: primary page, described on page, featured on page. Examples: "Albert Einstein mainEntityOfPage Wikipedia Article", "The Election mainEntityOfPage News Report", "Quantum Physics mainEntityOfPage Research Paper". Distinct from mainEntity, which indicates the primary entity described in a creative work.
maintainer: A maintainer relation between a creative work and the person or organization that manages its contributions and/or publication. Also called: project manager, curator, responsible party. Examples: "Software Package maintainer John Doe", "Dataset maintainer Open Data Initiative", "Website maintainer Webmaster Team".
makesOffer: An offering relation between an organization or person and the offer for products or services they provide. Also called: offers, provides, sells. Examples: "Retailer makesOffer Discounted Electronics", "Consultant makesOffer Business Strategy Services", "Restaurant makesOffer Dinner Menu".
manufacturer: A manufacturing relation between a product and the organization that produced it. Also called: produced by, made by, fabricated by. Examples: "Smartphone manufacturer Apple", "Automobile manufacturer Toyota", "Furniture manufacturer IKEA".
map: A map URL relation between a place and a URL pointing to its map. Also called: map link, geographic map, location map. Examples: "Central Park map Google Maps URL", "Eiffel Tower map OpenStreetMap URL", "Local Restaurant map Yelp Map URL". Distinct from maps, which is a plural form and essentially the same concept.
mapType: A map type relation between a map and its category from the MapCategoryType enumeration. Also called: map category, type of map, map classification. Examples: "Road Map mapType 'RoadMap'", "Satellite Image mapType 'SatelliteMap'", "Terrain Map mapType 'TerrainMap'".
maps: A map URL relation between a place and a URL pointing to its map. Also called: map link, geographic map, location map. Examples: "Central Park maps Google Maps URL", "Eiffel Tower maps OpenStreetMap URL", "Local Restaurant maps Yelp Map URL". Distinct from map, which is a singular form and essentially the same concept.
marginOfError: A margin of error relation between an observation and its quantitative value representing the error range. Also called: error margin, uncertainty range, confidence interval. Examples: "Poll Result marginOfError '±3%'", "Scientific Measurement marginOfError '0.5 units'", "Survey Data marginOfError '2 percentage points'".
masthead: A masthead relation between a news media organization and a creative work or URL listing its top editorial management. Also called: editorial board, management list, staff directory. Examples: "The New York Times masthead 'About Us' page", "BBC News masthead Editorial Leadership", "Local Newspaper masthead 'Our Team' section".
material: A material composition relation between a creative work or product and the material it is made from. Also called: made of, composed of, constructed from. Examples: "Wooden Chair material Wood", "Wool Sweater material Wool", "Paper Book material Paper".
materialExtent: A material extent relation between a creative work and the quantitative value or text describing the quantity or physical space of its materials. Also called: material quantity, physical extent, material volume. Examples: "Sculpture materialExtent '5 kg of bronze'", "Painting materialExtent '1 liter of oil paint'", "Document Archive materialExtent '10 cubic meters'".
mathExpression: A mathematical expression relation between a math solver and the expression it can solve, simplify, or transform. Also called: mathematical formula, equation, algebraic expression. Examples: "Equation Solver mathExpression 'x^2 - 3x = 0'", "Symbolic Calculator mathExpression 'sin(x) + cos(x)'", "Algebra Tool mathExpression '2y + 5 = 11'".
maxPrice: A maximum price relation between a price specification and the highest price in a given range. Also called: highest price, upper price limit, ceiling price. Examples: "Premium Tier maxPrice 99.99", "Luxury Car maxPrice 150000", "Concert Ticket maxPrice 250". Distinct from highPrice, which is used for AggregateOffer and refers to the highest price of all offers.
maxValue: An upper value relation between a monetary amount, property value, property value specification, or quantitative value and the highest value of a characteristic or property. Also called: maximum limit, upper bound, highest possible value. Examples: "Temperature Range maxValue 30", "Age Limit maxValue 65", "Credit Score maxValue 850". Distinct from maxPrice, which specifically refers to the highest price in a range.
maximumAttendeeCapacity: An attendee capacity relation between an event or place and the total number of individuals it can accommodate. Also called: maximum occupancy, total capacity, attendee limit. Examples: "Concert Venue maximumAttendeeCapacity 5000", "Conference Room maximumAttendeeCapacity 100", "Public Park maximumAttendeeCapacity 10000".
maximumEnrollment: An enrollment capacity relation between an educational or occupational program and the maximum number of students who can be enrolled. Also called: enrollment limit, student capacity, maximum participants. Examples: "Master's Program maximumEnrollment 50", "Workshop maximumEnrollment 20", "Online Course maximumEnrollment 500".
maximumIntake: A maximum intake relation between a dietary supplement, drug, drug strength, or substance and its recommended maximum dose schedule. Also called: maximum dosage, recommended limit, upper intake level. Examples: "Vitamin C Supplement maximumIntake '2000 mg per day'", "Pain Reliever maximumIntake '8 tablets in 24 hours'", "Caffeine maximumIntake '400 mg per day'".
maximumPhysicalAttendeeCapacity: A physical attendee capacity relation between an event and the maximum number of individuals who can physically attend. Also called: in-person capacity, venue limit, on-site capacity. Examples: "Hybrid Conference maximumPhysicalAttendeeCapacity 500", "Live Concert maximumPhysicalAttendeeCapacity 10000", "Workshop maximumPhysicalAttendeeCapacity 30". Distinct from maximumVirtualAttendeeCapacity, which refers to online attendees.
maximumVirtualAttendeeCapacity: A virtual attendee capacity relation between an event and the maximum number of individuals who can attend online. Also called: online capacity, virtual participant limit, streaming capacity. Examples: "Hybrid Conference maximumVirtualAttendeeCapacity 2000", "Webinar maximumVirtualAttendeeCapacity 500", "Online Class maximumVirtualAttendeeCapacity 100". Distinct from maximumPhysicalAttendeeCapacity, which refers to in-person attendees.
mealService: A meal service relation between a flight and the description of meals provided or available for purchase. Also called: in-flight meals, catering options, food service. Examples: "Flight BA249 mealService 'Complimentary hot meal and beverages'", "Flight AA123 mealService 'Snacks and drinks available for purchase'", "Flight LH456 mealService 'Vegetarian option available upon request'".
measuredProperty: A measured property relation between an observation or statistical variable and the property being measured. Also called: property measured, observed characteristic, variable property. Examples: "Temperature Observation measuredProperty 'temperature'", "GDP StatisticalVariable measuredProperty 'Gross Domestic Product'", "Survey Response measuredProperty 'satisfaction level'". Distinct from variableMeasured, which is a broader property for describing what is measured in a dataset.
measurementDenominator: A measurement denominator relation between an observation or statistical variable and the variable used as the denominator in a ratio or percentage. Also called: ratio denominator, base variable, reference variable. Examples: "Unemployment Rate Observation measurementDenominator 'Total Labor Force'", "Per Capita Income StatisticalVariable measurementDenominator 'Population'", "Percentage Change Observation measurementDenominator 'Initial Value'".
measurementMethod: A measurement method relation between a data catalog, data download, dataset, observation, property value, or statistical variable and the specific method used for measurement. Also called: method of measurement, specific technique, measurement approach. Examples: "Temperature Dataset measurementMethod 'Thermocouple'", "Survey Data measurementMethod 'Likert Scale'", "Chemical Analysis measurementMethod 'Spectrophotometry'". Distinct from measurementTechnique, which is a broader property that measurementMethod is a subproperty of.
measurementQualifier: A measurement qualifier relation between an observation or statistical variable and an enumeration providing additional qualification. Also called: observation qualifier, measurement attribute, data context. Examples: "GDP Observation measurementQualifier 'Nominal'", "Inflation Rate measurementQualifier 'Annualized'", "Population Count measurementQualifier 'Estimated'".
measurementTechnique: A measurement technique relation between a data catalog, data download, dataset, observation, property value, or statistical variable and the technique, method, or technology used for measurement. Also called: measurement approach, data collection method, analytical technique. Examples: "Molecule Concentration Dataset measurementTechnique 'Mass Spectrometry'", "Depression Rating Observation measurementTechnique 'Beck Depression Inventory'", "Water Quality Data measurementTechnique 'Chromatography'". Distinct from measurementMethod, which is a more specific subproperty.
mechanismOfAction: A mechanism of action relation between a dietary supplement or drug and the specific biochemical interaction producing its pharmacological effect. Also called: mode of action, pharmacological mechanism, how it works. Examples: "Aspirin mechanismOfAction 'Inhibits COX enzymes'", "Insulin mechanismOfAction 'Binds to insulin receptors'", "Antidepressant mechanismOfAction 'Increases serotonin levels'".
mediaAuthenticityCategory: A media authenticity category relation between a media review and its classification of a media object's manipulation rating. Also called: authenticity rating, manipulation category, media integrity. Examples: "News Video Review mediaAuthenticityCategory 'ManipulatedContent'", "Image Review mediaAuthenticityCategory 'FalseContext'", "Audio Clip Review mediaAuthenticityCategory 'TrueContent'".
mediaItemAppearance: A media item appearance relation between a media review item and the specific media object(s) grouped within it. Also called: associated media, media objects, grouped items. Examples: "Fact Check Item mediaItemAppearance 'Image of politician'", "Video Analysis Item mediaItemAppearance 'Clip from broadcast'", "Audio Review Item mediaItemAppearance 'Sound recording'".
median: A median value relation between a quantitative value distribution and its central value. Also called: middle value, central tendency, 50th percentile. Examples: "Income Distribution median 50000", "Test Score Distribution median 75", "Response Time Distribution median 200ms".
medicalAudience: A medical audience relation between a medical web page and its intended medical audience type. Also called: target medical audience, intended readership, healthcare professional audience. Examples: "Research Article medicalAudience 'Physicians'", "Patient Information Leaflet medicalAudience 'General Public'", "Medical Guideline medicalAudience 'Nurses'".
medicalSpecialty: A medical specialty relation between a hospital, medical clinic, medical organization, or physician and their area of medical expertise. Also called: clinical specialty, medical field, area of practice. Examples: "Dr. Smith medicalSpecialty 'Cardiology'", "City Hospital medicalSpecialty 'Pediatrics'", "Dermatology Clinic medicalSpecialty 'Dermatology'".
medicineSystem: A medicine system relation between a medical entity and the system of medicine it belongs to. Also called: healthcare system, medical tradition, therapeutic approach. Examples: "Acupuncture medicineSystem 'Traditional Chinese Medicine'", "Homeopathic Remedy medicineSystem 'Homeopathic Medicine'", "Evidence-Based Treatment medicineSystem 'Evidence-Based Medicine'".
meetsEmissionStandard: An emission standard compliance relation between a vehicle and the qualitative value, text, or URL indicating the emission standard it meets. Also called: emission compliant, environmentally certified, low emission. Examples: "Electric Car meetsEmissionStandard 'Zero Emission'", "New Diesel Car meetsEmissionStandard 'Euro 6'", "Hybrid Vehicle meetsEmissionStandard 'CARB LEV III'".
member: A member relation between an organization or program membership and an organization or person belonging to it. Also called: belongs to, is a part of, participant in. Examples: "Club Organization member John Doe", "Team ProgramMembership member Jane Smith", "Alliance Organization member Partner Company". Distinct from memberOf, which expresses the inverse relationship.
memberOf: A membership relation between an organization or person and the organization or program membership they belong to. Also called: belongs to, is a member of, affiliated with. Examples: "John Doe memberOf 'Local Sports Club'", "Acme Corp memberOf 'Industry Association'", "Jane Smith memberOf 'Premium Membership Tier'". Distinct from member, which expresses the inverse relationship.
members: A member relation between an organization or program membership and an organization or person belonging to it. Also called: includes members, comprises, consists of. Examples: "Club Organization members John Doe", "Team ProgramMembership members Jane Smith", "Alliance Organization members Partner Company". Distinct from member, which is a singular form and essentially the same concept.
membershipNumber: A membership number relation between a program membership and its unique identifier. Also called: member ID, membership ID, account number. Examples: "Loyalty Program membershipNumber '123456789'", "Gym Membership membershipNumber 'M-98765'", "Library Card membershipNumber 'LIB-001'".
membershipPointsEarned: A membership points relation between a member program tier, price specification, or program membership and the number of points earned. Also called: points accumulated, reward points, loyalty points. Examples: "Gold Tier membershipPointsEarned 5000", "Premium Membership membershipPointsEarned 1000", "Flight Booking membershipPointsEarned 250 miles".
memoryRequirements: A memory requirements relation between a software application and its minimum memory specifications. Also called: RAM requirements, memory needed, system memory. Examples: "Video Editor Software memoryRequirements '8 GB RAM'", "Operating System memoryRequirements '4 GB RAM'", "Game Application memoryRequirements '16 GB RAM'".
mentions: A mention relation between a creative work and a thing it references without necessarily being about. Also called: references, alludes to, cites. Examples: "News Article mentions 'Climate Change'", "Book mentions 'Historical Event'", "Speech mentions 'Famous Person'". Distinct from about, which indicates the primary topic of the creative work.
menu: A menu relation between a food establishment and its structured menu, text, or URL. Also called: food offerings, dining options, bill of fare. Examples: "Restaurant menu 'Italian Cuisine Menu'", "Cafe menu 'Breakfast & Lunch Menu URL'", "Diner menu 'Daily Specials Text'".
menuAddOn: An add-on relation between a menu item and additional menu items or sections that can be added to it. Also called: optional additions, side orders, customizable options. Examples: "Burger MenuItem menuAddOn 'Fries'", "Salad MenuItem menuAddOn 'Grilled Chicken'", "Pizza MenuItem menuAddOn 'Extra Toppings Section'".
merchant: A seller relation between an order and the organization or person acting as the seller. Also called: seller, vendor, retailer. Examples: "Online Order merchant Amazon", "Local Purchase merchant Boutique Store", "Service Booking merchant Freelancer".
merchantReturnDays: A merchant return days relation between a merchant return policy or seasonal override and the number of days or fixed date for product returns. Also called: return window, days to return, return period. Examples: "Standard Return Policy merchantReturnDays 30", "Holiday Return Policy merchantReturnDays 2024-01-31", "Electronics Return Policy merchantReturnDays 15".
merchantReturnLink: A merchant return link relation between a merchant return policy and a URL for product returns. Also called: return policy URL, returns page, refund link. Examples: "Store Return Policy merchantReturnLink 'https://example.com/returns'", "Online Retailer merchantReturnLink 'Customer Service Returns'", "Brand Return Policy merchantReturnLink 'Returns FAQ'".
messageAttachment: A message attachment relation between a message and the creative work attached to it. Also called: attached file, email attachment, message content. Examples: "Email messageAttachment 'Report.pdf'", "Chat Message messageAttachment 'Image.jpg'", "Forum Post messageAttachment 'CodeSnippet.txt'".
mileageFromOdometer: An odometer mileage relation between a vehicle and the total distance traveled as read from its odometer. Also called: odometer reading, total mileage, distance traveled. Examples: "Car mileageFromOdometer '50000 KMT'", "Truck mileageFromOdometer '120000 SMI'", "Motorcycle mileageFromOdometer '15000 km'".
minPrice: A minimum price relation between a price specification and the lowest price in a given range. Also called: lowest price, lower price limit, floor price. Examples: "Basic Tier minPrice 9.99", "Economy Car minPrice 20000", "Concert Ticket minPrice 50". Distinct from lowPrice, which is the lowest price of all offers in an AggregateOffer.
minValue: A lower value relation between a monetary amount, property value, property value specification, or quantitative value and the lowest value of a characteristic or property. Also called: minimum limit, lower bound, lowest possible value. Examples: "Temperature Range minValue 10", "Age Limit minValue 18", "Credit Score minValue 300". Distinct from minPrice, which specifically refers to the lowest price in a range.
minimumPaymentDue: A minimum payment due relation between an invoice and the monetary amount or price specification required at a given time. Also called: minimum amount payable, required payment, lowest payment. Examples: "Credit Card Invoice minimumPaymentDue $25.00", "Utility Bill minimumPaymentDue '10.00 EUR'", "Loan Statement minimumPaymentDue 'Payment Plan A'".
missionCoveragePrioritiesPolicy: A mission coverage priorities policy relation between a news media organization and a creative work or URL stating its coverage priorities or public agenda. Also called: editorial policy, coverage guidelines, journalistic priorities. Examples: "News Outlet missionCoveragePrioritiesPolicy 'Focus on local news and investigative journalism'", "Broadcaster missionCoveragePrioritiesPolicy 'Public Service Mandate'", "Digital Publisher missionCoveragePrioritiesPolicy 'Transparency and Accuracy Statement'".
mobileUrl: A mobile URL relation between an offer or product and a dedicated URL for its mobile site. Also called: mobile link, mobile website, responsive URL. Examples: "Product Offer mobileUrl 'https://m.example.com/product1'", "Service Listing mobileUrl 'https://mobile.service.com'", "E-commerce Product mobileUrl 'https://example.com/mobile/item123'". Distinct from url, which is a general URL and ideally should be responsive for all devices.
model: A model relation between a product and its product model or textual identifier. Also called: product model, version, type. Examples: "Smartphone model 'iPhone 15 Pro'", "Car model 'Toyota Camry'", "Laptop model 'MacBook Air M2'".
modelDate: A model date relation between a vehicle and the release date of its model. Also called: model year, release date, version date. Examples: "Car modelDate 2023-09-01", "Motorcycle modelDate 2024-01-15", "Truck modelDate 2022-07-01".
modifiedTime: A modified time relation between a reservation and the date and time it was changed. Also called: last modified, update time, change timestamp. Examples: "Flight Reservation modifiedTime '2023-10-26T10:30:00Z'", "Hotel Booking modifiedTime '2023-11-01T15:00:00Z'", "Restaurant Reservation modifiedTime '2023-12-05T18:45:00Z'".
molecularFormula: A molecular formula relation between a molecular entity and its empirical formula, representing the simplest whole number ratio of atoms. Also called: empirical formula, chemical formula, stoichiometric formula. Examples: "Water molecularFormula 'H2O'", "Glucose molecularFormula 'C6H12O6'", "Methane molecularFormula 'CH4'".
molecularWeight: A molecular weight relation between a molecular entity and its quantitative value or text representing its molecular weight. Also called: molecular mass, formula weight, molar mass. Examples: "Water molecularWeight '18.015 amu'", "Carbon Dioxide molecularWeight '44.01 g/mol'", "Ethanol molecularWeight '46.07 g/mol'".
monoisotopicMolecularWeight: A monoisotopic molecular weight value for a molecular entity. Also called monoisotopic mass, molecular mass (monoisotopic), exact mass. Examples: "Caffeine monoisotopicMolecularWeight 194.084473 g/mol", "Water monoisotopicMolecularWeight 18.010565 g/mol", "Aspirin monoisotopicMolecularWeight 180.042259 g/mol".
monthlyMinimumRepaymentAmount: A monthly minimum repayment amount associated with a payment card. Also called minimum monthly payment, required monthly payment, lowest monthly payment. Examples: "Credit Card A monthlyMinimumRepaymentAmount $25", "Credit Card B monthlyMinimumRepaymentAmount 2% of balance", "Store Card monthlyMinimumRepaymentAmount $15".
monthsOfExperience: A required number of months of experience for an occupational role. Also called experience duration, minimum experience, required experience in months. Examples: "Software Engineer Role monthsOfExperience 24", "Marketing Manager Position monthsOfExperience 60", "Entry-level Job monthsOfExperience 0".
mpn: A Manufacturer Part Number (MPN) identifying a product, demand, or offer. Also called manufacturer's part number, product part number, part number. Examples: "Laptop X mpn 'ABC-12345'", "Offer for Widget Y mpn 'WIDGET-987'", "Demand for Component Z mpn 'COMP-001'". Distinct from gtin, which is a globally unique identifier like UPC or EAN.
multipleValues: An indication of whether multiple values are allowed for a property value specification. Also called allows multiple entries, accepts multiple values, multi-valued. Examples: "Color Property multipleValues true", "Age Property multipleValues false", "Tag Property multipleValues true".
muscleAction: A description of the movement generated by a muscle. Also called muscle function, muscle movement, action of muscle. Examples: "Biceps Brachii muscleAction 'flexion of elbow'", "Triceps Brachii muscleAction 'extension of elbow'", "Deltoid muscleAction 'abduction of shoulder'".
musicArrangement: A musical arrangement derived from a music composition. Also called arranged version, musical adaptation, composition arrangement. Examples: "Beethoven's Symphony No. 5 musicArrangement 'Piano arrangement by Liszt'", "Bach's Cello Suite No. 1 musicArrangement 'Arrangement for guitar'", "Pop Song X musicArrangement 'Orchestral arrangement'".
musicBy: A composer or music group responsible for the soundtrack of a creative work. Also called soundtrack by, composer of, musical score by. Examples: "Movie X musicBy 'John Williams'", "TV Series Y musicBy 'Ramin Djawadi'", "Video Game Z musicBy 'Koji Kondo'". Distinct from composer, which is for the composer of a MusicComposition.
musicCompositionForm: The form or type of a music composition. Also called composition type, musical form, genre of composition. Examples: "Symphony No. 9 musicCompositionForm 'Symphony'", "Moonlight Sonata musicCompositionForm 'Sonata'", "Bohemian Rhapsody musicCompositionForm 'Rock Opera'". Distinct from genre, which is a broader classification of creative works.
musicGroupMember: A person who is a member of a music group. Also called band member, group member, musician in group. Examples: "The Beatles musicGroupMember 'John Lennon'", "Queen musicGroupMember 'Freddie Mercury'", "Fleetwood Mac musicGroupMember 'Stevie Nicks'". Distinct from member, which is a general property for any organization.
musicReleaseFormat: The format of a music release, indicating the type of recording media. Also called release format, media type, recording format. Examples: "Album X musicReleaseFormat 'CDFormat'", "Single Y musicReleaseFormat 'DigitalAudioTapeFormat'", "LP Z musicReleaseFormat 'VinylFormat'".
musicalKey: The key, mode, or scale used in a music composition. Also called key signature, composition key, tonal center. Examples: "Symphony No. 5 musicalKey 'C minor'", "Für Elise musicalKey 'A minor'", "Jazz Standard musicalKey 'Bb Major'".
naics: A North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code associated with an organization or business person. Also called NAICS code, industry classification code, business classification code. Examples: "Company A naics '511210' (Software Publishers)", "Person B naics '541611' (Administrative Management and General Management Services)", "Restaurant C naics '722511' (Full-Service Restaurants)". Distinct from isicV4, which is the International Standard Industrial Classification of All Economic Activities.
name: A name or title identifying a thing. Also called title, designation, appellation, label. Examples: "Book name 'The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy'", "Person name 'Alice Smith'", "Company name 'Acme Corp'". Distinct from alternateName, which is an alias or alternative name.
namedPosition: A specific named position or role played by a person or organization within a larger organization. Also called role name, position title, job title. Examples: "Athlete Role namedPosition 'Quarterback'", "Employee Role namedPosition 'Senior Software Engineer'", "Board Member Role namedPosition 'Treasurer'". Distinct from roleName, which is a more general description of a role.
nationality: A country representing the nationality of a person. Also called citizenship, country of origin, national identity. Examples: "Person A nationality 'United States'", "Person B nationality 'France'", "Person C nationality 'Japan'". Distinct from birthPlace, which is the location where a person was born.
naturalProgression: The expected progression of a medical condition if left untreated. Also called untreated course, disease progression, natural history of condition. Examples: "Common Cold naturalProgression 'resolves in 7-10 days'", "Untreated Diabetes naturalProgression 'leads to complications like neuropathy and kidney failure'", "Flu naturalProgression 'fever and body aches for 3-5 days, then recovery'". Distinct from prognosis, which is a forecast of the likely course of a disease.
negativeNotes: Negative considerations or drawbacks associated with a product or described in a review. Also called cons, disadvantages, downsides, criticisms. Examples: "Product X negativeNotes 'short battery life'", "Review Y negativeNotes 'poor customer service'", "Software Z negativeNotes 'steep learning curve', 'frequent crashes'". Distinct from positiveNotes, which describes favorable aspects.
nerve: A nerve providing innervation to a muscle. Also called innervated by, muscle innervation, nerve supply. Examples: "Biceps Brachii nerve 'Musculocutaneous nerve'", "Triceps Brachii nerve 'Radial nerve'", "Diaphragm nerve 'Phrenic nerve'". Distinct from nerveMotor, which describes the muscle controlled by a nerve.
nerveMotor: A muscle controlled by a nerve through a neurological pathway. Also called motor innervation, controls muscle, innervates muscle. Examples: "Radial Nerve nerveMotor 'Triceps Brachii'", "Musculocutaneous Nerve nerveMotor 'Biceps Brachii'", "Phrenic Nerve nerveMotor 'Diaphragm'". Distinct from nerve, which describes the nerve of a muscle.
netWorth: The total financial value of a person, calculated as assets minus liabilities. Also called personal wealth, financial worth, total assets. Examples: "Person A netWorth '$1,000,000'", "Person B netWorth '$500,000'", "Person C netWorth '$10,000'".
newsUpdatesAndGuidelines: A URL or web content providing news updates and guidelines related to a special announcement. Also called updates page, guidelines link, news and guidance. Examples: "COVID-19 Announcement newsUpdatesAndGuidelines 'https://example.com/covid-updates'", "Emergency Alert newsUpdatesAndGuidelines 'https://gov.example.org/emergency-guidelines'", "Product Recall newsUpdatesAndGuidelines 'https://company.com/recall-info'".
nextItem: A list item that immediately follows the current list item in an ordered sequence. Also called subsequent item, following item, next in list. Examples: "Item 1 nextItem 'Item 2'", "Page 3 nextItem 'Page 4'", "Step A nextItem 'Step B'". Distinct from previousItem, which links to the preceding item.
noBylinesPolicy: A policy statement from a news media organization explaining when authors are not credited in bylines. Also called anonymous author policy, byline exclusion policy, uncredited author policy. Examples: "News Org A noBylinesPolicy 'https://news.example.com/bylines'", "Journalism Company B noBylinesPolicy 'Our policy is to omit bylines for staff editorials.'", "Media Outlet C noBylinesPolicy 'https://media.example.org/editorial-standards#bylines'".
nonEqual: A qualitative value that is not equal to another qualitative value. Also called not equivalent to, different from, unequal to. Examples: "Value A nonEqual 'Value B'", "Color Red nonEqual 'Color Blue'", "Size Small nonEqual 'Size Large'". Distinct from equal, which indicates equivalence.
nonProprietaryName: The generic or non-proprietary name of a drug or dietary supplement. Also called generic name, common name, chemical name. Examples: "Drug X nonProprietaryName 'Acetaminophen'", "Supplement Y nonProprietaryName 'Ascorbic Acid'", "Medication Z nonProprietaryName 'Ibuprofen'". Distinct from proprietaryName, which is the brand or trade name.
nonprofitStatus: The legal nonprofit status of an organization in its primary place of business. Also called charitable status, tax-exempt status, non-profit classification. Examples: "Charity A nonprofitStatus 'Nonprofit501c3'", "Foundation B nonprofitStatus 'NonprofitType.Nonprofit501c4'", "Association C nonprofitStatus 'NonprofitType.Nonprofit501c6'".
normalRange: The range of acceptable values for a medical test in a typical patient. Also called reference range, healthy range, typical values. Examples: "Blood Pressure Test normalRange '120/80 mmHg'", "Glucose Test normalRange '70-99 mg/dL'", "Cholesterol Test normalRange 'Total <200 mg/dL'".
nsn: A NATO Stock Number (NSN) identifying a product. Also called NATO stock number, military stock number, supply classification number. Examples: "Military Radio nsn '5820-01-123-4567'", "Vehicle Part nsn '2510-00-987-6543'", "Medical Kit nsn '6545-01-000-1111'". Distinct from gtin, which is a commercial global trade item number.
numAdults: The number of adults included in a lodging reservation. Also called adult count, number of grown-ups, adult guests. Examples: "Hotel Reservation numAdults 2", "Vacation Rental numAdults 4", "Single Room Reservation numAdults 1". Distinct from numChildren, which specifies the number of children.
numChildren: The number of children included in a lodging reservation. Also called child count, number of kids, child guests. Examples: "Hotel Reservation numChildren 1", "Vacation Rental numChildren 3", "Family Suite Reservation numChildren 2". Distinct from numAdults, which specifies the number of adults.
numConstraints: The number of constraint property values defined for a constraint node. Also called constraint count, number of restrictions, defined constraints. Examples: "Statistical Variable A numConstraints 3", "Data Filter B numConstraints 2", "Query Parameter C numConstraints 1".
numItems: A limit on the number of items being shipped for which specific shipping conditions apply. Also called item quantity limit, shipping item count, maximum items. Examples: "Free Shipping Conditions numItems 'max 5'", "Bulk Discount Shipping numItems 'min 10'", "Special Rate Shipping numItems '1-3'". Distinct from orderQuantity, which is the quantity of a specific item in an order.
numTracks: The total number of tracks contained within a music playlist or album. Also called track count, song count, number of songs. Examples: "Album X numTracks 12", "Playlist Y numTracks 50", "EP Z numTracks 4". Distinct from numberOfEpisodes, which is for seasons or series.
numberOfAccommodationUnits: The total number of accommodation units in an apartment complex or for a specific floor plan. Also called total units, unit count, accommodation unit total. Examples: "Apartment Complex A numberOfAccommodationUnits 150", "Floor Plan B numberOfAccommodationUnits 10", "Building C numberOfAccommodationUnits 200". Distinct from numberOfAvailableAccommodationUnits, which specifies only the currently available units.
numberOfAirbags: The number or type of airbags present in a vehicle. Also called airbag count, vehicle airbags, safety airbags. Examples: "Car X numberOfAirbags 6", "SUV Y numberOfAirbags '8 (front, side, curtain)'", "Truck Z numberOfAirbags 2".
numberOfAvailableAccommodationUnits: The number of currently available accommodation units in an apartment complex or for a specific floor plan. Also called available units, vacant units, units for rent. Examples: "Apartment Complex A numberOfAvailableAccommodationUnits 10", "Floor Plan B numberOfAvailableAccommodationUnits 2", "Building C numberOfAvailableAccommodationUnits 15". Distinct from numberOfAccommodationUnits, which specifies the total (available + unavailable) units.
numberOfAxles: The number of axles on a vehicle. Also called axle count, vehicle axles, axles quantity. Examples: "Car X numberOfAxles 2", "Truck Y numberOfAxles 3", "Trailer Z numberOfAxles 4".
numberOfBathroomsTotal: The total integer count of all bathrooms (full, three-quarter, and half) within an accommodation or floor plan. Also called total bathroom count, bathroom total, sum of bathrooms. Examples: "Apartment A numberOfBathroomsTotal 2", "House B numberOfBathroomsTotal 3", "Hotel Room C numberOfBathroomsTotal 1". Distinct from numberOfFullBathrooms and numberOfPartialBathrooms, which specify specific types of bathrooms.
numberOfBedrooms: The total number of bedrooms in an accommodation, apartment complex, or floor plan. Also called bedroom count, number of sleeping rooms, bedroom total. Examples: "Apartment A numberOfBedrooms 2", "House B numberOfBedrooms 4", "Floor Plan C numberOfBedrooms 3". Distinct from numberOfBeds, which specifies the quantity of individual beds.
numberOfBeds: The quantity of a specific bed type available within a lodging unit. Also called bed count, quantity of beds, available beds. Examples: "King Bed Details numberOfBeds 1", "Twin Bed Details numberOfBeds 2", "Queen Bed Details numberOfBeds 1". Distinct from numberOfBedrooms, which specifies the number of rooms designated as bedrooms.
numberOfCredits: The number of credits or units awarded by a course or required for an educational occupational program. Also called credit hours, course units, program credits. Examples: "Calculus I Course numberOfCredits 3", "MBA Program numberOfCredits 60", "Certification Program numberOfCredits 10".
numberOfDoors: The number of doors on a vehicle. Also called door count, vehicle doors, doors quantity. Examples: "Sedan X numberOfDoors 4", "Coupe Y numberOfDoors 2", "Hatchback Z numberOfDoors 5".
numberOfEmployees: The number of employees working for an organization or targeted by a business audience. Also called employee count, workforce size, staff number. Examples: "Company A numberOfEmployees 500", "Small Business B numberOfEmployees 15", "Target Audience C numberOfEmployees '100-500'".
numberOfEpisodes: The total number of episodes within a creative work season, radio series, TV series, or video game series. Also called episode count, series episodes, season episodes. Examples: "TV Series X numberOfEpisodes 200", "Season 1 numberOfEpisodes 10", "Video Game Series Y numberOfEpisodes 5". Distinct from numTracks, which is for music.
numberOfForwardGears: The total number of forward gears available in a vehicle's transmission system. Also called forward gear count, transmission gears, gear ratio count. Examples: "Car X numberOfForwardGears 6", "Truck Y numberOfForwardGears 8", "Motorcycle Z numberOfForwardGears 5".
numberOfFullBathrooms: The total number of full and three-quarter bathrooms in an accommodation or floor plan. Also called full bathroom count, full baths, complete bathrooms. Examples: "Apartment A numberOfFullBathrooms 2", "House B numberOfFullBathrooms 3", "Hotel Room C numberOfFullBathrooms 1". Distinct from numberOfPartialBathrooms, which specifies half or quarter bathrooms. numberOfBathroomsTotal is the sum of all types.
numberOfItems: The total number of items contained within an item list. Also called item count, list size, total items. Examples: "Shopping Cart ItemList numberOfItems 5", "To-Do List numberOfItems 10", "Search Results List numberOfItems 100". Distinct from numItems (for ShippingConditions), which is a limit on items for shipping.
numberOfLoanPayments: The total number of payments contractually required to repay a loan. Also called loan payment count, repayment installments, number of installments. Examples: "Mortgage Repayment numberOfLoanPayments 360", "Car Loan Repayment numberOfLoanPayments 60", "Personal Loan Repayment numberOfLoanPayments 24".
numberOfPages: The total number of pages in a book. Also called page count, book length, total pages. Examples: "Novel X numberOfPages 350", "Textbook Y numberOfPages 800", "Children's Book Z numberOfPages 32". Distinct from pagination, which describes page ranges.
numberOfPartialBathrooms: The total number of half and quarter bathrooms in an accommodation or floor plan. Also called partial bathroom count, half baths, quarter baths. Examples: "Apartment A numberOfPartialBathrooms 1", "House B numberOfPartialBathrooms 2", "Hotel Room C numberOfPartialBathrooms 0". Distinct from numberOfFullBathrooms, which specifies full or three-quarter bathrooms. numberOfBathroomsTotal is the sum of all types.
numberOfPlayers: The number of people who can play a game or video game series, often expressed as a minimum, maximum, or range. Also called player count, game capacity, participant number. Examples: "Board Game X numberOfPlayers '2-4'", "Video Game Y numberOfPlayers '1 (single-player)'", "Online Game Z numberOfPlayers '100 (max)'".
numberOfPreviousOwners: The total number of previous owners of a vehicle, including the current owner. Also called prior owners, owner history count, past owners. Examples: "Used Car A numberOfPreviousOwners 1", "Vintage Vehicle B numberOfPreviousOwners 3", "New Car C numberOfPreviousOwners 0".
numberOfRooms: The total number of rooms in an accommodation or lodging business, excluding bathrooms and closets. Also called room count, total rooms, living space rooms. Examples: "Apartment A numberOfRooms 3", "House B numberOfRooms 6", "Hotel Suite C numberOfRooms 2". Distinct from numberOfBedrooms or numberOfBathroomsTotal, which specify specific types of rooms.
numberOfSeasons: The total number of seasons within a radio series, TV series, or video game series. Also called season count, series seasons, total seasons. Examples: "TV Series X numberOfSeasons 10", "Radio Series Y numberOfSeasons 3", "Video Game Series Z numberOfSeasons 5". Distinct from numberOfEpisodes, which is for individual episodes within a season or series.
numberedPosition: A number associated with an organization role, such as an athlete's jersey number. Also called role number, position number, identifier number. Examples: "Athlete Role numberedPosition 23", "Team Member Role numberedPosition 7", "Employee Role numberedPosition 101". Distinct from namedPosition, which is a textual name for a role.
nutrition: Nutrition information associated with a menu item or recipe. Also called nutritional facts, dietary information, food nutrition. Examples: "Chicken Salad MenuItem nutrition 'Calories: 350, Protein: 30g'", "Chocolate Chip Cookie Recipe nutrition 'Per serving: 150 kcal, 8g fat'", "Smoothie MenuItem nutrition 'Vitamin C: 100% DV'".
object: A thing upon which an action is carried out, potentially changing its state. Also called target, item acted upon, recipient of action. Examples: "Read Action object 'a book'", "Buy Action object 'a product'", "Edit Action object 'a document'". Distinct from instrument, which is the tool used to perform the action.
observationAbout: An entity, often a place, that an observation is about or associated with. Also called observed entity, subject of observation, related to observation. Examples: "Weather Observation observationAbout 'London'", "Patient Vitals Observation observationAbout 'John Doe'", "Traffic Count Observation observationAbout 'Main Street'".
observationDate: The date or date and time when an observation was made. Also called date of observation, observation timestamp, recorded date. Examples: "Weather Observation observationDate '2023-10-27'", "Medical Observation observationDate '2023-10-26T14:30:00'", "Astronomical Observation observationDate '2023-09-15'". Distinct from observationPeriod, which is the duration of the observation.
observationPeriod: The length of time over which an observation took place. Also called observation duration, period of observation, measurement period. Examples: "Clinical Trial Observation observationPeriod 'P6M'", "Weather Monitoring observationPeriod 'P24h'", "Patient Tracking observationPeriod 'P1Y'". Distinct from observationDate, which is the specific point in time of the observation.
occupancy: The allowed total occupancy in persons for an accommodation unit. Also called maximum occupancy, guest capacity, permitted persons. Examples: "Hotel Room occupancy 2", "Apartment occupancy 4", "Suite occupancy 6".
occupationLocation: An administrative area (region/country) where an occupational description is appropriate. Also called job location, employment region, occupational jurisdiction. Examples: "Software Engineer Occupation occupationLocation 'California'", "Doctor Occupation occupationLocation 'United Kingdom'", "Teacher Occupation occupationLocation 'New York State'". Distinct from workLocation, which is the specific place of work for a person.
occupationalCategory: A category describing a job, occupation, or educational program, often from a recognized taxonomy like O*NET-SOC or ISCO-08. Also called job category, occupation type, employment classification. Examples: "Job Posting occupationalCategory 'Software Development'", "Physician occupationalCategory 'General Practitioner'", "Work-Based Program occupationalCategory 'Construction Trades'". Distinct from industry, which is a broader classification of the economic sector.
occupationalCredentialAwarded: An occupational credential, such as a qualification, award, certificate, or diploma, awarded upon successful completion of a course or program. Also called credential earned, qualification awarded, program certification. Examples: "Course X occupationalCredentialAwarded 'Certificate of Completion'", "Program Y occupationalCredentialAwarded 'Bachelor of Science'", "Training Z occupationalCredentialAwarded 'Professional Certification'". Distinct from educationalLevel, which describes the level of education attained.
offerCount: The total number of individual offers aggregated for a product. Also called number of offers, offer quantity, total offers. Examples: "Product A AggregateOffer offerCount 10", "Service B AggregateOffer offerCount 5", "Item C AggregateOffer offerCount 20". Distinct from orderQuantity, which is the quantity of a specific item in an order.
offeredBy: An organization or person making an offer. Also called provided by, seller, vendor, offered from. Examples: "Product Offer offeredBy 'Acme Corp'", "Service Offer offeredBy 'John Doe'", "Event Ticket Offer offeredBy 'Ticketmaster'". Distinct from seller, which is a more specific term for a person or organization selling something.
offers: An offer or demand related to a product, service, event, or other item. Also called available offers, related offers, product offers. Examples: "Product X offers 'Offer to sell'", "Service Y offers 'Demand for service'", "Event Z offers 'Offer for tickets'". Distinct from hasOfferCatalog, which points to a catalog of offers.
offersPrescriptionByMail: An indication of whether prescriptions can be delivered by mail through a health plan formulary. Also called mail-order prescriptions, prescription delivery, home delivery of meds. Examples: "Health Plan A offersPrescriptionByMail true", "Formulary B offersPrescriptionByMail false", "Insurance Plan C offersPrescriptionByMail true".
openingHours: A textual representation of the general opening hours for a civic structure or local business. Also called business hours, hours of operation, store hours. Examples: "Restaurant X openingHours 'Mo-Fr 09:00-17:00'", "Library Y openingHours 'Sa-Su 10:00-18:00'", "Shop Z openingHours 'Mo-Su'". Distinct from openingHoursSpecification, which uses a structured object.
openingHoursSpecification: A structured specification of the opening hours for a place. Also called hours specification, detailed opening times, business hours details. Examples: "Museum A openingHoursSpecification 'OpeningHoursSpecification for Tuesday'", "Store B openingHoursSpecification 'OpeningHoursSpecification for weekends'", "Clinic C openingHoursSpecification 'OpeningHoursSpecification for holidays'". Distinct from openingHours, which is a simple text string.
opens: The specific time a place or service opens on a given day or days of the week. Also called opening time, start of business, daily opening hour. Examples: "Monday OpeningHoursSpecification opens '09:00'", "Weekend OpeningHoursSpecification opens '10:00'", "Weekday OpeningHoursSpecification opens '08:30'". Distinct from closes, which specifies the closing time.
operatingSystem: An operating system supported by a software application. Also called supported OS, compatible operating system, runs on. Examples: "Software X operatingSystem 'Windows 10'", "App Y operatingSystem 'iOS 16'", "Game Z operatingSystem 'macOS Ventura'".
opponent: A person who is an opponent in an exercise action. Also called adversary, competitor, rival. Examples: "Boxing Match opponent 'Mike Tyson'", "Chess Game opponent 'Deep Blue'", "Tennis Match opponent 'Serena Williams'". Distinct from participant, which is a general participant.
option: A text or thing representing an option available for a choose action. Also called choice, alternative, selection. Examples: "Choose Meal Action option 'Chicken'", "Choose Color Action option 'Blue'", "Choose Destination Action option 'Paris'". Distinct from object, which is the general item acted upon.
orderDate: The date or date and time when an order was placed. Also called date of order, purchase date, transaction date. Examples: "Order 123 orderDate '2023-10-27'", "Online Purchase orderDate '2023-10-26T10:00:00'", "Subscription Order orderDate '2023-09-01'". Distinct from paymentDueDate, which is when payment is expected.
orderDelivery: A parcel delivery associated with an order or order item. Also called delivery details, shipment, parcel tracking. Examples: "Order 123 orderDelivery 'Tracking Number XYZ'", "OrderItem A orderDelivery 'Delivered by UPS'", "Purchase Order orderDelivery 'Scheduled for next week'".
orderItemNumber: An identifier for a specific order item. Also called item ID, line item number, order line identifier. Examples: "OrderItem A orderItemNumber '001'", "OrderItem B orderItemNumber 'SKU-456'", "OrderItem C orderItemNumber 'LITM-789'". Distinct from orderNumber, which identifies the entire order.
orderItemStatus: The current status of an order item. Also called item status, line item status, fulfillment status. Examples: "OrderItem A orderItemStatus 'OrderProcessing'", "OrderItem B orderItemStatus 'OrderShipped'", "OrderItem C orderItemStatus 'OrderDelivered'". Distinct from orderStatus, which is for the entire order.
orderNumber: An identifier for an entire order or transaction. Also called transaction ID, purchase order number, order ID. Examples: "Customer Order orderNumber 'PO-12345'", "Online Transaction orderNumber 'TXN-67890'", "Sales Order orderNumber 'SO-001'". Distinct from orderItemNumber, which identifies a specific item within an order.
orderPercentage: A percentage value representing the fraction of the total order value charged as shipping cost. Also called shipping cost percentage, freight percentage, delivery fee rate. Examples: "Standard Shipping orderPercentage 0.05", "Express Shipping orderPercentage 0.10", "International Shipping orderPercentage 0.15". Distinct from shippingSettingsLink, which is a URL to shipping information.
orderQuantity: The number or quantity of a specific item ordered within an order item. Also called item quantity, ordered amount, number of units. Examples: "OrderItem A orderQuantity 2", "OrderItem B orderQuantity 5", "OrderItem C orderQuantity 1". Distinct from numItems (for ShippingConditions), which is a limit on total items for shipping.
orderStatus: The current status of an entire order. Also called order state, transaction status, fulfillment state. Examples: "Order 123 orderStatus 'OrderProcessing'", "Order 456 orderStatus 'OrderDelivered'", "Order 789 orderStatus 'OrderCancelled'". Distinct from orderItemStatus, which is for individual items within an order.
orderValue: A monetary amount representing the minimum or maximum order value for which specific shipping conditions are valid. Also called order total threshold, shipping value limit, purchase amount condition. Examples: "Free Shipping orderValue '$50.00'", "Discounted Shipping orderValue 'min $100.00'", "Special Rate Shipping orderValue 'max $20.00'".
