Distinct from orderPercentage, which is a rate based on order value.
orderedItem: An item (product, service, or another order item) that has been ordered. Also called purchased item, item in order, ordered product. Examples: "Order 123 orderedItem 'Laptop X'", "OrderItem A orderedItem 'Software License'", "Subscription Order orderedItem 'Premium Service'".
organizer: An organization or person responsible for organizing an event. Also called event planner, host, coordinator, promoter. Examples: "Conference X organizer 'Acme Events Inc.'", "Concert Y organizer 'Live Nation'", "Workshop Z organizer 'Jane Doe'". Distinct from performer, who participates in the event.
originAddress: The postal address of the shipper for a parcel delivery. Also called shipper address, sender's address, dispatch address. Examples: "Parcel Delivery 1 originAddress '123 Main St, Anytown'", "Shipment 2 originAddress 'Warehouse A, City B'", "Package 3 originAddress 'Sender's Home, Zip 12345'". Distinct from deliveryAddress, which is the recipient's address.
originalMediaContextDescription: Background information that aids in better interpretation of a media object, especially for decontextualized content in a media review. Also called media context, original context, background description. Examples: "Media Review A originalMediaContextDescription 'Video was originally posted on TikTok in 2020.'", "Image Review B originalMediaContextDescription 'Photo taken during a protest in 2018, not current event.'", "Audio Review C originalMediaContextDescription 'Clip is from a satirical podcast, not a news broadcast.'". Distinct from reviewBody, which is the main text of the review.
originalMediaLink: A link to the original version of media content, such as a web page or a direct media object file, in a media review. Also called source media link, original content URL, primary media source. Examples: "Media Review A originalMediaLink 'https://originalsource.com/video123'", "Image Review B originalMediaLink 'https://archive.org/image456'", "Audio Review C originalMediaLink 'https://podcast.example.com/episode789'". Distinct from url, which is the URL of the review itself.
originatesFrom: A vessel from which a lymphatic structure originates or receives afferents. Also called arises from, derived from, source vessel. Examples: "Lymphatic Vessel A originatesFrom 'Capillary Bed X'", "Thoracic Duct originatesFrom 'Cisterna Chyli'", "Lymphatic Capillary originatesFrom 'Interstitial Fluid'". Distinct from runsTo, which describes the destination.
overdosage: Information related to drug overdose, including signs, symptoms, treatments, and emergency contact details. Also called overdose information, toxicity details, emergency overdose guidance. Examples: "Drug X overdosage 'Symptoms include nausea and dizziness. Contact poison control immediately.'", "Medication Y overdosage 'Administer activated charcoal. Seek urgent medical attention.'", "Supplement Z overdosage 'May cause liver damage in high doses.'". Distinct from sideEffect, which describes adverse effects at normal doses.
ownedFrom: The date and time when ownership of a product was obtained. Also called acquisition date, purchase date, date acquired. Examples: "Car OwnershipInfo ownedFrom '2020-01-15'", "House OwnershipInfo ownedFrom '2018-06-01T10:00:00'", "Book OwnershipInfo ownedFrom '2023-03-10'". Distinct from ownedThrough, which is the date ownership ended.
ownedThrough: The date and time when ownership of a product was relinquished. Also called disposal date, date sold, ownership end date. Examples: "Car OwnershipInfo ownedThrough '2023-05-20'", "House OwnershipInfo ownedThrough '2022-11-30T16:00:00'", "Book OwnershipInfo ownedThrough '2024-01-01'". Distinct from ownedFrom, which is the date ownership began.
owner: A person or organization that owns a thing. Also called proprietor, possessor, title holder. Examples: "Car owner 'John Doe'", "Company owner 'Acme Corp'", "House owner 'Smith Family Trust'". Distinct from creator, who made the thing.
ownershipFundingInfo: Information describing the ownership structure, funding, and grants of an organization, particularly concerning editorial independence for news media. Also called funding transparency, ownership structure, financial backing details. Examples: "News Org A ownershipFundingInfo 'https://news.example.com/about/funding'", "Company B ownershipFundingInfo 'Privately held by XYZ Group.'", "Nonprofit C ownershipFundingInfo 'Funded by grants from various foundations.'". Distinct from funder, which specifically identifies the entity providing funds.
owns: A thing that is owned by an organization or person. Also called possesses, holds title to, has ownership of. Examples: "John Doe owns 'a car'", "Acme Corp owns 'a patent'", "Sarah owns 'her house'". Distinct from memberOf, which describes membership in a group.
pageEnd: The page number or identifier where a work (article, chapter, etc.) concludes. Also called ending page, last page, final page number. Examples: "Article X pageEnd 138", "Chapter Y pageEnd 'xvi'", "Report Z pageEnd 25". Distinct from pageStart, which is the beginning page. pagination is a general range.
pageStart: The page number or identifier where a work (article, chapter, etc.) begins. Also called starting page, first page, initial page number. Examples: "Article X pageStart 135", "Chapter Y pageStart 'xiii'", "Report Z pageStart 1". Distinct from pageEnd, which is the concluding page. pagination is a general range.
pagination: A textual description of page numbers or ranges for a work, not separated into distinct start and end properties. Also called page range, page numbering, page sequence. Examples: "Article X pagination '1-6, 9, 55'", "Chapter Y pagination '10-12, 46-49'", "Journal Entry Z pagination 'pp. 20-25'". Distinct from pageStart and pageEnd, which are specific start and end points.
parent: A person who is a parent of another person. Also called mother, father, progenitor. Examples: "Child A parent 'Parent B'", "Person X parent 'Mother Y'", "Person Z parent 'Father W'". Distinct from children, which describes the offspring.
parentItem: A hierarchical relation between a discussion item and its preceding item or a creative work it comments on. Also called part of, replies to, refers to, is a response to. Examples: A comment is a parent item of another comment. A question is a parent item of an answer. An answer is a parent item of a follow-up comment. Distinct from comment, which points from something to a comment about it.
parentOrganization: A hierarchical relation between an organization and the larger organization it belongs to. Also called belongs to, is a division of, is a subsidiary of, is part of. Examples: Google is a parent organization of YouTube. A local branch is a parent organization of its national headquarters. A department is a parent organization of its university. Distinct from subOrganization, which points from a larger organization to its smaller components.
parentService: A hierarchical relation between a broadcast service and a broader broadcast service it is a variation or component of. Also called belongs to, is a variation of, is part of, is a channel of. Examples: BBC One Scotland is a parent service of BBC One. A regional news channel is a parent service of a national news channel. A specific sports channel is a parent service of a broader sports network.
parentTaxon: A taxonomic relation between a taxon and its immediate higher-level taxon. Also called is a sub-taxon of, belongs to the taxon, is classified under. Examples: Homo is a parent taxon of Homo sapiens. Felidae is a parent taxon of Panthera. Mammalia is a parent taxon of Primates.
parents: A familial relation between a person and their biological or adoptive parents. Also called is a child of, has as a parent, is parented by. Examples: John is a parent of Mary. Jane is a parent of David. The parents of a child are their mother and father. Distinct from children, which points from a parent to their offspring.
partOfEpisode: A compositional relation between a clip and the episode it is a segment of. Also called is a segment of, is featured in, belongs to, is from. Examples: A highlight reel is part of an episode. A deleted scene is part of an episode. A short preview is part of an episode.
partOfInvoice: A financial relation between an order and the invoice that includes it for payment. Also called is included in, is billed on, is covered by. Examples: An online purchase order is part of an invoice. A service request order is part of an invoice. Multiple orders can be part of a single invoice.
partOfOrder: A logistical relation between a parcel delivery and the larger order it fulfills. Also called fulfills, belongs to, is a shipment for, is included in. Examples: A package delivery is part of an online shopping order. A food delivery is part of a restaurant order. A furniture shipment is part of a home goods order.
partOfSeason: A compositional relation between an episode or clip and the creative work season it belongs to. Also called belongs to, is featured in, is from, is a segment of. Examples: An episode is part of a season. A clip from a show is part of a season. The season finale is part of a season.
partOfSeries: A compositional relation between an episode, season, or clip and the creative work series it belongs to. Also called belongs to, is featured in, is from, is a segment of. Examples: An episode is part of a series. A season is part of a series. A clip from a show is part of a series. Distinct from partOfTVSeries, which is specifically for TV series.
partOfSystem: A biological relation between an anatomical structure and the anatomical or organ system it is a component of. Also called is a component of, belongs to, is found in, forms part of. Examples: The heart is part of the circulatory system. The lungs are part of the respiratory system. A bone is part of the skeletal system.
partOfTVSeries: A compositional relation between a TV episode, season, or clip and the TV series it belongs to. Also called belongs to, is featured in, is from, is a segment of. Examples: A TV episode is part of a TV series. A TV season is part of a TV series. A TV clip is part of a TV series. Distinct from partOfSeries, which is a more general property for any creative work series.
partOfTrip: A hierarchical relation between a trip and a larger, multi-day trip it is a segment of. Also called is a segment of, is a day of, is a leg of, belongs to. Examples: Day 1 of a vacation is part of the overall trip. A specific excursion is part of a larger travel itinerary. A flight segment is part of a multi-leg journey.
participant: A collaborative relation between an action and an organization or person who indirectly participated in it. Also called collaborated with, involved, assisted by, co-agent. Examples: A writing action has a participant co-author. A research project has a participant researcher. A meeting has a participant attendee. Distinct from agent, which is the primary actor of an action.
partySize: A descriptive attribute indicating the number of people a reservation is intended to accommodate. Also called number of guests, group size, capacity for. Examples: A restaurant reservation has a party size of four. A taxi reservation has a party size of two. A hotel booking has a party size of three.
passengerPriorityStatus: A descriptive attribute indicating the priority status assigned to a passenger for a flight reservation. Also called boarding priority, security status, passenger status. Examples: A flight reservation has a passenger priority status of 'FastTrack'. A flight reservation has a passenger priority status of 'Priority Boarding'. A flight reservation has a passenger priority status of 'Elite Member'.
passengerSequenceNumber: A descriptive attribute indicating the sequence number assigned to a passenger for a flight reservation by the airline. Also called boarding sequence, passenger number, flight sequence. Examples: A flight reservation has a passenger sequence number '001'. A flight reservation has a passenger sequence number 'A12'. A flight reservation has a passenger sequence number '34B'.
pathophysiology: A descriptive attribute detailing the changes in normal mechanical, physical, and biochemical functions associated with a medical condition or physical activity. Also called disease mechanism, functional changes, biological effects. Examples: Diabetes has a pathophysiology involving insulin resistance. Hypertension has a pathophysiology related to vascular stiffness. Intense exercise has a pathophysiology involving muscle microtrauma.
pattern: A descriptive attribute indicating the visual or design pattern of a creative work or product. Also called design, motif, print, style. Examples: A dress has a pattern of 'polka dot'. A fabric has a pattern of 'striped'. A flag has a pattern of 'Canadian flag'.
payload: A descriptive attribute indicating the maximum permitted weight of passengers and cargo a vehicle can carry, excluding the vehicle's own weight. Also called carrying capacity, load capacity, cargo weight limit. Examples: A truck has a payload of 1000 kg. A car has a payload of 500 kg. An aircraft has a payload of 20,000 lbs. Distinct from weight, which refers to the weight of the empty vehicle itself.
paymentAccepted: A descriptive attribute indicating the types of payment methods accepted by a local business. Also called accepted payment methods, payment options, forms of payment. Examples: A restaurant accepts 'Cash'. A store accepts 'Credit Card'. An online shop accepts 'Cryptocurrency'.
paymentDue: A temporal attribute indicating the date and time by which payment for an invoice or order is required. Also called due date, payment deadline, payment required by. Examples: An invoice has a payment due date of '2023-12-31T23:59:59'. An order has a payment due date of '2024-01-15'. The bill has a payment due date of 'next Friday'. Distinct from paymentDueDate, which is specifically a Date, not DateTime.
paymentDueDate: A temporal attribute indicating the date by which payment for an invoice or order is required. Also called due date, payment deadline, payment required by. Examples: An invoice has a payment due date of '2023-12-31'. An order has a payment due date of '2024-01-15'. The bill has a payment due date of '2024-02-28'. Distinct from paymentDue, which can include time information.
paymentMethod: A descriptive attribute indicating the specific method used for payment of an invoice or order. Also called method of payment, payment type, payment instrument. Examples: An invoice specifies 'Visa' as the payment method. An order used 'PayPal' as the payment method. The bill was paid via 'Bank Transfer'. Distinct from paymentMethodId, which is an identifier for the method.
paymentMethodId: A descriptive attribute providing an identifier for the specific payment method used for an invoice or order. Also called payment ID, transaction ID, payment reference. Examples: An invoice has a payment method ID '****1234'. An order has a payment method ID 'PAYPAL-XYZ789'. The payment has a method ID 'BANK-REF-ABC'.
paymentMethodType: A categorical attribute indicating the general type of a payment method. Also called payment category, payment classification. Examples: A payment method is of type 'CreditCard'. A payment method is of type 'Cash'. A payment method is of type 'Cryptocurrency'.
paymentStatus: A descriptive attribute indicating the current payment status of an invoice. Also called invoice status, payment condition, settlement status. Examples: An invoice has a payment status of 'PaymentComplete'. An invoice has a payment status of 'PaymentDue'. An invoice has a payment status of 'PaymentFailed'.
paymentUrl: A linking attribute providing the URL where payment for an order can be submitted. Also called payment link, checkout URL, pay now link. Examples: An order has a payment URL 'https://example.com/pay/123'. The invoice includes a payment URL 'https://secure.payment.com/invoice/XYZ'. The subscription has a payment URL for renewal.
penciler: A creative role relation between a comic issue, story, or visual artwork and the person who draws its primary narrative artwork. Also called artist, illustrator, sketch artist, line artist. Examples: A comic issue has a penciler named 'Jim Lee'. A comic story has a penciler 'Jack Kirby'. A visual artwork has a penciler 'Frank Miller'.
percentile10: A statistical attribute indicating the 10th percentile value within a quantitative value distribution. Also called 10th percentage point, lower decile. Examples: A distribution has a percentile10 of 10. The data shows a percentile10 of 5.5. The scores have a percentile10 of 60.
percentile25: A statistical attribute indicating the 25th percentile value within a quantitative value distribution. Also called 25th percentage point, first quartile. Examples: A distribution has a percentile25 of 25. The data shows a percentile25 of 12.5. The scores have a percentile25 of 70.
percentile75: A statistical attribute indicating the 75th percentile value within a quantitative value distribution. Also called 75th percentage point, third quartile. Examples: A distribution has a percentile75 of 75. The data shows a percentile75 of 37.5. The scores have a percentile75 of 90.
percentile90: A statistical attribute indicating the 90th percentile value within a quantitative value distribution. Also called 90th percentage point, upper decile. Examples: A distribution has a percentile90 of 90. The data shows a percentile90 of 45.5. The scores have a percentile90 of 95.
performTime: A temporal attribute indicating the duration required to execute instructions or a direction, excluding preparation time. Also called execution time, active time, task duration. Examples: A recipe's instructions have a perform time of 'PT30M'. A DIY project direction has a perform time of 'PT2H'. A workout routine has a perform time of 'PT45M'. Distinct from prepTime, which is the time to prepare supplies.
performer: A participation role relation between an event and an organization or person who performs at it. Also called artist, entertainer, presenter, actor. Examples: A concert has a performer 'Taylor Swift'. A play has a performer 'Meryl Streep'. A conference has a performer 'Dr. Jane Doe'. Distinct from performerIn, which points from a person to an event.
performerIn: A participation role relation between a person and an event in which they perform or participate. Also called performs in, participates in, acts in, presents at. Examples: John Doe is a performer in 'The Annual Gala'. Jane Smith is a performer in 'The City Marathon'. An actor is a performer in 'The New Play'. Distinct from performer, which points from an event to a person.
performers: A participation role relation between an event and its primary performers, who can be organizations or persons. Also called main artists, headliners, principal actors, featured performers. Examples: A concert has performers 'Coldplay'. A play has performers 'The Royal Shakespeare Company'. A festival has performers 'Various Artists'. Distinct from performer, which can be any performer, not necessarily the main one.
permissionType: A categorical attribute indicating the specific type of permission granted within a digital document permission. Also called access level, authorization type, privilege type. Examples: A digital document permission has a permission type of 'ReadPermission'. A digital document permission has a permission type of 'WritePermission'. A digital document permission has a permission type of 'CommentPermission'.
permissions: A descriptive attribute detailing the permissions required for a software application to function. Also called access requirements, app permissions, authorization needs. Examples: A mobile app requires permissions for 'full internet access'. A software application requires permissions for 'access to camera'. A game requires permissions for 'storage access'.
permitAudience: A targeting relation between a permit and the specific audience it is intended for. Also called target group, eligible recipients, intended users. Examples: A fishing permit has a permit audience of 'Local Residents'. A building permit has a permit audience of 'Licensed Contractors'. A student permit has a permit audience of 'University Students'.
permittedUsage: A descriptive attribute indicating the allowed uses or activities within an accommodation. Also called allowed uses, usage rules, permitted activities. Examples: An apartment has a permitted usage of 'Residential Only'. A hotel room has a permitted usage of 'Short-term Stay'. A conference hall has a permitted usage of 'Events and Meetings'.
petsAllowed: A descriptive attribute indicating whether pets are permitted in an accommodation or lodging business. Also called pet-friendly, animal policy, pet access. Examples: A hotel has 'pets allowed' set to 'true'. An apartment complex has 'pets allowed' set to 'Small dogs only'. A lodging business has 'pets allowed' set to 'false'.
phoneticText: A linguistic attribute providing a phonetic representation of pronounceable text using a specified markup. Also called pronunciation, phonetic transcription, IPA representation. Examples: The word 'hello' has a phonetic text of '/həˈloʊ/'. The city 'Houston' has a phonetic text of '/ˈhjuːstən/'. A name has a phonetic text for its pronunciation.
photo: A visual attribute linking a place to a single photograph depicting it. Also called image, picture, visual representation. Examples: A restaurant has a photo of its interior. A park has a photo of its main entrance. A landmark has a photo of its facade. Distinct from photos, which links to multiple photographs.
photos: A visual attribute linking a place to multiple photographs depicting it. Also called images, pictures, visual representations, gallery. Examples: A hotel has photos of its rooms and amenities. A museum has photos of its exhibits. A city has photos of its various attractions. Distinct from photo, which links to a single photograph.
physicalRequirement: A descriptive attribute detailing the physical activities or abilities required for a job posting. Also called physical demands, fitness requirements, job physicality. Examples: A job posting has a physical requirement of 'ability to lift 50 lbs'. A job posting has a physical requirement of 'standing for long periods'. A job posting has a physical requirement of 'manual dexterity'.
physiologicalBenefits: A descriptive attribute detailing the specific physiological benefits associated with a diet plan. Also called health advantages, bodily benefits, wellness effects. Examples: A diet has physiological benefits like 'improved cardiovascular health'. A diet has physiological benefits like 'weight loss'. A diet has physiological benefits like 'reduced inflammation'.
pickupLocation: A spatial attribute indicating the place where a taxi will pick up a passenger or a rental car can be collected. Also called collection point, pick-up point, embarkation point. Examples: A taxi reservation has a pickup location of 'Grand Central Station'. A rental car reservation has a pickup location of 'Airport Terminal 1'. The ride-share booking has a pickup location at 'Home Address'.
pickupTime: A temporal attribute indicating the date and time when a taxi will pick up a passenger or a rental car can be collected. Also called collection time, pick-up time, embarkation time. Examples: A taxi reservation has a pickup time of '2023-12-25T08:00:00'. A rental car reservation has a pickup time of '2024-01-01T10:30:00'. The ride-share booking has a pickup time of 'now'.
playMode: A descriptive attribute indicating the supported gameplay modes for a video game or series, such as single-player, multi-player, or co-op. Also called game mode, player configuration, gameplay style. Examples: A video game has a play mode of 'SinglePlayer'. A video game has a play mode of 'MultiPlayer'. A video game has a play mode of 'CoOp'.
playerType: A technical attribute indicating the specific media player type required to render a media object. Also called required player, media renderer, playback software. Examples: A video file has a player type of 'Flash'. A media object has a player type of 'Silverlight'. An audio stream has a player type of 'HTML5 Audio'.
playersOnline: A quantitative attribute indicating the current number of players connected to a game server. Also called active players, concurrent players, player count. Examples: A game server has 150 players online. The server shows 2000 players online. A specific instance has 10 players online.
polygon: A geographical attribute defining a polygon as a series of space-delimited points that enclose an area, with identical start and end points. Also called geographic boundary, area coordinates, shape definition. Examples: A geo shape has a polygon '30 10 40 40 20 40 10 20 30 10'. A region is defined by a polygon '50 0 60 30 40 30 50 0'. The park boundary is a polygon 'lat1 lon1 lat2 lon2 lat3 lon3 lat1 lon1'.
populationType: A categorical attribute indicating the common type of individuals or cases within a statistical population or variable. Also called demographic group, target group, study population. Examples: A statistical population has a population type of 'Adults'. A statistical variable has a population type of 'Children aged 5-12'. The study focuses on a population type of 'Patients with Condition X'.
position: An ordinal attribute indicating the sequential position of an item within a series or list. Also called order, rank, sequence number, index. Examples: A list item has a position of '1'. A chapter in a book has a position of 'Chapter 3'. A search result has a position of '5'.
positiveNotes: A descriptive attribute providing positive considerations, highlights, or pros for a product or an item being reviewed. Also called pros, advantages, benefits, highlights. Examples: A product has positive notes like 'Excellent battery life'. A review has positive notes like 'User-friendly interface'. The service has positive notes like 'Responsive customer support'. Distinct from negativeNotes, which provides negative considerations.
possibleComplication: A medical attribute describing a potential unexpected and unfavorable evolution or outcome of a medical condition. Also called potential adverse event, risk, secondary condition, complication risk. Examples: Diabetes has a possible complication of 'kidney failure'. Surgery has a possible complication of 'infection'. A medical condition has a possible complication of 'worsening symptoms'.
possibleTreatment: A medical attribute indicating a potential treatment, drug, or therapy to address a medical condition, sign, or symptom. Also called potential therapy, recommended treatment, intervention option. Examples: A medical condition has a possible treatment of 'antibiotics'. A symptom has a possible treatment of 'pain relievers'. Hypertension has a possible treatment of 'lifestyle modification'.
postOfficeBoxNumber: A descriptive attribute indicating the post office box number for a postal address. Also called PO box number, mailbox number. Examples: A postal address has a post office box number '12345'. The mailing address includes a post office box number 'P.O. Box 789'. The company's address has a post office box number 'Box 500'.
postOp: A medical attribute describing the postoperative procedures, care, or follow-ups associated with a medical device. Also called aftercare, post-surgery instructions, recovery protocol. Examples: A medical device has post-op instructions for 'wound care'. The implant has post-op guidelines for 'activity restrictions'. The procedure involves post-op follow-ups for 'device monitoring'.
postalCode: A geographical attribute indicating the postal code for a defined region, geo-coordinates, geo-shape, or postal address. Also called zip code, postcode, mailing code. Examples: A postal address has a postal code '94043'. A defined region covers the postal code 'SW1A 0AA'. The coordinates are associated with postal code '10001'.
postalCodeBegin: A descriptive attribute indicating the starting postal code (inclusive) of a specified range. Also called range start, first zip code, lower bound postal code. Examples: A postal code range has a postal code begin of '90001'. The delivery zone starts at postal code begin 'SW1A'. The service area's postal code begin is '10000'.
postalCodeEnd: A descriptive attribute indicating the ending postal code (inclusive) of a specified range. Also called range end, last zip code, upper bound postal code. Examples: A postal code range has a postal code end of '90099'. The delivery zone ends at postal code end 'SW1Z'. The service area's postal code end is '10099'.
postalCodePrefix: A descriptive attribute indicating a common textual prefix that defines a range of postal codes for a region, especially in non-numeric systems. Also called zip code prefix, postcode area, mailing code prefix. Examples: A defined region has a postal code prefix of 'SW1'. The delivery area uses postal code prefix 'BT'. The service covers postal code prefix 'N1'.
postalCodeRange: A geographical attribute specifying a defined range of postal codes that applies to a region. Also called zip code range, postcode range, service area by code. Examples: A defined region has a postal code range from '90001' to '90099'. The delivery zone is defined by a postal code range. The service area includes a postal code range specification.
potentialAction: A behavioral attribute indicating an idealized action in which a thing could potentially serve as the object. Also called possible action, available action, actionable item. Examples: A product has a potential action 'BuyAction'. A book has a potential action 'ReadAction'. A movie has a potential action 'WatchAction'.
potentialUse: A descriptive attribute indicating the intended use of a chemical substance or molecular entity by humans. Also called intended application, human use, purpose. Examples: A chemical substance has a potential use as 'fertilizer'. A molecular entity has a potential use as 'drug component'. The compound has a potential use in 'food preservation'.
practicesAt: A professional affiliation relation between an individual physician and the medical organization where they practice. Also called works at, affiliated with, employed by, is a doctor at. Examples: Dr. Smith practices at 'General Hospital'. Dr. Jones practices at 'City Clinic'. The physician practices at 'Family Health Center'.
preOp: A medical attribute describing the workup, testing, and preparations required before implanting a medical device. Also called pre-surgery instructions, pre-operative care, preparation protocol. Examples: A medical device has pre-op instructions for 'patient fasting'. The implant requires pre-op testing for 'compatibility'. The procedure involves pre-op preparations for 'sterilization'.
predecessorOf: A lineage relation between a product model and its newer, often superseding, variant. Also called replaced by, succeeded by, updated to, newer version is. Examples: iPhone 10 is a predecessor of iPhone 11. Model A is a predecessor of Model B. The old software version is a predecessor of the new one. Distinct from successorOf, which points from a newer variant to an older one.
pregnancyCategory: A medical attribute indicating the pregnancy category assigned to a drug. Also called drug safety in pregnancy, pregnancy risk classification. Examples: A drug has a pregnancy category of 'Category C'. The medication is assigned pregnancy category 'B'. This drug falls under pregnancy category 'X'.
pregnancyWarning: A medical attribute providing precautions, guidance, or contraindications regarding a drug's use during pregnancy. Also called pregnancy precautions, drug-pregnancy risks, maternal warnings. Examples: A drug has a pregnancy warning 'Consult doctor before use'. The medication includes a pregnancy warning about 'potential fetal harm'. There is a pregnancy warning against 'use in first trimester'.
prepTime: A temporal attribute indicating the duration required to prepare items for use in instructions or a direction. Also called preparation duration, setup time, readiness time. Examples: A recipe has a prep time of 'PT15M'. A DIY project has a prep time of 'PT30M'. A cooking instruction has a prep time of 'PT10M'. Distinct from performTime, which is the time to execute the instructions.
preparation: A medical attribute describing the typical preparation a patient must undergo before a medical procedure. Also called patient readiness, pre-procedure instructions, pre-op preparation. Examples: A medical procedure requires preparation like 'fasting for 8 hours'. The surgery involves preparation such as 'blood tests'. The diagnostic test needs preparation including 'avoiding certain medications'.
prescribingInfo: A linking attribute providing a URL to the official prescribing information for a drug. Also called drug information link, medication guide, prescribing details. Examples: A drug has prescribing info at 'https://example.com/drug-info/xyz'. The medication provides prescribing info via a URL. The pharmaceutical company offers prescribing info on its website.
prescriptionStatus: A descriptive attribute indicating the prescription status of a drug, such as whether it is prescription-only or over-the-counter. Also called drug availability, dispensing status, OTC/Rx status. Examples: A drug has a prescription status of 'PrescriptionOnly'. The medication has a prescription status of 'OverTheCounter'. This drug's prescription status is 'ControlledSubstance'.
previousItem: A sequential relation between a list item and the list item that immediately precedes it. Also called precedes, comes after, follows. Examples: List item 'B' has a previous item 'A'. The current item's previous item is the one before it. In a breadcrumb trail, the current page has a previous item. Distinct from nextItem, which links to the item that follows.
previousStartDate: A temporal attribute indicating the previously scheduled start date for an event that has been rescheduled or cancelled. Also called original start date, former start date, initial event date. Examples: A rescheduled event has a previous start date of '2023-03-15'. The cancelled concert had a previous start date of '2023-07-01T19:00:00'. The postponed meeting's previous start date was 'last Monday'. Distinct from startDate, which is the current or newly scheduled start date.
price: A financial attribute indicating the monetary value of an offer, product, or price component. Also called cost, rate, charge, amount. Examples: An offer has a price of '19.99'. A product has a price of '100'. The service has a price of '50.00'. Distinct from priceCurrency, which specifies the currency of the price.
priceComponent: A compositional relation between a compound price specification and its individual unit price components. Also called price breakdown, cost element, pricing detail. Examples: A compound price specification includes a price component for 'base rate'. The total price has a price component for 'tax'. The invoice lists a price component for 'shipping fee'.
priceComponentType: A categorical attribute identifying the specific type of a price component, such as a line item on an invoice. Also called component type, charge type, fee category. Examples: A unit price specification has a price component type of 'BasePrice'. A price component has a price component type of 'Tax'. A line item has a price component type of 'ShippingFee'.
priceCurrency: A financial attribute indicating the currency in which a price or price component is expressed. Also called currency type, monetary unit, unit of exchange. Examples: An offer has a price currency of 'USD'. A product's price currency is 'EUR'. The ticket price currency is 'GBP'. Distinct from price, which is the numerical value.
priceRange: A descriptive attribute indicating the general price range of a local business, often expressed symbolically. Also called cost level, affordability, price point. Examples: A restaurant has a price range of '$$'. A store has a price range of '$$$'. The cafe has a price range of '$'.
priceSpecification: A financial attribute linking a demand, offer, or trade action to one or more detailed price specifications, including unit price and charges. Also called pricing details, cost breakdown, fee structure. Examples: An offer has a price specification for its unit price. A demand includes a price specification for delivery charges. The trade action details its price specification.
priceType: A categorical attribute defining the specific type of a price, such as a list price, sale price, or manufacturer suggested retail price. Also called pricing category, cost classification, rate type. Examples: A unit price specification has a price type of 'ListPrice'. A price has a price type of 'SalePrice'. The product's price type is 'MSRP'.
priceValidUntil: A temporal attribute indicating the date after which an offered price is no longer valid or available. Also called offer expiry date, price expiration, valid until date. Examples: An offer has a price valid until '2023-12-31'. The discount price is valid until 'next month'. The special offer's price valid until is '2024-01-15'.
primaryImageOfPage: A visual attribute linking a web page to its main or most prominent image. Also called main image, featured image, hero image. Examples: A web page has a primary image of page 'logo.png'. The article page has a primary image of page 'main_illustration.jpg'. The product page's primary image of page is the 'product_hero.webp'.
primaryPrevention: A medical attribute indicating a preventative therapy used to avert the initial occurrence of a medical condition. Also called preventative measure, initial prevention, prophylactic therapy. Examples: A medical condition has a primary prevention of 'vaccination'. Heart disease has a primary prevention of 'healthy diet'. Infection has a primary prevention of 'hand washing'.
printColumn: A descriptive attribute indicating the column number where a news article appears in a print edition. Also called column number, print layout column. Examples: A news article appears in print column '3'. The story is in print column 'A-2'. The article's print column is 'Column 1'.
printEdition: A descriptive attribute indicating the specific edition of a print product in which a news article is published. Also called edition name, print version, publication edition. Examples: A news article appears in print edition 'Late City Edition'. The story is in print edition 'National Edition'. The article's print edition is 'Weekend Edition'.
printPage: A descriptive attribute indicating the exact page name where a news article is found in a print edition. Also called page number, print location, article page. Examples: A news article appears on print page 'A5'. The story is on print page 'B18'. The article's print page is 'Section C, Page 1'.
printSection: A descriptive attribute indicating the specific print section where a news article appeared. Also called section name, newspaper section, print category. Examples: A news article appears in print section 'Sports'. The story is in print section 'Business'. The article's print section is 'Opinion'.
procedure: A descriptive attribute detailing the procedure for setting up, using, or installing a medical device. Also called usage instructions, installation guide, operational steps. Examples: A medical device has a procedure for 'surgical implantation'. The equipment includes a procedure for 'daily calibration'. The device's procedure outlines 'user operation steps'.
procedureType: A categorical attribute indicating the specific type of a medical procedure, such as surgical or noninvasive. Also called procedure classification, intervention type, medical method. Examples: A medical procedure has a procedure type of 'SurgicalProcedure'. The diagnostic test has a procedure type of 'NoninvasiveProcedure'. The treatment is a procedure type of 'PercutaneousProcedure'.
processingTime: A temporal attribute indicating the estimated duration required to process a service request through a specific channel. Also called handling time, turnaround time, service duration. Examples: A service channel has a processing time of 'PT2H'. The online application has a processing time of 'P3D'. The customer support channel has a processing time of 'PT15M'.
processorRequirements: A technical attribute detailing the specific processor architecture required to run a software application. Also called CPU requirements, architecture compatibility, processor type. Examples: A software application has processor requirements of 'x86-64'. The program needs processor requirements 'ARM64'. The operating system specifies processor requirements 'IA64'.
producer: A creative role relation between a creative work and the person or organization responsible for its production. Also called production company, executive producer, creator, maker. Examples: A movie has a producer 'Steven Spielberg'. A music album has a producer 'Universal Music Group'. A TV series has a producer 'Shonda Rhimes'. Distinct from director, who is responsible for the creative vision.
produces: An outcome relation between a service and the tangible thing it generates or provides. Also called generates, yields, creates, provides. Examples: A government service produces a 'passport'. A licensing service produces a 'permit'. A printing service produces 'documents'.
productGroupID: A descriptive attribute providing a textual identifier for a product group. Also called group ID, product category ID, collection identifier. Examples: A product group has a product group ID 'APPAREL_TSHIRTS'. The product line has a product group ID 'ELECTRONICS_SMARTPHONES'. The collection's product group ID is 'HOME_FURNITURE'.
productID: A descriptive attribute providing a unique identifier for a product, such as an ISBN or GTIN. Also called item ID, product code, identifier, SKU. Examples: A book has a product ID 'isbn:978-0321765723'. A product has a product ID 'gtin13:1234567890123'. The item's product ID is 'MPN-XYZ-789'.
productSupported: A support relation between a contact point and the product or service it provides support for. Also called supports product, provides support for, related to product. Examples: "Apple Support contact point supports iPhone.", "Microsoft customer service supports Windows.", "Help desk supports enterprise software."
productionCompany: A production relation between a creative work (like a movie or series) and the organization responsible for its creation. Also called produced by, studio, made by, created by. Examples: "The movie 'Dune' was produced by Legendary Pictures.", "The TV series 'The Crown' was produced by Left Bank Pictures.", "The video game 'Cyberpunk 2077' was produced by CD Projekt Red."
productionDate: A production date relation between a product or vehicle and the specific date it was manufactured. Also called manufactured on, made on, creation date. Examples: "A 2023 Toyota Camry has a production date of 2022-11-15.", "A vintage car has a production date of 1965-03-01.", "A smartphone has a production date of 2024-01-20."
proficiencyLevel: A proficiency level relation between a technical article and the skill level required to understand its content. Also called skill level, required expertise, target audience level. Examples: "A Python tutorial has a proficiency level of 'Beginner'.", "A deep learning research paper has a proficiency level of 'Expert'.", "A guide to advanced calculus has a proficiency level of 'Intermediate'."
program: An association between a program membership and the specific member program it belongs to. Also called part of program, associated program, membership program. Examples: "A loyalty card membership is part of the 'Star Alliance Gold' program.", "A gym membership is part of the 'Premium Fitness' program.", "A frequent flyer membership is part of the 'SkyMiles' program.". Distinct from programName, which is the textual name of the program.
programMembershipUsed: A program membership application relation between a reservation and the loyalty program membership used for it. Also called applied membership, loyalty program for, membership applied to. Examples: "A flight reservation used a 'MileagePlus Gold' program membership.", "A hotel reservation used a 'Marriott Bonvoy Platinum' program membership.", "A car rental reservation used an 'Emerald Club' program membership."
programName: A program name relation between a program membership and the textual name of the program it represents. Also called name of program, membership program name. Examples: "A frequent flyer membership has a program name 'SkyMiles'.", "A hotel loyalty membership has a program name 'Hilton Honors'.", "A gym membership has a program name 'Gold's Gym Basic'.". Distinct from program, which links to a structured MemberProgram entity.
programPrerequisites: A prerequisite relation between an educational or occupational program and the requirements for enrollment. Also called required for program, program requirements, entry criteria. Examples: "A master's program has prerequisites of a bachelor's degree.", "A coding bootcamp has prerequisites of basic computer literacy.", "A certification program has prerequisites of specific work experience."
programType: A program type relation between an educational or occupational program and its classification or format. Also called type of program, program format, program category. Examples: "A university course is of program type 'classroom'.", "A medical residency is of program type 'internship'.", "A vocational training is of program type 'apprenticeship'."
programmingLanguage: A programming language relation between software source code and the language it is written in. Also called written in, coded in, language of. Examples: "A web application's backend is written in 'Python'.", "A mobile app's source code is in 'Swift'.", "A system utility is written in 'C++'."
programmingModel: A programming model relation between an API reference and its management paradigm (managed or unmanaged). Also called API model, management type. Examples: "A .NET API has a programming model 'managed'.", "A C++ library API has a programming model 'unmanaged'.", "A Java API has a programming model 'managed'."
pronouns: A pronoun relation between a person and the linguistic terms they use to refer to themselves. Also called preferred pronouns, self-identification pronouns. Examples: "A person uses pronouns 'she/her'.", "Another person uses pronouns 'they/them'.", "A third person uses pronouns 'he/him'."
propertyID: An identifier relation between a property value and a standard or site-specific code representing the characteristic. Also called characteristic ID, standard code, vendor ID. Examples: "A product's color property has a propertyID 'RAL 5010'.", "A material's hardness property has a propertyID 'Mohs 7'.", "A dimension property has a propertyID 'ISO 2768-1'."
proprietaryName: A proprietary name relation between a dietary supplement or drug and its exclusive, often trademarked, name. Also called brand name, trade name, registered name. Examples: "A dietary supplement has a proprietary name 'MegaVitamin'.", "A drug has a proprietary name 'PainAway'.", "A diet plan has a proprietary name 'KetoBlast'."
proteinContent: A protein content relation between nutrition information and the mass of protein present. Also called protein amount, grams of protein. Examples: "A serving of yogurt has a protein content of 10 grams.", "A protein bar has a protein content of 20g.", "Nutrition information shows a protein content of 50g per 100g."
provider: A provision relation between an action, work, program, or service and the organization or person that supplies or performs it. Also called supplied by, performed by, offered by, produced by. Examples: "A parcel delivery is provided by FedEx.", "A financial incentive is provided by the government.", "A medical service is provided by Dr. Smith."
providerMobility: A provider mobility relation between a service and its characteristic of being static or dynamic. Also called service mobility, mobility type. Examples: "A taxi service has a provider mobility 'dynamic'.", "A fixed-location restaurant service has a provider mobility 'static'.", "A mobile car wash service has a provider mobility 'dynamic'."
providesBroadcastService: A broadcast service provision relation between a broadcast channel and the specific broadcast service it offers. Also called channel offers, service on channel, carries service. Examples: "Channel 5 provides broadcast service 'News at 6'.", "BBC One provides broadcast service 'EastEnders'.", "A radio channel provides broadcast service 'Morning Show'."
providesService: A service provision relation between a service channel and the specific service it delivers. Also called channel delivers, service offered via, offers service. Examples: "An online portal provides service 'customer support'.", "A phone line provides service 'technical assistance'.", "A mobile app provides service 'online banking'."
publicAccess: A public access relation indicating whether a place is open to public visitors. Also called open to public, publicly accessible. Examples: "A park has public access 'true'.", "A private residence has public access 'false'.", "A museum has public access 'true'."
publicTransportClosuresInfo: A public transport closures information relation between a special announcement and details regarding public transport disruptions. Also called transport closure details, public transit alerts. Examples: "A special announcement includes public transport closures info about subway lines.", "An emergency alert provides public transport closures info for bus routes.", "A news update contains public transport closures info for train services."
publication: A publication relation between a creative work and the event of its publication. Also called published as, associated publication event. Examples: "A book has a publication event in 2023.", "A research paper has a publication event in a journal.", "A song has a publication event as a single."
publicationType: A publication type relation between a medical scholarly article and its classification according to a catalog like MeSH. Also called article type, MeSH type. Examples: "A medical article has a publication type 'Review'.", "A research paper has a publication type 'Clinical Trial'.", "A case study has a publication type 'Case Report'."
publishedBy: A publisher relation between a publication event and the organization or person responsible for it. Also called published by, issued by, released by. Examples: "A book's publication event was published by 'Penguin Random House'.", "A journal article's publication event was published by 'Elsevier'.", "A blog post's publication event was published by 'Jane Doe'.". Distinct from publisher, which refers to the publisher of the creative work itself.
publishedOn: A broadcast publication relation between a publication event and the broadcast service on which it was published. Also called aired on, broadcast via, released on service. Examples: "A TV show's publication event was published on 'BBC One'.", "A radio program's publication event was published on 'NPR'.", "A news segment's publication event was published on 'CNN'."
publisher: A publisher relation between a creative work or financial incentive and the organization or person that publishes it. Also called published by, issued by, released by. Examples: "A book has a publisher 'Penguin Random House'.", "A research paper has a publisher 'Nature Publishing Group'.", "A financial incentive has a publisher 'Government Agency'.". Distinct from publishedBy, which refers to the agent of a specific publication event.
publisherImprint: A publisher imprint relation between a creative work and the specific publishing division or imprint responsible for its release. Also called imprint of, published under imprint. Examples: "A comic book has a publisher imprint 'Vertigo Comics'.", "A novel has a publisher imprint 'Vintage Books'.", "A children's book has a publisher imprint 'Puffin Books'."
publishingPrinciples: A publishing principles relation between a creative work, organization, or person and the document outlining their editorial and ethical guidelines as a publisher. Also called editorial guidelines, ethics policy, publishing policy. Examples: "A news organization has publishing principles outlined on its website.", "A research journal adheres to specific publishing principles.", "A blogger follows certain publishing principles for their content."
purchaseDate: A purchase date relation between a product or vehicle and the date it was acquired by its current owner. Also called acquired on, bought on, ownership date. Examples: "A car has a purchase date of 2020-05-10.", "A smartphone has a purchase date of 2023-01-15.", "A house has a purchase date of 2018-07-22.". Distinct from productionDate, which is the date the item was manufactured.
purchasePriceLimit: A purchase price limit relation between a financial incentive and the maximum price an item can have to qualify for the incentive. Also called maximum price, price cap, qualifying price. Examples: "A rebate offer has a purchase price limit of $500.", "A discount coupon has a purchase price limit of €100.", "A loyalty bonus has a purchase price limit of £250."
purchaseType: A purchase type relation between a financial incentive and the specific kind of purchase required to qualify for it. Also called qualifying purchase, incentive purchase type. Examples: "A cashback offer requires a purchase type 'new customer'.", "A loyalty discount requires a purchase type 'repeat purchase'.", "A promotional offer requires a purchase type 'online only'."
qualifications: A qualification relation between a job posting or occupation and the specific credentials or skills required. Also called required skills, job requirements, eligibility criteria. Examples: "A software engineer job posting requires qualifications like a 'Bachelor's degree in Computer Science'.", "A doctor's occupation requires qualifications like 'Medical License'.", "A project manager role requires qualifications like 'PMP certification'."
qualifiedExpense: A qualified expense relation between a financial incentive and the types of expenses that are covered by it. Also called covered expenses, eligible costs, incentive scope. Examples: "A tax credit covers qualified expenses for 'energy-efficient appliances'.", "A grant covers qualified expenses for 'educational materials'.", "A voucher covers qualified expenses for 'groceries'."
quarantineGuidelines: A quarantine guidelines relation between a special announcement and information regarding quarantine rules. Also called isolation rules, self-quarantine instructions. Examples: "A special announcement provides quarantine guidelines for travelers.", "A public health update includes quarantine guidelines for close contacts.", "A government notice details quarantine guidelines for returning citizens."
query: A query relation between a search action and the textual string used for the search. Also called search term, search string, input query. Examples: "A search action used the query 'best restaurants near me'.", "A database search used the query 'customer ID 12345'.", "A web search used the query 'how to bake a cake'."
quest: A quest relation between a game or video game series and a specific task or mission that players can complete for a reward. Also called mission, task, objective. Examples: "A role-playing game features a quest to 'defeat the dragon'.", "A video game series includes a quest to 'collect all artifacts'.", "An adventure game has a quest to 'rescue the princess'."
question: A question relation between an ask action and the specific question being posed. Also called asked question, inquiry. Examples: "An ask action involves the question 'What is the capital of France?'.", "A survey asks the question 'How satisfied are you with our service?'.", "A forum post poses the question 'How do I fix this error?'."
rangeIncludes: A range inclusion relation between a property and a class that defines the expected type(s) for its values. Also called value type, expected type, data type. Examples: "The 'name' property has a range that includes 'Text'.", "The 'age' property has a range that includes 'Number'.", "The 'author' property has a range that includes 'Person' or 'Organization'."
ratingCount: A rating count relation between an aggregate rating and the total number of individual ratings contributing to it. Also called number of ratings, total ratings. Examples: "An aggregate rating has a rating count of 150.", "A product review summary has a rating count of 500.", "A movie's average rating has a rating count of 10,000."
ratingExplanation: A rating explanation relation between a rating and a brief text providing context or justification for the rating. Also called rating justification, explanation for rating, rating context. Examples: "A product rating includes a rating explanation 'The battery life was excellent, but the camera was disappointing'.", "A fact-check rating has a rating explanation 'The claim was partially true, lacking full context'.", "A service rating has a rating explanation 'The staff were friendly, but wait times were long'."
ratingValue: A rating value relation between a rating and its numerical or textual score. Also called score, rating score, value of rating. Examples: "A movie review has a rating value of 4.5.", "A product has a rating value of 'Excellent'.", "A restaurant has a rating value of 3 stars."
readBy: A narration relation between an audiobook and the person who performs the reading. Also called narrated by, performed by, voiced by. Examples: "The audiobook 'Harry Potter' is read by 'Stephen Fry'.", "An autobiography audiobook is read by 'the author'.", "A classic novel audiobook is read by 'a professional narrator'."
readonlyValue: A readonly value relation indicating whether a property's value is immutable. Also called immutable property, fixed value. Examples: "A property value specification has a readonly value 'true'.", "A configuration setting has a readonly value 'false'.", "A system identifier has a readonly value 'true'."
realEstateAgent: A real estate agent relation between a rent action and the real estate agent participating in it. Also called agent for rent, involved agent. Examples: "A rent action involves real estate agent 'John Doe Realty'.", "A property rental was facilitated by real estate agent 'ABC Properties'.", "The lease agreement was handled by real estate agent 'Smith & Co'."
recipe: A recipe relation between a cook action and the specific recipe used as an instrument. Also called recipe used, instructions for, cooking guide. Examples: "A cook action uses the recipe 'Classic Lasagna'.", "Baking a cake uses the recipe 'Chocolate Fudge Cake'.", "Preparing dinner uses the recipe 'Chicken Stir-fry'."
recipeCategory: A recipe category relation between a recipe and its classification, such as appetizer or entree. Also called category of recipe, dish type. Examples: "A soup recipe has a recipe category 'Appetizer'.", "A steak recipe has a recipe category 'Entree'.", "A cookie recipe has a recipe category 'Dessert'."
recipeCuisine: A recipe cuisine relation between a recipe and its culinary tradition or origin. Also called cuisine type, culinary style. Examples: "A croissant recipe has a recipe cuisine 'French'.", "A curry recipe has a recipe cuisine 'Indian'.", "A sushi recipe has a recipe cuisine 'Japanese'."
recipeIngredient: A recipe ingredient relation between a recipe and the components, often with quantities, required for its preparation. Also called ingredients for, recipe components, required items. Examples: "A cake recipe includes recipe ingredients '2 cups flour'.", "A salad recipe lists recipe ingredients 'lettuce, tomatoes, cucumber'.", "A stew recipe requires recipe ingredients 'beef, potatoes, carrots'."
recipeInstructions: A recipe instructions relation between a recipe and the steps or procedures for its preparation. Also called cooking steps, preparation guide, how-to. Examples: "A baking recipe provides recipe instructions 'Preheat oven to 350°F'.", "A cooking recipe details recipe instructions 'Chop vegetables, then sauté'.", "A cocktail recipe gives recipe instructions 'Mix ingredients, then shake with ice'."
recipeYield: A recipe yield relation between a recipe and the quantity or number of servings it produces. Also called servings, output quantity, recipe output. Examples: "A soup recipe has a recipe yield of '4 servings'.", "A cake recipe has a recipe yield of '12 slices'.", "A bread recipe has a recipe yield of '2 loaves'."
recipient: A recipient relation between an action (like sending or paying) and the audience, contact point, organization, or person receiving it. Also called receiver, intended for, sent to. Examples: "A message has a recipient 'John Doe'.", "A donation has a recipient 'Charity Organization'.", "A payment has a recipient 'Vendor Inc.'."
recognizedBy: A recognition relation between a credential and the organization that acknowledges its validity or value. Also called accredited by, validated by, acknowledged by. Examples: "A university degree is recognized by 'the Ministry of Education'.", "A professional certification is recognized by 'an industry association'.", "A medical license is recognized by 'the Medical Board'."
recognizingAuthority: A recognizing authority relation between a medical entity and the organization that officially endorses it within a system of medicine. Also called endorsed by, officially recognized by. Examples: "A medical treatment is recognized by 'the World Health Organization'.", "A medical specialty is recognized by 'the American Medical Association'.", "A traditional medicine practice is recognized by 'a national health ministry'."
recommendationStrength: A recommendation strength relation between a medical guideline recommendation and its categorized level of evidence or support. Also called strength of evidence, guideline strength. Examples: "A medical guideline recommendation has a recommendation strength 'Class I'.", "A treatment guideline has a recommendation strength 'Strong'.", "A diagnostic recommendation has a recommendation strength 'Grade B'."
recommendedIntake: A recommended intake relation between a dietary supplement and the suggested dosage schedule for a specific population. Also called suggested dosage, dosage instructions, intake guidelines. Examples: "A vitamin supplement has a recommended intake '1 tablet daily for adults'.", "A mineral supplement has a recommended intake '2 capsules twice a day'.", "A protein powder has a recommended intake '30g post-workout'."
recordLabel: A record label relation between a music release and the organization that issued it. Also called issued by, released by, label. Examples: "An album release is on the record label 'Universal Music Group'.", "A single release is on the record label 'Atlantic Records'.", "A compilation album is on the record label 'Sony Music'."
recordedAs: A recording relation between a music composition and an audio recording of that work. Also called recorded version, audio rendition. Examples: "A music composition 'Symphony No. 5' is recorded as 'Berlin Philharmonic recording'.", "A song 'Yesterday' is recorded as 'The Beatles' original recording'.", "A classical piece is recorded as 'a live performance album'.". Distinct from recordingOf, which is the inverse relation.
recordedAt: A recording location relation between a creative work and the event where it was recorded. Also called recorded during, captured at event. Examples: "A live album was recorded at 'Wembley Stadium Concert'.", "A documentary film was recorded at 'the Amazon Rainforest Expedition'.", "A podcast episode was recorded at 'a conference panel discussion'.". Distinct from recordedIn, which is the inverse relation.
recordedIn: A recording capture relation between an event and the creative work that captured all or part of it. Also called captured by, documented in, featured in. Examples: "A concert event was recorded in 'a live album'.", "A historical event was recorded in 'a documentary film'.", "A speech event was recorded in 'a news broadcast'.". Distinct from recordedAt, which is the inverse relation.
recordingOf: A recording of relation between a music recording and the music composition it represents. Also called rendition of, version of, based on composition. Examples: "A music recording 'Bohemian Rhapsody' is a recording of 'the Queen composition'.", "A classical track is a recording of 'Beethoven's Symphony No. 9'.", "A cover song is a recording of 'the original composition'.". Distinct from recordedAs, which is the inverse relation.
recourseLoan: A recourse loan relation indicating whether a loan or credit allows the lender to pursue the borrower for remaining debt beyond the collateral in case of default. Also called full recourse, borrower liability. Examples: "A mortgage loan is a recourse loan 'true' in some states.", "A business loan is a recourse loan 'true'.", "A non-recourse loan is a recourse loan 'false'."
referee: A referee relation between a sports event and the person officiating it to enforce rules. Also called officiated by, umpire, judge. Examples: "A football match has a referee 'Pierluigi Collina'.", "A tennis match has a referee 'Eva Asderaki-Moore'.", "A basketball game has a referee 'Joey Crawford'."
referenceQuantity: A reference quantity relation between a unit price specification and the specific quantity for which the stated price applies. Also called quantity for price, price per quantity. Examples: "A electricity price specification has a reference quantity '4 kWh'.", "A bulk discount has a reference quantity '10 units'.", "A service charge has a reference quantity '1 hour'."
referencesOrder: A references order relation between an invoice and the order(s) it pertains to. Also called related order, invoice for order. Examples: "An invoice references order 'Order #123'.", "A billing statement references order 'multiple orders'.", "A payment request references order 'Subscription Renewal'."
refundType: A refund type relation between a merchant return policy and the specific method of refund offered. Also called type of refund, refund method. Examples: "A return policy specifies a refund type 'FullRefund'.", "A store's policy offers a refund type 'StoreCredit'.", "An online retailer provides a refund type 'ExchangeOnly'."
regionDrained: A region drained relation between a lymphatic vessel or vein and the anatomical structure or system from which it removes fluid. Also called drains region, supplies drainage to. Examples: "The femoral vein drains region 'the leg'.", "A lymphatic vessel drains region 'the arm'.", "The hepatic portal vein drains region 'the digestive tract'."
regionsAllowed: A regions allowed relation between a media object and the geographical areas where its use is permitted. Also called allowed in, permitted regions, geographical availability. Examples: "A movie streaming service has regions allowed 'US, Canada'.", "A music video has regions allowed 'Europe'.", "A software download has regions allowed 'Worldwide'."
relatedAnatomy: A related anatomy relation between superficial anatomy and other anatomical structures or systems connected to it. Also called associated anatomy, connected to anatomy. Examples: "The skin of the forearm has related anatomy 'radius bone'.", "The superficial muscles of the back have related anatomy 'vertebral column'.", "The scalp has related anatomy 'cranium'."
relatedCondition: A related condition relation between an anatomical structure or system and a medical condition associated with it. Also called associated condition, condition of, affects condition. Examples: "The knee joint has a related condition 'arthritis'.", "The respiratory system has a related condition 'asthma'.", "The skin has a related condition 'eczema'."
relatedDrug: A related drug relation between a drug and other drugs that are similar or commonly prescribed alternatives. Also called alternative drug, similar medication, related medication. Examples: "A pain reliever has a related drug 'ibuprofen'.", "An antidepressant has a related drug 'SSRI'.", "A blood pressure medication has a related drug 'diuretic'."
relatedLink: A related link relation between a web page and a URL pointing to another relevant web page. Also called external link, associated link, further reading. Examples: "A news article has a related link to 'the source report'.", "A product page has a related link to 'customer reviews'.", "A blog post has a related link to 'a previous article'."
relatedStructure: A related structure relation between an anatomical system and structures that connect to or are associated with it, but are not part of the system itself. Also called associated structure, connected structure. Examples: "The circulatory system has a related structure 'the heart'.", "The nervous system has a related structure 'the brain'.", "The digestive system has a related structure 'the liver'."
relatedTherapy: A related therapy relation between an anatomical structure or system and a medical therapy associated with it. Also called associated therapy, treatment for. Examples: "The knee joint has a related therapy 'physical therapy'.", "The respiratory system has a related therapy 'inhaler treatment'.", "The skin has a related therapy 'topical cream application'."
relatedTo: A familial relation between two people, representing a generic family connection. Also called family member, kin, relative. Examples: "John is related to 'Jane'.", "Mary is related to 'Tom'.", "Aunt Sally is related to 'Nephew Bob'."
releaseDate: A release date relation between a product and the date it was made available to the public. Also called launch date, availability date, publication date. Examples: "A new smartphone model has a release date of 2024-03-01.", "A software update has a release date of 2023-11-15.", "A new car model has a release date of 2025-01-01.". Distinct from productionDate, which is when the item was manufactured.
releaseNotes: A release notes relation between a software application and a description of changes in its current version. Also called changelog, version updates, new features. Examples: "A software application has release notes detailing 'bug fixes and performance improvements'.", "A mobile app update includes release notes about 'new UI design'.", "A game patch has release notes describing 'balance changes and new content'."
releaseOf: A release of relation between a music release and the music album it originates from. Also called part of album, from album. Examples: "A music release 'Single A' is a release of 'Album X'.", "A digital track is a release of 'The Greatest Hits Album'.", "A vinyl edition is a release of 'Classic Rock Album'."
releasedEvent: A released event relation between a creative work and the publication event marking its release. Also called release event, launch event. Examples: "A movie has a released event 'Premiere at Cannes Film Festival'.", "A book has a released event 'Book Launch Party'.", "A video game has a released event 'E3 Announcement'."
relevantOccupation: A relevant occupation relation between a job posting and the specific occupation it describes. Also called job role, occupation type. Examples: "A job posting for 'Software Engineer' has a relevant occupation 'Software Developer'.", "A job posting for 'Nurse Practitioner' has a relevant occupation 'Registered Nurse'.", "A job posting for 'Marketing Manager' has a relevant occupation 'Marketing Professional'."
relevantSpecialty: A relevant specialty relation between a medical entity and the medical specialty where it is applicable. Also called applicable specialty, medical field. Examples: "A heart condition has a relevant specialty 'Cardiology'.", "A surgical procedure has a relevant specialty 'General Surgery'.", "A mental health disorder has a relevant specialty 'Psychiatry'."
remainingAttendeeCapacity: A remaining attendee capacity relation between an event and the number of available spots for attendees. Also called available seats, remaining tickets, open spots. Examples: "A concert has a remaining attendee capacity of 100.", "A workshop has a remaining attendee capacity of 5.", "A conference has a remaining attendee capacity of 500."
renegotiableLoan: A renegotiable loan relation indicating whether the interest payment terms of a loan or credit can be changed during its duration. Also called flexible terms, adjustable loan. Examples: "A business loan is a renegotiable loan 'true'.", "A fixed-rate mortgage is a renegotiable loan 'false'.", "A personal line of credit is a renegotiable loan 'true'."
repeatCount: A repeat count relation between a schedule and the total number of times a recurring event will occur. Also called number of repetitions, event occurrences. Examples: "A weekly meeting schedule has a repeat count of 10.", "A training course schedule has a repeat count of 5.", "A daily alarm schedule has a repeat count of 365."
repeatFrequency: A repeat frequency relation between a schedule and the interval at which events will recur. Also called recurrence interval, event frequency. Examples: "A meeting schedule has a repeat frequency 'weekly'.", "A workout plan has a repeat frequency 'every other day'.", "A subscription service has a repeat frequency 'monthly'."
repetitions: A repetitions relation between an exercise plan and the number of times an activity should be performed. Also called number of reps, rep count. Examples: "An exercise plan specifies repetitions '10' for push-ups.", "A weightlifting routine includes repetitions '3 sets of 8'.", "A cardio workout has repetitions '30 minutes'."
replacee: A replacee relation between a replace action and the entity that is being substituted. Also called item replaced, old item. Examples: "A replace action involves a replacee 'old battery'.", "A document update replaces 'version 1.0'.", "A software upgrade replaces 'legacy system'.". Distinct from replacer, which is the entity doing the replacing.
replacer: A replacer relation between a replace action and the entity that performs the substitution. Also called new item, replacement item. Examples: "A replace action involves a replacer 'new battery'.", "A document update uses a replacer 'version 2.0'.", "A software upgrade uses a replacer 'modern system'.". Distinct from replacee, which is the entity being replaced.
replyToUrl: A reply URL relation between user comments and the web address where a response can be submitted. Also called comment reply link, response URL. Examples: "A user comment has a reply to URL 'http://example.com/comment/123/reply'.", "A forum post has a reply to URL 'http://forum.com/thread/456#reply'.", "A blog comment has a reply to URL 'http://blog.com/post/789/comment'."
reportNumber: A report number relation between a report and the unique identifier assigned by its publisher. Also called report ID, document number. Examples: "A financial report has a report number 'FY2023-Q4'.", "A technical report has a report number 'TR-001-2024'.", "A government report has a report number 'GAO-24-123'."
representativeOfPage: A representative of page relation indicating whether an image object accurately reflects the content of the web page it appears on. Also called page representative, content summary image. Examples: "A thumbnail image is representative of page 'true'.", "A decorative image is representative of page 'false'.", "A product photo is representative of page 'true'."
requiredCollateral: A required collateral relation between a loan or credit and the assets needed to secure its repayment. Also called loan security, collateral for loan. Examples: "A car loan requires collateral 'the vehicle itself'.", "A business loan requires collateral 'company assets'.", "A mortgage requires collateral 'the property'."
requiredGender: A required gender relation between a people audience and the specific gender criteria for inclusion. Also called target gender, gender requirement. Examples: "An event targets a people audience with required gender 'female'.", "A survey specifies a required gender 'male'.", "A product is marketed to a people audience with required gender 'unspecified'."
requiredMaxAge: A required maximum age relation between a people audience and the upper age limit for inclusion. Also called max age, age limit. Examples: "A children's event targets a people audience with required max age '12'.", "A youth program has a required max age '25'.", "A senior discount applies to a people audience with required max age '99'."
requiredMinAge: A required minimum age relation between a people audience and the lower age limit for inclusion. Also called min age, age requirement. Examples: "An adult event targets a people audience with required min age '18'.", "A driving course has a required min age '16'.", "A senior discount applies to a people audience with required min age '65'."
requiredQuantity: A required quantity relation between a how-to item and the amount of that item needed. Also called quantity needed, amount required. Examples: "A how-to item 'sugar' has a required quantity '1 cup'.", "A crafting project needs a required quantity '5 sheets of paper'.", "A recipe step specifies a required quantity '2 eggs'."
requirements: A requirements relation between a software application and the necessary components or environments for its operation. Also called system requirements, dependencies, prerequisites. Examples: "A video game has requirements 'Windows 10, DirectX 12'.", "A Java application has requirements 'Java Runtime Environment 8+'.", "A design software has requirements 'macOS 10.15, 8GB RAM'."
requiresSubscription: A subscription requirement relation indicating whether an action access or media object necessitates a subscription for use. Also called subscription needed, paywall, access restriction. Examples: "A streaming movie requires subscription 'true'.", "A news article requires subscription 'false'.", "A premium feature requires subscription 'true'."
reservationFor: A reservation for relation between a reservation and the specific item or service being booked. Also called booked item, reserved item, subject of reservation. Examples: "A reservation is for 'Flight BA249'.", "A restaurant booking is for 'Dinner at The Fancy Bistro'.", "A hotel reservation is for 'Room 301'."
reservationId: A reservation ID relation between a reservation and its unique alphanumeric identifier. Also called booking ID, confirmation number. Examples: "A flight reservation has a reservation ID 'ABCDEF'.", "A hotel booking has a reservation ID 'H123456'.", "A car rental reservation has a reservation ID 'CR7890'."
reservationStatus: A reservation status relation between a reservation and its current state, such as confirmed or cancelled. Also called booking status, status of reservation. Examples: "A flight reservation has a reservation status 'Confirmed'.", "A hotel booking has a reservation status 'Pending'.", "A restaurant reservation has a reservation status 'Cancelled'."
reservedTicket: A ticket association between a reservation and the specific ticket for that reservation. Also called associated ticket, ticket for, ticket linked to.
