Examples: `Flight Reservation` reservedTicket `Boarding Pass #123`, `Concert Booking` reservedTicket `E-Ticket for Seat A12`, `Hotel Reservation` reservedTicket `Confirmation Ticket`.
responsibilities: A description of the duties and tasks associated with a job posting or occupation. Also called duties, tasks, job functions, accountabilities. Examples: `Software Engineer Job Posting` responsibilities `"Develop and maintain web applications"`, `Marketing Manager Occupation` responsibilities `"Oversee campaign strategy"`, `Doctor Job` responsibilities `"Diagnose and treat patients"`.
restPeriods: A specification of the recommended breaks or recovery times within an exercise plan. Also called break times, recovery intervals, downtime. Examples: `HIIT Workout Plan` restPeriods `"30 seconds between sets"`, `Marathon Training Schedule` restPeriods `"One rest day per week"`, `Weightlifting Routine` restPeriods `"90 seconds between exercises"`.
restockingFee: A charge applied for restocking returned products, specified as a monetary amount or a percentage. Also called return fee, re-shelving charge, return processing fee. Examples: `Standard Return Policy` restockingFee `"$5.00"`, `Seasonal Return Policy` restockingFee `"15% of item price"`, `Electronics Return Policy` restockingFee `"$25"`. Distinct from `returnFees`, which is an enumeration of the *type* of return fees, not the amount.
result: The outcome or product generated by an action. Also called outcome, product, output, consequence. Examples: `WriteAction` result `Book`, `CookAction` result `Meal`, `CreateAction` result `Artwork`. Distinct from `resultComment` and `resultReview` which are specific types of results.
resultComment: The specific comment created or sent as the outcome of a comment or reply action. Also called generated comment, comment outcome, produced comment. Examples: `CommentAction on Article` resultComment `User's Comment Text`, `ReplyAction to Forum Post` resultComment `Reply Comment`, `ReviewAction` resultComment `Reviewer's Feedback`. Distinct from `result`, which is a general outcome of any action.
resultReview: The specific review created as the outcome of a review action. Also called generated review, review outcome, produced review. Examples: `ReviewAction on Product` resultReview `Customer's Product Review`, `ReviewAction on Movie` resultReview `Critic's Movie Review`, `ReviewAction on Service` resultReview `User Service Feedback`. Distinct from `result`, which is a general outcome of any action.
returnFees: The category or type of fees associated with returning purchased products. Also called return charge type, fee for returns, return cost category. Examples: `Standard Return Policy` returnFees `ReturnShippingFees`, `Electronics Return Policy` returnFees `RestockingFees`, `Clothing Return Policy` returnFees `NoFees`. Distinct from `restockingFee`, which specifies the *amount* of a restocking fee.
returnLabelSource: The method by which a customer can obtain a return shipping label for a product. Also called return label provision, label acquisition method, shipping label source. Examples: `Standard Return Policy` returnLabelSource `InStore`, `Online Return Policy` returnLabelSource `PrintAtHome`, `Large Item Return Policy` returnLabelSource `AtPickup`.
returnMethod: The available method for returning a product, chosen from a predefined set of options. Also called return procedure, return channel, method of return. Examples: `Standard Return Policy` returnMethod `ReturnByMail`, `Retailer Return Policy` returnMethod `ReturnInStore`, `Online Store Policy` returnMethod `ReturnAtCounter`.
returnPolicyCategory: The classification or category of a merchant's return policy. Also called return policy type, return policy class, return policy kind. Examples: `Standard Return Policy` returnPolicyCategory `MerchantReturnFiniteReturnWindow`, `Electronics Return Policy` returnPolicyCategory `MerchantReturnNotPermitted`, `Clothing Return Policy` returnPolicyCategory `MerchantReturnUnlimitedWindow`.
returnPolicyCountry: The country designated as the destination for product returns under a merchant return policy. Also called return destination country, country for returns, return shipping country. Examples: `US Return Policy` returnPolicyCountry `"US"`, `European Return Policy` returnPolicyCountry `Country: Germany`, `International Return Policy` returnPolicyCountry `"CA"`.
returnPolicySeasonalOverride: A temporary modification or override of a standard merchant return policy for a specific season or period. Also called seasonal return policy change, temporary return policy, holiday return policy. Examples: `Standard Return Policy` returnPolicySeasonalOverride `Holiday Return Policy 2023`, `Summer Sale Policy` returnPolicySeasonalOverride `Extended Return Window`, `Black Friday Policy` returnPolicySeasonalOverride `Special Return Terms`.
returnShippingFeesAmount: The monetary cost associated with shipping products back for returns. Also called return shipping cost, return postage fee, shipping fee for returns. Examples: `Standard Return Policy` returnShippingFeesAmount `"$7.99"`, `Large Item Return Policy` returnShippingFeesAmount `"$25.00"`, `Free Returns Policy` returnShippingFeesAmount `"$0.00"`. Distinct from `returnFees`, which specifies the *type* of fee, not the amount.
review: A critical assessment or evaluation of an item, such as a product, service, or creative work. Also called item review, evaluation, critique, assessment. Examples: `Product: Smartphone` review `Customer Review`, `Movie: Inception` review `Film Critic's Review`, `Restaurant: The Fancy Bistro` review `Food Blogger's Review`. Distinct from `reviews`, which is a plural form and often implies a collection.
reviewAspect: The specific part, feature, or facet of an item that a review or rating pertains to. Also called review focus, aspect reviewed, rating dimension. Examples: `Restaurant Review` reviewAspect `"Service Quality"`, `Product Rating` reviewAspect `"Battery Life"`, `Movie Review` reviewAspect `"Acting Performance"`.
reviewBody: The main textual content or narrative of a review. Also called review text, review content, review description. Examples: `Customer Review` reviewBody `"This product exceeded my expectations..."`, `Book Review` reviewBody `"A compelling narrative with rich characters..."`, `Restaurant Review` reviewBody `"The ambiance was lovely, but the food was bland."`.
reviewCount: The total number of individual reviews contributing to an aggregate rating. Also called total reviews, number of reviews, review tally. Examples: `Product Aggregate Rating` reviewCount `150`, `Movie Aggregate Rating` reviewCount `5000`, `Service Aggregate Rating` reviewCount `75`.
reviewRating: The specific rating provided within a review. Also called rating in review, review's score, individual rating. Examples: `Customer Review` reviewRating `5 stars`, `Film Critic Review` reviewRating `8/10`, `Restaurant Review` reviewRating `3 out of 5`. Distinct from `aggregateRating`, which is the overall rating of the review *as a creative work*, not the rating *given by* the review.
reviewedBy: The person or organization responsible for reviewing the content of a webpage for accuracy or completeness. Also called content reviewer, page editor, accuracy checker. Examples: `Medical Information Page` reviewedBy `Dr. Jane Doe`, `News Article` reviewedBy `Fact-Checking Organization`, `Research Paper` reviewedBy `Peer Review Board`. Distinct from `author`, which indicates who created the content, not who reviewed it.
reviews: A collection of critical assessments or evaluations pertaining to an item, such as a product, service, or creative work. Also called item reviews, evaluations, critiques, assessments. Examples: `Product: Laptop` reviews `[Review 1, Review 2, ...]`, `Movie: Dune` reviews `[Critic Review, User Review]`, `Restaurant: Pizzeria` reviews `[Google Reviews, Yelp Reviews]`. Distinct from `review`, which typically refers to a single review.
riskFactor: A factor that increases the likelihood of a patient developing a specific medical condition. Also called predisposing factor, risk element, vulnerability factor. Examples: `Heart Disease` riskFactor `High Cholesterol`, `Diabetes` riskFactor `Obesity`, `Lung Cancer` riskFactor `Smoking`.
risks: The specific physiological dangers or adverse effects associated with a particular diet plan. Also called diet hazards, health risks of diet, diet side effects. Examples: `Keto Diet` risks `"Nutrient deficiencies"`, `Fad Diet` risks `"Metabolic imbalance"`, `Vegan Diet` risks `"Vitamin B12 deficiency if not supplemented"`.
roleName: The specific designation or title of a role performed by a person or organization. Also called role title, position name, function name. Examples: `Person in Movie` roleName `"Actor"`, `Team Member` roleName `"Quarterback"`, `Project Contributor` roleName `"Lead Developer"`.
roofLoad: The maximum permissible weight that can be carried on the roof of a vehicle, including cargo and any installations. Also called roof capacity, maximum roof weight, roof rack load limit. Examples: `SUV Model X` roofLoad `75 kg`, `Sedan Model Y` roofLoad `50 kg`, `Van Model Z` roofLoad `100 kg`. Distinct from `cargoVolume`, which refers to the internal cargo space.
rsvpResponse: The specific response (e.g., Yes, No, Maybe) provided to an RSVP request. Also called RSVP status, attendance response, invitation reply. Examples: `Wedding RSVP` rsvpResponse `RsvpResponseType: Yes`, `Conference RSVP` rsvpResponse `RsvpResponseType: No`, `Party Invitation` rsvpResponse `RsvpResponseType: Maybe`.
runsTo: The anatomical vessel or vasculature that a lymphatic structure extends towards or drains into. Also called drains into, extends to, efferent to. Examples: `Thoracic Duct` runsTo `Subclavian Vein`, `Lymphatic Capillary` runsTo `Collecting Lymphatic Vessel`, `Afferent Lymphatic Vessel` runsTo `Lymph Node`.
runtime: The specific platform or interpreter environment required for executing software source code. Also called execution environment, required platform, interpreter dependency. Examples: `Python Script` runtime `"Python 3.9"`, `Java Application` runtime `"Java Virtual Machine (JVM)"`, `Web App Frontend` runtime `"Node.js"`. Distinct from `runtimePlatform`, which is a broader property for software applications and source code.
runtimePlatform: The specific platform or interpreter environment required for executing a software application or source code. Also called execution environment, required platform, interpreter dependency. Examples: `Desktop Application` runtimePlatform `"Windows 10"`, `Mobile App` runtimePlatform `"iOS 15"`, `Web Service` runtimePlatform `"Node.js v16"`. Distinct from `runtime`, which is specifically for `SoftwareSourceCode`.
rxcui: The unique RxCUI identifier assigned to a drug within the RXNORM database. Also called RXNORM ID, drug identifier, RxCUI code. Examples: `Drug: Ibuprofen` rxcui `"6065"`, `Drug: Amoxicillin` rxcui `"700"`, `Drug: Paracetamol` rxcui `"161"`.
safetyConsideration: Any potential safety concerns, interactions, or adverse reactions associated with a dietary supplement. Also called supplement warnings, safety warnings, adverse effects. Examples: `St. John's Wort` safetyConsideration `"May interact with antidepressants"`, `Creatine Supplement` safetyConsideration `"Not recommended for individuals with kidney issues"`, `Vitamin D Supplement` safetyConsideration `"Avoid excessive dosage"`.
salaryCurrency: The currency in which the salary for a job posting or employee role is expressed. Also called pay currency, wage currency, compensation currency. Examples: `Software Engineer Job` salaryCurrency `"USD"`, `Marketing Manager Role` salaryCurrency `"EUR"`, `Doctor Position` salaryCurrency `"GBP"`.
salaryUponCompletion: The anticipated salary range or distribution for individuals who complete an educational or occupational program. Also called post-program salary, expected earnings, graduation salary. Examples: `Coding Bootcamp` salaryUponCompletion `MonetaryAmountDistribution: $70k-$90k`, `Nursing Program` salaryUponCompletion `MonetaryAmountDistribution: $60k-$80k`, `MBA Program` salaryUponCompletion `MonetaryAmountDistribution: $100k-$150k`.
sameAs: A URL that identifies the same real-world entity as the item, providing an unambiguous reference to its identity. Also called equivalent to, identical to, linked identity, canonical URL. Examples: `Person: Albert Einstein` sameAs `Wikipedia URL`, `Organization: Google` sameAs `Official Website URL`, `Product: iPhone` sameAs `Wikidata URL`. Distinct from `url`, which is a general URL for the item, not necessarily an identity link.
sampleType: The classification of a software code sample, indicating whether it is a full solution, snippet, script, or template. Also called code example type, sample category, code format. Examples: `GitHub Repository` sampleType `"full solution"`, `Blog Post` sampleType `"code snippet"`, `Configuration File` sampleType `"template"`.
saturatedFatContent: The quantity of saturated fat, typically measured in grams, within a food item's nutritional information. Also called saturated fat amount, grams saturated fat, fat content (saturated). Examples: `Nutrition Label` saturatedFatContent `5g`, `Food Item` saturatedFatContent `10 grams`, `Recipe` saturatedFatContent `2.5g`. Distinct from `fatContent`, which is the total fat.
scheduleTimezone: The specific timezone applicable to the times specified within a schedule. Also called schedule timezone, event timezone, time zone for schedule. Examples: `Meeting Schedule` scheduleTimezone `"America/New_York"`, `Flight Schedule` scheduleTimezone `"Europe/London"`, `Concert Schedule` scheduleTimezone `"Asia/Tokyo"`.
scheduledPaymentDate: The specific date on which an invoice is planned or expected to be paid. Also called payment due date, invoice due date, planned payment date. Examples: `Invoice #123` scheduledPaymentDate `2023-12-31`, `Utility Bill` scheduledPaymentDate `2024-01-15`, `Consulting Invoice` scheduledPaymentDate `2023-11-30`. Distinct from `paymentDueDate`, which is a more general term for when payment is due.
scheduledTime: The specific date or date and time when an action is planned to occur. Also called planned time, scheduled date, appointment time. Examples: `Meeting Action` scheduledTime `2023-10-26T10:00:00`, `Delivery Action` scheduledTime `2023-11-01`, `Maintenance Action` scheduledTime `2023-12-05T14:30:00`.
schemaVersion: The specific version of a schema, identified by a URL or string, that is utilized within a creative work. Also called schema identifier, schema release, version of schema. Examples: `Web Page Markup` schemaVersion `"10.0"`, `JSON-LD Data` schemaVersion `"https://schema.org/docs/releases.html#v10.0"`, `Dublin Core Document` schemaVersion `"http://dublincore.org/specifications/dublin-core/dces/1999-07-02/"`.
schoolClosuresInfo: Information regarding school closures, typically provided as a URL or web content within a special announcement. Also called school closing details, closure announcement, education disruption info. Examples: `Emergency Announcement` schoolClosuresInfo `URL to district website`, `Weather Alert` schoolClosuresInfo `Text about snow day`, `Public Health Notice` schoolClosuresInfo `WebContent on school status`.
screenCount: The total number of projection screens available within a movie theater. Also called number of screens, theater screens, cinema screens. Examples: `Multiplex Cinema` screenCount `12`, `Local Movie House` screenCount `3`, `IMAX Theater` screenCount `1`.
screenshot: An image or URL depicting a screenshot of a software application. Also called app screenshot, software image, UI capture. Examples: `Mobile App` screenshot `ImageObject of home screen`, `Desktop Software` screenshot `URL to gallery`, `Web Application` screenshot `Image of dashboard`. Distinct from `image`, which is a general image of the item.
sdDatePublished: The date when the structured data associated with a creative work was generated or published. Also called structured data publication date, metadata publish date, data generation date. Examples: `Article JSON-LD` sdDatePublished `2023-10-26`, `Recipe Structured Data` sdDatePublished `2023-09-15`, `Event Markup` sdDatePublished `2023-08-01`. Distinct from `datePublished`, which is the publication date of the creative work itself.
sdLicense: The license document, often specified by a URL, that governs the use of the structured data within a creative work. Also called structured data license, metadata license, data usage terms. Examples: `Dataset Markup` sdLicense `CreativeWork: Open Data License`, `Article Structured Data` sdLicense `URL to Creative Commons license`, `Recipe JSON-LD` sdLicense `URL to specific terms`. Distinct from `license`, which is the license for the creative work itself.
sdPublisher: The person or organization responsible for generating and publishing the structured data markup for a creative work. Also called structured data provider, metadata publisher, data markup creator. Examples: `Article Structured Data` sdPublisher `Schema.org Generator`, `Open Data Project` sdPublisher `University Research Group`, `Student Project` sdPublisher `Jane Doe`. Distinct from `publisher`, which is the publisher of the creative work itself.
season: A specific season within a radio, TV, or video game series. Also called series season, season of show, installment season. Examples: `TV Series: The Crown` season `CreativeWorkSeason: Season 4`, `Video Game Series: FIFA` season `URL to FIFA 23 Season`, `Radio Series: The Archers` season `CreativeWorkSeason: 2022 Season`. Distinct from `seasons`, which is the plural form.
seasonNumber: The numerical or textual identifier indicating a season's position within an ordered series of seasons. Also called season index, season position, season number in series. Examples: `TV Show Season` seasonNumber `1`, `Anime Series Season` seasonNumber `"Part 2"`, `Video Game Season Pass` seasonNumber `3`.
seasonalOverride: A temporary modification of shipping conditions that applies during a specific limited period, often seasonal. Also called seasonal shipping change, temporary shipping rules, holiday shipping policy. Examples: `Standard Shipping Conditions` seasonalOverride `OpeningHoursSpecification for Christmas`, `Summer Shipping Policy` seasonalOverride `OpeningHoursSpecification for June-August`, `Black Friday Shipping` seasonalOverride `OpeningHoursSpecification for Nov 25-28`. Distinct from `returnPolicySeasonalOverride`, which is specific to return policies.
seasons: A collection of seasons that constitute a radio, TV, or video game series. Also called series seasons, show seasons, installments. Examples: `TV Series: Game of Thrones` seasons `[Season 1, Season 2, ...]`, `Video Game Series: Call of Duty` seasons `[Modern Warfare Season, Cold War Season]`, `Radio Drama` seasons `[Season A, Season B]`. Distinct from `season`, which typically refers to a single season.
seatNumber: The specific identifier for a reserved seat, such as a number. Also called seat ID, seat number, specific seat. Examples: `Concert Ticket Seat` seatNumber `"27"`, `Airplane Seat` seatNumber `"14A"`, `Theater Seat` seatNumber `"Row C, Seat 5"`. Distinct from `seatRow` or `seatSection`, which are broader location indicators.
seatRow: The row identifier for a reserved seat. Also called row ID, seat row, row number. Examples: `Concert Ticket Seat` seatRow `"B"`, `Airplane Seat` seatRow `"14"`, `Theater Seat` seatRow `"Orchestra Row C"`. Distinct from `seatNumber` or `seatSection`.
seatSection: The section identifier for a reserved seat within a larger venue. Also called seat area, section name, seating zone. Examples: `Concert Ticket Seat` seatSection `"Orchestra"`, `Stadium Seat` seatSection `"Upper Deck"`, `Theater Seat` seatSection `"Balcony"`. Distinct from `seatNumber` or `seatRow`.
seatingCapacity: The maximum number of individuals that can be accommodated with seating in a vehicle, considering both physical space and legal limits. Also called passenger capacity, seat count, number of seats. Examples: `Car Model X` seatingCapacity `5`, `Bus Model Y` seatingCapacity `50`, `Airplane Model Z` seatingCapacity `200`.
seatingType: The classification or category of a seat, indicating its type or class. Also called seat class, seat category, type of seating. Examples: `Airplane Seat` seatingType `"Economy Class"`, `Theater Seat` seatingType `"Premium"`, `Train Seat` seatingType `"First Class"`.
secondaryPrevention: A preventative therapy or intervention aimed at preventing the recurrence of a medical condition after an initial episode. Also called relapse prevention, post-episode prevention, reoccurrence therapy. Examples: `Heart Attack` secondaryPrevention `Aspirin Therapy`, `Stroke` secondaryPrevention `Lifestyle Modification: Diet and Exercise`, `Depression` secondaryPrevention `Medical Therapy: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy`. Distinct from `primaryPrevention`, which aims to prevent the *initial* occurrence.
securityClearanceRequirement: A description or URL detailing the security clearance level or requirements necessary for a job. Also called clearance needed, security level, job clearance. Examples: `Government Job` securityClearanceRequirement `"Top Secret"`, `Defense Contractor Role` securityClearanceRequirement `URL to clearance guidelines`, `IT Security Position` securityClearanceRequirement `"Secret Clearance Required"`.
securityScreening: The specific type of security screening that a passenger is required to undergo for a flight reservation. Also called passenger screening, security check type, airport security process. Examples: `Flight Reservation` securityScreening `"TSA PreCheck"`, `International Flight` securityScreening `"Standard Security Screening"`, `Domestic Flight` securityScreening `"Enhanced Screening"`.
seeks: A demand for specific products or services expressed by an organization or person. Also called desires, looks for, requests, requires. Examples: `Company X` seeks `Demand for Software Developers`, `Person Y` seeks `Demand for Used Car`, `Organization Z` seeks `Demand for Consulting Services`. Distinct from `offers`, which is about what is provided.
seller: The organization or person that offers, sells, leases, lends, or loans goods or services. Also called vendor, merchant, provider, retailer. Examples: `BuyAction` seller `Amazon`, `Offer for Product` seller `Best Buy`, `Flight Booking` seller `Airline X`. Distinct from `customer` or `buyer`.
sender: The audience, organization, or person initiating and transmitting a message or action. Also called originator, dispatcher, message source, sender of message. Examples: `Email Message` sender `John Doe`, `ReceiveAction` sender `Customer Service`, `Broadcast Message` sender `News Organization`. Distinct from `recipient`, which is the receiving party.
sensoryRequirement: A description, defined term, or URL detailing the sensory abilities (e.g., hearing, vision) required for a job. Also called sensory abilities, perceptual requirements, job sensory needs. Examples: `Call Center Job` sensoryRequirement `"Excellent hearing"`, `Graphic Designer Role` sensoryRequirement `"Normal color vision"`, `Pilot Position` sensoryRequirement `URL to FAA medical standards`. Distinct from `physicalRequirement`, which is about physical capabilities.
sensoryUnit: The neurological pathway or anatomical structure that transmits sensory information to the brain or spinal cord. Also called sensory pathway, afferent pathway, nerve input. Examples: `Optic Nerve` sensoryUnit `Retina`, `Auditory Nerve` sensoryUnit `Cochlea`, `Median Nerve` sensoryUnit `Skin of Hand`. Distinct from `motorUnit`, which transmits motor commands.
serialNumber: A unique alphanumeric identifier assigned to a specific individual product. Also called product ID, unique identifier, item serial. Examples: `Laptop` serialNumber `"C02X12345678"`, `Offer for Phone` serialNumber `"SN12345ABC"`, `Demand for Specific Part` serialNumber `"XYZ98765"`. Distinct from `sku`, which is a merchant-specific identifier for a *type* of product, not an individual one.
seriousAdverseOutcome: A severe complication or side effect, such as death, disability, or life-threatening conditions, that may result from a medical device or therapy. Also called severe side effect, major complication, critical adverse event. Examples: `Chemotherapy` seriousAdverseOutcome `Severe Immunosuppression`, `Surgical Procedure` seriousAdverseOutcome `Infection`, `Medical Device Implant` seriousAdverseOutcome `Device Malfunction Leading to Injury`. Distinct from `adverseOutcome`, which is a more general adverse event.
serverStatus: The current operational status of a game server. Also called server state, game server condition, operational status. Examples: `Game Server A` serverStatus `Online`, `Game Server B` serverStatus `Offline`, `Game Server C` serverStatus `Maintenance`.
servesCuisine: The type of culinary style or cuisine offered by a food establishment. Also called cuisine type, food style, restaurant cuisine. Examples: `Restaurant: Italian Bistro` servesCuisine `"Italian"`, `Food Truck: Taco Heaven` servesCuisine `"Mexican"`, `Cafe: French Delights` servesCuisine `"French"`.
serviceArea: The geographical region or area where a service is available or provided. Also called service region, coverage area, operational zone. Examples: `Delivery Service` serviceArea `GeoShape: New York City`, `Local Business` serviceArea `AdministrativeArea: California`, `Customer Support` serviceArea `Place: United States`. Distinct from `areaServed`, which is a more general property for things like organizations.
serviceAudience: The specific group of people or entities for whom a service is intended or eligible. Also called target audience, service recipients, eligible users. Examples: `Healthcare Service` serviceAudience `Audience: Seniors`, `Educational Service` serviceAudience `Audience: Students`, `Financial Service` serviceAudience `Audience: Small Businesses`.
serviceLocation: The physical place where a service can be accessed or obtained. Also called service access point, physical service location, service venue. Examples: `Bank Service Channel` serviceLocation `Bank Branch`, `Government Service Channel` serviceLocation `City Hall`, `Repair Service Channel` serviceLocation `Repair Shop`. Distinct from `serviceArea`, which is the broader geographic region.
serviceOperator: The organization responsible for operating a government service, distinct from the primary provider. Also called service management, operating entity, service subcontractor. Examples: `Public Transport Service` serviceOperator `Transit Authority`, `Waste Collection Service` serviceOperator `Private Waste Management Company`, `National Park Service` serviceOperator `Local Park Management`. Distinct from `provider`, which is the primary organization offering the service.
serviceOutput: The tangible item or product that is generated or delivered as a result of a service. Also called service product, service deliverable, output of service. Examples: `Passport Application Service` serviceOutput `Passport`, `Permit Application Service` serviceOutput `Building Permit`, `Printing Service` serviceOutput `Printed Documents`.
servicePhone: The contact point, typically a phone number, used to access a service. Also called service contact number, service hotline, phone access. Examples: `Customer Support Channel` servicePhone `ContactPoint: 1-800-XXX-XXXX`, `Emergency Service Channel` servicePhone `ContactPoint: 911`, `Booking Service Channel` servicePhone `ContactPoint: Local Booking Line`. Distinct from `telephone`, which is a general phone number for an entity.
servicePostalAddress: The postal address designated for accessing a service via mail. Also called service mailing address, postal access address, mail-in service address. Examples: `Government Service Channel` servicePostalAddress `PostalAddress: P.O. Box 123`, `Mail-in Repair Service` servicePostalAddress `PostalAddress: Service Center Address`, `Subscription Service` servicePostalAddress `PostalAddress: Billing Department`. Distinct from `address`, which is a general address for an entity.
serviceSmsNumber: The contact point, typically a phone number, used to access a service via text message (SMS). Also called service text number, SMS access, text message service. Examples: `Customer Support Channel` serviceSmsNumber `ContactPoint: 555-TEXT-HELP`, `Alert Service` serviceSmsNumber `ContactPoint: 222-ALERTS`, `Booking Service` serviceSmsNumber `ContactPoint: 444-BOOK`. Distinct from `servicePhone`, which is for voice calls.
serviceType: The classification or category of a service being offered, such as government benefits or emergency relief. Also called service category, type of offering, service classification. Examples: `Government Service` serviceType `GovernmentBenefitsType: VeteransBenefits`, `Community Service` serviceType `"Emergency Relief"`, `Healthcare Service` serviceType `"Telemedicine"`.
serviceUrl: The URL of the website used to access a service. Also called service website, online service portal, service access URL. Examples: `Online Banking Channel` serviceUrl `URL: bank.com/online`, `Government Portal` serviceUrl `URL: gov.agency/services`, `E-commerce Service` serviceUrl `URL: shop.com/support`. Distinct from `url`, which is a general URL for an entity.
servingSize: The specified quantity of a food item that constitutes a single serving, expressed in terms of volume or mass. Also called portion size, single serving amount, recommended serving. Examples: `Nutrition Label` servingSize `"1 cup"`, `Cereal Box` servingSize `"30g"`, `Beverage Bottle` servingSize `"250ml"`.
sha256: The SHA256 cryptographic hash value of the content of a media object. Also called content hash, file hash, SHA256 checksum. Examples: `Image File` sha256 `"a1b2c3d4e5f6..."`, `Video Clip` sha256 `"f6e5d4c3b2a1..."`, `Document` sha256 `"1234567890ab..."`.
sharedContent: A creative work, such as an image, video, or audio clip, that is included or shared within a comment or social media posting. Also called embedded content, attached media, shared media. Examples: `Social Media Post` sharedContent `ImageObject: Photo of event`, `Blog Comment` sharedContent `VideoObject: YouTube link`, `Forum Post` sharedContent `AudioObject: Podcast snippet`. Distinct from `mentions`, which is a reference to another entity, not necessarily embedded content.
shippingConditions: The specific terms, constraints, and pricing details that apply to a shipping service. Also called shipping terms, delivery conditions, freight rules. Examples: `Standard Shipping Service` shippingConditions `ShippingConditions: Free Shipping over $50`, `Express Shipping Service` shippingConditions `ShippingConditions: Next-Day Delivery`, `International Shipping` shippingConditions `ShippingConditions: Customs Duties Apply`. Distinct from `shippingDetails`, which is for an offer.
shippingDestination: The specified geographical region or regions where shipping is available or targeted. Also called delivery destination, shipping region, target delivery area. Examples: `Shipping Rate Settings` shippingDestination `DefinedRegion: US Postal Codes 90000-90210`, `Offer Shipping Details` shippingDestination `DefinedRegion: European Union`, `Delivery Time Settings` shippingDestination `DefinedRegion: North America`. Distinct from `shippingOrigin`, which is where the shipment comes from.
shippingDetails: Comprehensive information regarding the shipping policies and available options for a specific offer. Also called offer shipping info, delivery options, shipping terms for offer. Examples: `Product Offer` shippingDetails `OfferShippingDetails: Free Standard Shipping`, `Service Offer` shippingDetails `OfferShippingDetails: Expedited Delivery Available`, `Limited Time Offer` shippingDetails `OfferShippingDetails: International Shipping Excluded`. Distinct from `shippingConditions`, which is for a shipping service.
shippingOrigin: The geographical region or location from which a shipment originates. Also called shipment source, origin of delivery, dispatch location. Examples: `Offer Shipping Details` shippingOrigin `DefinedRegion: California`, `Shipping Conditions` shippingOrigin `DefinedRegion: Warehouse A`, `International Shipment` shippingOrigin `DefinedRegion: China`. Distinct from `shippingDestination`, which is where the shipment goes.
shippingRate: The cost associated with shipping an item to a particular destination. Also called delivery cost, postage fee, freight charge. Examples: `Offer Shipping Details` shippingRate `MonetaryAmount: $5.99`, `Shipping Conditions` shippingRate `ShippingRateSettings: Calculated at Checkout`, `Shipping Rate Settings` shippingRate `MonetaryAmount: €10.00`. Distinct from `returnShippingFeesAmount`, which is for returns.
sibling: A familial relationship between two people who share at least one parent. Also called brother, sister, kin, family member. Examples: `John Doe` sibling `Jane Doe`, `Mary Smith` sibling `Tom Smith`, `Alice Brown` sibling `Bob Brown`. Distinct from `siblings`, which is the plural form.
siblings: A collection of familial relationships between a person and their brothers and sisters. Also called brothers and sisters, kin, family members. Examples: `John Doe` siblings `[Jane Doe, Peter Doe]`, `Mary Smith` siblings `[Tom Smith]`, `Alice Brown` siblings `[Bob Brown, Carol Brown, David Brown]`. Distinct from `sibling`, which typically refers to a single sibling.
signDetected: A medical sign or objective indicator identified through a medical test. Also called test finding, detected symptom, medical indicator. Examples: `Blood Test` signDetected `MedicalSign: Elevated White Blood Cell Count`, `X-Ray` signDetected `MedicalSign: Bone Fracture`, `Physical Exam` signDetected `MedicalSign: Swelling`. Distinct from `symptom`, which is a subjective experience.
signOrSymptom: An objective sign or subjective symptom that is a manifestation of a medical condition. Also called condition indicator, medical manifestation, health sign. Examples: `Flu` signOrSymptom `MedicalSignOrSymptom: Fever`, `Depression` signOrSymptom `MedicalSignOrSymptom: Persistent Sadness`, `Broken Leg` signOrSymptom `MedicalSignOrSymptom: Swelling`. Distinct from `diagnosis`, which is the identification of the condition itself.
significance: The medical or diagnostic importance of superficial anatomy, indicating how its characteristics may suggest underlying conditions or treatments. Also called clinical relevance, diagnostic implication, anatomical importance. Examples: `Skin Lesion` significance `"May indicate melanoma"`, `Swollen Lymph Node` significance `"Could suggest infection"`, `Discolored Nail Bed` significance `"Possible circulatory issue"`.
significantLink: A prominent and frequently clicked non-navigation URL found on a webpage. Also called important link, key URL, primary link. Examples: `Product Page` significantLink `URL to "Add to Cart"`, `Article Page` significantLink `URL to "Download PDF"`, `Homepage` significantLink `URL to "About Us"`. Distinct from `significantLinks`, which is the plural form.
significantLinks: A collection of prominent and frequently clicked non-navigation URLs found on a webpage. Also called important links, key URLs, primary links. Examples: `Product Page` significantLinks `[URL to "Buy Now", URL to "Reviews"]`, `Article Page` significantLinks `[URL to "Related Articles", URL to "Author Bio"]`, `Homepage` significantLinks `[URL to "Services", URL to "Contact"]`. Distinct from `significantLink`, which typically refers to a single link.
size: The standardized dimensions or measurement of a product or creative work. Also called dimensions, measurement, product size, item size. Examples: `T-Shirt` size `"XL"`, `Book` size `SizeSpecification: 6x9 inches`, `Shoe` size `QuantitativeValue: 10 US`. Distinct from `width`, `height`, `depth`, `weight`, which are specific dimensions.
sizeGroup: The classification or category of a product's size, often used in fashion to define target audiences. Also called size type, size segment, apparel size group. Examples: `Dress Size` sizeGroup `"Petite"`, `Jeans Size` sizeGroup `"Men's Big and Tall"`, `Children's Clothing` sizeGroup `"Toddler"`. Distinct from `sizeSystem`, which is the measurement system used.
sizeSystem: The specific system or standard used to define a product's size, such as a country code or measurement system. Also called sizing standard, measurement system, size convention. Examples: `Shoe Size` sizeSystem `"US"`, `Clothing Size` sizeSystem `"EU"`, `International Standard` sizeSystem `"ISO-EN13402"`. Distinct from `sizeGroup`, which is a category of sizes.
skills: The competencies, knowledge, or abilities possessed by a person or organization, or required for a job or occupation. Also called competencies, abilities, qualifications, expertise. Examples: `Job Posting: Software Engineer` skills `"Python, Java, SQL"`, `Person: Jane Doe` skills `"Project Management, Public Speaking"`, `Occupation: Doctor` skills `"Diagnosis, Patient Care"`. Distinct from `qualifications`, which are formal requirements.
sku: A merchant-specific Stock Keeping Unit (SKU) identifier for a product or service. Also called stock ID, product code, inventory identifier. Examples: `Product: Red T-Shirt` sku `"RTS-M-001"`, `Offer for Laptop` sku `"LAP-XYZ-PRO"`, `Demand for Item` sku `"ITEM-ABC-123"`. Distinct from `serialNumber`, which identifies a *specific individual* product.
slogan: A memorable phrase or motto associated with a brand, organization, product, or service. Also called motto, tagline, catchphrase, jingle. Examples: `Brand: Nike` slogan `"Just Do It."`, `Organization: WWF` slogan `"For a living planet."`, `Product: Apple iPhone` slogan `"Think Different."`. Distinct from `name`, which is the official name.
smiles: A line notation using ASCII strings to represent the chemical structure of a molecular entity. Also called chemical notation, molecular structure string, SMILES string. Examples: `Water Molecule` smiles `"O"`, `Ethanol` smiles `"CCO"`, `Benzene` smiles `"c1ccccc1"`. Distinct from `chemicalFormula`, which is a simpler representation of composition.
smokingAllowed: An indicator of whether smoking is permitted within a specific place. Also called smoking policy, smoke-free status, smoking permitted. Examples: `Restaurant` smokingAllowed `false`, `Hotel Room` smokingAllowed `true`, `Public Park` smokingAllowed `false`.
sodiumContent: A measurement of the sodium content in a nutrition information record. Also called "sodium amount", "amount of sodium", "sodium quantity". Examples: "NutritionInformation has sodiumContent 100mg", "The meal's sodiumContent is 500mg", "This food item's sodiumContent is low."
softwareAddOn: A relation between a software application and an additional software component that extends its functionality. Also called "software extension", "application add-on", "plugin for", "enhances software". Examples: "Photoshop has softwareAddOn a filter pack", "A game's softwareAddOn is a DLC", "This softwareAddOn provides new features for the main application."
softwareHelp: A relation between a software application and a creative work providing assistance or guidance for its use. Also called "application help", "software documentation", "user guide for software". Examples: "Microsoft Word has softwareHelp a user manual", "The app's softwareHelp is an online FAQ", "This softwareHelp explains how to use the program."
softwareRequirements: A dependency relation between a software application and other software, text, or URLs specifying necessary components for its operation. Also called "application dependencies", "required software", "system requirements", "prerequisites". Examples: "Game X has softwareRequirements DirectX 12", "This application's softwareRequirements include Java Runtime Environment", "The softwareRequirements list specific operating system versions."
softwareVersion: An identification of the specific version of a software application. Also called "application version", "version number", "software release". Examples: "Firefox has softwareVersion 120.0", "The softwareVersion of the operating system is Windows 11", "This program's softwareVersion is 3.1.4."
source: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."
sourceOrganization: An affiliation relation between a creative work and the organization on whose behalf its creator was working. Also called "commissioning organization", "producing organization", "organization behind", "publisher organization". Examples: "The research paper's sourceOrganization was MIT", "The documentary's sourceOrganization was BBC", "This report's sourceOrganization is the World Health Organization."
sourcedFrom: An anatomical origin relation between a nerve and the brain structure from which its neurons originate. Also called "originates from", "nerve pathway source", "derived from brain structure". Examples: "The optic nerve is sourcedFrom the diencephalon", "Cranial nerve V is sourcedFrom the brainstem", "This nerve's neurons are sourcedFrom the spinal cord."
spatial: A general spatial relation between a creative work and a place, used when more specific location properties are not applicable. Also called "related to place", "takes place in", "associated location", "geographic context". Examples: "The novel has spatial Paris", "The painting's spatial is a rural landscape", "This document's spatial is the Amazon rainforest.". Distinct from spatialCoverage, which indicates the specific geographic focus of the content.
spatialCoverage: A geographic focus relation between a creative work and the place(s) that are the primary subject or focus of its content. Also called "geographic scope", "covered area", "location focus", "content location". Examples: "A weather dataset has spatialCoverage New York State", "The historical map's spatialCoverage is ancient Rome", "This research paper's spatialCoverage is the Arctic region.". Distinct from spatial, which is a more general spatial association when the specific focus is not known.
speakable: A designation of sections within an article or webpage that are highlighted as particularly suitable for text-to-speech conversion. Also called "text-to-speech section", "audible content", "read-aloud section", "speech-optimized content". Examples: "The news article has speakable the main body text", "This webpage's speakable sections are identified by CSS selectors", "The speakable content is specified by a URL fragment."
specialCommitments: A description of any specific commitments or considerations associated with a job posting. Also called "job commitments", "employment considerations", "special hiring programs". Examples: "The job posting has specialCommitments VeteranCommit", "This role includes specialCommitments for military spouses", "The company lists specialCommitments for diversity initiatives."
specialOpeningHoursSpecification: A specification of unique or exceptional opening hours for a place, overriding its general schedule. Also called "holiday hours", "temporary hours", "exceptional opening times", "override opening hours". Examples: "The store has specialOpeningHoursSpecification for Christmas Eve", "The museum's specialOpeningHoursSpecification indicates extended hours on weekends", "Due to renovation, the library has specialOpeningHoursSpecification this month.". Distinct from openingHoursSpecification, which describes the regular, general opening hours.
specialty: A categorization of a webpage's content by its domain specialty. Also called "domain expertise", "content area", "subject specialty", "field of study". Examples: "This medical webpage has specialty Cardiology", "The research paper's specialty is Artificial Intelligence", "The blog post's specialty is Vegan Cooking."
speechToTextMarkup: An identification of the markup format used for pronounceable text, such as SSML or IPA. Also called "pronunciation markup", "text-to-speech format", "phonetic notation". Examples: "The pronounceable text uses speechToTextMarkup SSML", "The dictionary entry has speechToTextMarkup IPA", "This text's speechToTextMarkup specifies pronunciation details."
speed: A quantitative value representing the speed range of a vehicle. Also called "vehicle speed", "maximum speed", "speed capability", "velocity range". Examples: "The car has speed 200 KMH", "The boat's speed is 30 knots", "This vehicle's speed range is 0-120 mph."
spokenByCharacter: An attribution relation between a quotation and the character, person, or organization to whom it is attributed within a creative work. Also called "attributed to", "quote speaker", "character says", "uttered by". Examples: "The quote is spokenByCharacter Hamlet", "The dialogue was spokenByCharacter the CEO", "This line is spokenByCharacter a fictional narrator."
sponsor: A support relation between an entity (creative work, event, grant, study, organization, or person) and the person or organization providing financial or other backing. Also called "funded by", "supported by", "patron", "underwritten by". Examples: "The event has sponsor Acme Corp", "The medical study's sponsor is the NIH", "This artist has sponsor a private foundation."
sport: An identification of the type of sport associated with a sports event or organization. Also called "sport type", "athletic discipline", "game played". Examples: "The event's sport is Basketball", "The organization's sport is Soccer", "This competition features the sport of Gymnastics."
sportsActivityLocation: A specific location relation between an exercise action and the sports activity venue where it took place. Also called "exercise location", "training venue", "athletic facility", "gym location". Examples: "The run had sportsActivityLocation Central Park", "The workout's sportsActivityLocation was the local gym", "This exercise action took place at a sportsActivityLocation stadium.". Distinct from location, which is a more general location property.
sportsEvent: A specific event relation between an exercise action and the sports event during which it occurred. Also called "event of exercise", "competition event", "athletic event". Examples: "The sprint occurred during the sportsEvent Olympics", "The goal was scored in the sportsEvent World Cup match", "This action took place at a sportsEvent marathon.". Distinct from event, which is a more general event property.
sportsTeam: A participation relation between an exercise action and the sports team involved in it. Also called "team participated", "team involved", "athletic team". Examples: "The goal was scored by the sportsTeam Real Madrid", "The race involved sportsTeam Team USA", "This action was performed by a sportsTeam.". Distinct from participant, which is a more general participant property.
spouse: A marital relation between two persons who are married to each other. Also called "husband", "wife", "married to", "partner". Examples: "John has spouse Jane", "Mary's spouse is David", "The couple includes a spouse relationship.". Distinct from colleague, which indicates a professional relationship, or parent, which indicates a familial relationship.
stage: A classification of a medical condition by its applicable stage. Also called "condition stage", "disease stage", "progression stage". Examples: "The cancer has stage Stage III", "The medical condition's stage is early", "This disease is in stage 2."
stageAsNumber: A numerical representation of a medical condition stage. Also called "numerical stage", "stage number", "stage index". Examples: "Stage III has stageAsNumber 3", "The medical condition stage has stageAsNumber 2", "This stage is represented by stageAsNumber 1."
starRating: An official quality rating for a food establishment or lodging business, typically from a standards body. Also called "official rating", "quality rating", "hotel stars", "restaurant rating". Examples: "The hotel has starRating 5 stars", "The restaurant's starRating is 3 Michelin stars", "This lodging business received a 4-star rating.". Distinct from aggregateRating, which is a summary of user-generated reviews.
startDate: A temporal marker indicating the beginning date and time of an item, such as an event, program, or season. Also called "beginning date", "commencement date", "start time", "effective date". Examples: "The event has startDate 2023-10-26", "The program's startDate is September 1st", "This role's startDate was last Monday.". Distinct from dateCreated, which indicates when a creative work was first made.
startOffset: A temporal offset indicating the start time of a clip or action, measured in seconds from the beginning of a larger work. Also called "clip start time", "beginning offset", "time offset start", "seek start". Examples: "The video clip has startOffset 30 seconds", "The action's startOffset is 120 seconds into the recording", "This segment begins at startOffset 0."
startTime: A temporal marker indicating the beginning time of an action, reservation, or media segment. Also called "beginning time", "commencement time", "start of action", "reservation time". Examples: "The reservation has startTime 7:00 PM", "The action's startTime was 10:30 AM", "The media clip's startTime is 00:01:15.". Distinct from startDate, which specifies a date, while startTime focuses on the time of day or an offset.
statType: A classification of a statistical variable by the type of statistic it represents, such as mean or count. Also called "statistic type", "measurement type", "data type", "statistical measure". Examples: "The variable has statType mean", "This statistical variable's statType is count", "The statType indicates a median value."
status: An indication of the current state or status of a medical condition, procedure, or study. Also called "current state", "condition status", "study progress", "procedure status". Examples: "The medical study has status Recruiting", "The patient's condition status is stable", "The procedure's status is completed."
steeringPosition: A specification of the steering wheel's position in a vehicle, typically for cars. Also called "steering wheel side", "driver's side", "left-hand drive", "right-hand drive". Examples: "The car has steeringPosition LeftHandDriving", "This vehicle's steeringPosition is RightHandDriving", "The steeringPosition indicates where the driver sits."
step: A component relation between a how-to guide and a single instruction, section, or creative work that forms part of the process. Also called "instructional step", "how-to instruction", "process step", "guide step". Examples: "The recipe has step 'Chop vegetables'", "The guide's step is a video tutorial", "This how-to includes a step for assembly.". Distinct from steps, which refers to a collection of steps.
stepValue: A numerical value indicating the required granularity or increment for a property value specification. Also called "granularity", "increment value", "step size", "value interval". Examples: "The slider has stepValue 1", "The input field's stepValue is 0.5", "This property requires a stepValue of 10."
steps: A collection of individual instructions, sections, or creative works that constitute the steps of a how-to guide or section. Also called "how-to instructions", "procedure steps", "guide sections", "process stages". Examples: "The recipe has steps an ItemList of instructions", "The manual's steps include text and diagrams", "This how-to section outlines several steps.". Distinct from step, which refers to a single instruction or component.
storageRequirements: A specification of the storage space needed for a software application. Also called "disk space required", "memory requirements", "storage needs", "free space". Examples: "The game has storageRequirements 50 GB", "This application's storageRequirements are 200 MB", "The software lists storageRequirements on its download page."
streetAddress: A textual representation of the street address component of a postal address. Also called "address line", "house number and street", "road address". Examples: "The postal address has streetAddress 1600 Amphitheatre Pkwy", "The streetAddress is Main Street 123", "This address includes a streetAddress component."
strengthUnit: An identification of the units used to measure an active ingredient's strength in a drug. Also called "unit of strength", "dosage unit", "measurement unit". Examples: "The drug strength has strengthUnit mg", "The active ingredient's strengthUnit is grams", "This medication's strengthUnit is milliliters."
strengthValue: A numerical value representing the strength of an active ingredient in a drug. Also called "strength amount", "dosage value", "ingredient concentration". Examples: "The drug strength has strengthValue 325", "The active ingredient's strengthValue is 500", "This medication has a strengthValue of 10."
structuralClass: A classification of a joint based on how bones physically connect to each other. Also called "joint classification", "bone connection type", "anatomical joint type". Examples: "The knee joint has structuralClass synovial", "The skull sutures have structuralClass fibrous", "This joint's structuralClass is cartilaginous."
study: A relation between a medical entity and a medical study or trial that investigates it. Also called "related study", "investigated by study", "medical trial". Examples: "The drug has study a clinical trial", "The medical condition is part of a study", "This therapy is being evaluated in a study."
studyDesign: A specification of the design methodology for a medical observational study. Also called "observational study type", "research design", "study methodology". Examples: "The study has studyDesign CohortStudy", "The medical observational study's studyDesign is CrossSectionalStudy", "This research uses a studyDesign of CaseControlStudy."
studyLocation: A geographic relation between a medical study and the administrative area where it is conducted or was conducted. Also called "research location", "trial site", "study area", "geographic scope of study". Examples: "The medical study has studyLocation New York", "The clinical trial's studyLocation is Europe", "This study is taking place in a specific studyLocation."
studySubject: An investigative relation between a medical study and the medical entity (condition, therapy, drug, etc.) that is being investigated. Also called "subject of investigation", "research focus", "entity studied", "trial subject". Examples: "The medical study has studySubject a new drug", "The clinical trial's studySubject is a specific medical condition", "This study investigates a studySubject therapy."
subEvent: A hierarchical relation between a larger event and a smaller event that is a component or part of it. Also called "part of event", "component event", "nested event", "event within event". Examples: "The conference has subEvent a keynote speech", "The festival's subEvent is a specific concert", "This event includes a subEvent workshop.". Distinct from superEvent, which points from the smaller event to the larger one.
subEvents: A collection of hierarchical relations between a larger event and multiple smaller events that are components or parts of it. Also called "component events", "nested events", "events within event", "parts of event". Examples: "The conference has subEvents multiple presentations", "The festival's subEvents include several concerts and workshops", "This event comprises many subEvents.". Distinct from subEvent, which refers to a single component event.
subOrganization: A hierarchical relation between a parent organization and a smaller organization that is a part of it, such as a subsidiary. Also called "subsidiary", "division", "affiliated organization", "part of organization". Examples: "Google has subOrganization YouTube", "The university's subOrganization is the Computer Science Department", "This company owns several subOrganization entities.". Distinct from department, which is a more specific type of sub-organization.
subReservation: A component relation between a reservation package and the individual reservations it comprises. Also called "included reservation", "package component reservation", "individual booking". Examples: "The travel package has subReservation a flight booking", "The hotel package's subReservation is a spa appointment", "This reservation package includes multiple subReservation items."
subStageSuffix: A textual suffix indicating a substage within a medical condition stage. Also called "stage suffix", "sub-classification", "stage subdivision". Examples: "Stage IIIa has subStageSuffix 'a'", "The medical condition stage's subStageSuffix is 'b'", "This stage is further refined by a subStageSuffix."
subStructure: A component relation between an anatomical structure and the smaller anatomical structures that comprise it. Also called "component structure", "anatomical part", "composed of", "contains structure". Examples: "The heart has subStructure atria", "The brain's subStructure includes the cerebrum", "This anatomical structure is made up of several subStructure elements."
subTest: A component relation between a medical test panel and an individual medical test that is part of the panel. Also called "panel component", "included test", "part of test panel". Examples: "The blood panel has subTest a cholesterol test", "The medical test panel's subTest is a glucose measurement", "This panel includes several subTest procedures."
subTrip: A hierarchical relation between a larger trip and a smaller trip that is a component or segment of it. Also called "trip segment", "part of trip", "daily itinerary", "trip leg". Examples: "The multi-day journey has subTrip Day 1", "The grand tour's subTrip is the visit to Rome", "This trip includes several subTrip components."
subjectOf: A thematic relation between a thing and a creative work or event that is about it. Also called "topic of", "depicted in", "featured in", "covered by". Examples: "The person is subjectOf a biography", "The historical event is subjectOf a documentary", "This concept is subjectOf a research paper."
subtitleLanguage: An identification of the languages in which subtitles or captions are available for a broadcast event, movie, or TV episode. Also called "caption language", "available subtitles", "subtitle options". Examples: "The movie has subtitleLanguage English", "The TV episode's subtitleLanguage is Spanish", "This broadcast event offers subtitles in multiple subtitleLanguage options."
successorOf: A lineage relation between a newer product model and its previous, often discontinued, predecessor. Also called "replaces", "evolved from", "preceded by", "derived from". Examples: "iPhone 15 is successorOf iPhone 14", "The new car model is successorOf the previous generation", "This product is a successorOf an older variant."
sugarContent: A measurement of the sugar content in a nutrition information record. Also called "sugar amount", "amount of sugar", "sugar quantity". Examples: "NutritionInformation has sugarContent 20g", "The meal's sugarContent is 15g", "This food item's sugarContent is high."
suggestedAge: A quantitative value indicating the recommended age or age range for an intended audience or person. Also called "recommended age", "age range", "target age", "suitable age". Examples: "The toy has suggestedAge 3-5 years", "The audience specification includes suggestedAge 18+", "This product is for suggestedAge 6-12 months.". Distinct from suggestedMinAge and suggestedMaxAge, which specify only the minimum or maximum.
suggestedAnswer: A proposed response or set of responses to a question. Also called "possible answer", "proposed solution", "answer option", "response to question". Examples: "The question has suggestedAnswer 'Yes'", "The quiz question's suggestedAnswer is a multiple-choice list", "This question provides a suggestedAnswer for users."
suggestedGender: An indication of the recommended gender for an intended person or audience. Also called "target gender", "audience gender", "gender recommendation". Examples: "The clothing item has suggestedGender unisex", "The audience specification includes suggestedGender female", "This product is for suggestedGender male."
suggestedMaxAge: A numerical value indicating the maximum recommended age in years for an audience or user. Also called "maximum age", "upper age limit", "age cap". Examples: "The game has suggestedMaxAge 12", "The audience specification includes suggestedMaxAge 65", "This content is suitable up to suggestedMaxAge 18.". Distinct from suggestedAge, which specifies a range, and suggestedMinAge, which specifies only the minimum.
suggestedMeasurement: A quantitative value representing a suggested range of body measurements for an intended audience or person, often for wearable products. Also called "size recommendation", "body measurement range", "fit guide", "sizing suggestion". Examples: "The clothing item has suggestedMeasurement inseam 32-34 inches", "The size specification includes suggestedMeasurement height 170-190 cm", "This product is designed for a suggestedMeasurement chest 40-42 inches."
suggestedMinAge: A numerical value indicating the minimum recommended age in years for an audience or user. Also called "minimum age", "lower age limit", "age floor". Examples: "The game has suggestedMinAge 7", "The audience specification includes suggestedMinAge 18", "This content is suitable from suggestedMinAge 3.". Distinct from suggestedAge, which specifies a range, and suggestedMaxAge, which specifies only the maximum.
suitableForDiet: An indication of a dietary restriction or guideline for which a recipe or menu item is appropriate. Also called "dietary suitability", "dietary compliance", "dietary restriction friendly", "accommodates diet". Examples: "The recipe is suitableForDiet VeganDiet", "The menu item's suitableForDiet is GlutenFreeDiet", "This dish is suitableForDiet HalalDiet."
superEvent: A hierarchical relation between a smaller event and the larger event of which it is a part. Also called "part of larger event", "parent event", "contained within event", "main event". Examples: "The concert has superEvent the music festival", "The presentation's superEvent is the conference", "This workshop is part of a superEvent summit.". Distinct from subEvent, which points from the larger event to the smaller one.
supersededBy: A deprecation relation between an older term (property, class, or enumeration) and a newer term that replaces or supersedes it. Also called "replaced by", "obsoleted by", "succeeded by", "deprecated by". Examples: "OldProperty is supersededBy NewProperty", "The deprecated class is supersededBy a modern equivalent", "This enumeration value is supersededBy a more precise one."
supply: A resource relation between a how-to guide or direction and a consumable supply required for its execution. Also called "required supply", "consumable item", "material needed", "ingredient". Examples: "The recipe has supply flour", "The how-to direction requires supply glue", "This guide lists several supply items.". Distinct from tool, which refers to a non-consumable instrument.
supplyTo: An anatomical supply relation between an artery and the anatomical structure to which it provides blood. Also called "feeds blood to", "irrigates", "provides blood for", "vascularizes". Examples: "The carotid artery suppliesTo the brain", "The femoral artery suppliesTo the leg", "This artery suppliesTo various tissues."
supportingData: A data relation between a software application and the data feed that provides supplementary information or content. Also called "supplementary data", "data feed for", "application data source". Examples: "The mapping application has supportingData a traffic data feed", "The software application's supportingData is a weather feed", "This program uses supportingData for real-time updates."
surface: An identification of the material used as the surface for a visual artwork. Also called "artwork medium", "painting surface", "material base", "substrate". Examples: "The painting has surface canvas", "The drawing's surface is paper", "This artwork uses a wood surface."
syllabusSections: A component relation between a course and the syllabus entities that outline the content for each of its sections. Also called "course outline", "curriculum sections", "module syllabi", "course content breakdown". Examples: "The course has syllabusSections for each module", "The program's syllabusSections detail learning outcomes", "This course includes several syllabusSections."
target: A destination relation between an action and its intended entry point or URL. Also called "action destination", "target URL", "entry point for action", "leads to". Examples: "The search action has target a search results page", "The button's target is a specific URL", "This action points to a target entry point."
targetCollection: A specific collection relation between an update action and the collection of things that is the target of the action. Also called "collection to update", "target set", "destination collection". Examples: "The add action has targetCollection a list of items", "The update action's targetCollection is a database table", "This action modifies a targetCollection of documents.". Distinct from object, which is a more general target of an action.
targetDescription: A textual description of a node within an established educational framework. Also called "framework node description", "educational standard description", "learning objective description". Examples: "The alignment object has targetDescription 'Understand basic algebra'", "The educational framework node's targetDescription explains the competency", "This targetDescription details a specific learning outcome."
targetName: A textual name of a node within an established educational framework. Also called "framework node name", "educational standard name", "learning objective name". Examples: "The alignment object has targetName 'Algebra I'", "The educational framework node's targetName is 'Critical Thinking'", "This targetName identifies a specific skill."
targetPlatform: An identification of the type of platform for which an API reference is intended, such as phone or desktop. Also called "platform type", "development platform", "operating system target", "device target". Examples: "The API reference has targetPlatform iOS", "The software's targetPlatform is Windows Desktop", "This API is designed for targetPlatform Android."
targetPopulation: A textual description of the characteristics of the intended or typical population for a dietary supplement or dose schedule. Also called "intended users", "demographic target", "user group", "audience characteristics". Examples: "The supplement has targetPopulation 'adults'", "The dose schedule's targetPopulation is 'children aged 6-12'", "This product is designed for a targetPopulation of athletes."
targetProduct: A compatibility relation between software source code and the software application or operating system it is intended for. Also called "compatible with", "designed for", "applies to product", "software target". Examples: "The source code has targetProduct Windows 10", "The script's targetProduct is Microsoft Excel", "This code is written for targetProduct Linux."
targetUrl: A URL identifying a node within an established educational framework. Also called "framework node URL", "educational standard URL", "learning objective URL". Examples: "The alignment object has targetUrl 'http://example.com/algebra-standard'", "The educational framework node's targetUrl points to its definition", "This targetUrl links to a specific competency."
taxID: An identification of the tax or fiscal ID for an organization or person. Also called "fiscal ID", "tax identification number", "TIN", "VAT number". Examples: "The organization has taxID 12-3456789", "The person's taxID is their Social Security Number", "This company's taxID is its CIF."
taxonRank: A classification of a taxon by its taxonomic rank, often expressed as a URI from a controlled vocabulary. Also called "taxonomic level", "rank in taxonomy", "biological classification". Examples: "The taxon has taxonRank 'Family'", "The species' taxonRank is 'Species'", "This taxon is classified by taxonRank 'Genus'."
taxonomicRange: A classification of a biochemical entity by the taxonomic grouping of the organism it is related to. Also called "organism taxonomy", "species range", "biological range", "related taxon". Examples: "The protein has taxonomicRange 'Homo sapiens'", "The gene's taxonomicRange is 'Mus musculus'", "This biochemical entity is found within a specific taxonomicRange."
teaches: An educational relation between a creative work, education event, or learning resource and the competency or learning outcome it is designed to teach. Also called "educates on", "imparts knowledge of", "instructs in", "covers topic". Examples: "The course teaches 'Algebra'", "The learning resource teaches problem-solving skills", "This event teaches advanced programming concepts."
telephone: A textual representation of the telephone number for a contact point, organization, person, or place. Also called "phone number", "contact number", "telecom number". Examples: "The organization has telephone +1-555-123-4567", "The person's telephone is 555-987-6543", "The place lists its telephone number."
temporal: A general temporal relation between a creative work and a date or time, used when more specific temporal properties are not applicable. Also called "related to time", "time context", "associated temporal period", "timeframe". Examples: "The novel has temporal the 19th century", "The painting's temporal is the Renaissance era", "This document's temporal is the year 2020.". Distinct from temporalCoverage, which indicates the specific time period the content applies to.
temporalCoverage: A temporal scope relation between a creative work and the specific time period that its content describes or applies to. Also called "time period covered", "content timeframe", "temporal scope", "date range of content". Examples: "A census dataset has temporalCoverage 2011/2012", "The historical novel's temporalCoverage is 1939/1945", "This research paper's temporalCoverage is 2015-11/..". Distinct from temporal, which is a more general temporal association when the specific scope is not known.
termCode: A textual code that uniquely identifies a defined term within a defined term set. Also called "term identifier", "code for term", "vocabulary code". Examples: "The defined term has termCode 'ISBN-10'", "The medical term's termCode is 'ICD-10-CM'", "This term is identified by a termCode."
termDuration: A duration representing the length of a term of study within an educational or occupational program. Also called "term length", "semester duration", "quarter length", "study period duration". Examples: "The program has termDuration 15 weeks", "The educational program's termDuration is 10 weeks", "This course has a termDuration of one semester."
termsOfService: A textual or URL reference to the human-readable terms of service documentation for a service. Also called "service agreement", "user agreement", "terms and conditions", "legal terms". Examples: "The online service has termsOfService a link to its policy", "The software's termsOfService are available on its website", "This service requires agreement to its termsOfService."
termsPerYear: A numerical value indicating how many terms of study are offered per year within an educational or occupational program. Also called "terms offered annually", "semesters per year", "academic terms per year". Examples: "The program has termsPerYear 2", "The educational program's termsPerYear is 4 (quarters)", "This institution offers termsPerYear 3 (trimesters)."
text: The primary textual content of a creative work. Also called "content text", "body text", "written content", "main text". Examples: "The article has text 'Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet...'", "The book's text is its full narrative", "This creative work's text is its script."
textValue: The actual textual value that is being annotated for pronunciation. Also called "annotated text", "pronunciation text", "raw text". Examples: "The pronounceable text has textValue 'hello'", "The annotation applies to the textValue 'world'", "This entry's textValue is the word itself."
thumbnail: A smaller, preview image (thumbnail) associated with a creative work, such as an image or video. Also called "preview image", "thumbnail graphic", "miniature image", "small image". Examples: "The video has thumbnail a still frame", "The image gallery's thumbnail is a reduced version", "This creative work displays a thumbnail for quick viewing.". Distinct from image, which refers to the full-size image.
thumbnailUrl: A URL pointing to a smaller, preview image (thumbnail) relevant to a creative work. Also called "thumbnail link", "preview image URL", "miniature image URL". Examples: "The video has thumbnailUrl 'http://example.com/thumb.jpg'", "The image gallery's thumbnailUrl is a link to its preview", "This creative work provides a thumbnailUrl for quick access.". Distinct from url, which is a general URL for the thing itself.
tickerSymbol: A textual identifier representing the exchange-traded instrument associated with a corporation, typically an exchange and instrument name. Also called "stock symbol", "stock ticker", "exchange symbol", "trading symbol". Examples: "Apple Inc. has tickerSymbol NASDAQ AAPL", "The corporation's tickerSymbol is NYSE GOOG", "This company is identified by its tickerSymbol."
ticketNumber: A unique textual identifier for a ticket. Also called "ticket ID", "booking number", "reference number", "ticket code". Examples: "The concert ticket has ticketNumber 'ABC123XYZ'", "The flight ticket's ticketNumber is a unique alphanumeric code", "This ticket is identified by its ticketNumber."
ticketToken: A textual or URL reference to an asset, such as a barcode or QR code, that can be used for entrance with a ticket. Also called "entrance token", "access code", "QR code link", "barcode reference". Examples: "The ticket has ticketToken a QR code image URL", "The event ticket's ticketToken is a barcode string", "This ticket provides a ticketToken for entry."
ticketedSeat: An association between a ticket and the specific seat it grants access to. Also called "assigned seat", "seat number", "ticket seat allocation". Examples: "The concert ticket has ticketedSeat Row A, Seat 12", "The flight ticket's ticketedSeat is 23F", "This ticket is for a specific ticketedSeat."
timeOfDay: A textual description of the typical time of day an educational or occupational program runs. Also called "program schedule", "class time", "session time", "daily timing". Examples: "The program has timeOfDay 'evenings'", "The educational program's timeOfDay is 'weekends'", "This course is offered during timeOfDay 'mornings'."
timeRequired: A duration representing the approximate time typically needed for an audience to engage with or complete a creative work. Also called "completion time", "estimated duration", "reading time", "viewing time". Examples: "The article has timeRequired 10 minutes", "The course's timeRequired is 40 hours", "This creative work takes timeRequired 2 hours to watch."
timeToComplete: A duration representing the expected length of time to complete an educational or occupational program when attending full-time. Also called "program duration", "completion duration", "full-time study length", "expected completion time". Examples: "The degree program has timeToComplete 4 years", "The certification's timeToComplete is 6 months", "This program requires timeToComplete 2 years of full-time study."
timestamp: A timestamp relation between an instantaneous event and the specific date and time it occurred. Also called event time, occurrence time, moment of event. Examples: "Concert timestamp 2023-10-27T20:00:00", "Login timestamp 2023-11-01T09:30:15Z", "Photo timestamp 2023-05-15T14:22:00".
tissueSample: A tissue sample relation between a pathology test and the type of tissue required for it. Also called sample type, biopsy type, specimen type. Examples: "Biopsy test tissueSample 'liver tissue'", "Pathology test tissueSample 'lymph node'", "Diagnostic test tissueSample 'skin biopsy'".
title: A title relation between a job posting and the descriptive name of the job. Also called job name, position title, role title. Examples: "Job posting title 'Software Engineer'", "Job posting title 'Marketing Manager'", "Job posting title 'Data Scientist'".
titleEIDR: An EIDR title relation between a movie, TV episode, season, or series and its Entertainment Identifier Registry (EIDR) identifier at the work level. Also called EIDR work ID, entertainment ID, film/TV EIDR. Examples: "Movie titleEIDR '10.5240/7EC7-228A-510A-053E-CBB8-J'", "TV series titleEIDR '10.5240/B123-C456-D789-E012-F345-G'", "TVEpisode titleEIDR '10.5240/A1B2-C3D4-E5F6-G7H8-I9J0-K'". Distinct from editEIDR, which identifies a specific variant or expression of a work.
toLocation: A destination location relation between an action (like exercise, insert, move, or transfer) and the final place of the object or agent after the action. Also called destination, final location, arrival place. Examples: "MoveAction toLocation 'New York'", "TransferAction toLocation 'Warehouse B'", "ExerciseAction toLocation 'gym'". Distinct from location, which is the general place where something is or occurs.
toRecipient: A direct recipient relation between a message and the specific audience, contact point, organization, or person it was sent to. Also called direct addressee, message recipient, primary recipient. Examples: "Email toRecipient 'john.doe@example.com'", "Message toRecipient 'Marketing Department'", "SMS toRecipient 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from recipient, which is a more general property for any recipient.
tocContinuation: A table of contents continuation relation between a HyperToc entry and the next default HyperToc entry to play or render. Also called next entry, subsequent entry, continued by. Examples: "Chapter 1 tocContinuation 'Chapter 2'", "Segment A tocContinuation 'Segment B'", "HyperTocEntry 'Intro' tocContinuation 'Main Content'".
tocEntry: A table of contents entry relation between a HyperToc and one of its constituent HyperToc entries. Also called contains entry, includes entry, part of toc. Examples: "HyperToc tocEntry 'Introduction'", "HyperToc tocEntry 'Section 1.1'", "HyperToc tocEntry 'Conclusion'".
tongueWeight: A tongue weight relation between a vehicle and the permitted vertical load of an attached trailer. Also called trailer tongue load, vertical load rating, TLR. Examples: "Truck tongueWeight '150 kg'", "SUV tongueWeight '300 lbs'", "Vehicle tongueWeight '200 kg'".
tool: A tool relation between instructions or a direction and an object used but not consumed during the performance. Also called instrument, implement, equipment. Examples: "HowTo tool 'hammer'", "HowToDirection tool 'screwdriver'", "Recipe tool 'mixing bowl'". Distinct from instrument, which is a more general property for any object used in an action.
