torque: A torque relation between an engine specification and the turning force of the vehicle's engine. Also called engine torque, turning force, rotational force. Examples: "EngineSpecification torque '300 Nm'", "EngineSpecification torque '221 lb-ft'", "Vehicle engine torque '400 Nm'".
totalHistoricalEnrollment: A total historical enrollment relation between a course and the cumulative number of students who have ever enrolled in it. Also called cumulative enrollment, past enrollment count, historical student count. Examples: "Course totalHistoricalEnrollment '500'", "Course totalHistoricalEnrollment '1200'", "Course totalHistoricalEnrollment '75'".
totalJobOpenings: A total job openings relation between a job posting and the number of available positions. Also called number of vacancies, open positions, available roles. Examples: "JobPosting totalJobOpenings '3'", "JobPosting totalJobOpenings '1'", "JobPosting totalJobOpenings '5'".
totalPaymentDue: A total payment due relation between an invoice and the full amount owed. Also called total amount owed, invoice total, outstanding balance. Examples: "Invoice totalPaymentDue '$150.00'", "Invoice totalPaymentDue '€250.50'", "Invoice totalPaymentDue '$75.25'".
totalPrice: A total price relation between a reservation or ticket and its full cost, including taxes and shipping. Also called full cost, final price, reservation cost. Examples: "Reservation totalPrice '$120.00'", "Ticket totalPrice '€50.00'", "Flight reservation totalPrice '$350.75'".
totalTime: A total time relation between instructions or a direction and the overall duration required to perform them, including preparation. Also called overall duration, completion time, estimated time. Examples: "HowTo totalTime 'PT2H30M'", "HowToDirection totalTime 'PT15M'", "Recipe totalTime 'PT1H'".
tourBookingPage: A tour booking page relation between an accommodation, apartment complex, or place and a URL providing information on how to book a tour. Also called tour reservation page, booking link for tours, tour information URL. Examples: "Hotel tourBookingPage 'https://example.com/hotel-tours'", "ApartmentComplex tourBookingPage 'https://example.com/apt-tours'", "Museum tourBookingPage 'https://example.com/museum-tours'".
touristType: A tourist type relation between a tourist attraction, destination, or trip and the specific audience or type of tourist it is suitable for. Also called target tourist, suitable for, visitor type. Examples: "TouristAttraction touristType 'children'", "TouristDestination touristType 'adventure seekers'", "TouristTrip touristType 'visitors from Japan'".
track: A track relation between a music group or playlist and a music recording, typically a single song. Also called song, musical piece, recording. Examples: "MusicPlaylist track 'Bohemian Rhapsody'", "MusicGroup track 'Stairway to Heaven'", "Album track 'Track 3'". Distinct from tracks, which is a more general property for multiple music recordings.
trackingNumber: A tracking number relation between a parcel delivery and its unique identifier provided by the shipper. Also called shipment ID, parcel ID, delivery tracking code. Examples: "ParcelDelivery trackingNumber '1Z999AA10123456784'", "ParcelDelivery trackingNumber 'JD0001234567890123'", "ParcelDelivery trackingNumber '9400100000000000000000'".
trackingUrl: A tracking URL relation between a parcel delivery and the web address for monitoring its status. Also called shipment tracking link, parcel status URL, delivery tracking page. Examples: "ParcelDelivery trackingUrl 'https://example.com/track/12345'", "ParcelDelivery trackingUrl 'https://shipper.com/status?id=ABCDE'", "ParcelDelivery trackingUrl 'https://delivery.com/track/FGHIJ'".
tracks: A tracks relation between a music group or playlist and a music recording, typically a single song. Also called song, musical piece, recording. Examples: "MusicPlaylist tracks 'Bohemian Rhapsody'", "MusicGroup tracks 'Stairway to Heaven'", "Album tracks 'Track 3'". Distinct from track, which can also refer to an ItemList of music recordings.
trailer: A trailer relation between a creative work (like a movie, TV series, or episode) and its promotional video object. Also called promotional video, movie preview, teaser. Examples: "Movie trailer 'https://example.com/movie-trailer.mp4'", "TVSeries trailer 'https://example.com/series-teaser.webm'", "Episode trailer 'https://example.com/episode-preview.mov'".
trailerWeight: A trailer weight relation between a vehicle and the maximum permitted weight of an attached trailer. Also called towing capacity, maximum trailer weight, permitted trailer load. Examples: "Truck trailerWeight '5000 kg'", "SUV trailerWeight '3500 lbs'", "Vehicle trailerWeight '2000 kg'".
trainName: A train name relation between a train trip and the specific name of the train. Also called name of train, railway name, train service name. Examples: "TrainTrip trainName 'The Orient Express'", "TrainTrip trainName 'Shinkansen Nozomi'", "TrainTrip trainName 'Eurostar'".
trainNumber: A train number relation between a train trip and its unique identifier. Also called train ID, railway number, service number. Examples: "TrainTrip trainNumber 'TGV 9876'", "TrainTrip trainNumber 'Acela Express 2150'", "TrainTrip trainNumber 'IC 123'".
trainingSalary: A training salary relation between an educational or work-based program and the estimated earnings during the program. Also called program salary, stipend, apprenticeship wage. Examples: "WorkBasedProgram trainingSalary '$25,000/year'", "EducationalOccupationalProgram trainingSalary '€1500/month'", "Apprenticeship trainingSalary '$12/hour'".
transFatContent: A trans fat content relation between nutrition information and the amount of trans fat in grams. Also called grams of trans fat, trans fatty acid amount. Examples: "NutritionInformation transFatContent '0.5 g'", "NutritionInformation transFatContent '0 g'", "NutritionInformation transFatContent '1.2 g'".
transcript: A transcript relation between an audio or video object and the text of its spoken content. Also called audio text, video text, spoken content. Examples: "AudioObject transcript 'Hello, welcome to the podcast.'", "VideoObject transcript 'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.'", "Lecture recording transcript 'Today we will discuss quantum physics.'".
transitTime: A transit time relation between shipping conditions or delivery time and the typical delay between dispatch and customer receipt. Also called delivery time, shipping duration, lead time. Examples: "ShippingConditions transitTime 'PT3D'", "ShippingDeliveryTime transitTime '2-5 business days'", "ShippingConditions transitTime 'PT72H'".
translationOfWork: A translation of work relation between a creative work and the original work from which it was translated. Also called original work, source work, translated from. Examples: "CreativeWork 'Don Quixote (Spanish)' translationOfWork 'Don Quijote (original)'", "CreativeWork 'The Little Prince (English)' translationOfWork 'Le Petit Prince (French)'", "CreativeWork 'War and Peace (English)' translationOfWork 'Война и мир (Russian)'".
translator: A translator relation between a creative work or event and the organization or person responsible for adapting it to different languages or translating during an event. Also called translated by, language adapter, interpreter. Examples: "Book translator 'Edith Grossman'", "Conference translator 'Language Services Inc.'", "CreativeWork translator 'Google Translate'".
transmissionMethod: A transmission method relation between an infectious disease and how it spreads, such as a route or vector. Also called mode of transmission, spread mechanism, vector. Examples: "InfectiousDisease transmissionMethod 'direct contact'", "InfectiousDisease transmissionMethod 'Aedes aegypti'", "InfectiousDisease transmissionMethod 'airborne droplets'".
travelBans: A travel bans relation between a special announcement and information regarding restrictions on travel. Also called travel restrictions, ban on travel, travel advisories. Examples: "SpecialAnnouncement travelBans 'https://example.com/travel-restrictions'", "SpecialAnnouncement travelBans 'All international travel is suspended.'", "SpecialAnnouncement travelBans 'https://who.int/travel-guidance'".
trialDesign: A trial design relation between a medical trial and the specific methodology or structure of the trial. Also called study design, experimental design, trial methodology. Examples: "MedicalTrial trialDesign 'RandomizedControlledTrial'", "MedicalTrial trialDesign 'ObservationalStudy'", "MedicalTrial trialDesign 'DoubleBlindTrial'".
tributary: A tributary relation between a vein and the larger anatomical structure or organ system it flows into. Also called drains into, connects to, flows into. Examples: "Small saphenous vein tributary 'popliteal vein'", "Renal vein tributary 'inferior vena cava'", "Vein tributary 'larger vein'".
tripOrigin: A trip origin relation between a trip and its starting location, prior to any destinations. Also called starting point, departure location, point of origin. Examples: "Flight tripOrigin 'London Heathrow Airport'", "RoadTrip tripOrigin 'New York City'", "Trip tripOrigin 'Home Address'".
typeOfBed: A type of bed relation between bed details and the specific kind of bed available. Also called bed category, bed style, bed description. Examples: "BedDetails typeOfBed 'King size bed'", "BedDetails typeOfBed 'Twin bed'", "BedDetails typeOfBed 'Sofa bed'".
typeOfGood: A type of good relation between ownership information or a type and quantity node and the product or service it refers to. Also called product type, service type, item type. Examples: "OwnershipInfo typeOfGood 'Car'", "TypeAndQuantityNode typeOfGood 'Laptop'", "OwnershipInfo typeOfGood 'Software License'".
typicalAgeRange: A typical age range relation between a creative work or event and the expected age group of its audience. Also called age suitability, target age, recommended age. Examples: "Book typicalAgeRange '7-9'", "Movie typicalAgeRange '13+'", "Event typicalAgeRange 'all ages'".
typicalCreditsPerTerm: A typical credits per term relation between an educational or occupational program and the expected number of credits a full-time student would take in one term. Also called term credits, unit load per term, average credits. Examples: "EducationalOccupationalProgram typicalCreditsPerTerm '15'", "Program typicalCreditsPerTerm '12 units'", "WorkBasedProgram typicalCreditsPerTerm '9'".
typicalTest: A typical test relation between a medical condition and a medical test commonly performed for that condition. Also called common test, diagnostic test, standard test. Examples: "MedicalCondition 'Diabetes' typicalTest 'Blood Glucose Test'", "MedicalCondition 'Flu' typicalTest 'Rapid Flu Test'", "MedicalCondition 'Broken Bone' typicalTest 'X-ray'".
underName: An under name relation between a reservation or ticket and the organization or person for whom it is made. Also called booked for, reserved for, ticket holder. Examples: "Reservation underName 'John Doe'", "Ticket underName 'Acme Corp'", "Flight reservation underName 'Jane Smith'".
unitCode: A unit code relation between a property value, quantitative value, type and quantity node, or unit price specification and its unit of measurement, typically using UN/CEFACT Common Code or a URL. Also called measurement unit code, standard unit, UN/CEFACT code. Examples: "QuantitativeValue unitCode 'KGM'", "PropertyValue unitCode 'C62'", "UnitPriceSpecification unitCode 'USD'". Distinct from unitText, which is a free-form string for the unit of measurement.
unitText: A unit text relation between a property value, quantitative value, type and quantity node, or unit price specification and a string indicating its unit of measurement. Also called unit description, measurement label, custom unit. Examples: "QuantitativeValue unitText 'kilograms'", "PropertyValue unitText 'persons'", "UnitPriceSpecification unitText 'dollars'". Distinct from unitCode, which uses a standard code for the unit of measurement.
unnamedSourcesPolicy: An unnamed sources policy relation between a news media organization or organization and a statement about its policy on using unnamed sources. Also called anonymous sources policy, source confidentiality policy, disclosure policy. Examples: "NewsMediaOrganization unnamedSourcesPolicy 'https://example.com/sources-policy'", "Organization unnamedSourcesPolicy 'Our policy requires two independent sources.'", "News outlet unnamedSourcesPolicy 'https://example.com/ethics'".
unsaturatedFatContent: An unsaturated fat content relation between nutrition information and the amount of unsaturated fat in grams. Also called grams of unsaturated fat, unsaturated fatty acid amount. Examples: "NutritionInformation unsaturatedFatContent '5 g'", "NutritionInformation unsaturatedFatContent '10.2 g'", "NutritionInformation unsaturatedFatContent '3 g'".
uploadDate: An upload date relation between a media object and the date and time it was uploaded to a site. Also called date uploaded, publication date, submission date. Examples: "VideoObject uploadDate '2023-10-26T14:30:00Z'", "ImageObject uploadDate '2023-01-15'", "AudioObject uploadDate '2022-12-01T10:00:00'".
upvoteCount: An upvote count relation between a comment and the number of upvotes it has received. Also called positive votes, likes count, approval count. Examples: "Comment upvoteCount '15'", "Answer upvoteCount '100'", "Question upvoteCount '5'".
url: A URL relation between a thing and its web address. Also called web link, web address, online resource. Examples: "Product url 'https://example.com/product/123'", "Organization url 'https://example.com'", "Person url 'https://example.com/profile/john-doe'".
urlTemplate: A URL template relation between an entry point and an RFC6570 template used to construct the target URL for an action. Also called URL pattern, endpoint template, URI template. Examples: "EntryPoint urlTemplate 'https://example.com/search?q={query}'", "EntryPoint urlTemplate 'https://api.example.com/users/{id}'", "EntryPoint urlTemplate 'https://example.com/products/{category}/{id}'".
usNPI: A US NPI relation between a physician and their unique 10-digit National Provider Identifier issued in the United States. Also called NPI number, National Provider Identifier, US healthcare ID. Examples: "Physician usNPI '1234567890'", "Doctor usNPI '9876543210'", "Healthcare provider usNPI '1112223334'".
usageInfo: A usage info relation between a creative work and additional information about its use, including licensing options, citation conventions, or purchasing details. Also called usage guidelines, licensing information, rights information. Examples: "CreativeWork usageInfo 'https://example.com/usage-policy'", "Image usageInfo 'Commercial licenses available upon request.'", "Dataset usageInfo 'https://example.com/data-license'". Distinct from license, which indicates the specific license(s) applicable to the content.
usedToDiagnose: A used to diagnose relation between a medical test and a medical condition it is employed to identify. Also called diagnoses, identifies condition, screens for. Examples: "MedicalTest 'MRI' usedToDiagnose 'Brain Tumor'", "MedicalTest 'Blood Test' usedToDiagnose 'Anemia'", "MedicalTest 'X-ray' usedToDiagnose 'Fracture'".
userInteractionCount: A user interaction count relation between an interaction counter and the number of interactions for a creative work on a website or software application. Also called interaction tally, engagement count, user activity count. Examples: "InteractionCounter userInteractionCount '1200'", "InteractionCounter userInteractionCount '50000'", "InteractionCounter userInteractionCount '750'".
usesDevice: A uses device relation between a medical test and the medical device employed to perform it. Also called device used, equipment for test, test instrument. Examples: "MedicalTest 'Ultrasound' usesDevice 'Ultrasound Scanner'", "MedicalTest 'ECG' usesDevice 'Electrocardiograph'", "MedicalTest 'Blood Pressure Measurement' usesDevice 'Sphygmomanometer'".
usesHealthPlanIdStandard: A uses health plan ID standard relation between a health insurance plan and the standard used for interpreting its Plan ID. Also called plan ID standard, health plan identifier format, ID interpretation standard. Examples: "HealthInsurancePlan usesHealthPlanIdStandard 'HIOS'", "HealthInsurancePlan usesHealthPlanIdStandard 'https://example.com/custom-standard'", "HealthInsurancePlan usesHealthPlanIdStandard 'CMS Standard'".
utterances: An utterances relation between a HyperToc entry and the text of spoken words or lyrics occurring within that section of a media object. Also called spoken text, lyrics, dialogue. Examples: "HyperTocEntry utterances 'Hello, and welcome to the show.'", "HyperTocEntry utterances 'We're going to talk about this topic.'", "HyperTocEntry utterances 'The sun always shines on TV.'".
validFor: A valid for relation between a credential or permit and the duration of its validity. Also called duration of validity, valid period, effective duration. Examples: "Permit validFor 'P1Y'", "Credential validFor 'P5Y'", "License validFor 'P6M'".
validForMemberTier: A valid for member tier relation between a merchant return policy, offer, offer shipping details, price specification, or shipping service and the membership program tier(s) for which it is valid. Also called member tier eligibility, applicable member level, valid for membership. Examples: "Offer validForMemberTier 'Gold Member'", "MerchantReturnPolicy validForMemberTier 'Premium Tier'", "ShippingService validForMemberTier 'Bronze'".
validFrom: A valid from relation between a certification, demand, financial incentive, location feature specification, monetary amount, offer, opening hours specification, permit, or price specification and the date it becomes valid. Also called effective date, start date, activation date. Examples: "Offer validFrom '2023-11-01'", "Permit validFrom '2023-01-01T09:00:00'", "OpeningHoursSpecification validFrom '2024-01-01'". Distinct from validThrough or validUntil, which specify the end of validity.
validIn: A valid in relation between a certification, credential, or permit and the geographic area where it is valid. Also called valid region, applicable area, geographic validity. Examples: "Permit validIn 'California'", "Certification validIn 'European Union'", "Credential validIn 'United States'".
validThrough: A valid through relation between a demand, financial incentive, job posting, location feature specification, monetary amount, offer, or opening hours specification and the date after which it is no longer valid. Also called expiration date, end date, valid until. Examples: "Offer validThrough '2023-12-31'", "JobPosting validThrough '2023-11-30'", "OpeningHoursSpecification validThrough '2024-12-31'". Distinct from validFrom, which specifies the start of validity. Distinct from validUntil, which is similar but for Permit only.
validUntil: A valid until relation between a permit and the date it ceases to be valid. Also called permit expiration date, permit end date, validity end date. Examples: "Permit validUntil '2024-06-30'", "Permit validUntil '2025-01-01'", "Permit validUntil '2023-12-31'". Distinct from validThrough, which is a more general property for various items.
value: A value relation between a monetary amount, property value, or quantitative value and its specific numerical, textual, boolean, or structured content. Also called amount, quantity, content. Examples: "QuantitativeValue value '10'", "PropertyValue value 'red'", "MonetaryAmount value '99.99'".
valueAddedTaxIncluded: A value-added tax included relation between a price specification and whether VAT is part of the price. Also called VAT status, tax inclusion, includes VAT. Examples: "PriceSpecification valueAddedTaxIncluded 'true'", "PriceSpecification valueAddedTaxIncluded 'false'", "Offer price valueAddedTaxIncluded 'true'".
valueMaxLength: A value max length relation between a property value specification and the maximum allowed number of characters for a literal value. Also called maximum length, character limit, max characters. Examples: "PropertyValueSpecification valueMaxLength '255'", "PropertyValueSpecification valueMaxLength '50'", "Input field valueMaxLength '100'".
valueMinLength: A value min length relation between a property value specification and the minimum allowed number of characters for a literal value. Also called minimum length, min characters, required length. Examples: "PropertyValueSpecification valueMinLength '5'", "PropertyValueSpecification valueMinLength '1'", "Input field valueMinLength '10'".
valueName: A value name relation between a property value specification and the name used in URL templates and form encoding. Also called parameter name, form field name, URL variable name. Examples: "PropertyValueSpecification valueName 'color'", "PropertyValueSpecification valueName 'product_id'", "PropertyValueSpecification valueName 'search_query'".
valuePattern: A value pattern relation between a property value specification and a regular expression for validating literal values. Also called validation regex, input pattern, format regex. Examples: "PropertyValueSpecification valuePattern '[0-9]{5}'", "PropertyValueSpecification valuePattern '[a-zA-Z]+'", "PropertyValueSpecification valuePattern '^\d{3}-\d{2}-\d{4}$'".
valueReference: A value reference relation between a property value, qualitative value, or quantitative value and a secondary value providing additional information or context. Also called reference value, contextual value, measurement context. Examples: "QuantitativeValue valueReference 'Standard Temperature'", "PropertyValue valueReference 'Color Spectrum'", "QuantitativeValue valueReference 'RPM at max torque'".
valueRequired: A value required relation between a property value specification and whether the property must be filled to complete an action. Also called mandatory field, required property, input necessity. Examples: "PropertyValueSpecification valueRequired 'true'", "PropertyValueSpecification valueRequired 'false'", "Form field valueRequired 'true'".
variableMeasured: A variable measured relation between a dataset or observation and the variables that are measured within it. Also called measured variable, data variable, observation parameter. Examples: "Dataset variableMeasured 'Temperature'", "Observation variableMeasured 'Humidity'", "Dataset variableMeasured 'Patient Age'".
variantCover: A variant cover relation between a comic issue and a description of its variant printing cover. Also called alternative cover, special edition cover, variant description. Examples: "ComicIssue variantCover 'Bryan Hitch Variant Cover'", "ComicIssue variantCover '2nd Printing Variant'", "ComicIssue variantCover 'Sketch Cover Edition'".
variesBy: A varies by relation between a product group and the properties by which its variants differ. Also called variant properties, differentiating attributes, product variations. Examples: "ProductGroup variesBy 'color'", "ProductGroup variesBy 'size'", "ProductGroup variesBy 'material'".
vatID: A VAT ID relation between an organization or person and their value-added Tax ID with a national prefix. Also called VAT number, tax identification number, sales tax ID. Examples: "Organization vatID 'IT123456789'", "Person vatID 'DE987654321'", "Company vatID 'FR1122334455'".
vehicleConfiguration: A vehicle configuration relation between a vehicle and a short text describing its specific setup. Also called vehicle setup, car configuration, model description. Examples: "Vehicle vehicleConfiguration '5dr hatchback ST 2.5 MT 225 hp'", "Vehicle vehicleConfiguration 'limited edition'", "Vehicle vehicleConfiguration 'AWD, leather seats'".
vehicleEngine: A vehicle engine relation between a vehicle and information about its engine(s). Also called engine details, motor specification, power unit. Examples: "Vehicle vehicleEngine 'V8 engine'", "Vehicle vehicleEngine 'Electric motor'", "Vehicle vehicleEngine '2.0L Turbocharged'".
vehicleIdentificationNumber: A vehicle identification number relation between a vehicle and its unique serial number (VIN). Also called VIN, chassis number, serial number. Examples: "Vehicle vehicleIdentificationNumber '1G1AP52W691XXXXXX'", "Car vehicleIdentificationNumber 'JTDKN31V60JXXXXXX'", "Truck vehicleIdentificationNumber '3FAHP000000XXXXXX'".
vehicleInteriorColor: A vehicle interior color relation between a vehicle and the color or color combination of its interior. Also called interior color, cabin color, upholstery color. Examples: "Vehicle vehicleInteriorColor 'Black'", "Vehicle vehicleInteriorColor 'Beige Leather'", "Vehicle vehicleInteriorColor 'Grey Fabric'".
vehicleInteriorType: A vehicle interior type relation between a vehicle and the type or material of its interior. Also called interior material, upholstery type, cabin trim. Examples: "Vehicle vehicleInteriorType 'leather'", "Vehicle vehicleInteriorType 'synthetic fabric'", "Vehicle vehicleInteriorType 'wood trim'".
vehicleModelDate: A vehicle model date relation between a vehicle and the release date of its model. Also called model year, release date, version date. Examples: "Vehicle vehicleModelDate '2023-01-01'", "Car vehicleModelDate '2024'", "Vehicle vehicleModelDate '2022-09-15'".
vehicleSeatingCapacity: A vehicle seating capacity relation between a vehicle and the number of passengers it can seat. Also called seating capacity, passenger capacity, number of seats. Examples: "Vehicle vehicleSeatingCapacity '5'", "Vehicle vehicleSeatingCapacity '7 persons'", "Vehicle vehicleSeatingCapacity '2'".
vehicleSpecialUsage: A vehicle special usage relation between a vehicle and an indication of whether it has been used for special purposes like commercial rental or as a taxi. Also called special use, commercial use, past usage. Examples: "Vehicle vehicleSpecialUsage 'Taxi'", "Vehicle vehicleSpecialUsage 'Commercial Rental'", "Vehicle vehicleSpecialUsage 'Driving School'".
vehicleTransmission: A vehicle transmission relation between a vehicle and the type of component used for transmitting power to the wheels. Also called transmission type, gearbox type, drivetrain. Examples: "Vehicle vehicleTransmission 'Automatic'", "Vehicle vehicleTransmission 'Manual'", "Vehicle vehicleTransmission 'Continuously Variable Transmission'".
vendor: A vendor relation between a buy action and the organization or person selling the item. Also called seller, merchant, supplier. Examples: "BuyAction vendor 'Amazon'", "BuyAction vendor 'Local Bookstore'", "BuyAction vendor 'John Doe'". Distinct from seller, which is the current preferred term.
verificationFactCheckingPolicy: A verification fact-checking policy relation between a news media organization or organization and a disclosure about its verification and fact-checking processes. Also called fact-checking policy, verification standards, editorial policy. Examples: "NewsMediaOrganization verificationFactCheckingPolicy 'https://example.com/fact-check-policy'", "Organization verificationFactCheckingPolicy 'Our journalists verify all claims.'", "News outlet verificationFactCheckingPolicy 'https://example.com/editorial-standards'".
version: A version relation between a creative work and the specific iteration embodied by a resource. Also called edition, revision, build. Examples: "Software version '2.0'", "Book version '3rd Edition'", "Document version '1.5'".
video: A video relation between a creative work and an embedded video object. Also called embedded video, video content, media clip. Examples: "Article video 'https://example.com/intro-video.mp4'", "ProductPage video 'https://example.com/product-demo.webm'", "CreativeWork video 'https://youtube.com/watch?v=xyz'".
videoFormat: A video format relation between a broadcast event, broadcast service, or screening event and the type of screening or video broadcast used. Also called screening format, broadcast type, display format. Examples: "ScreeningEvent videoFormat 'IMAX'", "BroadcastEvent videoFormat 'HD'", "ScreeningEvent videoFormat '3D'".
videoFrameSize: A video frame size relation between a video object and its dimensions. Also called frame dimensions, video resolution, aspect ratio. Examples: "VideoObject videoFrameSize '1920x1080'", "VideoObject videoFrameSize '1280x720'", "VideoObject videoFrameSize '640x480'".
videoQuality: A video quality relation between a video object and its level of visual fidelity. Also called video resolution, visual quality, picture quality. Examples: "VideoObject videoQuality 'HD'", "VideoObject videoQuality '4K'", "VideoObject videoQuality 'SD'".
volumeNumber: A volume number relation between a publication volume and its identifying number or text within a multi-part work. Also called publication volume, series volume, book volume. Examples: "PublicationVolume volumeNumber '2'", "PublicationVolume volumeNumber 'iii'", "Journal issue volumeNumber '10'".
warning: A warning relation between a drug and any FDA or other safety advisories. Also called drug warning, safety advisory, health alert. Examples: "Drug warning 'May cause drowsiness.'", "Drug warning 'https://fda.gov/drug-warnings/xyz'", "Medication warning 'Do not exceed recommended dose.'".
warranty: A warranty relation between a demand or offer and the warranty promise(s) included. Also called guarantee, product warranty, service warranty. Examples: "Offer warranty '1-year limited warranty'", "Demand warranty '30-day money-back guarantee'", "Product offer warranty 'Manufacturer's warranty included'". Distinct from warrantyPromise, which is the specific promise object.
warrantyPromise: A warranty promise relation between a buy or sell action and the specific warranty promise(s) included in the offer. Also called guarantee details, warranty terms, promise of warranty. Examples: "BuyAction warrantyPromise 'Standard 1-year warranty'", "SellAction warrantyPromise 'Extended 2-year warranty'", "Action warrantyPromise 'Lifetime guarantee'". Distinct from warranty, which is a more general property for the warranty itself.
warrantyScope: A warranty scope relation between a warranty promise and the extent or coverage of the promise. Also called warranty coverage, scope of guarantee, warranty extent. Examples: "WarrantyPromise warrantyScope 'Parts and Labor'", "WarrantyPromise warrantyScope 'Limited to manufacturing defects'", "WarrantyPromise warrantyScope 'Worldwide'".
webCheckinTime: A web check-in time relation between a flight and the time when passengers can check in online. Also called online check-in time, digital check-in start, flight check-in window. Examples: "Flight webCheckinTime '2023-11-01T08:00:00Z'", "Flight webCheckinTime '24 hours before departure'", "Flight webCheckinTime '2023-10-27T10:00:00'".
webFeed: A web feed relation between a podcast series or special announcement and the URL for its data feed (e.g., RSS or Atom). Also called RSS feed, Atom feed, podcast feed URL. Examples: "PodcastSeries webFeed 'https://example.com/podcast.rss'", "SpecialAnnouncement webFeed 'https://example.com/updates.atom'", "Blog webFeed 'https://example.com/blog/feed'".
weight: A weight relation between offer shipping details, a person, a product, shipping conditions, or visual artwork and its mass. Also called mass, physical weight, item weight. Examples: "Product weight '1.5 kg'", "Person weight '70 kg'", "ShippingConditions weight '5 lbs'".
weightPercentage: A fractional weight contribution relation between shipping rate settings and a numerical value, indicating the proportion of weight used for price calculation. Also called weight fraction, weight ratio, weight factor, weight proportion. Examples: ShippingRateSettings weightPercentage 0.10, ShippingRateSettings weightPercentage 0.05, ShippingRateSettings weightPercentage 0.25.
weightTotal: A total weight capacity relation between a vehicle and a quantitative value, representing the maximum permitted loaded weight. Also called maximum weight, gross vehicle weight, total loaded weight, permitted weight. Examples: Truck weightTotal 40000 kg, Car weightTotal 2000 kg, Van weightTotal 3500 kg.
wheelbase: A wheelbase dimension relation between a vehicle and a quantitative value, specifying the distance between its front and rear wheel centers. Also called wheel distance, axle distance, inter-axle distance. Examples: Sedan wheelbase 2.7 meters, Motorcycle wheelbase 1.5 meters, SUV wheelbase 3.0 meters.
width: A width dimension relation between an item (such as a media object, product, or artwork) and a distance or quantitative value. Also called breadth, extent across, lateral dimension. Examples: Product width 10 cm, VisualArtwork width 50 inches, MediaObject width 1920 pixels.
winner: A winner relation between a losing action and the person who won it. Also called victor, triumphant participant, successful party. Examples: ChessMatchLoseAction winner Alice, RaceLoseAction winner Bob, CompetitionLoseAction winner Charlie.
wordCount: A word count relation between a creative work and an integer, indicating the total number of words in its text. Also called text length, word total, lexical count. Examples: Article wordCount 1500, Book wordCount 80000, BlogPosting wordCount 750.
workExample: An example relation between a creative work and another creative work, where the latter is a specific instance, realization, or derivation of the former. Also called instance, realization, derivation, edition, version. Examples: Novel workExample PaperbackEdition, Album workExample DeluxeEdition, Film workExample DirectorCut. Distinct from workTranslation, which is a linguistic rendition of the content in another language.
workFeatured: A featured work relation between an event and a creative work, indicating that the work is highlighted or showcased within the event. Also called showcased work, highlighted work, exhibited work. Examples: ExhibitionEvent workFeatured PaintingA, FestivalEvent workFeatured SculptureB, ConferenceEvent workFeatured ResearchPaperC. Distinct from workPerformed, which is a live rendition of a work, and workPresented, which is a specific presentation of a movie at a screening event.
workHours: A work hours relation between a job posting and a text description, specifying the typical schedule or shifts for the position. Also called working schedule, shift pattern, typical hours. Examples: JobPosting workHours "9am-5pm, Mon-Fri", JobPosting workHours "Night Shift", JobPosting workHours "Flexible".
workLocation: A work location relation between a person and a contact point or place, identifying where the person performs their professional duties. Also called employment location, office address, workplace. Examples: John workLocation MainOffice, Jane workLocation RemoteHome, CompanyEmployee workLocation BranchOffice. Distinct from homeLocation, which is a person's residential address.
workPerformed: A performed work relation between an event and a creative work, indicating that the work is enacted or presented live during the event. Also called enacted work, live presentation, staged work. Examples: TheaterEvent workPerformed "Hamlet", ConcertEvent workPerformed "Symphony No. 5", DancePerformance workPerformed "Swan Lake". Distinct from workFeatured, which is a general showcasing, and workPresented, which is specifically for movies at screening events.
workPresented: A presented work relation between a screening event and a movie, identifying the film shown during that event. Also called screened movie, film shown, featured film. Examples: ScreeningEvent workPresented "The Matrix", FilmFestivalEvent workPresented "Parasite", DriveInMovie workPresented "Jaws". Distinct from workFeatured, which is a general showcasing, and workPerformed, which is for live enactments.
workTranslation: A translation relation between a creative work and another creative work, where the latter is a linguistic rendition of the former's content in a different language. Also called translated version, linguistic adaptation, foreign language edition. Examples: OriginalNovel workTranslation EnglishEdition, Poem workTranslation FrenchVersion, TechnicalManual workTranslation SpanishTranslation. Distinct from workExample, which is an instance or edition in the same language, not a linguistic translation.
workload: A workload relation between an exercise plan and an energy or quantitative value, representing the physiological output or energy expenditure of the exercise. Also called energy expenditure, exercise intensity, physical output. Examples: RunningPlan workload 500 kcal, WeightliftingPlan workload 2000 kJ, CyclingPlan workload 300 watts.
worksFor: An employment relation between a person and an organization, indicating the organization for which the person is employed. Also called employed by, affiliated with, works at, employed at. Examples: Employee worksFor CompanyA, Consultant worksFor AgencyB, Professor worksFor UniversityC. Distinct from memberOf, which indicates general membership in a group, not necessarily employment.
worstRating: A worst rating relation between a rating and a number or text, specifying the lowest possible value within that rating system. Also called minimum rating, lowest score, bottom value. Examples: RatingSystem worstRating 1, ReviewRating worstRating "Terrible", StarRating worstRating 0. Distinct from bestRating, which specifies the highest possible value.
xpath: An XPath relation between a speakable specification or web page element and an XPathType, identifying the XML Path Language expression used to locate the element. Also called XML path, element path, locator path. Examples: WebPageElement xpath "//div[@id='main']", SpeakableSpecification xpath "//h1", ArticleBody xpath "//article/p[1]". Distinct from cssSelector, which uses CSS selectors for element identification.
yearBuilt: A construction year relation between an accommodation and a number, indicating the year in which the accommodation was built. Also called construction year, built year, year of construction. Examples: Hotel yearBuilt 1985, ApartmentBuilding yearBuilt 2010, House yearBuilt 1950.
yearlyRevenue: A yearly revenue relation between a business audience and a quantitative value, representing the annual income generated by the business. Also called annual revenue, annual income, gross annual earnings. Examples: TargetAudience yearlyRevenue "$1M - $5M", BusinessAudience yearlyRevenue "over $10M", StartupAudience yearlyRevenue "under $500K".
yearsInOperation: An operational age relation between a business audience and a quantitative value, indicating the number of years the business has been active. Also called business age, operational duration, years active. Examples: TargetAudience yearsInOperation "5-10 years", BusinessAudience yearsInOperation "over 20 years", StartupAudience yearsInOperation "under 2 years".
yield: A yield relation between a how-to guide and a quantitative value or text, specifying the quantity or type of output produced by following the instructions. Also called output quantity, resulting amount, production yield. Examples: HowToRecipe yield "12 cookies", HowToCraft yield "1 paper airplane", HowToGuide yield "5 liters of jam".
